dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Whether a school near you runs the full IB continuum or picks the Diploma up at 16 changes what a student arrives with. The notes below say what each programme assumes, and what that means for the kind of tutor a Dubai family should be looking for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level subjects and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level is where specialist supply thins out: the content runs deeper, the extra papers are the ones that separate grades, and a tutor who is comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically comfortable above it. Match by level explicitly, in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session and apply to UK, North American and UAE universities in parallel. Several Dubai schools run the Diploma alongside A Level, so a Year 11 family is choosing routes rather than following one, and the useful tutor for that fortnight is someone who has taught both and can read a marked IGCSE paper against each.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-marked on A to D bands rather than by percentage, which trips up families arriving from a British or Indian system mid-stream. The tutoring need here is usually translation: what the band descriptor is asking for, and how a competent piece of work ends up in a 5-6 band. Subject knowledge matters less at this stage than fluency in the criteria.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP-to-DP transition is where the requests cluster, particularly in mathematics. Schools that run both place the personal project in Year 11, and a student whose Year 11 was spent on that project often enters DP1 with an algebra gap nobody noticed. A diagnostic in the first six weeks of DP1 is cheaper than a rescue in DP2.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examinations and no percentages. Parents searching for a tutor at this stage usually want reading fluency, number sense or English as an additional language, none of which need an IB specialist. What they do need is someone who will not import a British Year 5 scheme of work into an inquiry classroom and confuse the child.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies under KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils and a prohibition on combining the two groups. A non-Arab child beginning Arabic as an additional language is the most common primary request in the emirate, and it is a language-teaching brief rather than an IB one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses inside it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so the tutoring brief is identical for those subjects and absent for the career-related units, which the provider assesses.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so a proximity search returns almost nothing relevant and a family has no local peer group to compare with. The practical approach is to treat the Diploma courses as the tutorable part and ask the school's coordinator what evidence the reflective project criteria actually require.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Below, the topic inside each subject that generates most of the requests we receive from Dubai families. Not the whole syllabus — the specific place where a cohort reliably stalls, which is also the place a weekly session earns its fee fastest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium at Standard Level; organic mechanisms and the data-analysis demands of Paper 3 at Higher Level. Requests spike in DP1 term two, when the internal investigation design lands at the same time as the first serious equilibrium questions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion, then the written-explanation questions that ask for a reason rather than a number. Higher Level students who handle the mathematics comfortably often arrive needing help only with the prose half of the paper, which is a different lesson entirely.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and proof at Higher Level; the step up from IGCSE algebra in the first term of DP1 at both levels. This is the single most requested subject and level combination across Dubai, and the one where early-evening availability is tightest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical tests and the written conclusion that must follow them, plus documented calculator work. Students moving here from Analysis and Approaches mid-course often underestimate the modelling content and overestimate how much of it is arithmetic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions on unfamiliar contexts, and the Higher Level extension topics that arrive late in DP2. Recall is rarely the problem in Dubai cohorts; applying a known process to a named organism in a graph is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram-to-prose linkage, and the evaluation paragraph that must end in a judgement. Higher Level calculation questions are a separate brief and often need only two or three sessions once the formulae are secure.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Applying a tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool. The marks a Dubai cohort usually leaves on the table sit in the application and evaluation strands of the case study, not in the content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the global issue in the Individual Oral. Students fluent in English but schooled outside a literature tradition often need technique vocabulary before anything else, which is a short and very productive brief.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Text-type conventions for the writing paper and the structured conversation in the oral. The requests here come disproportionately from families whose child changed curriculum mid-secondary and landed in B rather than A.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1 and the Higher Level regional option essays. The constraint is almost always named detail: dates, figures, named actors. Sessions that build a usable case-study bank move marks faster than essay practice alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and the Higher Level resource-management topics. Supply is thin across the whole region at Higher Level, so this is one to ask about early rather than in the term it becomes urgent.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Turning a topic into a knowledge question, and the exhibition's requirement to tie an object to a prompt. A single block of three or four sessions at the right moment usually does more here than a standing weekly slot.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: Proximity is not meaningless in Dubai — it decides when a session can start, not who should teach it. The notes below record what each district's commute does to an evening, which is the part of the map that still matters once the lesson is online.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Large school population with a heavy CBSE presence and a smaller IB cohort, so a local search returns plenty of tutors and few Diploma specialists. Pupils are generally home by 3pm, making a 4pm start workable on weekdays.

regions.name: Motor City, Sports City and Dubai Studio City
regions.note: Several schools inside the ring but Diploma provision concentrated in two of them. The internal road network keeps the school run short, so 4.30pm sessions hold up even in term-time traffic.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing catchments where many secondary pupils travel out to Barsha or Sustainable City schools. Return times drift to 4.45pm or later, which pushes a realistic weekday slot to 6pm.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Dense apartment stock with students spread across a dozen schools. The scheduling constraint here is a quiet room rather than the road, and a pair of headphones usually resolves it.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Sits next to the university cluster, which means plenty of undergraduate tutors advertising locally and few Higher Level subject specialists. Pupils at the nearby schools are generally home before 3.30pm.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities feeding schools in Arabian Ranches and Emirates Hills. Secondary pupils are rarely home before 4.15pm, and sport on two evenings a week narrows the usable slots to three.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Short physical distances and a long single access road, so a 20-minute journey can become 40 at the wrong hour. Families here tend to prefer a fixed 6.30pm slot that the traffic cannot move.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Mizhar
regions.note: One full IB continuum school plus several large schools on other curricula, so households often run two systems at once. Early slots at 4pm are realistic, which matters for students carrying three Higher Levels.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City, Al Garhoud and Deira
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster ask most often for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and for English A Paper 1 work. It is also the part of the city where a local search returns the fewest Diploma-specific results, because the schools on other curricula dominate the tutoring market here.

schoolClusters.city: The Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park and Al Furjan
schoolClusters.note: A newer cluster with two full continuum schools, so Diploma students here have been criterion-marked for years and arrive with the vocabulary already in place. The requests skew towards Higher Level sciences, which is also where the supply across the region is thinnest.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park
schoolClusters.note: A mixed cluster where IB, British and Indian curricula sit within a few kilometres of each other. Families here frequently have two children on two systems, and the practical question is which child needs a specialist and which needs a generalist.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Three shapes a Dubai family uses, chosen by what the calendar is doing rather than by preference. The first two are standing commitments; the third is a block with an end date, which is usually the right answer when a single component is the problem.

modes.title: One subject, one standing slot
modes.description: A fixed 60-minute session each week on a single subject at a named level, in the same slot so the family stops negotiating it. Suits a Higher Level subject across a full term, and suits the DP1 student who is not yet in trouble but is working harder than the result suggests.
bullets: Same time every week, set around the real return commute
One subject, one level, one specialist
Marking between sessions, not inside the hour
Review at week six against the baseline script

modes.title: Two subjects, two specialists
modes.description: Where a student needs Chemistry and Mathematics rather than science and maths, the right answer is two tutors who each teach one of them. Families often resist this because one tutor sounds simpler; the marked papers usually make the case within a fortnight.
bullets: Separate specialists, separate slots, one point of contact
Each tutor works from that subject's own marked scripts
Session notes arrive separately and stay subject-specific
Either subject can be paused without disturbing the other

modes.title: A short component block
modes.description: Four to six sessions aimed at one named thing: Paper 3 technique, source analysis in History Paper 1, documented calculator work in Applications and Interpretation, or the structure of a Theory of Knowledge exhibition. Ends on a date, with a marked piece of work at the start and at the finish.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns in a city of 227 private schools
paragraphs: A local search is a filter, and it is worth knowing what it filters on. It sorts by the business address a provider has published, by whether a listing claims to serve your community, and by advertising spend. None of those three correlate with whether anyone in the result teaches Higher Level Chemistry. The sort is working correctly; it is answering a different question from the one the family has.

The practical effect in Dubai is a results page dominated by generalists and tuition centres in the areas with the most centres, which are not necessarily the areas with the most Diploma students. Al Quoz and Al Barsha carry a disproportionate share of the city's tuition premises; Nad Al Sheba and the Sustainable City carry a disproportionate share of its continuum IB students. The map and the need do not line up.

Worth testing before you shortlist anyone: ask which level of which subject they teach this academic year, and which paper they would start on. A specialist answers in one sentence with a component in it. A generalist answers with a subject group. The question takes ten seconds and removes most of a local results page.
The table below sets out what a proximity search genuinely narrows and what it leaves entirely unaddressed, so you can see which of your decisions it is actually helping with.

One more thing a local result page hides. Tuition premises in Dubai cluster where commercial rent and footfall make sense, which is not where Diploma cohorts are largest, so the geography of the supply has very little to do with the geography of the need.

sections.heading: The twenty-minute radius, district by district
paragraphs: If a tutor has to travel, the radius they will realistically serve is about twenty minutes at the hour your child is free — which in Dubai is the hour when Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Khail Road and the Business Bay crossing are all at their worst. That radius is a different shape in every district, and in some of them it contains no Diploma schools at all.

Think of it as two numbers rather than one. The first is when your child is physically home and fed, which is set by the school bus route and nothing else. The second is the latest hour at which a 17-year-old absorbs new content, which most families put somewhere between 7.30pm and 8pm. The usable window between those two numbers is often ninety minutes, and a visiting tutor spends a third of it on the road.

The table below is the version of the map that still matters. It pairs each district with the school cluster it feeds and a session start that holds up in term time, drawn from what Dubai families actually book rather than from distances on a map.

Once the lesson is on video the first number is the only one that counts. The session starts when the student sits down, and the slot can be 4pm in Mirdif and 6.30pm on the Palm without anybody negotiating with the traffic.

Worth writing both numbers down before you ring anybody. A family that knows its child is home at 4.45pm and fading by 7.45pm has a three-hour window and a clear question to ask; a family that has not counted it will accept whatever slot is offered and wonder in March why the sessions stopped working.

sections.heading: Which Higher Level subjects Dubai is actually short of
paragraphs: Supply is uneven by subject and level, and no provider in this market publishes that. It is the most useful thing a family can know before booking, because it determines whether the right answer is to start next week or to accept a date three weeks out and plan around it. We would rather give a date than put a Higher Level student with someone meeting the syllabus for the first time.

The pattern is consistent. Standard Level humanities and both Standard Level maths routes are comfortably covered. Higher Level sciences are tighter, with Chemistry and Physics the tightest in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window because the same hours are in demand across the Gulf. Computer Science and the less common Language B options at Higher Level are the thinnest of all, and those are worth asking about a term early rather than a week late.

The dates in the table are match times, meaning how long it typically takes to put a named specialist in front of a student for a trial, not a promise about a particular week. They move with the calendar: the fortnight after mock results and the eight weeks before the May session are the two points where everything tightens at once.

If the honest answer for your combination is a wait, you will get a wait and a date. What you will not get is a generalist described as a specialist, which is the standard failure mode of a marketplace that sorts by distance.

sections.heading: Where the marks go, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: A tutor matched by distance starts with a conversation about confidence. A tutor matched by component starts with a marked script and a known failure pattern. The patterns below are the ones that repeat across Dubai cohorts, grouped by the Diploma's own subject groups, and each has a different remedy with a different number of sessions attached to it.

Two of them are worth singling out because they are cheap to fix and expensive to ignore. The first is the command-term misread, which costs most in the essay-based subjects and almost nothing in mathematics. The second is unnamed detail in the humanities: a Geography or History answer that describes a general process scores in the bottom half of the band however well written it is, and the fix is a case-study bank rather than more essay practice.

The third pattern is the one families least expect. Strong students in Physics and both mathematics routes frequently lose marks not on the mathematics but on the prose — the question that asks for a reason instead of a value. That is a writing lesson inside a science subject, and a tutor who only sets more calculation questions will never touch it.
None of this is visible in a search result. It becomes visible in the first marked paper, which is why the trial lesson in our process starts with one.

The remedy column matters as much as the diagnosis. A command-term problem is four sessions of work; a missing case-study bank is closer to eight; dropped accuracy marks in mathematics can be largely cleared in two or three. Knowing which one you have is what stops a family paying for the wrong eight weeks.

sections.heading: What a session fixes that an evening of revision does not
paragraphs: A student revising alone practises what they can already do. It is not laziness; it is the only thing available, because the questions they get wrong produce no feedback and so no learning. Three hours of unsupervised past papers tends to consolidate the existing mark rather than move it, which is why a family can see real effort and no improvement and conclude the child is not trying.

A session breaks that loop in three ways. It picks the question the student would have avoided. It watches the working rather than the answer, which is where the diagnosis lives. And it marks against the published scheme, so the student sees the mark allocation instead of a tick or a cross. None of those three requires a tutor in the room, and all three require a tutor who knows the component.

The second thing a session does is set the next week's work precisely. Not "revise equilibrium" but four named questions, in an order, with the hard one third rather than last. Dubai students are generally busy rather than idle, and a vague instruction is what loses the week.

The third is pace. Left alone, a student will spend three weeks on the topic they find interesting and avoid the one that is costing marks. A session that opens with ten minutes on last week's weak topic makes avoidance impossible without anybody raising their voice.

There is a fourth gain, and it is the one students mention themselves. Somebody is expecting the work on Tuesday, which converts a vague intention into a fixed appointment. In a Dubai term with three internal deadlines in the same fortnight, that single external deadline is often what keeps a subject from being quietly dropped.

sections.heading: The nearest subject teacher may be the one person who cannot help
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, applied for through its app, website and e-services system.

The constraint that matters for a proximity search sits in the code of conduct attached to that permit, and in ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff as reported by Gulf News: a teacher may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on it. The direction of travel is clear either way.

So the most appealing result in a local search — your child's own subject teacher, who already knows the class and the deadlines — is frequently the one arrangement that should not be made. Asking a teacher to tutor your child privately puts their position at risk, not yours, and a professional will decline. It is better not to ask.

What a parent can verify is simpler than it sounds. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, ask what their relationship to your child's school is, and ask the question in writing so the answer is in writing. Any provider that treats those as awkward questions has told you something useful.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges once the car is counted
paragraphs: Published AED figures in this market, read in October 2026, are set out below. They are other providers' rates rather than ours: IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and a plan's cost depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week it genuinely needs. What the table adds to the usual price list is the travel column, because that is the part a near-me search is implicitly buying.

A visiting tutor's rate carries the journey inside it whether or not the invoice says so. Bestimate's Dubai figures for in-home one-to-one run AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is roughly the cost of a car in evening traffic, and it buys presence in the room rather than more teaching.

Monthly packages in this market sit at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Compare those on sessions and on minutes, not on the headline: eight shorter online sessions and four long in-home ones are different products, and the second spends a chunk of each visit settling in.

Ask three questions before agreeing any rate in Dubai. Does the figure include VAT. Does it include marking and written feedback outside the session. And what is the cancellation window, since a slot cancelled at 4pm for a school event is a cost somebody absorbs.

sections.heading: Why distance stops mattering once the lesson is on video
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions on this page are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so tutor and student work on the same script at the same moment. A scanned past paper can be marked up by both of them while they talk.

What that buys is the match. A Higher Level Physics student in Al Warqa is matched to a Higher Level Physics specialist rather than to the nearest available science teacher, and the search runs across the whole pool instead of a twenty-minute radius. For the subjects named earlier as tight, that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

It also buys back the minutes. A visiting tutor's hour contains the journey, the arrival, the settling and the departure; a video session contains the hour. Marking happens between sessions rather than in the first ten minutes, so an hour that costs less is also an hour with more teaching inside it.

The honest limitation is physical. Bench practical work and exhibition-based arts components happen at school and belong to the school. What a video session can do with them is the design, the data analysis and the write-up against the published criteria, which is where the majority of those components' marks actually sit.

For families moving between emirates or travelling in term time, the same property helps in a duller way: the slot survives the move. A student in a hotel in Abu Dhabi for a fortnight keeps the Tuesday session, which is not true of any arrangement that depends on somebody driving to a particular building.

sections.heading: Choosing by component instead of by community
paragraphs: The practical replacement for a proximity search is a four-line brief, and it takes a minute to write. Subject. Level. The paper or component causing trouble. The date of the next assessment that matters. Send that with one marked script and the shortlisting problem largely solves itself, because most tutors will self-select out of a brief that names a component.

Then ask the three questions a near-me search cannot answer. Who exactly will teach the sessions. Where marking happens and whether it sits inside the paid hour. And what the first six weeks would target, in component terms. A specialist answers all three quickly. Anyone who answers in generalities about confidence and rapport is describing a different service.

Use the trial lesson as a measurement rather than a meeting. Ours is free, takes no card details, and produces a written diagnosis you keep whether you continue or not: what the script showed, which topics are secure, what the first three sessions would do. Compare two of those diagnoses side by side and the decision is usually obvious.

If the answer for your combination is that nobody suitable is free, we say so and give a date. That is a worse answer than yes and a much better one than a generalist with a confident manner, which is what sorting by distance eventually produces.

Keep the brief when you have written it. Families who end up changing tutor once, for perfectly ordinary reasons, find that the same four lines plus an updated marked script restarts the process in a day rather than a fortnight, because the hard thinking was done the first time.

process.title: Write the four-line brief
process.description: Subject, level, the component causing trouble, and the date of the next assessment that counts. Four lines does more than a long conversation about how your child is finding school, because it lets us check real availability in that exact subject and level before anybody promises you anything.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A mock paper, a unit test, a returned draft with the teacher's comments. One marked page lets the specialist arrive at the trial with a hypothesis instead of an introduction, and it is the difference between a first session that diagnoses and one that gets acquainted.

process.title: Hear the honest availability
process.description: We tell you the match time for that subject and level and whether the slot you want exists in the Gulf evening window. If it is two weeks, you hear two weeks. Nobody is put in front of a Higher Level student on the basis that they teach the subject group.

process.title: Free trial, with a written diagnosis
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details. The student attempts a timed question, the tutor marks it against the published scheme, and you receive a note naming the secure topics, the gaps and what the first three sessions would target. Yours either way.

process.title: Fix the slot and the review date
process.description: Agree the weekly time around your real return commute rather than around a map, and set the week-six review in the same message. Sessions run live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and a session note reaches you within 24 hours of each one.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry means a Higher Level Chemistry teacher, named before you book. Because the lesson is online, that match is made across the whole pool rather than inside a twenty-minute drive of your community, which is where the specialists are not.

whyPoints.title: Availability told straight
whyPoints.description: We publish which subjects and levels are tight in the Gulf evening window and give a real match time. If the honest answer is a two-week wait for Higher Level Computer Science, that is the answer you get rather than a generalist with a confident manner.

whyPoints.title: The hour contains an hour
whyPoints.description: No journey, no settling, no arrival. Marking happens between sessions against the published scheme, so the paid time goes on teaching and diagnosis. That is a larger difference in useful minutes than most of the rate differences in this market.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the real commute
whyPoints.description: A 4pm slot works in Mirdif and does not work on the Palm, and we set the time from when your child is actually home rather than from a distance on a map. Slots can also move after school events without a travel cost attached to the change.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered in writing
whyPoints.description: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Ask us about permit status and the tutor's relationship to your child's school, and you get the answer in writing. We claim no regulator's approval for ourselves.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Feedback by criterion, delivered separately from the document, with the student's dated drafts untouched. IB Gram does not write, complete or edit Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays, and says so on every page.

faqs.question: Does an IB tutor near me in Dubai mean a tutor in the same community?
faqs.answer: It usually means a provider whose published address or service-area claim sits near yours, which is not the same thing. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, and a community with four schools inside a ten-minute drive may have only one running the Diploma. The person who teaches Higher Level Chemistry to a dozen students in your area is probably already teaching them. Sorting by distance returns generalists and tuition centres from the districts with the most premises, not the specialists for your subject.

faqs.question: How late can a tuition session realistically start in Mirdif on a school night?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most of Dubai, which is the useful part. Pupils in Mirdif and Al Mizhar are generally home by about 3.15pm, so a 4pm start is workable without touching the evening. Compare that with Dubai Marina or Jumeirah Village Circle, where a 4.45pm return pushes a sensible slot to 6pm. Set the time from when your child is actually home and fed, not from a distance on a map. On video the session begins when they sit down.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to staff across Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are consistently tight in the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window, because the same hours are in demand across the whole Gulf. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most requested combination overall. Computer Science at Higher Level and the less common Language B options are thinnest of all. If your child is taking any of those, ask about availability a term before it becomes urgent rather than in the week the mock result arrives.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai students most often lose marks in Chemistry Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Two places. Energetics and equilibrium produce the heaviest content losses, usually a dropped sign convention or an explanation that describes a shift without naming what drives it. The second is Paper 3, where the marks are for handling unfamiliar data and evaluating a method rather than for recall. Organic mechanisms lose marks on curly-arrow placement rather than on the chemistry. All three show up on a marked script within one session, which is why we ask for one before the trial.

faqs.question: What does a twenty-minute radius around Dubai Marina actually contain?
faqs.answer: At 5pm on a weekday, less than the map suggests. The Marina, JBR and Palm Jumeirah sit behind a small number of access roads, so a twenty-minute journey becomes forty at the wrong hour. The schools most Marina secondary pupils attend are in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim rather than in the Marina itself. A tutor willing to travel into that radius at that hour is a short list, and it is not sorted by who teaches your child's subject.

faqs.question: Does Sheikh Zayed Road traffic change what time our lesson should start?
faqs.answer: It changes when your child is home, which is the only number that matters once the lesson is online. For households in Business Bay, Downtown and the Marina, the return commute lands between 4.30pm and 5pm in term time, so a 6pm or 6.30pm fixed slot is more reliable than an earlier one that keeps slipping. For a visiting tutor it changes much more, because the journey sits inside the hour you are paying for and inside the window your child can still concentrate in.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a distant subject specialist?
faqs.answer: For homework supervision at 11 or 12, a competent generalist nearby is fine and cheaper. For a Higher Level Diploma subject it is not a close call. Higher Level content runs deeper than Standard Level, the extra papers are the ones that separate grades, and a tutor who has not taught that syllabus will be reading it alongside your child. Distance is irrelevant to a video lesson, so the only thing being traded away by choosing locally is subject depth.

faqs.question: Which Dubai areas have the most IB World Schools within one drive?
faqs.answer: Al Barsha and Barsha South hold the densest cluster in the emirate, followed by the newer catchments around Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and the Sustainable City, and the continuum schools serving Mirdif and Al Jaddaf. Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda have large school populations with proportionally fewer Diploma cohorts, which is exactly where a local tutor search returns the least relevant results. Check what your own school offers on KHDA's site rather than relying on a tutoring site's list.

faqs.question: What does a session fix in Physics Paper 2 that revision at home does not?
faqs.answer: Three things. It picks the question your child would have skipped, which is where the diagnosis lives. It watches the working rather than the answer, so a method mark lost to a missing line gets caught. And it marks against the published scheme, so the student sees where the marks actually sit on an extended-response question. Physics students in Dubai cohorts are usually strong numerically and thin on written explanation, and unsupervised past papers consolidate that imbalance rather than correcting it.

faqs.question: How soon can a Dubai family be matched with a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject and the slot. Standard Level maths and humanities usually within a few days. Higher Level Chemistry or Physics in the 5pm to 7pm window is more often one to two weeks. Higher Level Computer Science can be two to three. We give you the real figure before you commit, and if it is a wait you get a date rather than a substitute. The two tightest points in the year are the fortnight after mock results and the eight weeks before the May session.

faqs.question: Do tutors drive to homes in Dubai, or is this taught over video?
faqs.answer: Over video, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Other providers in this market do travel, and their published rates reflect it at roughly AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for qualified online teaching. What you lose is somebody in the room. What you gain is a match made on subject and level rather than on a twenty-minute radius.

faqs.question: What does the market charge per hour for an IB tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published AED figures read in October 2026 run from about AED 45-150 an hour for a generalist or university student online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 where a tutor travels to an address, AED 200-450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500-650 or more at the examiner-experienced end. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. Ask whether VAT and marking are inside the figure, because both move the real cost per useful hour.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth a weekly session?
faqs.answer: Rarely weekly, often a block. The course asks students to turn topics into knowledge questions and to tie an object to a prompt in the exhibition, and both are skills that respond to three or four well-timed sessions rather than to a standing slot across two years. The right moments are when the exhibition prompts are issued and when the essay titles are released. A tutor may give criterion feedback on a draft; a tutor may not write or rewrite any part of it.

faqs.question: Our child studies Business Management Higher Level. What is the weak point?
faqs.answer: Application, almost always. Students learn the tools, draw them neatly, and then write an answer that never touches the stimulus material, which leaves the application and evaluation marks on the table. The quantitative questions lose marks on formula recall rather than on interpretation, which is a two-session fix. Higher Level students should also check how much of their grade sits in the internal assessment, because that is where an early, criterion-led conversation pays for itself several times over.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know which school in Dubai our child attends?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the calendar rather than the status. Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines for coursework, their own mock windows and their own moderation timetable, and a tutor working to the wrong dates is useful in the wrong month. Hand over the school's assessment calendar at the first session. We name schools on this page as market context only, and we claim no affiliation with, or endorsement from, any of them.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody suitable is free in the week we want to start?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. We would rather leave a slot empty than put a Higher Level student with somebody who teaches the subject group but not the level, because six weeks of that costs more than a fortnight of waiting. If the wait is long, we will say which component could usefully be worked on in the meantime and what your child can do unsupervised without consolidating the same errors.

intro.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 3 is a search with a hidden assumption inside it: that the right tutor is a person who can reach your villa. Arabian Ranches 3 sits on the far side of Al Qudra Road, in the Dubailand belt, with Emirates Road on one flank and the Dubai-Al Ain corridor on the other. Draw a twenty-minute drive radius around it in the evening and you capture a few thousand households, a handful of tuition centres on Hessa Street and whoever happens to be free between six and eight. Draw the same circle around a Diploma syllabus instead and you capture a different, much more useful set of people.

The Diploma is not one qualification. It is six courses, each with its own assessment grid, sat at Standard or Higher Level, plus three core components that are marked against published criteria. A tutor who is strong on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is usually not the same person who can take apart a Chemistry internal assessment or coach a Theory of Knowledge exhibition. Hiring by postcode means hiring whoever is nearest and hoping the subject match follows. It rarely does, and the cost of the mismatch is a term.

This page is written from the syllabus rather than the map. It sets out what the Diploma actually assesses, which command terms carry which marking expectations, where students in this part of Dubai lose marks in each subject group, how the internal assessment criteria are weighted letter by letter, and how past papers should be worked so that they teach something rather than confirm what a student already knows. It also states the market price for tuition in the Dubailand villa communities in AED, with the source of each band.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one to one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording your child can rewatch before a test. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches 3 or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate limit, not an apology. It is the reason a family on this side of Al Qudra Road can book a Physics Higher Level specialist for a Tuesday at seven rather than settling for a generalist who lives in Motor City.

What follows is long because the Diploma is detailed and because the pages currently ranking for this search are not. The best of them runs to roughly 2,300 words and carries no data table at all. If you only have five minutes, read the command-terms table, the internal assessment table and the AED rate table, then skip to the fourteen questions at the end.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Arabian Ranches 3 households request most, with what each one actually assesses and the point in it where marks reliably disappear. The description is the diagnostic; it is what a first session is spent establishing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, calculus. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens. Marks go on unjustified steps, missing 'hence' links and algebra done in the head. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and harder integration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same five topic headings with a modelling and technology emphasis, and a graphic display calculator permitted in every paper. Students lose marks by quoting calculator output without the statistical reasoning behind it, misreading regression context and skipping units. HL carries matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical testing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is short and extended response. Marks go on describing a graph instead of explaining the physics behind it, on uncertainty treatment, and on fields and circular motion. HL extends every theme rather than adding separate options.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around structure and reactivity, with a data booklet available in the examination that many students never learn to use at speed. Losses cluster in organic mechanisms drawn without curly arrows, energetics sign conventions and equilibrium explanations that restate Le Chatelier rather than applying it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led, with heavy demand on precise terminology and on reading unfamiliar data. Students who revise by rereading notes stall at a 4 or 5. The gain comes from writing answers to the command term and from practising the graph and table questions that carry a disproportionate share of Paper 2 marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade more than content recall. Axes mislabelled, no shift arrow, no reference to the diagram in the prose: three marks gone before the argument starts. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, each with a tight word allowance, and HL adds quantitative policy work.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by writing about theme while ignoring how the text is built. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to argue in ten minutes.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-led: students must apply named frameworks to a case rather than describe them. Marks go on generic answers that would fit any company and on ignoring the stimulus material. HL adds depth in operations and a business research project with a strict word limit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects answering an internal assessment prompt. The common failure is writing about the topic instead of about knowledge. Coaching consists of question framing, counter-argument structure and object selection, with the writing left entirely to the student.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in one subject, supervised by a teacher at school. Marks go on a question too broad to answer, a method section that cannot be replicated and an engagement record completed the week before submission. Support means question narrowing, source criticism and structural feedback only.

sections.heading: The Diploma as a tutor reads it: six groups, two levels, one core
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate takes one subject from each of six groups — studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with a second subject from groups one to five permitted instead of an art. Three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. Each is graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42 subject points, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix contributes up to 3 more for a ceiling of 45.

The level difference is content, not polish. An SL course is built on 150 teaching hours and an HL course on 240. Those ninety extra hours are additional syllabus, longer papers and, in several subjects, an extra paper. A parent who assumes HL means the same material taught harder will misread why their child is suddenly behind: the HL class has simply covered things the SL class never meets. This is the single most common misunderstanding in a first consultation from this community.

The core is where points are quietly won and lost. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research in one subject with a named supervisor at school. Theory of Knowledge is a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Both are marked against published criteria, both are submitted to internal deadlines set by your child's coordinator, and neither may be written by anyone other than the student. A tutor's job on the core is to interrogate the question and the method, then hand the writing back.

sections.heading: Command terms: the part of the mark scheme nobody is taught
paragraphs: Every IB question opens with a command term, and every command term has an assessment objective attached to it. A student who answers 'explain' with a description has written something true and scored nothing. This is the cheapest grade in the Diploma to recover, because it costs no new content: it is a reading habit, and eight weeks of deliberate practice fixes it. It is also almost never taught explicitly, because class time goes on syllabus coverage.

The diagnosis is quick. Take a marked Paper 2 and highlight the command term in each question the student lost marks on. The pattern is usually one of two things: the student answered a lower-order term when a higher-order one was asked, or they answered the right term but stopped before the mark scheme did. 'Evaluate' without a judgement, 'justify' without a reason, 'compare' with two separate paragraphs and no point of contact — each of these is a specific, repeatable loss.

The table below lists the terms that cause the most damage in science, maths and individuals-and-societies papers, with what the mark scheme expects and the loss that follows when a student misreads it. Work through it with your child's own script in front of you, question by question, rather than reading it as a reference list. The terms are defined in the subject guides on ibo.org; read them there for the exact wording for your subject, because the emphasis shifts slightly between guides and a term that means one thing in Biology can carry a narrower expectation in Economics.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: Grades do not fall evenly across a paper. In almost every Diploma subject the losses concentrate in two or three identifiable places, and a tutor who knows where they are can diagnose a script in a single session. This is the difference between a specialist and a capable graduate: both can do the maths, but only one can look at a lost mark and name the habit that caused it.

In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches the non-calculator paper is the hinge. Students who have done all their practice with a graphic display calculator cannot manipulate surds and logarithms at speed, and they lose method marks for steps done mentally. In Physics the loss is uncertainty and graph interpretation: a candidate who can calculate a gradient but cannot say what it represents forfeits the explanation marks that carry the band. In Chemistry it is organic mechanisms and the sign conventions in energetics.

In the humanities the pattern inverts: content is rarely the problem, structure is. Economics candidates lose marks on diagrams that are drawn but never referenced in the prose. English candidates write about what a text says instead of how it works. Business Management candidates apply a framework in the abstract rather than to the stimulus company. None of these is a knowledge gap, which is why rereading notes does not move the grade and marked past-paper work does. A single session spent reading two marked scripts against the published scheme will usually identify every one of them by name, and that list is what the first month of tutoring should be built around.

sections.heading: Internal assessment, criterion by criterion and mark by mark
paragraphs: Most Diploma subjects carry an internal assessment worth around a fifth of the final grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Because it is coursework, it is the most controllable component on the whole programme — and because it is coursework, it is where academic-honesty rules bite hardest. A student who knows the criterion letters and their mark allocations is working to a visible target. One who does not is guessing.

The criteria are not interchangeable between subjects. A Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with the mathematics itself carrying the largest share and personal engagement and reflection carrying three marks each. The science investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, which means evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis — a distribution that surprises most students, who spend their time on the practical and their last evening on the evaluation.

A tutor's role here is bounded and worth stating plainly. The tutor may help narrow a research question, question a method, point to a criterion the draft does not yet address and explain what the descriptor means. The tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply content. IB Gram does not produce assessed work for students, and a tutor who offers to is putting the candidate at risk of a malpractice finding that no grade is worth. Ask any tutor you hire, here or elsewhere, where they draw that line before the first session.

sections.heading: Past papers, worked so that they teach instead of confirm
paragraphs: Most students use past papers as a thermometer. They sit one, score what they always score, feel briefly worse and move on. Used properly a past paper is the single most efficient teaching tool in the Diploma, and the difference is entirely in the order of operations. Read the mark scheme for a question before answering it, not after. A student who has seen how the marks are allocated writes a different answer, and the habit transfers to questions they have never seen.

The second change is to stop sitting whole papers for most of the term. Whole papers measure; question sets teach. Pick the six questions on one topic across six sessions, work them under time, then mark them against the scheme and write one line in an error log naming the cause of each lost mark. After four weeks that log, not the scores, is the tutoring plan. Nearly every student's log collapses into three or four recurring causes, and those are fixable in a term.

Sourcing matters too, and here the honest answer is a limit. IB Gram does not host or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are the boards' copyright and your child's school holds the licensed access. Ask the subject teacher or the DP coordinator for the papers, work from the official subject guides on ibo.org, and treat any website offering a free library of recent IB papers with real caution.

paragraphs: The process is short. You send the subject, the level, the school and the last marked piece of work; we read the script before the call rather than after it; a specialist is proposed with their subject background stated; a trial session runs before a block is booked. Nothing in that sequence requires anybody to drive anywhere, which is why a 7pm Tuesday slot is actually a 7pm Tuesday slot.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. Niche Higher Level combinations — Further Mathematics, a less commonly taught group 2 language, Music, some Design Technology work — have thin coverage inside the UAE, and when they do we say so rather than placing a generalist and hoping. The alternative we offer is a specialist outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed in advance, with the time-zone implication stated before you commit. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

One legal point worth knowing before you hire anyone, in or out of this community. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted by MoHRE work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the MoHRE service page lists a two-working-day completion time with applications made through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure you read online with caution. Ask any tutor you hire whether they hold the permit.

process.title: Send the script, not just the subject
process.description: The fastest diagnostic is your child's last marked paper or internal assessment draft. Tell us the subject, the level, the school and what the teacher's comment said. A photograph of two marked pages tells a subject specialist more about where the marks are going than a thirty-minute conversation about how the term has gone.

process.title: Match by syllabus and level, then by availability
process.description: We match on the exact course — Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, not 'maths' — and on the assessment your child is closest to. Only then do we look at the calendar. The subject background of the proposed tutor is stated plainly, including what they have taught and at which level, so you can judge the fit yourself.

process.title: Run a trial session and read the summary
process.description: A trial session happens before any block is booked. Afterwards you get a written summary naming the two or three habits causing the lost marks and what the first month will target. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose a different tutor rather than asking you to persevere with one that is not working.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot around the Dubailand school run
process.description: Sessions in this community mostly work at 6.30pm or later, because children bussed to Nad Al Sheba, The Villa or Al Barsha South are not home and fed before then. The slot is fixed weekly so it becomes routine, and it can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without losing the sequence.

process.title: Review against the mark scheme every fourth session
process.description: Every fourth session is a short timed piece marked against the official scheme, with the error log updated and sent to you. The measure is not a predicted grade; it is whether the three named habits are still costing marks. When one stops appearing, the plan moves to the next thing on the log.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course code, not on the postcode
whyPoints.description: A specialist is selected for the exact course and level your child sits, which is a different question from who lives nearest Arabian Ranches 3. Over video the geography stops mattering and the syllabus starts to, which is the whole reason UAE delivery is online rather than a compromise we are apologising for.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down and held
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, Extended Essays and Theory of Knowledge essays are coached, questioned and marked against the criteria. They are never written, rewritten or edited to completion by a tutor. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and we will not imitate it.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, with the source of each band
whyPoints.description: The AED bands above are attributed to the competitor or rate survey that published them, with the month they were collected. Three of six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all. A parent should be able to see the market before they talk to anybody, including us.

No page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit; several route UAE parents to a foreign phone number without mentioning where the tutor sits.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, never claimed
whyPoints.description: KHDA inspects Dubai private schools, ADEK does Abu Dhabi, SPEA does Sharjah, and the Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. We explain what each one does and link to it. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation, and no tutor on this site is ever described as carrying a regulator's approval.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the Dubailand evening
whyPoints.description: Session times assume a long school run, a late dinner and a sibling in a different year group. Slots run into the evening, sessions are recorded for rewatching, and timing shifts during Ramadan and exam fortnight rather than being cancelled and lost.

faqs.question: Is there any Diploma school inside Arabian Ranches 3, or do we have to look further out?
faqs.answer: Arabian Ranches 3 has no school on the community itself, Diploma or otherwise. Families here use the inner Dubailand ring — Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, Ranches Primary in Arabian Ranches 2, Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights in Dubai Sports City and South View in Remraam — and then widen to Nad Al Sheba, The Villa and Al Barsha South for secondary. Check each school's current KHDA listing for the programmes it is licensed to offer, because provision changes between intakes and a school's website is not always current.

faqs.question: Why does hiring an IB tutor by distance from our villa go wrong so often?
faqs.answer: Because distance selects for availability rather than subject. The Diploma is six separate courses with six separate mark schemes, and the person who can diagnose a lost mark in Chemistry Higher Level is usually not the person who can do it in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A twenty-minute evening radius around Arabian Ranches 3 contains a few thousand households and no subject panel. Selecting on the course code instead gives you a specialist, and over live video that specialist is as reachable as a neighbour in Mudon.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our villa in Arabian Ranches 3 for Diploma lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording your child can rewatch. The market does offer visiting tutors, at AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and up to AED 500 from independent tutors, with travel from this part of Dubailand priced inside that rate.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between a Standard Level and a Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: Content, and the hours to deliver it. An SL course is built on 150 teaching hours, an HL course on 240. Those extra ninety hours are additional syllabus rather than the same material taught more intensively, and in several subjects they bring an extra paper: Mathematics adds Paper 3, English Language and Literature adds the HL essay. A student struggling in an HL class is often not behind on the shared content at all — they are meeting syllabus their SL classmates never see.

faqs.question: How many points does my child actually need, and where do the last three come from?
faqs.answer: Six subjects graded 1 to 7 give a maximum of 42 points. The final three come from a matrix combining the Extended Essay grade with the Theory of Knowledge grade, for a ceiling of 45. The Diploma is awarded at 24 points subject to conditions on individual grades and on completing the core, which your child's coordinator will confirm. University offers in the UAE and abroad are quoted in total points with subject-specific requirements attached, so check the exact HL grades a target course asks for before fixing a revision plan.

faqs.question: My child understands the content but keeps losing marks. What is usually causing that?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command term. Every IB question opens with one, each has an assessment objective behind it, and answering 'explain' with a description scores nothing even when everything written is true. Take a marked Paper 2, highlight the command term on every question that lost marks, and the pattern appears within ten minutes. It is the cheapest recovery in the Diploma because it needs no new content — just deliberate practice against the definitions published in the subject guides.

faqs.question: How are the marks split inside a science internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation in Physics, Chemistry and Biology is worth 20% of the final grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation therefore carries exactly as much weight as data analysis, which surprises most students, because the practical work gets weeks and the evaluation gets one evening. Knowing the split changes how the time is spent, and that is usually worth more than any single piece of subject teaching.

faqs.question: Exactly what can a tutor do on a Mathematics exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test whether the topic is broad enough to sustain course-level mathematics, check that the mathematics used matches the level, explain what each criterion descriptor means, and mark a draft against those descriptors so the student knows which criterion is weak. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot rewrite passages, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply the mathematics. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and the writing must be the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Who should supply the IB past papers and mark schemes our child practises on?
faqs.answer: From your child's school. Schools hold licensed access to IB, Cambridge and Pearson material, and the DP coordinator or subject teacher can release papers and mark schemes appropriately. IB Gram does not host, supply or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because those are the boards' copyright. Use the official subject guides on ibo.org for syllabus detail, and treat any site offering a free library of recent IB papers with real caution — much of that material is hosted without permission.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start for a child bussed home to this community?
faqs.answer: For most families here, 6.30pm or later. A child travelling back from Nad Al Sheba, The Villa or Al Barsha South is not home, changed and fed before six, and a session that starts while a student is still eating teaches very little. Because lessons run over video there is no additional travel to absorb at either end, so a 6.30pm start is a 6.30pm start. Weekend morning slots work well for internal assessment and Extended Essay sessions, which need longer blocks.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is permitted through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, the MoHRE service page lists a two-working-day completion time, and applications go through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it; those operating without one face penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition in DP1 or should we wait until the final year?
faqs.answer: DP1 is where the cheap gains are. The content taught in the first year reappears in the final papers, the internal assessment is usually started in DP1, and the habits that cost marks — mental algebra, unreferenced diagrams, uncertainty ignored — are easier to change before they have been rehearsed for eighteen months. Families who start in the final term of DP2 are paying for a rescue rather than a build, and the realistic target narrows accordingly. No tutor can promise a particular outcome at any point in the programme.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches with Physics is a common and genuine pairing, because the mathematical technique overlaps. Chemistry with Biology is less often a real pairing than it looks, because the extended-response demands differ. We would rather tell you that two specialists are needed than place one tutor across two subjects for convenience, and the subject background of each proposed tutor is stated so you can judge the overlap yourself.

faqs.question: Our Higher Level subject is an unusual one and nobody local teaches it. Then what?
faqs.answer: We say so. Coverage inside the UAE is thin for some Higher Level combinations, including Further Mathematics, less commonly taught group 2 languages and parts of Design Technology. Rather than place a generalist, we offer a specialist based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, named and disclosed before you commit, with the time-zone implication stated. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to a foreign number without saying where the tutor sits.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still have to be studied alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support for these subjects is a separate stream from Diploma subject tuition, and material must follow the approved content.

Lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Dubailand school run.

intro.heading: The map answers a question JLT does not have
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in JLT is a reasonable thing to type and an expensive way to sort the answer. Jumeirah Lake Towers is a tower district built around four man-made lakes, wrapped by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and the DMCC free zone in its middle. It has nurseries. It has no secondary school of its own. Every school-age child living in these clusters commutes out, most of them across Sheikh Zayed Road into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, or up the interchange towards Jumeirah Village and The Meadows. Distance from your tower therefore tells you almost nothing about who can teach a Diploma component, and quite a lot about who is willing to spend an hour in traffic to try.

Price is where that confusion becomes visible. Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026, run from AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, through AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, to AED 270 at TutorChase and AED 650 at BartyED. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Those are other providers' numbers, not ours. Read together, they say something useful: the spread is driven as much by format and travel as by teaching, and three of the six pages currently ranking for these searches publish no price at all.

This page is written from the money, because that is the decision a JLT family is actually making. Four leaks account for most of the waste we see. Families buy hours instead of naming a component, so nothing gets diagnosed and the same hours get bought again next term. They pay a travel premium for a tower address, which buys a car journey rather than better teaching. They buy at the wrong level, paying Standard Level depth for a Higher Level problem. And they compress the whole budget into the six weeks before papers, which is the most expensive hour in the calendar and the least able to rebuild a topic that was never learned.

A plain word on delivery before any of the rest matters. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so they sit between the school bus and the hour when a 17-year-old stops absorbing anything. IB Gram does not offer home visits in JLT, in Dubai, or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The exchange is deliberate and worth stating in cash terms: you give up the person at the door and you stop paying for the Sheikh Zayed Road crossing, which on the published in-home bands is a meaningful share of every hour billed.

There is a regulatory reason the nearest qualified adult is also the wrong default. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Its code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff are reported to do the same. So the physics teacher two towers away may be the one person legally unable to take your child.

None of this makes proximity worthless. It sets the clock. The school bus route decides when your child is home, fed and still functional, and in JLT that hour varies by half an hour or more depending on which school the family chose and which exit the bus uses. That is a real constraint and this page takes it seriously. What proximity does not decide is who should teach Chemistry at Higher Level, and paying as though it did is the single most reliable way to spend AED 20,000 across a Diploma and change nothing.
