sections.heading: What a proximity search returns when you type it from a Meadows villa
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result. There are directory listings that rank by paid placement rather than distance. There are agency pages that name Dubai but publish no address and no rate. And there are independent tutors advertising a service area that happens to include Emirates Living. None of these results tells you the thing you want to know, which is whether the person has taught the specific subject at the specific level your child is sitting.

The research behind this page looked at the pages currently ranking for queries like this one across the UAE. Three of six published no price at all. The two that did quoted United States dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. Five of six carried no comparison table of any kind. The best page in the set ran to roughly 2,300 words and named no neighbourhood. A search that looks local is being answered by pages that are not local at all.

The second problem is availability. IB Higher Level specialists are scarce in absolute terms, not just locally. A community of villas, however well served by schools, contains a handful of people qualified to teach Chemistry HL and almost nobody who has supervised a Historical Investigation. Distance is a filter that removes the specialists first, because specialists are rare and rare things are rarely nearby. Drop the distance filter and the pool becomes national instead of residential.

sections.heading: The Meadows school day, counted backwards from the bus
paragraphs: Dubai private schools finish earlier than many parents arriving from Europe expect, and secondary finishes later than primary within the same school. Add the bus route through Emirates Living, add a co-curricular commitment two days a week, and the gap between the last lesson of the school day and the first possible tutoring session narrows to something quite specific. Planning a session at 16:00 for a Year 13 student who is bussed back from Al Barsha is planning a session that will be missed.

Confirm your own school's published timings rather than relying on an average, because they differ by school and by year group, and several Dubai schools run a shorter day on one weekday. The shape, though, is consistent: primary children are home first and have energy until roughly 18:00, secondary students are home later and work better after a break and food than immediately on arrival. A Diploma student asked to think hard at 16:15 after a 06:30 start is being set up to fail.

The practical rule we use with Emirates Living families is that the session slot should be the second thing fixed, after the school day and before anything else. Fixtures, Arabic support classes at school, and the drive to a sibling's activity all compete for the same two hours. A slot that survives for a full term is worth more than a slightly better slot that collapses in week three.

sections.heading: Which schools The Meadows actually feeds, and what that means for tutoring
paragraphs: The cluster around The Meadows carries both of Dubai's dominant tracks at once. The British curriculum is the largest in the emirate by enrolment at around 37%, with Indian at 26% and United States at 14%, and the IB sits at roughly 7%. Inside Emirates Living that national pattern compresses into a few hundred metres: an IB World School inside The Meadows, a large British school in The Springs, and two more within a ten-minute drive. Siblings in one villa are often sitting criterion-marked MYP assessments and Cambridge IGCSE papers in the same fortnight.

This has a direct consequence for anyone hiring one tutor for a household. The MYP wants criteria addressed explicitly in a task designed by the school; IGCSE wants a mark scheme answered in the command words of a specific syllabus code. A tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in the other, and the parent discovers this in week four rather than week one. Matching by programme rather than by postcode avoids an expensive detour.

KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes outcomes on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Those reports are worth reading for the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band: inspectors comment on attainment and progress by subject and phase, which is often the first written confirmation a parent gets that a particular department is struggling. We do not restate any school's rating here, because a rating should be read from KHDA's own publication rather than from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What IB support costs around Emirates Living, in dirhams
paragraphs: Most pages answering this query refuse the question. Of the UAE competitor pages examined for this project, three published no figure at all and one has a frequently asked question that asks the price and then declines to answer it. The two that did publish quoted dollars. A Dubai parent needs a dirham band, so here is one, drawn from providers' own published rate cards and from a published Dubai tutoring cost table, surveyed in October 2026.

Read the table as the market, not as our price list. These are the figures other providers put in public, and they vary by tier rather than by neighbourhood. Nobody charges a Meadows premium for an online lesson; what varies between communities is the in-home figure, because that number carries travel. A tutor crossing Dubai at 17:30 is charging for the journey whether the invoice itemises it or not, and at Emirates Living distances that is commonly a quarter to a third of the hour's value.

Two further costs are routinely left out of comparisons. The first is the cancellation cost of a plan that depends on a car: a single evening of heavy traffic removes a session that has already been paid for. The second is the cost of the wrong match. Six sessions with a generalist who re-teaches the textbook is not cheaper than four with a specialist who diagnoses a component, even at double the hourly figure. On IB Gram the trial lesson exists for exactly that reason: one lesson in one subject, before any payment, so the match is tested before it is bought.

For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is one of the few education costs in Dubai that did move this year, which makes it worth costing properly rather than by instinct.

sections.heading: The Diploma core, and where a Meadows family loses time
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service run alongside the six subjects for two years, and together the first two contribute up to 3 points on the 45-point scale. Three points decides university offers. It is also the part of the Diploma that no subject tutor is automatically responsible for, which is why it is the part that drifts. A student can be well supported in Maths and Physics and still arrive at Year 13 with an Extended Essay research question that cannot carry 4,000 words.

The Extended Essay fails or succeeds at the question. A question that is too broad produces description; one that is too narrow produces an essay with nothing to argue. Supervision happens inside the school and belongs there. What a tutor can legitimately contribute is pressure on the question, discussion of method and sources, and written feedback on drafts the student has produced. Authorship stays with the student at every stage, and any provider offering otherwise is offering an IB malpractice investigation.

TOK is the component students most often dismiss and most often lose marks on. The exhibition asks for three objects tied to a prompt, and the essay answers one of six prescribed titles. Both are marked on the quality of the knowledge argument, not on opinion. The useful intervention is structural: a claim, a counterclaim that is actually in tension with it, a real example from a named area of knowledge, and a statement of what follows. That is teachable in four sessions.

CAS is not graded but it is a completion requirement, and an incomplete CAS portfolio blocks the Diploma regardless of points. Meadows students with heavy sports commitments usually have the activity strand covered and the service and reflection strands thin. A reminder in November of Year 12 is worth more than a rescue in March of Year 13.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor must not step over
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries internal assessment, and every piece of it is submitted with an authenticity declaration from both student and supervisor. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, with consequences that reach as far as the loss of the Diploma. This is not a theoretical risk in this market. Our research found a provider in the UAE search results selling finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is a product no honest tutoring service can sell and no parent should buy.

The permitted territory is wide and useful. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for in plain words, interrogate a research question, discuss whether a method will produce data worth analysing, model a worked analysis on a different data set, read a student's own draft and say where the argument thins, and teach the referencing convention. All of that raises marks and none of it touches authorship.

The forbidden territory is narrow and absolute. The tutor supplies no sentences, no paragraphs, no data, no diagrams and no corrections typed into the student's file. Feedback arrives as comments and questions for the student to act on, in their own words, in their own document. If a tutor has been near the keyboard, the declaration the student signs is no longer true.

There is a related rule parents should know. Abu Dhabi's education authority has set professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the national private tuition permit carries a code of conduct in the same spirit. Treat an offer of private lessons from your child's own classroom teacher as a problem rather than an advantage, and verify the current rule with the relevant authority before acting on it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai IB education that international tutoring pages ignore completely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set its current requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with an April 2026 date for schools whose year begins in April. A family can be entirely focused on Higher Level Physics and be caught out by an Arabic report instead.

KHDA's requirements are specific enough to matter. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and the Moral, Social and Cultural strand in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. There is also a hard limit on content: using different or additional material for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Any tutor working on Arabic or Islamic Education must therefore work with the school's own prescribed material rather than a parallel scheme of their own invention.

Practically, Arabic as an additional language is where most non-Arab Meadows families need support, and it is a long game rather than an examination sprint. Twenty minutes of spoken practice three times a week moves a child further than a ninety-minute session once a fortnight, and the school's own reporting cycle is the right place to check whether it is working.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two details are worth knowing before you ask a tutor about it. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you it is expensive or difficult has not applied for it. And the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Holding the permit is a baseline of compliance rather than a mark of subject expertise.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so we do not quote one. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is why no honest online platform should describe itself using KHDA permit language.

Ask a prospective tutor three questions. Do you hold the private tuition work permit, and when does it expire? Which syllabus and board have you taught, by code? Can you show a marked piece of student work with your own feedback on it, with identifying details removed? The third question is the most revealing and almost nobody asks it.

sections.heading: Getting started from The Meadows, including what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the school, the programme, the subjects and levels, and what the last report or marked paper actually said. We propose a tutor matched to those components and offer a trial lesson in one subject before any payment is taken. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and we propose a different person rather than defending the first one. If it is right, we fix a slot that fits your weekday and hold it.

Here is the part other pages leave out. Coverage is not infinite. For a common subject at Standard Level the match is usually quick. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a less commonly taught language, or a niche internal assessment, there may be no suitable tutor free in the window you want. When that happens we say so and give you the honest options: a different slot, a short wait, or a different component to start on while the right person becomes available. What we do not do is place a generalist in a specialist's chair and let you find out in February.

Progress is tracked against the only measures that mean anything in the IB: criterion marks on internal assessment, component-level performance on past papers under timed conditions, and the school's own reporting. We do not promise a grade and no honest provider can, because the grade depends on a student's work in an examination room nobody controls. What can be promised is a diagnosis you can read, a plan with dates on it, and a tutor who knows the component.

A last note on timing. Dubai schools sit the May examination session, so the useful work happens in the fifteen months before it rather than the final six weeks. Confirm the exact session dates with your school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site; we deliberately publish no IB examination date here because we have not been able to verify one from the IB directly.

A message saying Physics HL, Paper 2 extended response, last mock 4, internal assessment due in six weeks is enough to match precisely. The more precisely you describe where the marks are going, the shorter the path to the right tutor.

Location is not a filter because lessons are delivered over live video. That is the single change that makes a specialist available to an Emirates Living household at all.

process.description: We set the slot after your school's finish time and your fixtures, not before them. For most Meadows secondary students that means 16:45, 17:30 or 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. A slot that survives a whole term beats a theoretically better slot that collapses in week three.

process.description: At six weeks we look at criterion marks, timed past-paper components and the school's own feedback, and decide whether to continue, change the target or change the tutor. Reviewing on a fixed date stops a plan drifting for a term because nobody wanted an awkward conversation.

whyPoints.description: Higher Level specialists are scarce nationally. A twenty-minute radius around Emirates Living removes them first, because rare things are rarely nearby. Online delivery replaces a residential pool with a national one, and the difference shows up in the quality of the diagnosis in the first lesson.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in The Meadows, or will the lesson be online?
faqs.answer: The lesson is online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions for Meadows students are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's own marked work open in front of both people. The reason is not cost. It is that a Higher Level specialist in a given subject is scarce nationally, so filtering by a twenty-minute radius around Emirates Living removes exactly the people you were searching for. You get the specialist instead of the neighbour.

faqs.question: Which IB and British schools do children in The Meadows and Emirates Living usually attend?
faqs.answer: Emirates International School - Meadows sits inside the community and runs the PYP, MYP and Diploma. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is the other main IB option nearby. On the British side, Dubai British School Emirates Hills is in The Springs and Regent International School is in The Greens, with Dubai College in Al Sufouh and the Al Barsha cluster a little further out. All are regulated by KHDA. Programme offerings change, so confirm with the school directly. We name these as neighbourhood context and claim no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can a Year 13 student in The Meadows realistically start a weekday session?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student bussed back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, 16:00 is usually too early and the realistic windows are 16:45, 17:30 or 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. Primary children can work earlier and lose focus later, so the 15:30 to 16:15 slot suits them better. Check your own school's published finish time rather than an average, because Dubai schools differ by year group and several run a shorter day once a week. The slot that matters is the one that survives a full term, not the one that looks best on paper in September.

faqs.question: Does driving to a tutor in Dubai Marina really cost us a whole evening?
faqs.answer: Roughly two hours, for one hour of teaching. Dubai Marina, JBR and JLT sit fifteen to twenty-five minutes from Emirates Living off-peak and longer at 18:00, so a round trip plus a 60-minute lesson consumes about an hour and fifty minutes. Al Barsha or Jumeirah pushes that to two hours; Mirdif or Deira past two and a half. The practical effect is that only one subject fits per evening and a second weekly session becomes unrealistic. A video lesson consumes sixty minutes, which is why two subjects can share one evening.

faqs.question: My child is at Emirates International School - Meadows. Will the tutor follow that school's own deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing we ask for. The school's internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and reporting dates are what the plan is built backwards from, because those are the dates that actually exist for your child. A tutor working to a generic syllabus timeline will be a month out of step by the second term. Send the assessment calendar, the last report and one marked script at the start. The marked script is the most useful document in the set, because it shows the fault signature rather than the summary.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in Emirates Living usually need?
faqs.answer: Two 60-minute sessions a week in the weak subject, placed on separate evenings, is the pattern that works most often. Splitting the week matters more than the total: Higher Level content needs sleep between exposures, and a single 120-minute block at the weekend produces less retention than two shorter sittings. Add a defined task of 30 to 40 minutes between sessions, marked against the real criteria. Where two subjects need help, two separate specialists on one shared calendar beats one generalist covering both at a shallower level.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Maths HL and Chemistry HL for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a compromise. Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Chemistry at Higher Level are both specialist courses with their own assessed components, and the number of people genuinely strong in both is small. Where a single tutor can do it well, we will say so. More often we propose two specialists sharing one calendar, which costs no more per hour online and produces a sharper diagnosis in each subject. The convenience of one person is real but it is bought with depth.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for the Higher Level subject we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Coverage is not infinite, and a narrow Higher Level combination, a less commonly taught language or an unusual internal assessment can mean no suitable specialist is free in the window you want. When that happens the options are an alternative slot, a short wait for the right person, or starting on a different component in the meantime. What we will not do is put a generalist in a specialist's chair and let you discover the mismatch in February, which is the standard failure in this market.

faqs.question: Do we need a dedicated study space in a Meadows villa for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Not a dedicated room, but a fixed place. What matters is a desk at the right height, a door that can be closed, a wired or strong connection, headphones with a microphone, and paper. The student should be able to write and be seen writing, because a tutor who can watch the working can catch the error at the point it happens. Villas in The Meadows usually have the space; apartment households in The Views or The Greens often do better with headphones and a shared family rule about the hour than with a new piece of furniture.

faqs.question: Can Meadows sessions move to post-iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. Dubai school days shorten during Ramadan and the useful hours of the evening move, so a slot that worked in February stops working. Most families shift to a post-Iftar session or move the work to late morning on non-school days. Internal assessment deadlines rarely move to match, which is why Ramadan is the period where plans quietly fall behind. Agreeing the revised slot before the month starts, rather than improvising in week one, is what keeps the sequence of sessions intact.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working in Dubai need a permit, and should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE, which lists Private Tutor Licensing as a service on its own site with a two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors around Emirates Living charge per hour in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rate cards surveyed in October 2026 put generalist online tutors at AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and a premium examiner tier above AED 500. In-home visits sit higher, commonly AED 180 to 500, because the travel is inside the hour. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Those are market figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without breaking IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can press on the research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words, discuss whether a method will generate usable evidence, teach the subject content the essay depends on, explain the assessment criteria in plain words, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced. The tutor supplies no sentences, no data and no typed corrections, and supervision remains with the school. Any provider offering a finished Extended Essay is offering an IB malpractice case against your child, whatever it is called on the invoice.

faqs.question: Do you cover Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Support has to follow the school's prescribed material, because using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects. For non-Arab families the usual need is Arabic as an additional language, where short frequent spoken practice beats long infrequent sessions.

faqs.question: What does the trial lesson actually involve for a Meadows family?
faqs.answer: One lesson, in one subject, before any payment is taken. The tutor works through a piece of the student's own recent work, usually a marked script or a current assessment task, and uses it to identify where the marks are going rather than covering new content. Afterwards you get a short written diagnosis: what the student can already do, the specific fault pattern, and what the first four sessions would target. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose a different tutor rather than arguing for the first one.

faqs.question: How will we know the tutoring is working, without being in the room?
faqs.answer: Three measures, all of which exist independently of the tutor. First, criterion marks on internal assessment tasks set by the school, which are the IB's own instrument. Second, component-level performance on past papers sat under timed conditions, tracked per paper rather than as a single percentage. Third, the school's own reports and parent meetings. We review all three at week six and decide whether to continue, change the target or change the tutor. No honest provider promises a grade, because the grade is decided in an examination room nobody controls.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.closingBody: If you have reached this page from a search for an IB tutor near me in The Meadows, the most useful thing you own is not a radius. It is the last marked script your child brought home. Send that, the school, the subjects and the levels, and we will match a specialist to the component where the marks are going and offer a trial lesson in one subject before any payment. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in a slot built around your school day rather than around Al Khail Road. If the right specialist is not free, you will hear that too.

intro.heading: What "near me" really means once the school bus has gone
paragraphs: The Views is four clusters of towers looking over the Emirates Golf Club fairways, with Panorama, Travo, Turia, Mosela and the Fairways buildings holding most of the families. It is a small community with a very particular rhythm. Almost nobody here drives their child to school: the bus routes feed out towards The Meadows, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Emirates Hills in the morning and come back in a narrow band in the afternoon. That single fact decides when tutoring can happen, and it is the reason searching for an IB tutor near me in The Views is a different problem from searching for one in a villa community with its own school on the doorstep.

Work the clock backwards. A Diploma student at a British-curriculum school in Al Sufouh finishes lessons in the middle of the afternoon, then waits for the bus, then sits in the traffic that builds on Al Sufouh Road and Sheikh Zayed Road from about half past three. Home is somewhere between 4pm and 4.45pm. Add a shower, a swim session at the Views Health Club, a music lesson or a CAS commitment, and dinner, and the usable study window is 6pm to 9pm on a school night. On Fridays, when most Dubai private schools finish before lunch, the window is wide open from early afternoon.

A tutor who lives in The Views would still only solve the geography problem. The harder problem is subject match. A single Diploma cohort in this catchment might need Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Physics HL, Chemistry SL, Economics HL, English A Language and Literature, Arabic B and an extended essay supervisor in History. No neighbourhood of a few thousand apartments contains a specialist in each of those who is also free at 7pm on a Tuesday. The choice is not between a local tutor and an online one. It is between the right subject specialist on a screen and whoever happens to be within a twenty-minute drive.

That is why every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family in The Views runs live over video, one-to-one, in the student's own time zone. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Stating that plainly matters more than hiding it behind a search phrase, because the alternative is a parent clearing a Tuesday evening for someone who was never going to arrive. What the family gets instead is a tutor chosen for the subject, the level and the hour, with the whiteboard, the past paper and the mark scheme on a shared screen.

The rest of this page is written from the school run outwards. It sets out which schools this catchment actually feeds and when their days end, how much of the evening the commute eats, what a realistic weekly pattern looks like across a Diploma year, what the Dubai market charges in dirhams, what KHDA inspection bands do and do not tell you about your child's own grades, and how to check that a tutor is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE. Nothing on it is a price list for IB Gram; the AED figures are the market's, attributed to the source that published them.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.programmesIntro: The Views sits inside a catchment that runs the full IB continuum as well as the British route, so the programme your child is on depends almost entirely on which school the bus goes to. Each of the three has a different pressure point, and each needs a different kind of hour from a tutor.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, which makes it hard for a parent to see what is being assessed. What travels forward into MYP and Diploma is reading fluency, written structure and number sense. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic: find out whether the child can hold a multi-step calculation, read for inference, and write a paragraph that answers the question asked.
programmes.countryNote: Regent International School in The Greens is the nearest PYP setting to The Views and takes a large share of the community's primary children. Its day finishes early enough that a 4.30pm session is realistic for a Year 5 or Year 6 child, which is unusual in this catchment. Younger children work better in thirty to forty minute blocks twice a week than in one long hour.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks on a one to eight scale against four criteria per subject, and the criteria are published. Most of the panic a parent feels in MYP comes from not knowing which criterion the low mark sat in. A tutor's first job is to read the report against the subject's criteria, identify whether the gap is knowledge, application, communication or reflection, and then teach to that criterion rather than to the topic.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows runs the full IB continuum, so a Views child there moves from MYP straight into Diploma inside the same building and the same reporting language. Families whose children are at a British school in Al Barsha instead face a harder switch at 16, because IGCSE grading and MYP criteria measure different things and the Year 11 report does not translate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the extended essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The external papers are only part of the grade: each subject carries an internal assessment worth twenty to thirty per cent, written largely outside lesson time. The failure mode is not weak teaching. It is six subjects and three core components all asking for independent work in the same four months of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in The Views lose their evenings to CAS and to the travel in and out of Emirates Living more than they lose them to homework. A Tuesday and Thursday 7pm pattern, held for a term, moves more marks than a crash block in April. The one slot worth protecting is Friday after lunch, when nothing competes with it and a two-hour internal assessment review is actually possible.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects The Views and Emirates Living families ask for most often, with the part of each course where the marks tend to go. Sessions are built around your child's own school scheme of work and internal deadline dates.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The HL course adds proof, complex numbers and a third paper. Marks are lost on Paper 1 because it is sat without a calculator and students have practised with one, and in the exploration because the mathematics chosen is too thin to show command of the syllabus. Sessions split between non-calculator fluency and exploration design.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI leans on statistics, modelling and graphical calculator technique. Most lost marks are procedural: the wrong regression model, a hypothesis test stated without its conditions, or a modelling answer that never returns to the context it came from. Technology fluency on the specific handheld the school uses matters here more than in AA.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The current course is organised around five themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Students who are comfortable with the content still drop marks on graph linearisation, uncertainty propagation and the extended response that asks them to explain rather than calculate. Maths fluency is the hidden prerequisite at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity are taught as linked ideas rather than as separate units, so a gap in bonding reappears later in energetics and in organic mechanisms. Multiple-choice marks are usually knowledge; extended-response marks are usually explanation. The scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate real data in the hours available.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rewards precise terminology and punishes vagueness. The common failures are command-term blindness, writing a description where an explanation was asked for, and statistics in the investigation handled by instinct rather than by test. Work usually begins with the student's own past-paper script, annotated against the published mark scheme.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and the individual oral asks the student to connect a global issue to two texts. Strong readers underperform because they summarise instead of analysing. Sessions drill a repeatable approach to an unseen text and build the oral around an issue the student can actually sustain for ten minutes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The diagram is the argument. Marks go missing when axes are unlabelled, when the evaluation paragraph restates the analysis, and when the HL quantitative paper is met without practice. The portfolio of commentaries on published news articles is best started early, while the news cycle is still giving usable material.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A content-light, technique-heavy course. Tools are easy to learn and hard to apply to a case study under time pressure, and the HL extension on organisational change is where strong students stall. The internal assessment stands or falls on whether the chosen organisation gives the student real data to work with.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the expectations differ. Diploma Arabic B is a different animal from school Arabic: it is assessed on productive skills under timed conditions, which is where most of the gap sits.

subjects.name: Extended essay and Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The extended essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor inside the school; TOK carries an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. A tutor's role is questioning, structure and feedback on the student's own drafts. The work itself has to be the student's, and IB academic honesty rules make that non-negotiable.

sections.heading: The school day in this catchment, hour by hour
paragraphs: A parent in The Views searching for an IB tutor near me is trying to find an hour, and the hour is set by the bus. Dubai private schools in this catchment finish between the early and middle afternoon, but the finish time is not the arrival time. A child at a school in Al Sufouh who walks out of a lesson at 2.45pm may not be in the lobby of Travo until 4.15pm, because the bus does three other communities first and crosses Sheikh Zayed Road to do it. The gap between finish and arrival is where most tutoring plans quietly fail.

The table below sets out the pattern families in this community report, school by school, with the earliest session start that is actually realistic once the bus, the uniform and a glass of water are accounted for. It is not a timetable published by any school and no school has confirmed it; treat it as a planning tool and check your own child's bus schedule against it. What matters is the shape rather than the exact minute: the nearer the school, the earlier the viable slot, and the difference between the nearest and the furthest school in this catchment is about ninety minutes of the evening.

Two things follow. The first is that a single household with children at two different schools has two different viable start times, which is a scheduling problem a tutoring centre cannot solve and a screen can. The second is that for anyone at a school on the far side of Sheikh Zayed Road, a 5pm session simply does not exist on a school night. Booking one guarantees a rushed, resentful hour. Families who accept a 6.30pm or 7pm start and protect it get a calmer lesson and a tutor who is not waiting ten minutes for someone to arrive.

The third consequence is about Fridays. Most Dubai private schools run a short Friday, finishing before or around lunchtime, and there is no bus queue and no homework backlog yet. A Friday afternoon session can run to ninety minutes or two hours without the student fading, which is why internal assessment work and extended essay drafting belong there rather than on a Wednesday night.

sections.heading: What the commute actually costs over a Diploma year
paragraphs: The case against driving to a tuition centre is arithmetic rather than opinion. A one-hour lesson at a centre in Dubai Marina, Barsha Heights or Al Barsha costs a Views family the hour plus two drives plus parking plus the waiting. Outside peak, the round trip from Panorama to a centre in Al Barsha is a modest errand. At 6.30pm on a school night, with Sheikh Zayed Road and the Al Barsha interchanges loaded, it is not. Families consistently report that a one-hour centre lesson removes something closer to two and a half hours from the evening.

Run that across a Diploma year and the number stops being trivial. Two centre sessions a week for thirty-four teaching weeks is roughly sixty-eight lessons. If each one removes ninety minutes of travel and waiting on top of the lesson, that is more than a hundred hours of a student's year spent in a car, almost all of it in the window when they are least able to work and most in need of food and sleep. It also consumes a parent's evening twice a week, which is why centre attendance so often lapses in DP2 exactly when it is needed most.

Online delivery takes that overhead to zero, and it changes what is possible inside the hour as well. A shared screen means the student's own marked script, the official syllabus page and the past paper sit side by side, annotated live and saved. Nothing has to be photographed and sent later. A student can stay in their own room with their own files and their own graphical calculator, which is the one they will have in the exam hall.

The honest counterweight is that online needs three conditions and fails without them. A wired or strong connection, a quiet door that closes, and a device with a real keyboard and screen rather than a phone. In an apartment in Travo or Mosela with siblings and a shared study table, the third condition is the one that breaks. It is worth solving before the first lesson rather than after the third one has been interrupted.

sections.heading: A realistic week, and where the extra hour has to come from
paragraphs: Diploma students in this community rarely fail for lack of ability. They fail because six subjects, an extended essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS all demand independent hours, and the independent hours were already spoken for. Swim training at the Views Health Club, football in Emirates Hills, a music grade, a CAS project that meets on a Saturday, and a weekly family commitment take an evening each. Nobody sat down and planned a week that contains no revision; it just arrived that way.

The planning move that works is to audit the week before buying tutoring. Write out the seven days in hours, mark everything already fixed, and look at what is left after 6pm and on Friday afternoon. Most students in The Views find three usable blocks: two weekday evenings and Friday. That is the budget. A tutoring plan that needs four weekday evenings will not survive October, and a plan that quietly assumes the student revises between 10pm and midnight is a plan to make them ill.

Having found the blocks, spend them by assessment weight rather than by anxiety. An internal assessment worth twenty per cent of a subject grade, due in eleven weeks, deserves one of those blocks for a month. A topic the student finds unpleasant but which carries few marks does not. This is where a tutor who knows the assessment structure earns the fee: not by teaching more content, but by telling you which of the three blocks to spend on what, and when to stop.

The pattern most families settle on is one weekday evening on the weakest examined subject, one weekday evening rotating between the other two Higher Levels, and Friday afternoon reserved for whichever coursework deadline is closest. It survives a term because it does not fight the school run, and it can absorb a mock series without being rebuilt.

sections.heading: Term dates, Ramadan and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Dubai private schools run a three-term year, with the long break through the summer, a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break. For a Diploma student the shape of that calendar matters more than its exact dates, because the external papers sit in the May session and every internal deadline is pulled forward to clear the way. By the time the spring break arrives, the coursework should be finished. Students who are still writing in April are revising and drafting at the same time, and both suffer.

Ramadan reshapes the working day for part of the year. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter and lower-energy, and the productive window moves to after Iftar. For a family in The Views this is a scheduling change rather than a pause: a 9pm or 9.30pm session after the meal is often the best hour of the day during that month, and it is far easier to hold online than it would be by driving anywhere. Observing and non-observing households in the same building end up on different clocks, which is another thing a screen handles better than a room.

The one calendar instruction worth following is to get the real dates from two places rather than from a tutoring website. School term dates, assessment weeks and internal deadlines come from your child's own school calendar and IB coordinator. Examination timetables come from the board: Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs and revise them, so the live PDF is the only version worth planning against. IB session and results dates should be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org; no date on this page is a substitute for either source.

Counting backwards from the May session is the habit that separates a calm DP2 from a frantic one. Internal assessments finished before the spring break. Mock scripts marked and analysed, not just sat. A revision plan built from those scripts in January rather than a generic one bought in March. None of that requires a tutor, but all of it is easier with someone looking at the same calendar once a week.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Emirates Living, in dirhams
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The figures below are market rates in AED collected from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and each band is attributed. Our own position is a free trial lesson and a quoted rate after the subject and level are known, because an hour of Mathematics HL exploration supervision is not the same product as an hour of MYP support.

Read the table as a map of what you are buying rather than a ladder to climb. The bottom band buys content delivery from someone who knows the material; it is reasonable value for a Year 7 who needs a topic re-explained and poor value for a DP2 student who needs assessment technique. The specialist band buys someone who has taught the specific syllabus and marked against the published criteria. The premium band is bought mainly for the final weeks before papers, and at that point the thing being bought is judgement about what to leave out.

Three cost traps show up repeatedly in this catchment. Buying hours before diagnosing the problem, so the first four sessions are spent finding out what a marked script would have shown in twenty minutes. Buying group classes for a Higher Level subject, where the whole value of the hour is that the questions are the student's own. And buying a long weekly commitment in DP1 that burns out before the term when it would have mattered. A shorter, later, better-targeted plan usually costs less and does more.

Whatever the band, ask three questions before paying. Which syllabus and which board has this tutor actually taught, with the code. What will the first session produce, in writing. And does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A provider that cannot answer the first question specifically is selling you an hour of generic help at a specialist price.

sections.heading: KHDA ratings, and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band for each school. Parents in The Views use those bands to choose schools, which is what they are for, and then occasionally use them to decide whether tutoring is necessary, which is not what they are for.

An inspection band is a judgement about a school as an institution: teaching quality across the whole roll, leadership, inclusion, the way it uses assessment data. It is not a judgement about your child's Physics Higher Level grade. A strongly rated school can still have a Diploma cohort where half the students have never been taught how a mark scheme awards an explanation mark, because that is a specific skill rather than a measure of institutional quality. The useful question is not how the school is rated but what your child's last marked script shows.

The context around Dubai's private sector is worth knowing for a different reason. Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment share at thirty-seven per cent and the IB at seven per cent. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, and announced seven new private schools for that year, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places. More IB places means more Diploma cohorts and more demand for the same small pool of Higher Level specialists.

One more thing a report does not tell you. Both ADEK in Abu Dhabi and the MoHRE permit code of conduct restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why the obvious solution of hiring your child's own teacher privately is the wrong one to pursue. Press reporting on the ADEK rules should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone relies on the exact wording, but the direction is clear enough to plan around.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost no competing page answers, and it is the one that protects a family. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. u.ae records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, that it is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two details matter to a parent. The permit costs nothing, so anyone presenting a fee as the reason they do not hold one is telling you something else. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are, in u.ae's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you either; Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. If a figure is quoted at you as fact, treat it as sales pressure.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. That needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and no regulator endorsement of any kind: it is an independent matching platform, and it names KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and MoHRE on these pages to explain what they do, not to borrow their authority.

The practical version is short. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit and under which category. Ask whether they currently teach at your child's own school, and if so, do not proceed. And apply the same scepticism to any claim of accreditation: a provider describing itself as approved by a UAE regulator or an examination board should be asked to produce the permit or centre number, because the honest answer is usually that no such thing exists for a tutoring platform.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, and the extended essay and Theory of Knowledge sit alongside them. All of it must be the student's own work, authenticated by the school. This is the part of the market where real damage gets done: one provider found in the UAE research for this project sells finished internal assessments outright, which is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger that falls on the student, not the seller.

The boundary is workable and clear once stated. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain how the published criteria award marks, interrogate a proposed research question until it is narrow enough to answer, teach the statistics or the referencing convention, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. Feedback means comments and questions on their text. It does not mean supplied sentences, a rewritten paragraph, or a document that comes back with new prose in it.

In practice the most valuable session is the earliest one. A Chemistry investigation with a question too broad to generate usable data in ten hours cannot be rescued by excellent writing later; a mathematics exploration built on a topic too thin to show command of the syllabus caps its own mark in criterion E regardless of presentation. Half an hour spent narrowing the question at the start is worth more than three hours of polishing at the end, and it is also the kind of help that is unambiguously legitimate.

Parents should also know where the authoritative deadlines live. The school's IB coordinator sets the internal checkpoints, and they are earlier than the IB's own upload dates because the school needs marking time. Ask for the written internal calendar in September of DP2 and plan the Friday afternoon sessions against it. Any tutor who cannot work to your school's calendar is working to their own, which is a sign they are selling hours rather than help.
bullets: Legitimate: content teaching, criteria explanation, question design, feedback on the student's own draft
Not legitimate: supplying text, rewriting a draft, or any finished component
The earliest session is the most valuable, because scope decides the mark ceiling
Internal school deadlines run earlier than the IB's own upload dates

process.title: Tell us the school, the subject and the hour
process.description: Which school the bus goes to, which programme and level, and the two or three evening slots your family can genuinely hold. The school matters because it sets the arrival time and the internal deadline calendar; the slot matters because a tutor who is not free then is not a candidate.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent marked paper, test or report tells us more in ten minutes than a conversation does in an hour. It shows whether the gap is content, technique, timing or command-term reading, and it stops the first paid sessions being spent on diagnosis you have already paid the school to do.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: Not a sales call. A live one-to-one lesson at your chosen hour with the tutor you would keep, working on the actual topic. You see the teaching, your child sees the screen-share and the whiteboard, and we see whether the match is right before anyone pays.

process.title: Fix the slot and work to the school's calendar
process.description: Agree the weekly pattern, protect Friday afternoon for coursework if there is coursework, and align the plan to your school's internal deadlines. If a specialist is not free at your hour, we say so and give you the honest options rather than substituting a generalist quietly.

whyPoints.title: The hour is chosen around the bus, not around us
whyPoints.description: Sessions in The Views are scheduled after the school run has landed and the uniform is off, on Gulf Standard Time. For most households in this catchment that means 6pm or later on a school night, with Friday afternoon kept for the longer coursework work.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not the nearest available adult
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Physics student needs someone who has taught that course and marked against its criteria. Matching by syllabus rather than by postcode is the whole reason online works better here than a search for whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive.

whyPoints.title: Stated plainly: delivery is online
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live over video, one-to-one. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, and no page here will suggest otherwise. Saying it before you book is more useful than a search phrase that implies something we do not sell.

whyPoints.title: Prices from the market, with the source named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, so you can check it. Our own rate follows the free trial, once the subject and level are known, rather than being presented as a single number for every hour.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, question design and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing written for them, nothing supplied as text. That boundary protects the student's diploma, which matters more than any single internal assessment mark.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in The Views, or is the lesson online?
faqs.answer: The lesson is online. IB Gram arranges live one-to-one video tuition for families in The Views and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The practical reason is supply: a community of a few thousand apartments does not contain a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL specialist, a Physics HL specialist and an Economics HL specialist who are all free at 7pm. Matching by syllabus rather than by driving distance is what makes the right tutor available at the hour your family can actually hold.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after the school run in The Views?
faqs.answer: It depends on which school the bus goes to. Children at Regent International School in The Greens are home early enough for a 4.30pm start. Students returning from Emirates Hills generally cannot begin before 6pm, and anyone crossing Sheikh Zayed Road from Al Sufouh or Al Barsha should plan on 6.30pm or 7pm. Booking a 5pm slot for a child at a school on the far side of that road produces a rushed hour and a tutor waiting. Friday afternoon, after the short school day, is the most productive slot in the week.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in The Views actually attend?
faqs.answer: The nearest is Regent International School in The Greens, which takes a large share of the community's primary children. Emirates International School Meadows runs the full IB continuum a short drive away. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Dubai British School Emirates Hills sit north of the golf course. The second ring, ten to twenty-five minutes out, includes Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and American School of Dubai. Those schools are named to describe the catchment; no affiliation with any of them is implied.

faqs.question: Does driving to a tuition centre in Dubai Marina make sense for one hour of maths?
faqs.answer: Rarely, on a school night. The hour becomes closer to two and a half once two drives, parking and the waiting are counted, and the drive happens in the window when a Diploma student is least able to work. Across two sessions a week for a teaching year that is roughly a hundred hours in a car. A centre makes sense if the specific tutor is only available there, or for a practical that genuinely needs equipment. For paper technique, mark-scheme work and exploration supervision, a shared screen does more inside the hour.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma students in Emirates Living usually start with?
faqs.answer: One or two, and almost never more. The constraint is not willingness but the number of usable evening blocks: after swim training, a music lesson, a CAS commitment and a family evening, most students in this catchment have two weekday slots and Friday afternoon. A plan built on four weekday evenings collapses by October. The pattern that survives a term is one evening on the weakest examined subject, one rotating between the other Higher Levels, and Friday afternoon reserved for whichever coursework deadline is nearest.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, can a Views family shift the slot to after Iftar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many families that becomes the best hour of the day during the month. School hours shorten, afternoons run at lower energy, and a 9pm or 9.30pm session after the meal is calmer and more productive than anything before it. Because delivery is online there is no drive to fit around the meal, which is the main reason this works better than an arrangement that requires travel. Households that are not observing keep their usual slot, and the same tutor can hold both patterns in the same week.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai three-term calendar mean for when revision should start?
faqs.answer: It means the coursework has to be finished before the spring break, not during it. Dubai private schools run three terms with the external papers in the May session, so every internal deadline is pulled forward to give the school marking time. A student still drafting an internal assessment in April is revising and writing at once and does both badly. The useful sequence is coursework complete by the spring break, mock scripts analysed rather than merely sat, and a revision plan built from those scripts in January.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor about the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. u.ae records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold it and under which category. Because it costs nothing, a tutor who cites expense as the reason for not holding one is telling you something else.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors charge per hour around Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, taken from providers' own published pages and Bestimate's 2026 rate table, run roughly AED 45-150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200-450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500-650 at the premium end. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180-500. Monthly packages of around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the market. Those are the market's figures, not ours; IB Gram quotes after a free trial, once the subject and level are known.

faqs.question: My child is at Emirates International School Meadows. Will the tutor know that timetable?
faqs.answer: The tutor works to your child's own scheme of work and internal deadline calendar rather than to a generic syllabus run, so the first thing we ask for is the school's written assessment calendar. Emirates International School Meadows runs the full IB continuum, which means a student there moves from MYP criteria straight into Diploma assessment inside the same reporting language. That continuity is an advantage, and it changes what the early sessions should cover: less translation between grading systems, more time on the assessment technique the external papers reward.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share one booking slot?
faqs.answer: Not the same lesson, if they are at different levels. One-to-one means the questions are the student's own, and that is most of the value in a Higher Level subject. What does work in this community, where many households have siblings on different bus routes, is two consecutive slots on the same evening, or the same tutor across two subjects on different nights. Staggering two children in one evening is considerably easier online than at a centre, because the second lesson starts the moment the first ends.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for Physics HL at 7pm on a Tuesday?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than quietly substituting a generalist. The honest options are a different hour with the right specialist, a different evening in the same week, a short wait for the slot to open, or starting with a diagnostic session and a written plan while the match is found. For narrow combinations such as Higher Level Physics with a specific internal assessment deadline, a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time is sometimes the only way to get real subject depth, and we say so when that is the case.

faqs.question: Does a strong KHDA inspection band mean my child does not need a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, because the two things measure different objects. A KHDA band judges a school as an institution: teaching across the whole roll, leadership, inclusion, how assessment data is used. It says nothing about one student's Physics Higher Level grade. Strongly rated schools still have Diploma students who have never been shown how a mark scheme awards an explanation mark, because that is a specific skill rather than a measure of institutional quality. The more useful evidence is your child's last marked script, read against the published criteria.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay without breaking the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the content, explain how the published criteria award marks, interrogate the research question until it is answerable, teach referencing and method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. Feedback means comments and questions on the student's text. It never means supplied sentences or a rewritten section. The most valuable session is the earliest one, because an unanswerable question caps the mark no matter how well the later writing goes.

faqs.question: How quickly can a first lesson be arranged for a student in The Views?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for mainstream Diploma subjects at a weekday evening slot, and longer for narrow combinations such as a Higher Level science tied to a specific coursework deadline. The sequence is short: tell us the school, the subject, the level and the two or three hours you can hold; send one marked script; then take a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor at your chosen hour. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and nothing has been spent.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.closingHeading: Start with the hour you can actually hold
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.closingBody: The useful first step for a family in The Views is not a tutor search. It is twenty minutes with the week written out in hours, marking what is already fixed, to see which two evening blocks and which part of Friday are genuinely free. Bring those blocks, the school name, the subject and one marked script, and we will match a tutor to the syllabus and the slot and put a free trial lesson in front of you before anything is paid. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. If the specialist your child needs is not free at your hour, we will tell you that instead of filling the slot with someone else.

dubai/ib-tutors.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are grouped by what they actually teach. A Group 4 scientist is not interchangeable with a Group 3 essay marker, and neither is much use on a Maths AA exploration. Pick the subject and the level your child sits, and the shortlist narrows to people who have marked that paper's style of answer before.

intro.heading: Six subject groups, six different problems to solve
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate in Dubai carries six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The six are not six versions of the same task. Group 1 asks for a sustained literary argument under timed conditions. Group 4 asks for precise manipulation of data and a 10-hour individual investigation written to five criteria. Group 5 asks for fluent algebraic technique and a calculator paper that punishes rounding. A parent who books one generalist for all of it has bought the average of six different jobs.

That is why the plural in this search matters. Families type IB tutors in Dubai because they have worked out, usually around the first set of DP1 reports, that the Chemistry problem and the English problem are unrelated. The Chemistry grade is sitting at 4 because the pupil cannot read a Paper 1 multiple-choice stem for the trick in it. The English grade is sitting at 4 because the Paper 2 comparative essay keeps describing two texts instead of comparing them. Those need two different people and two different fixes.

Dubai makes the specialist match harder than it looks. The emirate runs 227 private schools across 17 licensed curricula, and the Diploma is a minority programme inside that market, taken by roughly 7% of the private-school roll. A school may run a single DP cohort of thirty, which means one teacher for Physics HL and SL combined. When that pupil needs help outside class, the pool of people within driving distance who have actually taught Physics HL in the last three years is small. The pool who have taught it online, across every IB school in the emirate, is not.

So the honest structure of this page is diagnostic rather than promotional. Each section below takes a subject group, sets out what its components are worth, and names the specific thing Dubai candidates get wrong in it. If you recognise your child in one of those paragraphs, you now know which specialist to ask for. If you recognise your child in three of them, you know the sequence to book them in, because the Extended Essay deadline and the Group 4 investigation window do not move to suit a tutoring schedule.

Every lesson described here is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a Dubai family that trade is usually favourable, because the constraint on quality here has never been the commute. It has been whether anyone within reach has sat in a room marking that exact paper. A Dubai Marina family gets a Chemistry Higher Level specialist instead of whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive, and the session that would have been spent in traffic is spent on Paper 1 stems instead.

Group 3 marks are lost on command terms: evaluate, examine, to what extent
