process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: Before anything is booked, send the most recent marked Accounting paper, the mark scheme the school used, and your child's own list of questions they abandoned. A photograph of each page is enough. This is what turns the first session into diagnosis rather than a general chat about how the subject is going.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson
process.description: A 30-minute one-to-one lesson over live video, at no cost and with no card details taken. The tutor works two questions from the script with your child and writes up what the errors were. You keep that write-up whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree the ranked plan
process.description: You receive the three costliest error patterns in order, with an estimate of the marks tied to each and the number of sessions each is likely to need. Choosing to fix the top two and ignore the third is a reasonable decision, and it is easier to make when the marks at stake are written down.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons already in the timetable. Each one ends with a note of what was marked, which marks were gained and lost, and what the student is practising before the next session.

process.title: Fortnightly timed paper
process.description: Every second week the student sits a timed question set or full paper, which is marked against the published mark scheme and returned with per-question timing. The comparison is against their own previous attempt, which is the only comparison that tells you anything useful.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and decide
process.description: At six weeks you get the series of marks, the topic log and an honest view on whether the remaining gap needs more sessions, a different tutor, or nothing at all. If the answer is that the school's teaching is now enough, that is what the review says.

whyPoints.title: The script is read before the first paid hour
whyPoints.description: Most Accounting tuition begins with a syllabus and a start date. Ours begins with the last marked paper, because the paper already contains the diagnosis. It is the difference between paying to be taught the subject again and paying to recover the specific marks that went missing.

whyPoints.title: Marking is included, not an extra
whyPoints.description: A full paper marked against the published mark scheme, with a question-by-question breakdown, is part of the session rather than a separate purchase. On a subject assessed entirely by written paper, marking is where most of the diagnostic value sits, and a rate that excludes it is not cheaper.

whyPoints.title: Both boards, not just the popular one
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0452 and Pearson 4AC1 overlap in content and differ in question style. Tutors on this page have taught to both, which matters for the many Dubai students who changed school mid-course and are now sitting a paper written in a style they have never practised.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and saying so before you enquire is better than discovering it after. It is also what makes a specialist available regardless of which community you live in.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can audit
whyPoints.description: Session notes, a topic log, a fortnightly series of marked papers and per-question timing. The point is that you can tell whether the money is working without taking anyone's word for it, including ours, and can stop at six weeks if it is not.

whyPoints.title: No price invented, no outcome promised
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are market bands with the source named. No tutor can promise a grade, and the ones who do are selling something other than teaching. What can be promised is marked work, named error patterns and a record of what moved.

faqs.question: Which Accounting syllabus does my child's Dubai school actually use?
faqs.answer: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai enter candidates for Cambridge IGCSE Accounting, code 0452, and a smaller number use Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting, code 4AC1. The code appears on the school's option booklet, on any past paper sent home, and on the exam entry statement. It matters because the two boards differ in paper structure and question phrasing even where content overlaps, so a student practising the wrong board's papers is rehearsing the wrong format. If you cannot find the code, ask the head of commerce directly rather than guessing from a textbook cover.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell from one marked paper what is going wrong in Accounting?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and more reliably than from a school report. A marked script shows which adjustments were attempted, which were abandoned, where own-figure marks carried a wrong number forward, and whether marks stop at the point a question changes from calculation to comment. One paper is enough to rank the two or three error patterns costing the most marks. What one paper cannot show is pace under full exam conditions if the paper was a short unit test, which is why a timed paper is sat early in any block.

faqs.question: Why does my child balance the trial balance in class but not in the exam?
faqs.answer: Almost always timing rather than understanding. In class the trial balance is the task; in the exam it arrives after a long question that has already eaten the thinking time, and the checking at the end gets cut. The marked script shows this clearly: accurate early work, then arithmetic slips concentrated in the final questions. The fix is practice at speed on the mechanical parts, so that double entry and balancing run without conscious effort and the available time goes to the parts that need judgement.

faqs.question: How many hours of Accounting tuition does a Year 11 student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: If the problem is diagnosable error patterns rather than missing content, a block of eight to twelve one-hour sessions across a term is a common shape, with a timed paper every second week. If a whole topic such as limited company accounts or incomplete records was never secured, add three or four sessions for that topic alone. Starting six weeks before a series changes the arithmetic: the hours go into converting existing knowledge into marks rather than into new teaching, and the gains are narrower but faster.

faqs.question: What does Accounting tuition cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE and A Level specialist. Those bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026. Ask what the rate includes: full-paper marking against the mark scheme is the line most often missing from a cheaper quote.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Accounting tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. For Accounting that works well, because the material is annotated scripts, ledger layouts and screen-shared statements. It also widens the choice of tutor: a family in Jebel Ali or Mirdif gets someone who marks Accounting papers weekly rather than the nearest generalist who is free that evening.

faqs.question: Is Accounting a sensible IGCSE option choice for my child?
faqs.answer: It suits students who are accurate, who tolerate repetitive procedure, and who are willing to write short evaluative paragraphs. It does not reward students who want to discuss ideas without precision, because format and labelling carry real marks. Before choosing it, check two practical things at the school: how many candidates it entered in the last series, and whether the same teacher also carries the A Level group. A single-teacher option subject gives you no second opinion inside the school if something goes wrong.

faqs.question: What is the suspense account and why does it cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: The suspense account holds the difference when a trial balance does not agree, and it is cleared as each one-sided error is corrected. Marks are lost in a predictable way: candidates correct the errors in the ledger accounts, score those marks, then leave the suspense account with a balance or omit it entirely, losing the marks tied to the reconciliation. It is a procedural habit rather than a concept, which is why it is one of the cheapest sets of marks to recover in a short block of sessions.

faqs.question: My child gets the ratios right but still loses marks on the analysis. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the analysis marks are written marks, awarded for using the figures just calculated. A candidate who computes a current ratio of 1.4 and then writes that liquidity looks weak without citing 1.4 has answered a general question rather than this one. Examiners reward a stated position, a figure from the candidate's own working as support, and a limitation or comparison. That is a three-sentence structure a student can rehearse, and it typically recovers three to six marks per paper.

faqs.question: Can we use Cambridge past papers if the school enters us with Edexcel?
faqs.answer: For content practice, yes, with care. The topics overlap heavily, so Cambridge questions on control accounts or depreciation are useful drills. For exam rehearsal, no: paper structure, mark allocation and command-word phrasing differ, and a student who has only sat the other board's papers meets unfamiliar instructions under time pressure. Sit timed papers from the board your child is actually entered with, and use the other board's material for topic practice only. Both boards publish specimen papers on their own sites.

faqs.question: What evidence should I expect after each Accounting session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was marked, which marks were gained and lost, the error pattern behind the losses, and what your child is practising before the next lesson. Every second week, a marked timed paper with per-question timing and a comparison against the previous attempt. At six weeks, the full series plus a topic log showing which syllabus areas are now secure. If a fortnight produced nothing because the school ran three assessments that week, the note should say that too.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

faqs.question: Is KHDA involved in approving private Accounting tutors?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai, where u.ae describes it as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Individual tutors fall under the MoHRE permit route instead. KHDA does issue an Educational Services Permit, but that is a licence for a training institute with premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Any tutoring service describing itself as carrying KHDA approval should be asked to show that permit number.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start Accounting support before the series?
faqs.answer: Four weeks still changes marks, but it changes a narrower set of them. In that window the work is layout discipline, labelling, showing workings, timing per question and answering the command word that was asked. Those are the cheap, propagating marks and they can move a borderline candidate. What four weeks cannot do is secure a topic never taught properly, such as manufacturing accounts or incomplete records. If a whole topic is missing, be honest about choosing between covering it and protecting the rest of the paper.

faqs.question: Where does IGCSE Accounting lead after Year 11 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The direct route is Cambridge International AS and A Level Accounting, code 9706, where the step up is in written analysis rather than bookkeeping. Other students move into BTEC Business, A Level Economics or Business, or a university foundation year. Check that your child's Dubai school actually timetables 9706 before assuming continuity, because several schools offer Accounting at 16 and not at 18. Note also that UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education.

If you would rather read first, the Dubai hub page lists every IB and IGCSE subject covered for families across the emirate, with the same AED market bands and the same online delivery stated on each one.

intro.heading: The price question, answered rather than deflected
paragraphs: A Dubai parent researching IGCSE support meets a strange wall. The pages ranking for this search are detailed about pedagogy and silent about money. One of the best-written competitor pages in the set has a frequently-asked-questions block that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. Another quotes a price in its structured data that contradicts the price in its own body copy. A third prices in US dollars for a market that transacts in dirhams. The effect is that parents end up phoning five providers to assemble a range that could have been published on a page.

So here is the range. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors are advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit broadly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, with travel built in, run from about AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting them at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200-500. Dedicated IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. Premium named tutors go higher again, with BartyED advertising AED 650.

Those are other organisations' published figures, with the source named, and they are the market rather than our price list. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Knowing the range is only half of a buying decision. The other half is knowing what moves a number inside it, because the same subject at the same level can be quoted at AED 150 and AED 450 by two people who both believe they are being reasonable. Tier, specification familiarity, examiner experience, session length, commitment length, travel, format and timing all move it. So does urgency: a family calling six weeks before a June series is negotiating from a weak position and should know that before they call.

IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not run group classes at a venue in Dubai and we do not send tutors to UAE addresses - in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. That matters to the cost conversation in a specific way: the travel component that pushes in-home rates to the AED 180-500 band is not in the price, and the tutor is matched to the specification rather than to the half-hour radius around your community.

dubai/igcse-classes.programmesIntro: Cost varies by stage more than parents expect, because the scarcity of tutors who have taught a specific paper changes with the level. These are the four stages Dubai families buy.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to buy and the one most often skipped. Rates sit at the lower end of every published band because the content is widely taught and the tutor pool is deep. The work here is algebraic fluency, scientific writing and reading stamina, assessed through Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests offered in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is where a relocating student's gap first becomes visible, and where fixing it is least expensive. A Year 9 arriving from another system who is drilled on written-examination convention for one term rarely needs the intensive Year 11 package that the same student would otherwise buy two years later at three times the hourly rate.

programmes.name: Year 10 IGCSE, Core and Extended
programmes.description: Mid-band pricing, and the stage with the best return per dirham because there is time for the work to compound. Buying one session a week through Year 10 generally costs less in total than buying three a week through the spring of Year 11, and it produces the tier evidence that protects sixth-form options.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically fix tier entries during or at the end of Year 10. Families who spend here are buying a decision as much as a grade, since Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available and that ceiling is read by A Level and IB Diploma admissions two years later.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam-term intensive
programmes.description: The most expensive stage, for two reasons that have nothing to do with teaching quality. Demand concentrates into January through April, and specialists with a free evening slot in February are scarce. Specialist IGCSE rates in the AED 200-450 band are quoted most often for exactly this window.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock seasons in November and late February drive two demand spikes. Booking a regular slot in September costs less than buying the same slot in February, and any provider telling you otherwise has not looked at their own diary. Rates do tighten closer to exams, which is a supply fact rather than a sales tactic.

programmes.name: Retake and grade-lift blocks
programmes.description: Short, narrow and usually the best-value purchase available, because the problem is normally technique on one paper rather than a missing syllabus. A six-week block on specific question types costs a fraction of a two-year engagement and often does the required job.
programmes.countryNote: The deadlines sit before the information. Pearson's International GCSE November series ran its final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge final entries for a March 2027 series fall on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Budget for the entry fee at the chosen centre as well as the tuition.

dubai/igcse-classes.subjectsIntro: Subjects do not cost the same, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Each note says roughly where a subject sits in the market band and how many hours families typically end up buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in Dubai and therefore the most competitive pricing, generally available across the full published range. Families typically buy one weekly hour through Year 10 and two through Year 11. The large recoverable loss is unwritten method, which is cheap to fix and does not need a premium tutor.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mid to upper band. Fewer tutors are genuinely comfortable with the Alternative to Practical paper than claim to be, and that paper is where a meaningful share of marks sits. Ask about it explicitly before agreeing a rate; it is the fastest way to tell a specialist from a generalist.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with demand concentrated in the spring of Year 11 around moles, electrolysis and organic pathways. Students usually need fewer hours than they fear, because the losses cascade from one or two specific skills rather than spreading across the syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mid band with good availability. The hours go on command-term discipline rather than content, which means a shorter engagement than parents budget for. A student losing marks by describing where the paper asked them to explain does not need a term of re-teaching.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium in the IGCSE market. Few tutors in any one part of Dubai have taught these specifications, so rates sit at the specialist end and availability is the binding constraint rather than price. This is also where online matching changes the answer completely.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Wide pool, wide price range, and the greatest variation in actual usefulness. A tutor who teaches writing well is not the same as one who teaches the mark tariffs on the summary and directed-writing tasks, and only the second moves an IGCSE grade. Ask which they do.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Lower to mid band with strong availability in Dubai. The efficient purchase is short and structural: recognising each reading task's fixed shape within the first ten seconds. Students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course need more hours, and should be priced accordingly.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Mid band, and unusually efficient to buy. Application and evaluation habits are teachable in a handful of sessions, and diagram conventions in Economics can be drilled out in two. Families frequently over-buy here because the subjects feel content-heavy.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Upper band because of a supply quirk: tutors who can program are plentiful, tutors who can teach the board's pseudocode convention and trace-table method are not. Verify the second rather than the first before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Mid band, with hours concentrated on source interrogation and the extended response rather than case-study recall. A short engagement that installs a fixed reading order for resource questions generally outperforms a long one spent revising content.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Mid to upper band and tight on availability in the evening slots Dubai families want. KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so demand is structural rather than seasonal.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Lower to mid band. The cheapest useful hour in the whole set is often the one spent marking the specification against the student's revision list, because scope confusion here wastes more time than any content gap does.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: The useful comparison is not between brands but between business models, because the model explains the price. A marketplace that matches you to a university student has a different cost base from an agency that recruits qualified subject teachers, and both differ from a tuition centre carrying premises, a licence and staff in Dubai. A freelance tutor driving to your community is pricing their car and their evening as well as their teaching.

The table sets these out with the AED bands each model advertises and the source of the figure. Everything in it is another organisation's published rate, named and dated to October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list, and a provider that quotes you a number should be able to tell you what it includes, how long the session is, and whether the figure is per hour or per lesson - those are three different questions and they are frequently conflated.

Two patterns are worth noticing. The first is that the in-home band carries a visible travel premium: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online. The second is that the top of the market is defined by scarcity rather than by format - a specialist in a thinly taught specification commands AED 200-450 or more whether they are on a screen or in a room.

What this means practically is that comparing two quotes requires normalising them first. Per hour or per lesson. Sixty minutes or fifty. Travel included or added. Materials included or billed. One subject or two. Cancellation terms. A quote of AED 200 that is a fifty-minute lesson with a two-session cancellation notice is not cheaper than AED 220 for a full hour with twenty-four hours' notice, and most families never get far enough into the detail to see that.

sections.heading: Group classes against one-to-one: the arithmetic nobody writes down
paragraphs: Group classes look like obvious value and sometimes are. The honest way to compare them is per student per hour of direct attention, not per student per hour of elapsed time, because those two numbers diverge sharply as the group grows. In a class of six, a student receives on average ten minutes of individual attention in an hour. At AED 80 a head that is good value if the content is genuinely new to all six, and poor value if five of them are there for a different reason than your child.

The deciding question is whether the students share the problem. A group works when everyone is meeting a topic for the first time: a new unit, a shared syllabus gap, a timed-paper practice session where the clock does the teaching. A group fails when the members have different error patterns, because the tutor has to choose whose problem to address, and your child's problem may not be chosen.

This is also where diagnosis pays for itself. A parent who knows their child is losing marks to unwritten method and timing does not need a group class on electrolysis, however cheap it is. A parent with no diagnosis buys whatever is on offer and hopes some of it lands. The hour spent getting a marked script read properly changes which product you should buy, and often saves more than it costs.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number inside the band
paragraphs: Two tutors can quote AED 150 and AED 400 for the same subject and level and both be pricing rationally. The variables are visible once named, and knowing them turns a quote from a mystery into a negotiation you can hold up your end of.

Scarcity dominates. A tutor who has actually taught Cambridge Additional Mathematics or Edexcel Further Pure Maths is rare in any one part of Dubai, and rarity sets the price regardless of format. Tier matters next: Extended and Higher work commands more than Core and Foundation because fewer tutors are secure in the extension content. Timing matters third, and it is the one families control least well - a February slot in a Year 11 exam run costs more than the same slot booked in September, because by February the diaries are full.

Then there are the structural variables. Session length, since a fifty-minute 'hour' is common and should be asked about. Commitment length, since a term booked up front usually prices below a rolling week. Travel, which is the whole difference between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band. Whether materials are included. Whether a second subject with the same tutor attracts a different rate. And urgency, which is a real factor and an uncomfortable one.

sections.heading: The extras that appear after you have committed
paragraphs: The headline rate is rarely the whole invoice, and the gap between them is where most of the dissatisfaction in this market lives. None of the following is dishonest in itself; the problem is that they are usually disclosed at the point of billing rather than the point of decision.

Registration or matching fees, charged once at the start by some agencies. Materials and printing, where a provider supplies workbooks. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged separately from the first lesson. Late-cancellation charges, which vary from twenty-four hours' notice to a full session forfeited, and which matter enormously in a city where a school fixture can move with a day's notice. Rescheduling limits per month. Minimum commitment terms, which can mean a term's notice to stop. Peak-season surcharges in the exam run. Travel surcharges on in-home arrangements for outlying communities. And payment-method differences, where a card payment carries a fee that a bank transfer does not.

The right move is to ask for all of it in writing before the first paid session, in one message with numbered questions. A provider who answers crisply has thought about it. A provider who answers in generalities will be answering in generalities when there is a dispute. This is not a sign of bad faith on their part so much as a sign that the terms do not exist in a form anyone can read, which amounts to the same thing in practice.

On VAT specifically, the only safe position is to ask whether a quoted figure includes it and to get the answer in writing. The tax treatment of education and tuition services in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring provider's summary, and this page does not state it. What a provider can and should tell you is whether the number they just quoted is the number you will pay.
bullets: Ask for every charge in writing before the first paid session
Confirm the session length in minutes, not as 'an hour'

Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT and keep the answer

sections.heading: Tuition in context: fees, the 2026-27 freeze and exam entry costs
paragraphs: Tutoring is a small line next to a Dubai school fee, and placing it next to the other education costs a family carries makes it easier to judge. The emirate's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

That freeze is the right anchor for a tuition budget conversation this year, because it means the rest of the education bill is flat while tutoring is not. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More capacity changes where families can study; it does not change what an hour of specialist teaching costs.

The other cost families forget is exam entry, which is paid through the school in the normal case and directly to a centre for a private candidate. Entry fees are set by the centre rather than the board and vary, so the number has to come from your school's exams officer or from the centre you approach. A retake plan with no entry-fee line in it is an incomplete plan, and the fee is usually payable well before the papers - Cambridge final entries for a March 2027 series fall on 27 November 2026.

The table puts the pieces together. Figures attributed to published sources are marked as such; where a number depends on your own school or centre, the table says so rather than inventing a figure. We publish no fee list for IB Gram here because the right number depends on subject, tier, frequency and availability, and the consultation after the free trial lesson is where it belongs.

sections.heading: How many hours a subject really needs
paragraphs: The hourly rate is only half the cost. The other half is the number of hours, and that is where families both over-buy and under-buy badly. Over-buying looks like three sessions a week in an attempt to feel safe. Under-buying looks like six sessions booked eight weeks before a June series for a syllabus that was never learned.

The honest ranges are narrower than the market implies. A single diagnosed content gap in one topic is commonly three to five sessions with practice between them. A technique habit - method lines, command terms, units - takes two or three weeks of short frequent drilling rather than a term. A full year of maintenance support in one subject through Year 10 is typically thirty to thirty-five hours spread across the year. An exam-term intensive in one subject is typically ten to sixteen hours concentrated into eight to twelve weeks.

What drives the total up is not difficulty but diffusion. A student with no diagnosis consumes hours on whatever they mention each week, and the same topics recur because nothing was fixed. A student with a ranked error log consumes fewer hours to better effect, which is the practical argument for spending one of the first hours on measurement rather than teaching.

There is one case where more hours genuinely is the answer, and it should be named: a student arriving mid-course in the second term of Year 11 from a different system, with real content gaps across a syllabus and no time. That is a triage situation, and the right conversation includes narrowing the subject set with the school or planning for a later series rather than buying into a window that cannot hold the work.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest quote is sometimes the expensive one
paragraphs: A low rate is not a red flag by itself. A capable university student teaching Year 9 algebra at the bottom of the published band is good value and the right purchase for that job. The problem arises when a low rate is bought for a job it cannot do: Extended-tier Chemistry eight weeks from a series, or a specification the tutor has never seen a paper from. That hour is not cheap; it is a term spent and a term lost.

There is also a compliance dimension that Dubai families should understand, because it is almost entirely absent from competitor pages. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, under the service named 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists a two-working-day completion time and no fees.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published - press reporting notes that the ministry did not specify amounts or detail the penalties - so any specific figure circulating online is unverified and we will not repeat one. The permit itself being free of charge is the point worth knowing: a tutor cannot cite permit cost as a reason for a rate.

Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual's work permit, and it is why 'KHDA approval' is a phrase to treat carefully: it applies to institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and makes no claim of approval or endorsement by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: Judging whether a term was worth the money
paragraphs: At renewal, the question is not whether the sessions happened or whether your child liked them. It is whether the losses that were costing marks in week one are still costing marks in week twelve. That is answerable if the work was documented and unanswerable if it was not, which is the practical reason to insist on written session notes and marked papers from the start rather than at the end.

Three things are worth looking at. The error log, compared with its first version: have the labels changed? Two marked papers from the same specification, placed side by side: has the loss moved from method to something else, which is progress even if the score is similar? And the student's own account of what they do differently in the exam hall, which is often the clearest signal of all.

A flat score with a changed error profile is a term that worked. A flat score with an identical error profile is a term that did not, and the correct response is to change the approach rather than to add hours - adding hours to an activity that is not working simply buys more of the thing that is not working. That sounds obvious written down and it is the most common error in this market.

It is also worth asking what the alternative use of the money was. For some families, one diagnostic session plus a disciplined home routine outperforms a term of weekly tuition, and nobody selling tuition has an incentive to say so. We would rather say it, partly because it is true and partly because the families who come back are the ones who were told the truth the first time.

sections.heading: Getting started without overbuying
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest useful thing, which is a diagnosis. Bring the most recent marked mock script and the exam entry statement listing each subject's board, code and tier. The free trial lesson includes a short timed question so that the first conversation is about evidence rather than impressions, and it costs nothing - no card details are taken to book it.

Then buy the smallest block that could work. One subject, one weekly slot, four weeks, with an explicit review at the end against the error log. That is a modest commitment and it produces enough evidence to decide properly. Families who start by booking three subjects at two sessions a week have bought certainty rather than information, and they generally spend more for less.

Ask us the uncomfortable questions up front. What is the rate, per how many minutes, and does it include VAT. What are the cancellation terms in hours. What happens if the first match is wrong. Which of my child's subjects are you thin on. And: is tuition actually the right purchase here, or is it a mock-reading problem we could hand back to you to act on. All five have answers and you should have them in writing before the first paid session.

Finally, the format, stated plainly. These are live one-to-one video lessons on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram operates no centre or classroom in Dubai and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The cost consequence is straightforward: there is no travel component in the number, and the tutor is chosen for the specification rather than for living within half an hour of your community.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE classes cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates fall into bands. Budget online tutoring and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit broadly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits run about AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Dedicated IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors higher again. Those are other providers' own published figures as of October 2026, not our price list.

faqs.question: Are small group IGCSE classes better value than one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the students share the problem. Compare per student per hour of direct attention rather than per hour of elapsed time: in a group of six, each student receives roughly ten minutes of individual attention. That is excellent value when all six are meeting a new topic together, and poor value when five of them need something your child does not. A diagnosis changes the answer, which is why a marked script read properly is often the purchase that should come first.

faqs.question: What should a monthly IGCSE tuition package in Dubai actually include?
faqs.answer: Ask for the number of sessions, their length in minutes, the subjects covered, whether unused sessions carry over, the rescheduling allowance per month, and the notice period to stop. Packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A package is only good value if the sessions get used, so the rescheduling terms matter more than the headline figure for a family with a fixture-heavy school calendar.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects tend to cost more per hour in Dubai, and why?
faqs.answer: Scarcity rather than difficulty sets the price. Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics carry a clear premium because very few tutors in any one part of the city have taught those specifications. Computer Science sits high for a related reason: tutors who can program are plentiful, tutors who can teach the board's pseudocode convention and trace-table method are not. Extended and Higher tier work costs more than Core and Foundation. Mathematics, Biology and the English specifications have the deepest pools and therefore the most competitive pricing.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai go up closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and it is a supply fact rather than a sales tactic. Demand concentrates between January and April for a June series, the number of evening slots is fixed, and specialists with a free Tuesday at 6pm in February are scarce. Booking a regular slot in September costs less than buying the same slot in February, and it also gives the work time to compound. If you are starting late, expect the upper end of the published band and a shorter list of available tutors, particularly in the thinly taught specifications.

faqs.question: Is an advertised AED rate per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask, because both conventions are in use and a fifty-minute 'hour' is common. The question matters more than it looks: AED 200 for fifty minutes is AED 240 an hour, which moves a quote from one market band into another. Get the session length in minutes, confirm whether the figure is per session or per sixty minutes, and ask whether a 45-minute option exists at the same hourly basis - for drilling work two shorter sessions a week often beat one long one on both effect and cost.

faqs.question: Should I expect VAT to be added to a tutoring invoice in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider whether the figure they quoted includes it, and keep the answer in writing. The VAT treatment of education and tuition services in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own published guidance rather than for any tutoring company's summary, and this page deliberately does not state it. What a provider can tell you, and should, is whether the number on the quote is the number you will pay. A provider who cannot answer that about their own invoice has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What extras should I ask about before paying for a term of classes?
faqs.answer: Registration or matching fees, materials and printing, separate diagnostic or assessment charges, the late-cancellation window in hours, the rescheduling allowance per month, minimum commitment and notice to stop, peak-season surcharges during the exam run, travel surcharges where an in-home arrangement applies, and whether a card payment carries a fee a transfer does not. Ask for all of it in one numbered message before the first paid session. A crisp written answer tells you the terms exist; a vague one tells you they will be vague during a dispute too.

faqs.question: How many hours does one IGCSE subject usually need across Year 11?
faqs.answer: Narrower ranges than the market implies. A single diagnosed content gap in one topic is commonly three to five sessions with practice between them. A technique habit such as writing method lines or reading command terms takes two to three weeks of short frequent drilling. Year-long maintenance in one subject runs roughly thirty to thirty-five hours spread across the year, and an exam-term intensive is typically ten to sixteen hours concentrated into eight to twelve weeks. Hours multiply when there is no diagnosis, because the same topics recur without ever being fixed.

faqs.question: Why can the cheapest IGCSE tutor in Dubai turn out to be the most expensive choice?
faqs.answer: Because a rate is only cheap relative to the job. A capable university student teaching Year 9 algebra at the bottom of the published band is good value. The same tutor taking on Extended-tier Chemistry eight weeks before a series has been bought for a job they cannot do, and the cost is a lost term rather than the hourly fee. Ask what specification they have taught, which papers, and at which tier. Also ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years and is required of individuals tutoring in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is specification experience rather than general competence. Physics and Mathematics is a common and credible pairing. Chemistry and Biology is plausible. Mathematics and English is possible but rarer at a specialist standard, and a tutor who claims five subjects across both boards is usually claiming breadth they cannot evidence. Where one tutor genuinely covers two subjects there is often a package rate and always a scheduling advantage. Where they do not, two specialists at fewer hours each is the better purchase.

faqs.question: What happens financially if we decide to stop after one or two lessons?
faqs.answer: That depends on the terms you agreed, which is exactly why they should be in writing first. With us the trial lesson is free and takes no card details, and we would rather you stopped after a short block than committed to a term that was not working. In the wider market, watch for minimum commitment periods, notice requirements measured in sessions rather than days, and prepaid packages with no refund on unused sessions. Ask for the stopping terms before the starting terms; the answer tells you how confident the provider is.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE classes with IB Gram take place at a venue anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no centre, classroom, office or branch in the UAE, and does not provide home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the country - in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Classes are delivered as live one-to-one or paired video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. The cost effect is direct: the travel element that lifts in-home rates into the AED 180-500 band is absent from the number, and the tutor is selected for the specification your child sits rather than for proximity to your community.

faqs.question: How do school fees and tutoring costs compare for a Dubai family this year?
faqs.answer: School fees are the far larger line and, unusually, they are flat: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Tutoring is not frozen. Published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Exam entry fees, set by your school or centre, sit alongside both.

faqs.question: How do I judge at renewal whether a term of classes was worth the money?
faqs.answer: Compare the error log with its first version and put two marked papers from the same specification side by side. If the losses have moved - method fixed, timing now the main problem - the term worked even if the score is similar, because a different problem is a nearer problem. If the error profile is identical, the term did not work, and the correct response is to change the approach rather than add hours. Ask your child what they now do differently in the exam hall; that answer is often the clearest signal available.

dubai/igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: These tutors coach exam performance as well as content. Each one marks to the published Cambridge or Pearson scheme, labels losses by cause, and can name the command-term traps on the specific paper your child will sit.

intro.heading: Why a student who knows the work still loses fourteen marks
paragraphs: Open almost any marked IGCSE script from a Dubai Year 11 who is stuck in the middle grades and the pattern is the same. The content is there. The student can tell you about electrolysis or about the quadratic formula or about the causes of a trade deficit. What the script shows is something narrower and more fixable: an answer with no intermediate working, a question that asked for an explanation and received a description, a number without a unit, and three questions at the end of the paper attempted in four minutes.

Add those up and they commonly reach eight to fourteen marks on a single paper. On most IGCSE grade scales that is one or two whole grades. No amount of additional content teaching retrieves them, because they were never content losses. This is the gap coaching is for, and it is the reason this page is organised around causes of lost marks rather than around a syllabus tour.

The distinction matters commercially too. A family who diagnoses a timing problem and buys a term of topic revision has bought the wrong product, usually at AED 150 to 300 an hour based on the market rates providers publish. It is a common and expensive mistake, and it happens because nobody put the script under a lamp first. A mock paper is the cheapest diagnostic instrument available to a Dubai parent and it is almost always sitting in a school bag, unread by anyone except the student who got the score.

Coaching in this sense is unglamorous. It involves reading the mark scheme out loud in the student's own script, which is tedious. It involves doing one calculation forty times until the working writes itself under pressure, which is dull. It involves sitting with a clock. The reason to do it anyway is that it is the highest-yield work available in the final year, and it is the part of preparation that schools, carrying thirty students a class, have the least capacity to deliver individually.

Everything here is delivered as one-to-one live video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Dubai school week. IB Gram does not run a coaching centre in the UAE and does not send tutors to Dubai addresses; in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. For this particular kind of work the online format is not a compromise at all - the script, the mark scheme, the annotation and a visible timer sit in one shared window, and the marked file is still there next week.

One more thing before the detail. Coaching of this kind is not a replacement for the school. The teacher has the syllabus, the internal assessment record and thirty other students, and in most Dubai schools they are doing that job well. What they do not have is the room to sit with one student and read a mark scheme aloud against that student's own script for twenty minutes. That is the gap, it is narrow, and it is where an outside hour is worth paying for.

dubai/igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Coaching looks different at each stage of the IGCSE route, because the thing that limits a grade changes as the exam gets closer. These are the four stages Dubai families ask about.

programmes.name: Year 9: before the options are fixed
programmes.description: The useful work here is habit formation rather than exam technique: writing method lines without being asked, labelling axes, reading a question twice, recording units. None of it is examined yet, which is exactly why it is cheap to install now and expensive to install in Year 11. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint results, offered in March, May and October, are the earliest reliable signal a parent gets.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage is complicated by arrival timing. Students joining a British-curriculum school from a CBSE or American background in Year 9 have usually met the content but not the written-examination conventions, and a Checkpoint result reads lower than their understanding warrants. Coaching that fixes convention at this point prevents a misread tier decision a year later.

programmes.name: Year 10: building the paper habits
programmes.description: The first year of the course, where topics are taught for the first time and the tier decision is approaching. Coaching here means converting new content into examinable form straight away rather than a year later - every new topic practised as a past-paper question within a fortnight of being taught, and the command terms of that subject introduced as vocabulary.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally make tier entries during or at the end of Year 10, and the decision is evidenced by internal assessment. A student whose exam technique is weak looks like a student who should sit the lower tier, and the grade ceiling that follows is permanent. Fixing technique in Year 10 is therefore a decision about Year 12 options.

programmes.name: Year 11: mocks, then the series
programmes.description: The year coaching is most often bought, and the year it has the narrowest window to work in. The sequence that works is: mock papers marked by cause, one error pattern attacked at a time, timed-condition practice from January, and paper-order strategy agreed before the first real paper. Content revision continues but stops being the main event.
programmes.countryNote: Mock windows in Dubai schools commonly fall in November and again in late February, which produces two genuine diagnostics in the right order. Families who treat mocks as a verdict waste them. Families who treat them as data get the single most useful document of the whole two years.

programmes.name: Post-results: the retake or lift
programmes.description: A single grade short of a sixth-form condition is usually a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, which makes it unusually responsive to coaching. The work is narrow by design: the specific paper, the specific question types that cost the marks, and timed practice. A whole-subject re-teach is rarely the right purchase.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's International GCSE November series and Cambridge's November and, where available, March series are the practical windows, and their entry deadlines fall before the grades that would justify an entry arrive. Agree the plan in June rather than in August.

dubai/igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Each note below names the error pattern that costs the most marks in that subject rather than summarising its content. These are the things coaching actually works on.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Unwritten method is the largest recoverable loss in the whole qualification. Both boards award method marks explicitly, so a wrong final answer with clear working can outscore a wrong answer with none. The drill is mechanical: every question, every time, one line per step, until it survives the clock.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit conversion and formula rearrangement under pressure. Candidates who can quote the equation lose the mark by substituting centimetres into a formula expecting metres, or by rearranging on the fly and dropping a reciprocal. Writing the formula, then the substitution, then the answer with its unit is three marks of insurance.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cascading errors from unbalanced equations. One wrong coefficient in part (a) removes the follow-through marks in later parts unless the working is explicit enough for an examiner to award them. The coaching drill is to balance, check atom counts, then annotate the mole ratio before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term blindness, more than in any other subject. A question asking the candidate to explain water movement in a root hair cell wants water potential, the partially permeable membrane and the direction named. A description of water moving in scores a fraction of the available marks and feels like a correct answer.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Scope confusion. Students revise content that is not on their route and skip content that is, because the specification subsets are not obvious from a textbook. A single session spent marking the syllabus document against the student's revision list routinely saves a fortnight.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Tariff blindness on the summary and directed-writing tasks. The mark scheme awards content points, and elegant prose that misses them caps the score. Coaching here is largely counting: how many points are available, how many the student found, and how long they spent not finding the rest.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Question-type unfamiliarity rather than language weakness, particularly for students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course. The reading tasks have fixed shapes, and recognising the shape in the first ten seconds is a trainable skill that changes the whole paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Analysis without application. A correct definition about no particular firm earns the knowledge mark and nothing beyond it. The fix is a sentence frame applied to every case study until it is automatic: the concept, then this business, then the consequence, then the judgement with a reason.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Loose diagrams. Axes unlabelled, curves unnamed, the shift drawn but the new equilibrium not marked. Each omission is a mark, they recur on every diagram question in the paper, and the entire problem can be drilled out in two sessions.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Narrative instead of interrogation. The case study is recalled accurately and the source is ignored, which caps the response in the middle band. Coaching teaches a fixed reading order for any resource question: what it shows, what it does not show, and what that means for the question asked.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Provenance left on the table. Source questions award marks for using who wrote it, when and why, and most mid-band answers treat sources as neutral information. The drill is a provenance sentence before any content sentence, every time, until it is habit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode written as Python. The written paper assesses the board's own pseudocode convention, trace tables and data representation, and fluent programmers lose marks on notation. Trace tables in particular reward a slow, ruled, row-by-row method that nobody adopts voluntarily.

dubai/igcse-coaching.regionsTitle: Dubai communities these sessions run into
dubai/igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Coaching is scheduled around what the Dubai week leaves free, which differs by district. These notes are about timing and workload, not about where a tutor sits - delivery is over video.

regions.note: Short school runs and a high density of secondary provision, so students here often carry heavy co-curricular timetables. Coaching slots are frequently squeezed to 45 minutes twice a week rather than one long session.

regions.name: Dubailand and Villanova
regions.note: Long outbound commutes and younger cohorts in several of the newer schools. Requests here tend to arrive in Year 9 and Year 10, which is the cheaper end of the problem to solve.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Tower living with limited quiet space in the afternoon. Later slots work better, and families here more often ask for shorter, more frequent drill sessions than for weekly hour-long blocks.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Villa districts with schools inside the community and sport running until early evening. The realistic coaching window starts at 7pm, which suits timed-paper work because the student is past the school day entirely.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods feeding long-standing British-curriculum schools with settled exam results. Requests here are usually about moving a 6 to a 7 rather than about rescuing a pass, which is almost entirely technique work.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah Village, Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills
schoolClusters.note: A fast-growing cluster where several schools are still working through their first full IGCSE cycles. Students we support from these catchments most often need command-term and paper-technique work rather than content recovery.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai South, Jebel Ali and Dubai Investment Park
schoolClusters.note: Outlying catchments with long commutes and a mix of British and Indian-curriculum provision. Timing discipline is the standing request here, partly because students arrive home late and practise under fatigue.

modes.description: Short, frequent sessions attacking one labelled cause at a time. Forty-five minutes twice a week beats ninety minutes once, because the point is repetition under mild pressure rather than explanation. Each session ends with three questions of the same type to be done before the next one.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks on any IGCSE paper
paragraphs: Every IGCSE paper is written in a controlled vocabulary. 'State' and 'explain' are not stylistic variants; they instruct the examiner what to accept, and the mark tariff follows from them. A student who treats them as synonyms will write a long answer to a one-mark question and a one-line answer to a four-mark question, and will lose marks at both ends while working harder than the candidate who read the verb.

This is the single most under-taught thing in exam preparation, and it is almost entirely absent from the competitor pages on this search. It is also the fastest intervention available. Most students can be taught the twelve command terms that appear across their subjects in two sessions, and the effect shows up on the next timed paper rather than three months later.

The table below sets out the terms that recur most across Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE papers in the sciences, mathematics and the social subjects, with what the examiner is actually looking for and the error that usually appears instead. Both boards publish their own command-term guidance in the syllabus and specification documents, and those are the authoritative versions - this is a working summary, not a substitute.

The drill is simple and dull. Take ten past-paper questions. Cover the question body. Read only the command term and the mark allocation, and predict the shape of the answer: how many distinct points, whether a reason is required, whether a judgement is needed. Then read the question. Students who do this twenty times stop writing essays in response to 'state' within a fortnight.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THE EXAMINER IS ACTUALLY LOOKING FOR
rows: A paragraph, costing time rather than marks
What is observed or what happens, in sequence
An explanation of why, which is a different question
A cause linked to an effect, with a mechanism
A description of what happens, with no 'because'
Working shown line by line, then the answer with a unit
The final answer alone, discarding method marks
A plausible application of principle to a new context
A recalled textbook fact about a different context
Explicit linked statements covering both items
Two separate descriptions with no comparative language
Both sides plus a judgement with a reason
One side argued well, with no judgement at the end
An approximate paraphrase that misses the key term

sections.heading: The error patterns that cost Dubai candidates the most marks
paragraphs: After enough marked scripts the losses stop looking random. They cluster, they repeat within a student, and they are specific enough to attack one at a time. What follows is the list that recurs most across the Dubai Year 10 and Year 11 scripts that come through these sessions, with the drill that removes each one.

Two things are worth noticing about the list. First, almost none of these are knowledge failures - the student could do the question in conversation. Second, each one has a mechanical fix, which is why coaching works faster than re-teaching. A habit that takes three weeks to install is worth more than a topic that takes three weeks to re-explain, because the habit pays out on every question in the paper rather than on the two questions about that topic.

The order matters. Attack the pattern with the largest mark count first, not the one that is easiest to fix or the one the student finds most annoying. That is the whole purpose of labelling and counting lost marks rather than simply noting them: it produces a ranking, and the ranking is what makes the next four weeks worth paying for.

One caveat about the cost column. The figures are the typical range seen across marked scripts rather than a measured average with a sample size behind it, and they vary by subject and by paper. Treat them as a guide to which pattern deserves attention first, not as a published statistic. The number that matters is the one from your child's current script, counted by a person who marked it strictly to the scheme rather than estimated from memory.

table.caption: EIGHT RECURRING ERROR PATTERNS AND THE DRILL THAT REMOVES EACH
rows: One line per step on every question, including the easy ones
Command term read as a synonym
All subjects, worst in Biology and Geography

Unit written before the number is calculated, not after
Full accuracy carried through, rounded only at the final line
Balance, count atoms, annotate the mole ratio before calculating
