sections.heading: Timing is a budgeting problem, and it is solvable on paper
paragraphs: A candidate who loses six marks in the last section has not run out of ability. They have overspent earlier, usually on a question they could already do, because writing more felt like working harder. The exam is a budget: a fixed number of minutes to collect a fixed number of marks, and every paper has an implied spending rate that can be calculated before the student ever sits it.

The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly with a Year 11 because it is persuasive in a way that advice is not. Take the paper's total marks and its duration, subtract five minutes for reading and checking, and divide. That is the marks-per-minute rate the paper requires. Then take the student's last mock and work out where they actually spent the time. The mismatch is usually concentrated in two or three questions.

From there the rules are simple and the discipline is hard. A hard move-on rule: if a question has consumed its budget and has not yielded, leave it and return. An order strategy: some candidates do better collecting the back-end marks first, which is permitted and rarely considered. And a checking allocation that is genuinely protected rather than theoretically reserved, because unchecked unit and transcription errors are among the cheapest marks on the paper.

Practising this requires real exam conditions, which almost no student imposes on themselves. A visible clock, no phone, no pausing to look something up, and a strict stop. Over video that is easier to enforce than it sounds: the timer is on the shared screen, the tutor is watching, and the script is photographed and marked immediately afterwards while the decisions are still fresh enough to discuss.

table.caption: MARKS PER MINUTE - WHAT A PAPER ACTUALLY DEMANDS
rows: Six-mark questions attempted first and over-run
One stubborn algebra question consuming ten minutes
Drawing graphs slowly, then rushing the evaluation
Evaluation questions left unfinished at the end

sections.heading: The Alternative to Practical paper, and why it rewards vocabulary
paragraphs: Most Dubai science candidates on the Cambridge tiered specifications sit an Alternative to Practical paper rather than a live practical examination. It assesses experimental method in writing, and it is one of the highest-yield papers to coach because the skill it tests is narrow, explicit and almost never taught as a skill in its own right.

What it rewards is naming. The independent variable, the dependent variable, the variables held constant and how. The instrument and its precision. A repeat and a mean. An anomalous result identified and what to do about it. An improvement that is actually an improvement rather than 'be more careful'. A student who writes 'measure the temperature and record the results' has described something true and collected very little, because the mark scheme is looking for specific nouns.

The graph questions carry their own set of marks and their own set of avoidable losses: axes the wrong way round, a scale chosen so the points occupy a quarter of the grid, points plotted without a sharp pencil, a line of best fit drawn through the first and last points rather than through the distribution. Each is a mark, and all of them are mechanical.

This is also the clearest answer to parents who worry that online coaching cannot cover practical work. The paper is a writing paper. Method rehearsal, variable identification, instrument precision and graph technique transfer perfectly over a shared screen. Where a school enters a component requiring laboratory work, that work happens at school under the school's supervision, and coaching prepares the method and the write-up conventions beforehand.
bullets: Name the independent, dependent and controlled variables explicitly, every time
State the instrument and its precision rather than the action
Identify anomalies and say what you would do about them
'Be more careful' is never an improvement; a named change is

sections.heading: What a mark converts to, and why boundaries move
paragraphs: Parents often ask what score equals a grade 7, and the honest answer is that it depends on the series. Grade boundaries are set after each examination to account for the difficulty of that particular paper, which means a raw mark that earned one grade last June may sit a boundary either side of it this June. Boards publish boundaries after each series, and those published tables are the only reliable reference.

The practical consequence for coaching is that planning to a target raw mark is reasonable and planning to a historical boundary is not. The sensible approach is to look at the spread of recent boundaries for the specification, plan for the upper end of that spread, and treat anything closer than three or four marks to a boundary as a coin toss rather than a result. Students sitting three marks under a boundary are the population for whom technique work pays the most, because three marks is one unwritten method line and one unit.

A second point about boundaries belongs here because it affects tier decisions. On tiered specifications the lower tier caps the grade available regardless of raw mark, so a student scoring near the top of the Core or Foundation paper cannot reach the top grades at all. That is a structural ceiling rather than a boundary effect, and it is the reason a tier conversation has to happen before entries close rather than after a strong mock.

We do not reproduce or distribute boundary tables, syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. They are published by Cambridge Assessment International Education and by Pearson and should be read on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. A provider offering to supply you with a library of those files is telling you how it treats rules generally.

sections.heading: The diagnostic session, in detail
paragraphs: The first session is not a lesson, and a family should be suspicious of a coaching service that starts by teaching. It is a measurement exercise, and it has a shape. Thirty minutes of timed work from a real past paper on the correct specification, done with a visible clock while the tutor says nothing. Then the marking, strictly to the published scheme, with the student watching rather than being handed a score afterwards.

The marking happens in four passes. The raw mark, done without generosity. Then every lost mark labelled by cause: recall, method, arithmetic, command term, units, or time. Then the labels grouped and counted, which converts a score into a ranked diagnosis. Then one cause selected and three further questions found that attack it. That output - a ranked list and a first target - is the deliverable of the session.

What this produces for a parent is unusually concrete. Not 'your child needs to work on algebra', but 'eleven marks lost: five to unwritten method, three to command terms, two to units, one to recall, and the recall gap is in one named topic'. That is actionable by the family even without further sessions, which is why we are content for some people to buy only the diagnostic and leave.

Doing this over video has a practical advantage worth naming. The script is photographed or shared on screen, the mark scheme sits beside it, and the annotation is saved as a file with a date on it. Six weeks later, the second diagnostic can be placed next to the first and compared directly. A paper sheet handed over in a living room does not survive to be compared with anything.
bullets: Thirty minutes of timed work before any teaching happens
Four marking passes: mark, label, group, target
Output is a ranked diagnosis and one first target, in writing
Files are dated so the next diagnostic can be compared with this one

sections.heading: Coaching through the Dubai mock season
paragraphs: Dubai's British-curriculum schools typically run mock examinations in November and again in late February, and those two windows are the most valuable and most wasted resource in the IGCSE year. They are valuable because they produce a full marked script under something close to real conditions, which is the only instrument that reveals timing behaviour. They are wasted because the script is usually read once, for the score, and then filed.

The right sequence is to coach lightly before a mock and heavily after it. Before: confirm the timing plan, rehearse the question-order strategy, and resist the urge to cram new content, which displaces sleep and rarely appears on the paper. After: the full post-mortem, with every lost mark labelled, and a revised ranking for the next eight weeks.

The February mock has a particular function in Dubai, because it falls close enough to a June series to be predictive but far enough away to be fixable. A student whose February script shows the same error ranking as their November script has not been doing the work between them, and that is a conversation about practice rather than about hours. A student whose ranking has changed - method fixed, timing now the main loss - is on track, even if the score has barely moved.

Ramadan is the other calendar feature that reshapes this. The school day shortens, routines move, and a 5pm session that worked in January becomes the worst slot available. Sessions shift to a post-Iftar window, lengths shorten slightly, and the fortnight either side of Eid is treated as consolidation rather than new work. Because lessons are delivered over video, moving a slot costs nothing beyond a message.

sections.heading: What coaching never includes
paragraphs: A coaching relationship that touches assessed work has a boundary, and it is not a soft one. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has produced and point at where a criterion is not met, and set more practice. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final state, or develop an investigation on the student's behalf.

The Gulf market makes this worth stating plainly. One site in this search landscape sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is malpractice, it is detectable, and the penalty falls on the student rather than the seller. A coaching service worth its fee will refuse that request and explain why, and will be more useful than the one that does not, because the skills it builds transfer to the examination where no help is available.

There are three other things we do not do. We do not promise grades or grade improvements, because no honest tutor can - a coach can remove avoidable losses and cannot control a boundary. We do not publish satisfaction statistics or star ratings we cannot evidence with real, countable, attributable data. And we do not claim approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram holds none of those and operates no premises in the UAE.

What we will do is tell you when coaching is the wrong purchase. If a diagnostic shows genuine content gaps across half a syllabus eight weeks before a series, more technique sessions will not fix it and someone should say so. Sometimes the right advice is to narrow the subject set with the school, plan for a later series, or spend the money on nothing at all.
bullets: Criteria explained, method rehearsed, feedback given on the student's own work
No text supplied for submission and no investigation developed on their behalf
No grade promises, no unevidenced statistics, no regulatory claims
A straight answer when coaching is not the right purchase

sections.heading: Starting: bring a marked paper
paragraphs: The most useful thing a Dubai parent can bring to a first conversation is the most recent marked mock script, with the mark scheme if the school released it. Second best is the exam entry statement with each subject's board, code and tier. With either of those, a coaching plan can be built in one session. With neither, the first two sessions go on discovery.

The free trial lesson is the right place to test whether a coach is specification-literate. Ask them what the papers are worth on that code, which command terms carry the most marks in that subject, and where candidates typically lose time on the particular paper your child sits. Specifics come back from someone who has coached that paper. Generalities come back from someone who knows the subject, and generalities are what the mark scheme declines to reward.

Expect a direct answer about availability. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English, Business Studies, Economics and Geography are well covered at both tiers and on both boards. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics and the less commonly entered languages are thin, and in those cases the honest options are a wait, a different pattern, or a recommendation to look elsewhere.

On format, to leave no room for doubt: sessions are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no coaching centre in Dubai and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE - in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For error-pattern work the screen is genuinely the better room: the script, the scheme, the timer and the annotation sit in one frame, and the whole record is saved with the date on it.
bullets: Bring the most recent marked mock, or the exam entry statement
Test the trial for paper-specific knowledge

process.title: Send the script
process.description: The most recent marked mock paper, with the mark scheme if the school released it, plus the subject's board, code and tier. One marked script tells a coach more than an hour of conversation, because it contains the behaviour rather than a description of it.

process.title: Timed diagnostic
process.description: Thirty minutes of real past-paper work under a visible clock during the free trial lesson, with no teaching and no prompting. This establishes the baseline and, more importantly, shows how the student behaves when the clock is running rather than how they behave when helped.

process.title: Four-pass marking and ranking
process.description: The raw mark taken strictly to the scheme, every lost mark labelled by cause, the causes grouped and counted, and one target selected. The output is a ranked written diagnosis, which is the document the whole plan is built from.

process.title: Drill the biggest-loss cause
process.description: Short, frequent sessions on one labelled cause at a time, with three same-type questions set between sessions. A pattern is declared fixed only when it survives a timed question, not when the student can do it slowly with help.

process.description: A second timed paper, marked the same way, placed beside the first. If the ranking has changed the plan is working even when the score has barely moved; if the ranking is identical, the conversation is about practice between sessions rather than about buying more hours.

process.title: Mock post-mortem and final-run plan
process.description: After each school mock, a full post-mortem produces a revised ranking and a timing plan for the series. From January the emphasis moves almost entirely to timed-condition work and question-order strategy.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session measures rather than teaches. A score is converted into a ranked list of causes, so the money goes to the largest loss instead of the most obvious topic.

whyPoints.title: Drills, not explanations
whyPoints.description: A habit that survives exam pressure needs repetition, not insight. Sessions are short and frequent by design, with practice set between them and a rule that nothing counts as fixed until it holds under a clock.

whyPoints.title: The boards' own vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Command terms, mark tariffs and practical-method language are taught in the wording Cambridge and Pearson publish, and those documents are linked rather than redistributed.

whyPoints.title: Mocks used as data
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools produce two full marked scripts a year in November and February. Both get a proper post-mortem, which is where most of the diagnostic value in the whole course sits.

whyPoints.title: An error log a parent can read
whyPoints.description: What was lost, to what cause, how many marks, and whether it recurred. Two minutes of reading tells you what an hour bought, which is more than any progress report will.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the ceiling
whyPoints.description: Coaching removes avoidable losses. It cannot move a grade boundary, change an entry tier or replace a missing half-syllabus, and we will say so rather than sell sessions into a problem they cannot solve.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE coaching and ordinary subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tutoring generally teaches content the student has not mastered. Coaching works on how the student converts what they know into marks: method lines written down, command terms read correctly, units recorded, time budgeted across the paper. The two are different purchases and they suit different problems. A student who cannot do the topic needs teaching. A student who can do the topic in conversation and still drops twelve marks a paper needs coaching, and buying the wrong one of these is the most common and most expensive mistake families make.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Dubai IGCSE candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: 'Explain' and 'describe' confused with each other, which costs two to four marks on most science papers. 'Suggest', which asks for principle applied to an unfamiliar context and usually receives a recalled textbook fact. 'Compare', which requires explicitly linked statements and usually receives two separate descriptions. And 'evaluate' or 'discuss', which carry the biggest tariffs and are regularly answered with one side argued well and no judgement at the end. Both Cambridge and Pearson publish their own command-term guidance in the syllabus documents, and those are the versions to work from.

faqs.question: My child understands the topic but still drops marks - what is actually going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of four things, and a marked script will tell you which. Method not written down, which discards marks the scheme awarded explicitly for working. Command terms read as synonyms, so the answer addresses a question that was not asked. Units and significant figures. Or time, with marks left uncollected in the final section because earlier questions were over-answered. Add them up on a real script and they commonly total eight to fourteen marks, which is one or two grades on most scales. None of them responds to more content revision.

faqs.question: How do I read a mock paper myself to work out what to fix first?
faqs.answer: Go through it four times. First, confirm the raw mark against the scheme without being generous. Second, write a label next to every lost mark: recall, method, arithmetic, command term, units or time. Third, count the labels and rank them. Fourth, pick the one at the top of that list and find three more questions of the same type. That converts a score into a plan, and it is the single most useful hour a Dubai parent can spend on an IGCSE year. If the top cause is recall in one named topic, that is a teaching problem; otherwise it is technique.

faqs.question: Why does my child run out of time on papers they can otherwise do?
faqs.answer: Because they are overspending early on questions they already know, which feels like working hard. Every paper has an implied rate: total marks divided by minutes available, less five for reading and checking. That is usually somewhere around 0.7 to 1 mark per minute depending on the paper. Compare it with where the time actually went in the last mock and the overspend is usually concentrated in two or three questions. The fixes are a hard move-on rule, a considered question order, and a checking allocation that is genuinely protected rather than theoretically reserved.

faqs.question: What does the Alternative to Practical paper actually test?
faqs.answer: Experimental method in writing. Naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables and how each is controlled. Stating the instrument and its precision rather than the action. Including a repeat and a mean. Identifying an anomalous result and saying what you would do about it. Proposing an improvement that is a named change rather than 'be more careful'. The graph questions carry separate marks for scale, axes, plotting accuracy and the line of best fit. All of this is a writing skill, which is why it coaches well over video and why it is rarely taught explicitly in class.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grade boundaries move between series, and should we plan around them?
faqs.answer: They move, because boundaries are set after each examination to account for that paper's difficulty. Boards publish the tables after each series and those published versions are the only reliable reference. The practical implication is to plan to a raw mark with margin rather than to a historical boundary, and to treat anything within three or four marks of a boundary as genuinely uncertain. That margin is exactly where technique work pays most: three marks is one unwritten method line plus one missing unit, which is a fortnight of drilling rather than a term of revision.

faqs.question: How many sessions does one weak IGCSE topic usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: A genuine content gap in a single topic is commonly three to five sessions, with practice between them, assuming the underlying skills are in place. A technique habit takes longer in weeks but less time in hours: two or three weeks of short, frequent drilling, because the point is repetition rather than explanation. The slow case is a topic that depends on a missing earlier skill - mole calculations resting on weak ratio work, for instance - where the fix has to go back a level first. A diagnostic distinguishes these in one session.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start coaching eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: For technique work, no - eight weeks is enough to remove most avoidable losses, and that is often worth a grade. For a half-learned syllabus, it is too late and an honest coach should say so rather than sell into it. The practical plan at eight weeks is narrow: diagnose from the most recent mock, pick the two largest error causes, drill those, and run weekly timed papers with a strict post-mortem. New content is added only where a diagnostic shows a specific named gap that appears reliably on the paper.

faqs.question: Should my child practise past papers untimed or under exam conditions?
faqs.answer: Both, in the right order. Untimed practice is for learning a method and should be used while a habit is still being installed - there is no point rushing something that is not yet automatic. Timed practice is for proving the habit survives pressure, and it is the only way to see timing behaviour at all. Most students do neither properly: they do papers at a vague pace with the answers nearby. A visible clock, no phone, no lookups and a hard stop is the condition that makes the result mean anything.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is the subject or the exam technique?
faqs.answer: Ask your child to explain a question they got wrong, verbally, without writing. If they can explain it correctly, the knowledge is there and the loss was technique - method, command term, units or time. If they cannot, it is content. Do this across six or eight wrong answers on a mock and the split becomes obvious, usually within fifteen minutes. The reason it matters is cost: a term of topic revision bought for a timing problem is wasted money at the AED 150 to 300 an hour that providers in this market publish for qualified online tutors.

faqs.question: Can coaching compensate for an IGCSE subject my child's school is teaching weakly?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is worth being realistic about the limits. Coaching can cover syllabus content, teach the paper and build technique, and that handles most of what a weak teaching year costs. What it cannot replace is laboratory time, coursework supervision where a component requires it, or the internal assessment decisions the school makes. If a department has changed hands mid-course - which happens, including in schools with strong overall inspection outcomes - read the subject-level judgements in the school's inspection report rather than the headline band before deciding how much outside support to buy.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram run IGCSE coaching classes at a centre in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no centre, office or branch in the UAE, and does not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Coaching is delivered as live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. For this kind of work the screen is arguably the better room: the script, the mark scheme, a visible timer and the annotation all sit in one frame, the whole thing is saved with a date, and a second diagnostic six weeks later can be compared directly with the first.

faqs.question: How should coaching change during the Dubai mock season?
faqs.answer: Light before, heavy after. Before a mock, confirm the timing plan and the question-order strategy and resist cramming new content, which displaces sleep and rarely appears on the paper. After it, run the full post-mortem: every lost mark labelled, the causes counted and ranked, and the next eight weeks rewritten from that ranking. Dubai schools commonly mock in November and again in late February, which gives two genuine diagnostics in a useful order. A February script showing the same ranking as November means practice between sessions is not happening.

faqs.question: What will a coach refuse to do with my child's assessed IGCSE work?
faqs.answer: Supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, or develop an investigation on the student's behalf. What a coach may do is explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has already produced, point at where a criterion is not yet met and set further practice. One site in this search landscape sells completed assessed work outright; that is malpractice and the penalty falls on the student. A coach who cannot say which side of that line a request falls on has answered the question.

dubai/igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the syllabus
dubai/igcse-coaching.closingBody: IGCSE coaching in Dubai earns its fee when it finds the marks a student is already entitled to and is losing to habit. That begins with one marked paper, four passes of honest marking and a ranked list of causes - not with a tour of the syllabus. Send the most recent mock script and the subject's board, code and tier, take the free trial lesson, and ask the coach to name where candidates lose time on that specific paper. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in short frequent blocks built around your child's school week.

intro.heading: A crash course is a dated block of hours, not a rescue service
paragraphs: Most families searching for an IGCSE crash course in Dubai are between eight and sixteen weeks from a paper. The school has already submitted entries, the mock results have come back, and one or two subjects are sitting a grade or two below where the predicted grades need them. What is wanted is not a year of weekly tuition. It is a finite number of hours, pointed at a specific component, with a visible end date.

That is a reasonable thing to buy, and it is a different product from weekly support. A crash course has a fixed count of hours, a named target component, and a plan that runs out on the day of the paper. It works when the syllabus has largely been taught and the marks are being lost in technique, timing, command-term reading and topic gaps that can be closed one at a time. It does not work as a substitute for two years of teaching that never happened. Being honest about which of those two situations you are in is the single most useful thing a parent can do before paying for a block.

The reason it has to be dated is that IGCSE entry deadlines sit months ahead of the exam itself. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, plus a March series available in some regions, and each series has its own entry cut-off. For the March 2027 series Cambridge publishes final entries due 27 November 2026, an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results released on Direct on 13 May. A block of hours bought in January cannot change a tier decision locked in November. It can still change a grade.

Dubai makes this more acute than most markets, because the private-school sector here is unusually large and unusually British. KHDA reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools for 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. That means a very large cohort sitting IGCSE in a compressed window, in schools whose own revision clinics are necessarily group-sized, and a tutoring market that reprices itself every January. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places.

This page is built around the level in the URL rather than around a sales pitch. It sets out what IGCSE actually assesses, component by component, with the syllabus codes Dubai schools use. It names where marks are genuinely lost, which is rarely where parents assume. It counts the block backwards from the paper. It publishes the AED bands the Dubai market charges, attributed. And it says plainly what a tutor may and may not touch on work that has to be the student's own. Lessons are delivered one-to-one online; IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, because home visiting is a service offered only in India.

dubai/igcse-crash-course.programmesIntro: An IGCSE crash course in Dubai is usually bought at one of four points in a child's school career, and the right block looks different at each. Below are the four stages, what each actually assesses, and what Dubai schools in particular do with them.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two or three years before IGCSE begins, ending in Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Checkpoint is not a public qualification and carries no certificate value, but Dubai schools use it to set IGCSE groups and to decide who is steered towards Core and who towards Extended. A block of hours here is about closing arithmetic, algebraic fluency and written-answer structure before the stakes rise.
programmes.countryNote: Several large Dubai British schools set IGCSE sets at the end of Year 9 and review them only once. Families who intervene in Year 9 are buying a tier, which is worth more than the same hours bought in Year 11. A Checkpoint-stage block in Dubai is also where Arabic as an additional language usually appears as a competing demand on the week, because KHDA requires it alongside the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: Core papers cap the available grade, usually at C or grade 4 depending on the subject and board. The content is narrower, the questions are more structured, and marks are lost mostly on recall and on reading the command term. A crash course on Core is about converting near-misses into secure marks: unit conversion, graph reading, data extraction, and writing exactly as much as the mark allocation asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Core matters in Dubai for a specific reason. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. A Core grade can satisfy that threshold. Parents who assume Core closes every door are often wrong about the equivalency arithmetic, and that is worth checking before paying for a tier change.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended papers carry the full grade range to A* or grade 9 and add topics the Core papers never reach: in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 that includes functions, vectors and more demanding trigonometry; in Physics 0625 it adds the harder electricity, waves and nuclear content. Marks are lost on multi-step problems where a single early slip removes every follow-on mark, and on questions that ask for explanation rather than calculation.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the default in most Dubai British-curriculum schools, and it is where crash courses are most often bought. A Dubai cohort frequently sits eight to ten subjects, which compresses revision time per subject far below what a UK cohort taking nine spreads it across. That is the real argument for spending a block on one or two subjects rather than thinly across all of them.

programmes.name: What IGCSE feeds into at 16
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide sixth-form entry in Dubai, and the two routes diverge sharply. International A Level typically asks for a grade 6 or 7 in the subject to be continued; IB Diploma asks for breadth across six groups plus a maths route choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. A crash course in Year 11 is often really about keeping a route open rather than about the certificate itself.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools split hard at 16. Some run only A Level, some only IB, a few both. The 2026-27 intake adds four UK-curriculum and three IB schools, which widens the choice but does not soften the entry grades. Before buying a block, it is worth asking the school which specific IGCSE grade gates the sixth-form course your child wants, because the answer is often one subject rather than an average.

dubai/igcse-crash-course.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often buy a crash course for, with the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel code and the component where the marks usually go. Codes matter because the same subject name covers two different papers across the two boards.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers on each tier, non-calculator and calculator on Edexcel, both calculator-permitted on Cambridge 0580. Marks are lost on multi-step algebra where an early error removes follow-through, on bearings and vectors, and on failing to show method where method carries the marks. A block here is mostly timed past-paper work with every lost mark categorised.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the single most reliable source of lost marks: series and parallel reasoning, potential dividers, and power calculations under time pressure. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards a specific style of answer about variables, repeats and sources of error. Extended adds nuclear and the harder wave content. Sessions drill the answer shape, not just the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative-analysis tables are where grades move. Students who can describe a reaction often cannot write it with state symbols and correct charges, and that gap costs marks on every paper. Organic chemistry at Extended rewards pattern recognition across homologous series rather than memorisation of individual reactions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Marks are lost on long-answer questions where the mark scheme wants three distinct points and the student writes one point three times. Genetics, transport in plants and homeostasis repay structured diagram work. A block usually becomes a sequence of mark-scheme comparisons on the student's own written answers.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise lifting plus explanation, and directed-writing tasks reward audience and register more than vocabulary. The commonest loss is writing a good essay that does not answer the question asked. Sessions work on annotation speed, planning in under five minutes, and the difference between summarising and analysing a passage.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A large share of Dubai candidates sit ESL rather than First Language, and the two are marked on different criteria. Marks are lost on exercise-three note-taking, where answers must be lifted accurately, and on the summary task's word limit. Speaking is assessed separately and rewards extended responses rather than correct but short ones.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most students draw them without labelling axes or shifting the right curve. Evaluation questions ask for a judgement with a reason, not a list of both sides. A crash course here is largely about diagram discipline and about recognising which of four or five standard analytical frames the question is asking for.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward applying theory to the specific business in the stem. Generic answers that would fit any company score in the lowest band however well written. Calculation questions on break-even, cash flow and ratios are reliable marks that students skip under time pressure. Sessions rehearse applied phrasing and the order in which to attack the paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation, networks and security is memorisable and under-revised. Paper 2 algorithms and pseudocode require writing, tracing and correcting code by hand, which students who code on a screen find unexpectedly hard. Trace tables and dry runs are the exercises that move the grade fastest.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606 / 0580 extension)
subjects.description: Taken by Dubai students heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Calculus, functions and harder trigonometry appear early, and the paper assumes algebraic fluency that Year 11 has not finished building. A block here is usually bought to protect a sixth-form place rather than to lift a certificate grade.

dubai/igcse-crash-course.regionsIntro: Dubai is wide, and the practical question is rarely distance. It is what time a session can realistically start once school transport, Arabic and Islamic Education lessons, and the drive home are accounted for. Online delivery removes the tutor's travel from that calculation entirely; here is what the week usually looks like by community.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Dense with long-established British schools and short school runs, so a 16:30 or 17:00 start is realistic on most weekdays. Families here often want a single subject block rather than a full timetable rebuild.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Apartment living with little quiet study space and a long inbound commute for a visiting tutor. A video session at 18:00 avoids the Sheikh Zayed Road problem altogether and is why most Marina blocks run on weekday evenings.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Villa communities with a long school bus ride at both ends of the day. Students are often home only after 16:00, which pushes sessions to 17:30 or later and makes Saturday morning blocks popular in the final six weeks.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A mixed school catchment with several Indian and British-curriculum schools close together. Sibling bookings are common, and the usual pattern is two different subjects back to back in one evening rather than a shared session.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Fast-growing catchment where new intakes mean large IGCSE sets. Parents here most often ask for help with one component rather than a subject, which suits a short, tightly scoped block.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several universities, so students here are frequently thinking about A Level and IB entry grades at the same time as the IGCSE paper. Blocks often include a route conversation about Mathematics 0606.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Younger families and a high turnover of school registrations, which means mid-year arrivals joining an IGCSE course already half-taught. A diagnostic matters more here than anywhere, because the gap is content rather than technique.

regions.name: Deira, Oud Metha and Bur Dubai
regions.note: The older school districts, with large cohorts and group revision widely available through the school itself. The honest advice here is often to use the school clinic for breadth and buy one-to-one hours only for the single weakest component.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai: Jumeirah, Al Barsha and the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of UK-curriculum IGCSE entries in the emirate. Sets are large, mock timetables are compressed into a fortnight, and most schools publish predicted grades shortly after. Students we support sit Cambridge and Edexcel papers side by side across this cluster, sometimes within the same family.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and inland Dubai: Mirdif, Festival City, Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: A broader curriculum mix, with British-curriculum schools sitting alongside Indian and IB schools in the same catchment. Transport times are longer, which is why evening and weekend sessions dominate here, and why a block built around two fixed weekly slots tends to survive the term better than a flexible one.

dubai/igcse-crash-course.modesIntro: There are three shapes a crash course can take, and the right one depends almost entirely on how many weeks are left and whether the syllabus has been taught. All three run one-to-one over live video, with the same tutor throughout the block.

modes.title: The sixteen-week block
modes.description: Two sessions a week from roughly mid-January to the June series, or from September to the November series. There is enough time here to re-teach content as well as drill technique, which makes it the only shape that reliably fixes a syllabus gap rather than an exam-skill gap. It is also the version where a mid-block review can change the plan without losing the target.

modes.title: The six-week component sprint
modes.description: Three or four sessions a week aimed at one named paper, usually the one the mock exposed. No attempt is made to cover the whole syllabus. The session sequence is set by the mark categories from the marked script: every lost mark is sorted into recall, method, command term or timing, and the block spends its hours in proportion to what that count shows.

modes.title: The half-term intensive
modes.description: A concentrated run of daily or near-daily sessions through a school break, often the February or spring half term, or the weeks after the mock results land. It works because nothing else is competing for the day, and it fails when it is used to replace term-time work rather than to consolidate it. Pacing matters: three focused hours beat six unfocused ones.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE crash course actually buys you
paragraphs: An IGCSE crash course in Dubai buys a fixed number of one-to-one hours, aimed at one or two named components, between now and a paper date that is already fixed. That is the whole product. It is not a shorter version of a two-year course, and anyone selling it as one is selling something that cannot be delivered. What it changes is the conversion rate between what a student knows and what a marker can award.

That distinction decides whether a block is worth buying. Look at the mock script rather than the mock grade. If the answers show the content is there but arrive unfinished, mis-read or unstructured, a block of hours is a genuinely efficient purchase, because exam technique responds quickly to one-to-one correction. If whole topics are blank, the honest answer is that eight weeks of tuition will lift the grade by less than a parent is hoping and the money is better spent on a longer, cheaper weekly arrangement, or on a tier conversation with the school.

There is a second thing a block buys, which parents rarely ask for and usually value most afterwards: an accurate picture. A marked diagnostic with every lost mark categorised tells you whether the predicted grade is optimistic or pessimistic, and which subject is actually the weakest. Dubai students commonly sit eight to ten IGCSE subjects. Knowing which two deserve the hours is worth more than spreading the same budget across all ten and moving none of them.

What it cannot buy is a changed tier, a changed board, a later entry, or any influence over the paper. Those are school and board decisions with their own deadlines, and a tutor who implies otherwise should be treated with suspicion. The useful version of the service is narrower and more honest than the marketing in this market usually suggests.

sections.heading: What each IGCSE paper actually assesses, by code
paragraphs: The single most useful thing to establish before a crash course starts is which syllabus code your child is entered for. Dubai schools run Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel side by side, sometimes in the same building, and the same subject name hides genuinely different papers. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 cover similar content but differ in calculator rules, paper structure and the way grades are reported. A tutor preparing the wrong one wastes the block.

Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a UAE family that is not a trivia point: it means the date a tutor plans backwards from must come from the school's own statement of entry, not from a timetable found online.

The table below sets out the components Dubai families most often buy help with, with the code, the paper pattern and where the marks reliably go. Every row comes from the current public syllabus structure for that code. It is deliberately specific about component names, because asking a tutor which paper number they are preparing is the fastest way to find out whether they know the syllabus or only the subject.

One more practical note. Science candidates in most Dubai schools sit the alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory exam. That paper tests the language of experimental method, not laboratory skill, and it is the component most often under-prepared because it looks like the easy one. It rewards precise answers about independent and dependent variables, controls, repeats and specific sources of error, in the phrasing the mark scheme expects.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost in a Dubai cohort
paragraphs: Across marked scripts, lost marks fall into four categories, and the proportions are consistent enough to plan around. Recall gaps, where the content was never secure. Method gaps, where the student knows what to do but writes too little for the marker to award the steps. Command-term failures, where a question asking for an explanation receives a description, or a question asking for a calculation receives a sentence. And timing, where the final questions are blank or rushed. Only the first of those four needs re-teaching.

In a Dubai cohort there is a fifth pressure that is specific to the market. Students here commonly sit more subjects than their UK counterparts, and they do so alongside KHDA's mandatory subjects, which apply in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies occupy real timetable space. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least twenty-five minutes. Those lessons are not optional and they are not the place to find revision time.

What that means in practice is that the week is already full before any tutoring is added. A crash course that adds four hours without removing anything tends to collapse by week three. The version that survives is the one that names what is being dropped: a club, a second sport, or the low-value habit of re-reading notes. Re-reading feels productive and produces almost no retrieval, which is why an error log built from the student's own marked work is the more useful artefact to carry through a block.

The diagnostic is what makes this concrete. One marked paper, every lost mark tagged with one of the four categories, produces a count. If two thirds of the losses are method and command term, the block is technique work and six weeks is plenty. If half are recall, the block needs to be longer or narrower. That count, not a conversation about confidence, is what a plan should be built from.

sections.heading: The block counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: A crash course should be planned from the exam date outwards, not from today forwards. The reason is that the dates that constrain you are not the exam itself but the ones before it: the entry deadline, the forecast-grade deadline, the mock window and the school's internal coursework dates. Several of those have already passed by the time most families start looking, and a plan that ignores them promises things it cannot deliver.

Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series make the shape of this clear. Final entries are due 27 November 2026, three months before the exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, which is during the exam period itself. Results reach centres on Direct on 13 May, with certificates following in late June. The gap between entry and exam is the window in which a crash course can do anything at all, and it opens before most parents have seen a mock result.

Pearson Edexcel sits on a different rhythm. International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any date you plan around should be read off the live official timetable rather than a copy of one.

Build the plan backwards in four moves. Fix the paper date from the statement of entry. Count back two weeks and mark that as the point where new content stops and only past papers run. Count back six weeks and mark the mid-block review. Then place the sessions. What is left is an honest number of hours, which is usually smaller than the number a family imagined they had.

sections.heading: What a crash course costs in Dubai, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai parents do not transact in. The bands below are market rates read from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. Our own pricing follows a free trial lesson and a marked diagnostic, because quoting a block before reading a script is guesswork.

The number that moves most between January and June is the specialist band. Demand for IGCSE help in Dubai concentrates in the eight weeks before the June series, and tutors with genuine subject depth are booked out first. A family starting in April is choosing from a smaller pool at a higher rate than the same family starting in January, which is the strongest practical argument for booking early rather than any claim about outcomes.

Watch the per-hour comparison carefully. A monthly package of AED 799 for eight online sessions looks cheaper per hour than a specialist rate until you check the session length and whether the tutor is a subject specialist or a generalist. In-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions carry the tutor's travel inside the price. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Two costs sit outside the tutoring line and are worth budgeting for. Private-candidate entry fees, if your child is sitting outside a school, are paid to the centre and vary by subject count. And the opportunity cost of the wrong block: six weeks of hours spent on the wrong subject is not recoverable in a year with a fixed exam date. That is the real argument for paying for a diagnostic first.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against a Dubai revision centre
paragraphs: The alternative most Dubai families weigh against a one-to-one block is a group revision course at a centre, often in Al Barsha, Karama or Deira, sold as a fixed number of hours per subject. The headline price per hour is lower. Whether it is better value depends on one variable: how far your child's weak component is from the median weak component of the group.

In a group of twelve, the course has to teach to the middle. If your child's problem is the same as most of the room, that is efficient and the lower rate is real value. If the problem is specific, which it usually is once you have read a marked script, a large share of the paid hours is spent on topics that were not the issue. The arithmetic flips quickly: eight group hours at a low rate that address one relevant topic cost more per useful hour than three one-to-one hours that address three.

There is also the Dubai travel reality. A centre session means two journeys, often across Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst time of day, which turns a two-hour class into a three-and-a-half-hour commitment for the family. Online delivery removes that entirely. It also removes the geographic constraint on the tutor: a student in Arabian Ranches is not limited to tutors willing to drive to Arabian Ranches at 17:00, which is what actually restricts subject specialism in this market.

To be fair to the group option, it has two genuine advantages. Peer pace keeps some students working who would not work alone, and the published hour count makes budgeting simple. The combination many families land on is sensible: the school's own revision clinic or a centre course for breadth, and a short one-to-one block for the single component the diagnostic identified. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, so the comparison here is between group delivery and one-to-one online rather than between online and a tutor at the door.

sections.heading: Five subjects at E or 3: how equivalency changes which hours matter
paragraphs: Which subject should get the block is often answered badly, because parents and students pick the subject that feels worst rather than the one that carries the most consequence. Ministry of Education equivalency gives you a structural reason to choose differently, and almost nobody in this market explains it.

For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the IGCSE count. One page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the five-subject rule is what the sourced reporting says.

That reframes the triage. If your child is sitting nine subjects and is secure in six, the subject at risk of falling below grade 3 matters more to the equivalency file than the subject sitting at grade 5 and hoping for a 7, even though the second one feels more urgent in the house. If the sixth-form place depends on a specific grade in a specific subject, that subject takes priority instead. Either way the decision should be made against a written requirement, not a feeling.

For the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the sourced reporting, so no IB equivalency figure is published here. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not by a tutor; verify your own case through the official channel, and treat any provider that offers to manage it for you with caution.

sections.heading: What a crash-course tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more on IGCSE than parents expect, because several subjects carry components that must be the student's own work, and because the market contains providers selling exactly the thing that gets a candidate disqualified. One provider found in this SERP sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

The boundary is straightforward to state. A tutor may teach content, explain a mark scheme, model a technique on a different question, ask questions about a draft, point at a paragraph and say that the argument does not follow, and mark the student's own practice under timed conditions. A tutor may not supply text that ends up in the submission, nor produce the work on the student's behalf under any framing, however it is packaged. If a provider's offer is that something arrives finished, that is the line being crossed.

Related to this: a tutor should not be handing over syllabus documents, past-paper bundles, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing them is copyright infringement. Current material is available through the boards' own sites and through the school, and that is where a tutor should point you. Referencing and linking is fine; redistributing is not.

One more boundary that is specific to the UAE. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is Abu Dhabi policy as reported in the press rather than Dubai regulation, but the principle is worth applying anywhere: your child's own classroom teacher is not the right person to pay privately.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to run private sessions in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and the regulation is more specific than most providers admit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so no amount is quoted here.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, beginning with initial approval, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. This is why the phrase describing tutors as holding regulator approval should be read sceptically: the permit in question belongs to institutes with premises, and IB Gram does not hold it or claim it.

What to do with this as a parent is simple. Ask any individual tutor, including ours, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and to show it. Ask a centre which authority licenses it and for the permit reference. Both are reasonable questions with checkable answers, and the willingness to answer them tells you most of what you need to know about who you are dealing with.

process.title: Send the marked script, not the grade
process.description: The useful starting point is a photograph of the most recent marked mock, plus the statement of entry showing board, tier and paper numbers. From those two documents a tutor can tell you whether a block will move the grade and roughly how many hours it needs. A conversation about confidence cannot do that.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the block
process.description: The trial is with the specific tutor, not a sales call, and it runs on a real past-paper question so you can see how a correction is actually made. If the match is wrong, say so afterwards and we change the tutor rather than the price. Nothing is committed at this stage.

process.title: Diagnostic paper marked and categorised
process.description: Your child sits one full past paper under timed conditions. Every lost mark is tagged as recall, method, command term or timing, and the counts are shared with you. That table decides the length of the block and which component gets the hours; it is also the baseline the mid-block review compares against.

process.title: The block is scheduled around the real week
process.description: Sessions are fixed to the same slots each week in Gulf Standard Time, set around school transport, Arabic and Islamic Education lessons, and whatever else already occupies the evening. Fixed slots survive a term better than flexible ones. During Ramadan sessions typically move to a post-Iftar or late-morning time for the whole block.

process.title: Mid-block review and a written reallocation
process.description: At roughly the halfway point the error log is compared against the original diagnostic. Where a category has closed, those hours move elsewhere; where one has not moved, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing. You receive this in writing, including the honest version if the block is not working.

whyPoints.title: Codes and paper numbers, not subject names
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the syllabus code and component your child is actually entered for, because Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are different papers with different rules. A tutor who cannot say which paper number they are preparing is preparing a subject rather than an exam, and that difference shows up in the marks.

whyPoints.title: A diagnostic before a quote
whyPoints.description: Blocks are quoted after a marked paper, not from a phone call. That is slower to buy and it occasionally means telling a family that a block is not the right purchase. It is also the only way to know whether the hours will be spent on technique, which moves fast, or content, which does not.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from your statement of entry
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates centres to one of six timetable zones and says explicitly that the correct zone version must be used. We plan from the dates on your child's own statement of entry rather than from a published timetable that may belong to another zone or series.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Sessions are delivered live over video, one student and one tutor, at Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, and that is written on every page rather than discovered at booking. Removing the commute is also what lets a Dubai family reach a genuine subject specialist.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page carry the provider or source that publishes them and the date they were read. We do not present market figures as our own pricing, and we do not publish satisfaction percentages or star ratings we cannot evidence with countable, dated reviews.

whyPoints.title: The boundary on assessed work is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, models and marks. No text produced by a tutor reaches a submission, on any component, on any board. This market contains providers selling finished coursework, and being specific about where the line sits is more useful to a parent than a reassuring phrase.

faqs.question: How many hours should an IGCSE crash course in Dubai actually run for?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of the four mark-loss categories dominates. If the marked script shows mostly method, command-term and timing losses, twelve to eighteen one-to-one hours across six weeks will usually move a grade, because exam technique responds quickly to correction. If recall losses dominate, meaning whole topics are missing, the same eighteen hours will move much less, and a longer weekly arrangement at a lower hourly rate is the better purchase. The honest sequence is to mark one paper, count the categories, then decide the hours. Deciding the hours first and discovering the category later is how families end up buying a second block.

faqs.question: My child's mock came back two grades below the predicted grade. Is a block still worth it?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but for a different reason than parents expect. A two-grade gap between mock and prediction usually means the prediction was built on classwork rather than timed performance, and timed performance is exactly what a block improves. Look at the script: if the answers show knowledge arriving late, unfinished or in the wrong form, that gap closes faster than it looks. If the paper has blank topics, the prediction was optimistic and the realistic target is one grade, not two. Either way, ask for the diagnostic to be marked before agreeing a number of hours, and ask what the tutor expects to be achievable.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code is my child entered for, and why does it change the plan?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, and it matters because the same subject name covers different papers. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 differ in paper structure and calculator rules. Cambridge Physics 0625 includes an alternative-to-practical paper with its own answer conventions. A tutor preparing the generic subject rather than the specific code will drill content that is correct but mis-aimed, and the alternative-to-practical paper in particular is the component most often left unprepared because it looks straightforward. Send the statement of entry before the first session.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting four weeks before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Four weeks can still change marks, but only on technique, and only if you are ruthless about scope. At that distance nothing new should be taught. The block becomes timed papers, marked against the scheme, with every loss logged and the next session targeting the largest category. Realistically that is one grade on one subject rather than improvement across a timetable. The common mistake at four weeks is spreading hours across three subjects, which moves none of them. Pick the component with the clearest technique gap, spend the hours there, and leave the rest to the school's own revision programme.

faqs.question: What do Dubai providers actually charge per hour for IGCSE help?
faqs.answer: Published rates across the Dubai market run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget or university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE or A Level specialist. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those figures come from provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than an IB Gram price list. Our own figure follows the free trial and the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Do rates in Dubai go up the closer we get to the June series?
faqs.answer: The effective rate does, though published rate cards often do not change. What changes is availability: demand concentrates in the eight weeks before the June papers, and tutors with real subject depth fill their timetables first. A family booking in April is choosing from a smaller pool than the same family booking in January, and the specialist band is where that bites. The practical consequence is that booking early buys access to a better match rather than a discount. It is also why a block that starts after the mock results rather than after the Easter break tends to go better.

faqs.question: Can a block of hours change my child from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: No, and this is worth being clear about before money changes hands. Tier is an entry decision made by the school and submitted to the board by a deadline that sits months before the exam. Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, closed final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period starting 3 February. Once that is submitted, the papers your child sits are fixed. What a block can do is raise the grade achieved on the tier entered, which on Core usually means converting near-misses into secure marks. If you want a tier changed, that conversation belongs with the school well before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: How does a crash course fit around Arabic and Islamic Education lessons?
faqs.answer: It has to be built around them, because they are not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. That time is already in the timetable before any tutoring is added. The practical answer is that a block has to replace something rather than sit on top of everything, and the thing most worth dropping is usually unstructured note re-reading. Sessions themselves work best in fixed evening slots that the family has deliberately cleared.

faqs.question: Can crash-course sessions shift to a post-Iftar slot once Ramadan starts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a block running through Ramadan that is usually the better arrangement rather than a concession. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and a 17:00 session that worked in January stops working. Two patterns tend to hold: a late-morning slot on non-school days, or a post-Iftar session roughly ninety minutes after sunset. Either way the move should be made for the whole block rather than week by week, because a fixed slot is what keeps a short block intact. Eid days are planned out in advance and the hours redistributed rather than lost.

faqs.question: Is a group revision course at a Dubai centre better value than one-to-one hours?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the test is specific: how close is your child's weak component to the median weak component in the room? A group course has to teach to the middle. If the problem is shared, the lower rate is real value and the peer pace helps. If the problem is particular, which a marked script usually shows it to be, a large share of the paid hours goes on topics that were not the issue, and the cost per useful hour climbs above one-to-one. Many Dubai families use both: the centre or school clinic for breadth, a short one-to-one block for the one component.

faqs.question: Does my child's school revision clinic make paid hours unnecessary?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth exhausting the free option first. School clinics are teacher-led, cost nothing extra and cover the syllabus again, which is exactly right if the gap is content. What they cannot easily do is work through one student's own marked script line by line and correct the specific habit costing marks, because the group size does not allow it. The sensible sequence is to use the clinic, then look at the next marked paper. If the same category of loss is still there after the clinic, that is the signal that one-to-one hours would add something the clinic cannot.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it and to show it; ask a centre with premises which authority licenses it. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help with the written coursework my child has to submit?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills it needs, explain the assessment criteria, model a technique on a different question, ask questions about a draft and say where an argument does not follow. A tutor cannot supply text that ends up in the submission, and no framing changes that. One provider found in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying that is a malpractice risk for the student, not a shortcut. If a provider's offer is that something arrives finished, that is the line. Ask directly how feedback is given, and expect the answer to involve questions rather than paragraphs.

faqs.question: If we are sitting as a private candidate rather than through a school, does a block work differently?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. First, you own the administration that a school would normally handle: finding a registered exam centre, meeting its entry deadline, and holding your own statement of entry with the correct timetable zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and says the right zone version of the timetable must be used, so that document matters more to a private candidate than to anyone else. Second, there is no school clinic, no mock programme and no predicted grade, so the diagnostic paper is doing more work. Plan for one extra timed paper early in the block.

faqs.question: Which subject should get the hours if we can only afford one block?
faqs.answer: Decide it against a written requirement rather than a feeling. If a sixth-form place depends on a specific grade in a specific subject, that subject wins. If the concern is Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the requirement is five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from those five, so the subject at risk of dropping below that line matters more than the one going from a 5 to a 7. Write the requirement down, check the predicted grades against it, and the choice usually makes itself.

faqs.question: What happens if the block is not working by the third session?
faqs.answer: You should be told, in writing, rather than discovering it at the end. Our mid-block review compares the running error log against the original diagnostic, and if a category has not moved the approach changes rather than the hours being increased. Sometimes the right answer is a different tutor, which we arrange without renegotiating the block. Occasionally the right answer is that the gap is content rather than technique and a short intensive block was the wrong purchase, in which case saying so is more useful than selling another six weeks. Ask at the outset how that conversation would be handled.

dubai/igcse-crash-course.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper, then decide
dubai/igcse-crash-course.closingBody: An IGCSE crash course in Dubai is worth buying when a marked script shows the knowledge is there and the marks are being lost on the way to the page. It is worth skipping when whole topics are blank, and a good tutor will tell you which of the two you are looking at. Send the most recent marked mock and the statement of entry, take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the block, and let the diagnostic set the hours. Sessions run one-to-one over live video at Gulf Standard Time, built backwards from the paper date your child's school has already entered.
