intro.heading: The code on the entry form decides everything else
paragraphs: There is a conversation that happens in the first session of almost every IGCSE booking from Dubai. The tutor asks which board the student sits, and nobody in the room knows. The student says Maths. The parent says Cambridge, because a sibling sat Cambridge four years ago. The entry confirmation, when somebody finds it, says 4MA1, which is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A. The tutor has just spent fifteen minutes preparing the wrong paper structure.

This is not a trivial administrative detail. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover overlapping content in different papers, with different tiering, different calculator rules and different grade scales. Cambridge splits 0580 into a Core tier that cannot award above a C and an Extended tier that runs A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher tiers and reports on a 9 to 1 scale. A student revising from Cambridge past papers for an Edexcel entry will meet question styles they have never practised, and will lose marks for reasons that have nothing to do with their mathematics.

Dubai makes this more likely than most cities, because the private-school market here is unusually mixed. UK-curriculum schools hold 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment across 227 schools, and those schools choose their boards subject by subject. It is entirely normal for one Dubai student to sit Cambridge for the sciences, Pearson Edexcel for Maths and English, and a third board for a language, because each department picked the specification it preferred. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four of them UK curriculum, so the mix is widening rather than settling.

So this page is organised around the assessment rather than around the city. It starts with how to find out which board and tier your child is actually entered for, then works through what each one assesses: the papers, the tier ceilings, the practical arrangement in the sciences, the 9 to 1 scale against A* to G, and the three series a year with their entry deadlines. After that it gets specific about where IGCSE marks go missing, subject by subject, because the pattern differs sharply between Maths, the sciences and the essay subjects.

The last part of the page covers the things that follow the result: the five subjects the UAE Ministry of Education counts for equivalency, the private-candidate route for a student sitting a paper their school does not offer, and the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement that runs alongside the IGCSE timetable in every Dubai private school. Lessons themselves are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai; visiting a student's address is a service we offer only in India.

Three series a year, six timetable zones, and the entry deadline nobody watches
The five subjects the ministry counts, and the two it does not

dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes sit under the word IGCSE in Dubai, and they are not interchangeable. The two main international boards run separate specifications; the stage below feeds into them; and the stage above determines which tier and which subjects a student should have taken in the first place.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes beginning with 0: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a First Language 0500, History 0470, Economics 0455. Most subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Reporting is on the A* to G scale outside the United Kingdom. Examination series run in June and November, with a March series available in some regions.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the board a majority of Dubai British-curriculum schools use for the sciences, and it is also the board whose zone timetabling catches families out. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A Dubai centre's timetable is not the one published for a different zone.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes beginning with 4: Mathematics A 4MA1, Mathematics B 4MB1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1, English Literature 4ET1, Business 4BS1, Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher where it applies, reporting is on the 9 to 1 scale, and practical skills in the sciences are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical examination.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live timetable on their site rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage that feeds the IGCSE entry decision. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which give a diagnostic picture before tiering choices are made. There is no public qualification here and no grade that follows the student, but there is the clearest evidence available of whether a Core or Extended entry is the honest one.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage is where the real decision gets made and then quietly forgotten. A Year 9 student placed on a Core pathway in Mathematics has a grade ceiling of C two years before anybody mentions it, and moving up a tier later in Year 10 is possible but needs the gap closed deliberately. Families who ask about tiering in Year 9 rather than Year 11 have options; families who ask in the spring of Year 11 are usually told the entry is already lodged.

programmes.name: What follows: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The route after IGCSE determines which subjects and tiers matter now. A Level entry requirements are usually expressed as specific IGCSE grades in the subject, often a 6 or a B as a minimum and a 7 or an A for the sciences and Mathematics. IB Diploma Higher Level choices carry similar expectations. A Core-tier entry that caps at C can close a Higher Level or A Level door that the student otherwise had open.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students split at 16 in a way that is specific to this market: most British-curriculum schools here run IGCSE at 16 and then offer A Level, the IB Diploma, or both in the same building. That choice is made in Year 11 while IGCSE examinations are being revised for, which is poor timing. The practical answer is to decide the post-16 route before the IGCSE tier is locked, because the tier constrains the route rather than the other way round.

dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Ten IGCSE subjects Dubai families ask about most, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes, the paper structure and the part that actually loses marks. Where a subject is tiered, the tier matters more than the tutoring: it sets the grade ceiling before any revision begins.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a ceiling of grade C; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and runs A* to E. From the 2025 syllabus one paper in each pair is taken without a calculator, so check the syllabus year on cambridgeinternational.org. Marks are lost to unshown method, premature rounding, and answers given without units.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at their tier, and then either Paper 5 as a practical test or Paper 6 as the alternative to practical. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Lost marks cluster in electricity, graph interpretation and any question using the word explain, which is answered as a description.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the preventable loss. The practical arrangement mirrors Physics: Paper 5 or Paper 6 at Cambridge, written-paper assessment at Pearson. Students who write balanced equations without state symbols, or who skip the units in a concentration calculation, lose marks they had earned.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three sciences and the one where revision style matters most. Rereading notes produces grade 5s. The marks sit in command-term discipline, in naming the structure rather than describing it, and in data questions where a candidate states a trend without quoting the figures from the table in front of them.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Two routes for students not taking three separate sciences. Combined Science gives one grade; Co-ordinated Sciences gives a double award. Content is reduced rather than easier, and the examination still asks for the same technique. Check which one your child is entered for, because past papers for the three separate sciences are the wrong practice material.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition at Cambridge; a reading and writing paper with a coursework option at Pearson. The reliable loss is in reading questions answered from memory of the passage rather than from the passage, and in writing tasks that ignore the stated form, audience and purpose, which carry marks independently of the quality of the prose.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in 0510, a separately reported speaking component. Marks are lost in the short-answer reading section, where candidates copy a whole sentence when one word was wanted, and in the summary task, where answers exceed the word limit or add opinion the mark scheme does not reward.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: Cambridge Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 · Pearson 4EC1 and 4BS1
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the grade in Economics: a correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks that prose cannot recover. In Business, the loss is in application, where a candidate explains a concept in general terms rather than applying it to the named business in the case material, which is where the application and analysis marks sit.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.levels: Cambridge Geography 0460 and History 0470 · Pearson 4GE1 and 4HI1
subjects.description: Both reward structure over content volume. In Geography, case-study specificity and command-term matching decide the mark; vague answers about a named region score in the middle band whatever the knowledge behind them. In History, source questions ask for provenance and purpose, and candidates who summarise the source content score about half of what is available.

subjects.name: Arabic and the KHDA-mandated subjects
subjects.levels: Cambridge Arabic First Language 0508 · Islamiyat 0493 · the KHDA stream
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The content is set by the Ministry of Education and may not be varied by the school. Where a student also sits an IGCSE Arabic or Islamiyat paper, the examination technique is ordinary Cambridge technique.

dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.regionsTitle: Which board the schools near you tend to use
dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Because lessons are delivered over live video, an area changes two things for us and no others: what time a session can realistically start, and which boards the local schools tend to enter their students for. The second is useful information, and nobody else publishes it by community.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Al Safa
regions.note: Long-established British-curriculum schools with mature examination departments, mostly Cambridge for the sciences and mixed for Mathematics. Early finishes make a 4pm session workable here more often than elsewhere.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City and Motor City
regions.note: Newer British schools with smaller Year 11 cohorts, which often means a single teacher per science. Pearson Edexcel entries are more common in these schools than the city average.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment and townhouse communities feeding schools across the southern corridor. Students here frequently commute past two or three other schools, so cohorts are mixed and board questions need checking per subject.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities with established British schools nearby and a high proportion of students continuing into A Level in the same building. Tier decisions in Year 9 and 10 are the live question here, not Year 11 revision.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A dense older-Dubai schooling corridor with a wide curriculum mix, including Indian-curriculum schools alongside British ones. A student moving from CBSE into IGCSE in Year 10 is a common case in this area.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University-adjacent communities served by newer British schools. Evening traffic is lighter than in the central corridor, so later slots are more workable and weekend mornings are less oversubscribed.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Jumeirah Village Triangle
regions.note: Fast-growing family communities where students attend schools in several directions. Many families here moved mid-Key-Stage, which makes a board change part-way through Year 10 more frequent than it should be.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Eastern Dubai, served by a mix of British and IB continuum schools. Students at IB continuum schools here may sit IGCSE at 16 before the Diploma, so the same family can be dealing with two boards and two assessment cultures at once.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Older British-curriculum provision with long-running examination departments. Students here usually arrive with correct content knowledge and a technique problem, which is a short job rather than a long one.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: The most selective concentration in the city, with several schools whose A Level entry requirements set the IGCSE grade a student needs. Tier and grade-ceiling conversations here start early.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Jumeirah Park
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with smaller Year 11 groups. Where one teacher covers a whole science, an outside specialist for the second science changes the most, and board questions need checking subject by subject.

schoolClusters.city: Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: Eastern Dubai, with a mix of British schools and IB continuum schools that still enter students for IGCSE at 16. Families here often deal with two boards across one child's subject list.

dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.modesIntro: Four ways to buy IGCSE preparation, each matched to a different diagnosis rather than to a different budget. The right one depends on whether the gap is content, technique, the practical paper or the tier itself.

modes.title: Paper-specific work against the syllabus code
modes.description: One paper at a time, against the actual specification. A student entered for Cambridge 0620 Extended works Paper 2, Paper 4 and the practical option separately, because the three ask for different things and a general chemistry session helps none of them specifically. This is the default format and the one that produces the clearest week-to-week evidence.

modes.title: Two-board coverage when school and practice material differ
modes.description: The commonest fixable problem in Dubai. A student sits Pearson 4MA1 and has been revising Cambridge 0580 papers, or the reverse. The first job is to establish the correct specification, replace the practice material, and teach the question styles the student has never seen. It takes one session to diagnose and a few weeks to correct.

modes.title: Practical-paper preparation
modes.description: Cambridge science candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Both are examinable skills and both are taught rather than absorbed in a laboratory. Variables, tabulation, uncertainty, graph plotting and the evaluation question are the content, and all of it works over a shared screen.

modes.title: Year 10 groundwork before the Year 11 crunch
modes.description: The cheapest and least popular format. A student working steadily through Year 10 can move tier, close a content gap properly, and reach Year 11 needing technique rather than teaching. Families who book in Year 10 end up buying fewer total hours than families who wait, which is the opposite of what most parents expect.

sections.heading: Find the board and the tier before anything else
paragraphs: IGCSE exam preparation in Dubai starts with two facts: the syllabus code your child is entered for, and the tier. Everything else on this page depends on them. The code is a four-character string on the entry confirmation the school issues, and it looks like 0580, 0625, 4MA1 or 4PH1. A code starting with a zero is Cambridge International; a code starting with a four is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The tier is the word Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher next to it.

If you cannot find the entry confirmation, there are three other routes. The front cover of any past paper the school has issued carries the code. The examinations officer can confirm both the code and the tier in an email, and is used to being asked. And the student's textbook almost always carries the specification on the cover, though this is the least reliable of the three because departments change boards without changing books. Checking takes a few minutes and prevents weeks of revision against the wrong paper.

Why it matters at this level of detail: the boards differ in ways that show up on the paper rather than in the syllabus summary. Cambridge 0580 Extended sits two papers; Pearson 4MA1 Higher sits two papers of different lengths with a different question style and a formula sheet with different contents. Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical paper; Pearson assesses the same skills inside the written papers. The grade scales are different. A student who practises the wrong board's papers for six weeks has rehearsed the wrong examination.

In Dubai this is a live problem rather than a theoretical one, because schools pick boards department by department. The same student can hold a Cambridge code for Chemistry, a Pearson code for Maths and a third for a language. Ask the question once, per subject, in writing, and keep the answer somewhere findable. It is the single highest-value thing a parent can do in the first week of Year 11, and it costs nothing.
bullets: Codes starting with 0 are Cambridge International; codes starting with 4 are Pearson Edexcel
The tier word next to the code sets the grade ceiling
Check the entry confirmation, a past paper cover, or the examinations officer

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: The two boards are not graded on a common scale, do not structure their papers the same way, and do not tier identically. Neither is harder in the abstract; they are differently shaped, and a student suited to one can be poorly served by the other. The table below sets out the pairings Dubai families meet most, with codes, so that a parent can match a child's entry to the right practice material in one reading.

The clearest structural difference is in the sciences. Cambridge requires a practical component, taken either as Paper 5, a timed practical test in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about practical work. The choice is made by the centre, not the student, and it changes the preparation entirely. Pearson's International GCSE sciences assess practical skills within the written papers, so there is no separate practical examination to prepare for but the same skills still appear in the question set.

Mathematics differs in tiering vocabulary and in calculator policy. Cambridge 0580 splits Core and Extended, and from the 2025 syllabus one paper in each pair is sat without a calculator; confirm the syllabus year that applies to your child's cohort on the Cambridge site, because transitional cohorts exist. Pearson 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher and allows a calculator in both papers. A student moving between the two mid-course meets a genuinely different examination, not a relabelled one.

English is where the practical difference is largest for the student. Cambridge 0500 and Pearson 4EA1 both reward reading precision and a controlled register, but the task formats and the mark distribution differ, and Pearson offers a coursework route some centres take. For any of these pairings, the operational instruction is the same: practise the board the entry names, and treat the other board's past papers as unfamiliar material rather than extra revision.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the grade ceiling nobody mentions in Year 11
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in an IGCSE entry and the least discussed. In Cambridge Mathematics 0580, a Core entry sits Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C. An Extended entry sits Papers 2 and 4 and is graded A* to E. In the tiered sciences the pattern repeats: the Core paper pair caps at C, the Extended pair reaches A*. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work on the same principle with the 9 to 1 scale.

That ceiling has consequences past Year 11. A Dubai school's A Level entry requirement for Mathematics is commonly a grade 7 or an A at IGCSE; for the sciences it is often similar. An IB Diploma Higher Level choice carries comparable expectations. A student entered at Core has been excluded from those routes by an administrative decision taken in Year 10, usually on the basis of a Year 9 assessment, and frequently without the family understanding what was being decided.

The honest position is that Core exists for a reason and is the right entry for some students. A student who would score a D on the Extended papers scores a C on Core, and a C is better than a D. The problem is not the tier; it is the tier chosen by default and then never revisited. If a student placed on Core in Year 10 has improved substantially during the year, the entry can sometimes be changed, but only before the final entry deadline, which sits months before the examination.

The practical instruction for a Dubai parent is therefore specific. Ask in the autumn term of Year 10 which tier each subject is being entered at and on what evidence. Ask again in the autumn term of Year 11, before entries close, whether the tier still reflects the student's current work. If a tier change is wanted, that is the conversation, and it needs a body of marked work behind it rather than a request. The table below sets out what each tier can reach.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: the practical arrangement in the Cambridge sciences
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates take one of two practical components, and which one is decided by the centre. Paper 5 is a practical test, sat in a laboratory under examination conditions with apparatus. Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, a written paper about experimental work: reading a described method, tabulating results, plotting, calculating gradients, identifying variables, spotting the flaw in a procedure and suggesting an improvement. Both carry real marks and both are examinable skills.

Families consistently underprepare for whichever one applies, because it does not feel like content. It is, though: tabulation conventions, significant figures carried consistently, axes chosen to use the available grid, a line of best fit rather than dot-to-dot, uncertainty treated properly, and an evaluation answer that names a specific limitation rather than saying the experiment could be more accurate. None of that is learned by doing experiments casually in class; it is learned by doing past practical questions and having them marked.

All of it works over a shared screen. The student completes a tabulation or a graph on paper or on a tablet, shares it, and the tutor annotates the errors live: a column heading without units, a reading recorded to the wrong precision, an axis starting at a value that wastes half the grid. For Paper 5 candidates the apparatus work happens at school, but the recording, processing and evaluation that carry the marks are the same skills and can be rehearsed in full from a desk.

Pearson International GCSE science candidates have no separate practical paper, which does not mean no practical questions. The same skills appear inside the written papers, and the same marks go missing for the same reasons. Confirm which arrangement applies, then practise it specifically, because it is among the highest-yield parts of the whole IGCSE science preparation and one of the least contested by other tutors.

sections.heading: Grades 9 to 1, A* to G, and the number the ministry asks for
paragraphs: Dubai parents deal with two IGCSE grading scales at once, and the schools rarely explain the relationship. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G outside the United Kingdom, with 9 to 1 used for certain syllabuses taken in the UK. Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1. A family with one child's result in letters and another's in numbers is not comparing like with like unless they know the mapping.

The mapping is approximate by design rather than exact, because the scales were not built to align one to one. Broadly, a 9 sits above the old A*, an 8 straddles A* and A, a 7 maps to A, a 6 to B, a 5 to a high C, and a 4 to a standard C. Below that, a 3 corresponds roughly to a D and a grade 2 to an E. Universities and sixth forms publish their requirements in whichever scale they prefer, and most now state both.

The number that matters for the UAE is lower than most families expect. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for this search states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published figure is five.

Two cautions follow. First, equivalency is a floor for recognition, not an entry requirement for a competitive university course, and nobody should treat a grade 3 as a target. Second, equivalency is a government process administered by the ministry and the emirate attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it or assist with it, and tutoring is not required for it. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before relying on any figure, including the ones restated here.

sections.heading: Three series a year, six zones, and the deadline nobody watches
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. A March series operates in some regions. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. That gives a Dubai family more than one route to a result, and more than one deadline to miss.

The zone point is specific to Cambridge and catches families out every year. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. A timetable found online is not automatically your centre's timetable. Get it from the school's examinations officer.

The entry deadline is the one that quietly removes options. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows the shape clearly: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Final entries therefore close more than two months before the first paper, and a tier change after that date is not available.

Pearson's published pattern is similar in principle. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is why every date in the table below should be confirmed against the live official timetable rather than trusted from a page like this one.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: The pattern of lost marks at IGCSE is different from the pattern at Diploma or A Level, and it is different between subjects within IGCSE. Knowing which pattern applies turns a vague request for help into a specific, short piece of work. In almost every case the diagnosis comes from one marked paper rather than from a conversation, which is why the first session is usually spent on a script rather than on teaching.

In Mathematics, the loss is method marks. IGCSE mark schemes award marks for shown steps, and a student who works in their head forfeits them on answers that are correct. Add premature rounding, missing units and answers left as a calculator decimal where an exact form was required, and a confident mathematician loses a grade without a single conceptual error. The fix is mechanical and fast: write the method, carry full precision, round once at the end.

In the sciences the loss is linguistic. Command terms mean specific things, and explain is the one that costs most: a question asking for an explanation and receiving a description scores roughly half. Add equations without state symbols, graph axes without units, and data answers that state a trend without quoting the figures that show it, and the pattern is consistent across Physics, Chemistry and Biology. These are a few weeks of targeted work, not a term.

In the essay and case-study subjects the loss is structural. History source questions ask for provenance and purpose and receive summaries of the source. Geography answers refer to a named case study in terms that would fit anywhere. Business answers explain a concept in the abstract rather than applying it to the company in the stimulus material, which is exactly where the application and analysis marks live. English reading answers are written from memory of the passage instead of from the passage. Every one of those is a technique fix with a visible effect on the next marked paper.

Sciences: explain answered as describe; equations without state symbols

sections.heading: What the first month of sessions actually fixes
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what changes and when. The honest answer for IGCSE preparation is that the first month produces visible movement if the problem is technique and produces a plan if the problem is content. Those are different outcomes and it is worth knowing which one you are buying before the first invoice rather than after the fourth.

A technique-led first month looks like this. Session one is a marked script and a diagnosis against the correct specification. Session two attacks the largest single leak, which is usually method marks in Mathematics or command terms in the sciences. Session three sets a full paper to time, which is frequently the first time the student has sat one. Session four marks that paper and compares the error list with session one's. A student losing eight marks a paper to presentation and method commonly recovers most of them inside this cycle.

A content-led first month looks different and should be described differently. Session one establishes which topics are genuinely absent rather than shaky. Sessions two to four teach the largest absent topic properly, with work set between sessions. There is no timed paper in month one, because a timed paper on content the student has not met measures nothing. The honest target here is a grade rather than three, across a term rather than a month, and a provider promising otherwise is selling something that cannot be delivered.

Both versions produce the same artefacts, which is how a family can tell progress from activity: a marked script per cycle, a written error list that shrinks, and a mark on a timed paper that either moves or does not. We publish no grade-improvement statistics on this site, because any such figure needs a sample size, a date and a method behind it, and nobody in this market publishes those. What we can show is the student's own sequence of marked papers, which is better evidence for your child than an average would be.

sections.heading: Private candidates: sitting a paper your school does not offer
paragraphs: Some Dubai students need a subject their school does not enter candidates for, or a resit in a series their school does not run. The route is the private candidate route: the student registers through an examination centre that accepts external candidates, sits the paper there, and receives the certificate directly. It is ordinary and well established, and it is also administratively unforgiving in ways that catch families out.

The constraints are practical. A private candidate must find a centre in Dubai that accepts external entries for the specific board and subject, and must do so well before the final entry deadline, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026. Subjects with a practical or a speaking component are harder to place as a private candidate than written-only subjects, because the centre has to run the component. Fees are set by the centre and vary, so ask for the total rather than the per-subject figure.

What preparation looks like for a private candidate differs from preparation for a school candidate in one important respect: there is no teacher behind it. A school candidate has a department, a scheme of work and internal deadlines. A private candidate has a specification and a deadline. That makes the syllabus document itself the working plan, and it makes coverage tracking the main job of the first few sessions: which objectives are covered, which are not, and in what order the remainder will be taught.

One restriction is worth stating plainly, because it applies to any provider. Examination board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material. We reference and link them rather than reproducing or supplying them, and for unreleased material supplying it would be a malpractice exposure as well as an infringement. A student's own legitimately obtained copy, from their centre or from the board's public pages, is the material a session works from.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. These subjects sit on the same timetable as IGCSE preparation and compete with it for the student's week, which is a planning fact rather than an inconvenience.

The organisational rules are specific and they explain a lot of what families observe at school. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arabs study Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural strand in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter for anyone planning a week. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential rather than a general claim.

For content, there is a hard constraint that shapes how any tutoring in these subjects can honestly be described: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That means support in these subjects is language and study-skills work against the set content, not an alternative syllabus. No competitor page researched for this market has a section on these subjects at all, which is why families planning an IGCSE year rarely account for them until the timetable is already full.

process.title: Send the code and the tier
process.description: Message us the syllabus code from the entry confirmation and the tier word next to it: 0620 Extended, 4MA1 Higher, 0625 Core. With that we can match a tutor who has marked those exact papers and can tell you in the first reply which components the student should be practising first.

process.title: Send one paper sat to time
process.description: A past paper from the correct board, completed under timed conditions without notes. We mark it against the published criteria and report the pattern: method marks, command terms, timing, or genuine content gaps. That report is what the first session is built on, and it decides whether this is a four-week job or a term.

process.title: Confirm the practical arrangement
process.description: For Cambridge sciences, find out from the examinations officer whether the centre enters candidates for Paper 5 or Paper 6. They need entirely different preparation and it is the most commonly neglected component of the whole entry. Pearson candidates confirm instead that practical skills sit inside the written papers.

process.title: Take the trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute session per student over live video, with no card details taken. The tutor works through part of the marked script with the student. You finish with a named tutor, a view on the number of weeks, and the student's own opinion of whether the session was useful, which is the opinion that determines whether the booking works.

process.title: Work paper by paper, review on marks
process.description: Sessions are planned around one paper at a time rather than one topic, with questions set between them and marked at the next. Every few weeks, read the marks on the timed papers. If they are moving, continue. If they are not moving after four marked papers, the plan changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.title: Codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: This page names 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0500, 0455, 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1 because the code is the examination. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole seven-page Dubai area cluster we researched, which is why so many Dubai students revise the wrong board's papers.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation, early
whyPoints.description: A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade at C or 5 and can close A Level and IB Higher Level routes. We raise it in the first reply rather than after entries close, because the final entry deadline for a Cambridge series sits months before the first paper and a tier change after it is not available.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper treated as examinable
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 and Paper 6 carry real marks and are taught, not absorbed. Tabulation, significant figures, graph work, variable identification and the evaluation question all work over a shared screen with the student's own attempt annotated live. Most preparation plans skip this component entirely.

whyPoints.title: Board dates cited to the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from those boards' own published pages, with the series named. Cambridge's zone rule is quoted because it is the error that costs a candidate a paper. Confirm every date against the live official timetable, which is linked rather than restated.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; visiting a student's address is a service we run only in India. For an IGCSE student the practical gain is a tutor who has marked the specific paper rather than one who lives within a short drive.

whyPoints.title: Official material linked, not supplied
whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We cite and link them and work from the student's own legitimately obtained copies. IB Gram holds no examination-board or regulator accreditation and claims none anywhere on this site.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE exam preparation in Dubai actually have to cover?
faqs.answer: Four things, in this order. The syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations. The papers for that entry, taken one at a time rather than as a subject. The practical arrangement in the sciences, which at Cambridge is either Paper 5 or Paper 6. And technique: method marks, command terms, data presentation and timing, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit for a student who knows the content. A single marked past paper from the correct board tells you which of these the student actually needs.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE paper does my child sit if the school entered them for the Core tier?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge Mathematics 0580, a Core entry sits Papers 1 and 3 and the grade cannot exceed C. An Extended entry sits Papers 2 and 4 and is graded A* to E. In the tiered sciences, a Core candidate takes the Core multiple-choice and theory papers plus either Paper 5 or Paper 6, again capped at C. Pearson's equivalent split is Foundation and Higher on the 9 to 1 scale, with Foundation reaching grade 5. Ask the examinations officer which tier each subject is entered at, and ask before the final entry deadline, because the tier cannot be changed after it.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's school uses Cambridge or Edexcel for Maths?
faqs.answer: Three reliable routes. The entry confirmation the school issues carries the syllabus code: anything starting with a zero, like 0580, is Cambridge International, and anything starting with a four, like 4MA1, is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The front cover of any past paper the department has issued carries the same code. And the examinations officer will confirm the code and the tier by email, which is a routine request. Ask per subject rather than once, because Dubai schools commonly choose boards department by department, so one student can sit two or three different boards.

faqs.question: What is the Alternative to Practical paper and how is it revised?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 in the Cambridge sciences is a written paper about experimental work, taken instead of Paper 5, the laboratory practical test. It asks a candidate to read a described method, tabulate results, plot a graph, calculate a gradient, identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, find the weakness in a procedure and suggest a specific improvement. It is revised by doing past practical questions and having them marked properly, which works entirely over a shared screen: the student completes a table or a plot, shares it, and the errors are annotated live, column by column.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai IGCSE students lose the most marks in the sciences?
faqs.answer: In language rather than in science. The largest single leak is command-term drift: a question that says explain receives a description and scores roughly half. The second is chemical and physical notation, with balanced equations missing state symbols and quantities missing units. The third is data questions, where a candidate states a trend without quoting the figures from the table that demonstrate it. The fourth is the practical component, which students treat as common sense rather than as an examinable skill. All four are technique problems and respond to a few weeks of marked papers rather than a term of teaching.

faqs.question: What does a 9-1 grade mean next to the old A* to G scale?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G outside the United Kingdom, with 9 to 1 used for certain syllabuses sat in the UK; Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1. The mapping is approximate rather than exact: a 9 sits above the old A*, an 8 straddles A* and A, a 7 maps to A, a 6 to B, a 5 to a high C and a 4 to a standard C, with 3 corresponding roughly to a D. Sixth forms and universities publish requirements in whichever scale they prefer, and most state both. Ask your target school which scale their stated requirement uses.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Dubai student need for MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for this search states six; the published figure is five. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is a government process and not something a tutoring provider performs.

faqs.question: Does the June series or the November series suit a Year 11 retake better?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the result is needed for and when. Pearson International GCSE examinations run in May and June and in November, and Cambridge runs June and November series with a March series in some regions. The published turnaround is the deciding factor: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit produces a result in the following January, which may be after a sixth-form offer has been settled. A June retake gives a longer preparation window but arrives a year later. Check both against the live official timetables before committing.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish six different exam timetable zones?
faqs.answer: Because examinations are sat across many time zones and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones to manage that. The consequence for a family is operational rather than theoretical: Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. A timetable found through a search engine is not automatically your centre's. Get the zone-correct version from the school's examinations officer and plan revision against that one.

faqs.question: When is the final entry deadline for a Cambridge IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, which is why it removes options quietly. The published worked example is the March 2027 series: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May, and certificates follow in late June. The practical consequence is that any tier change, subject change or additional entry has to be settled in the autumn term, not in the spring. Confirm your own series deadline with the school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE papers in Dubai as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an examination centre in Dubai that accepts external candidates for that board and subject. The constraints are administrative rather than academic: the centre must be found and the entry lodged before the series deadline, subjects with practical or speaking components are harder to place because the centre has to run them, and fees are set by the centre rather than by the board. Ask for the total cost rather than a per-subject figure. Preparation for a private candidate works from the specification document itself, because there is no school scheme of work behind it.

faqs.question: How many weeks of preparation does one IGCSE subject realistically need?
faqs.answer: A technique problem in one subject is usually eight to twelve weeks at one session a week, with a full paper sat to time every third week. A content problem, where whole topics are genuinely absent rather than shaky, is a term or more and the honest target is one grade rather than three. The distinction comes from a marked script, not from a conversation: a student losing marks evenly across every question has a content gap, while one who scores well until question six and stops has a timing problem that three timed papers can fix.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education left out of the five-subject equivalency count?
faqs.answer: Yes. The published rule for the British track is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That is separate from the school requirement: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes strictly prohibited. So a student must study them at school while they do not count towards the ministry's five. Verify both positions on moe.gov.ae and the KHDA guidance before planning around either.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE exam preparation session fix in the first month?
faqs.answer: If the problem is technique, the first month usually produces visible movement: session one is a marked script and a diagnosis, session two attacks the largest leak, session three sets a full paper to time, and session four marks it against the first error list. A student losing eight marks a paper to method and presentation commonly recovers most of them in that cycle. If the problem is content, the first month produces a plan rather than a mark change, because a timed paper on unmet content measures nothing. Knowing which case applies before booking is the point of sending a script first.

faqs.question: Is there a point where starting IGCSE preparation is too late?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be worth doing, but late enough to change what is worth doing. With more than ten weeks left, content work is still feasible. Inside six weeks, content rebuilding is not, and the useful purchase is timed papers marked against the criteria, because that attacks technique, which is where a prepared student's missing marks are. Inside two weeks, the highest-value work is paper discipline: timing per question, command-term matching, showing method, and reading the question twice. Nobody should be selling a content block two weeks before a paper.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE exam preparation sessions cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150, while budget online providers advertise lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A tutor in the room costs more because travel is priced into every hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350. These are the market's published figures with their sources, not an IB Gram price list. Start with the trial lesson, which is one 45-minute session per student with no card details taken.

dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Send us the code, not the subject
dubai/igcse-exam-preparation.closingBody: The fastest way to a useful first session is a message with two things in it: the syllabus code on your child's entry confirmation and one past paper from that board sat to time. With those we can name the papers that matter, tell you whether the practical component is Paper 5 or Paper 6, say whether this is a technique job of a few weeks or a content job of a term, and match a tutor who has marked those specific papers. The trial lesson is one 45-minute session per student over live video with no card details taken. Lessons run one-to-one on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE at Extended tier and at Core, across Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses. Each one works to a named syllabus code rather than to a general subject, because Paper 4 of 0580 and Paper 2 of 4MA1 reward different habits.

intro.heading: What families in Dubai are really asking for when they search for home tuition
paragraphs: The phrase "IGCSE home tuition in Dubai" gets typed into Google by a parent holding a school report. Something in it is wrong. Either a predicted grade slipped, or a mock paper came back with a mark that does not match the effort going in at the kitchen table. Home tuition is the word parents reach for because it means the opposite of a crowded classroom: one adult, one child, undivided attention. That instinct is correct. The delivery assumption behind it is the only part worth revisiting.

Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school pupils as of the 2024-25 year, with 37% of that enrolment following a UK curriculum. That makes IGCSE the single largest qualification cohort in the emirate at age 16. It also means the tutoring market here is deep but uneven. There are plenty of people who will teach maths. There are far fewer who can tell you that your child is losing four marks a paper on 0580 Paper 4 because they are rounding mid-calculation rather than at the end, and then show you the three questions where it happened.

That is the difference this page is built around. IGCSE is not a general knowledge test. It is a tightly specified syllabus with numbered papers, published assessment objectives, and command words that mean exact things. "State" wants one line. "Explain" wants a mechanism. "Suggest" wants a plausible answer the examiner has never seen before, marked on reasoning rather than recall. A tutor who does not teach that distinction explicitly is leaving marks on the table every single paper, no matter how well they know the content.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition as one-to-one live video lessons. We do not send a tutor to a Dubai address, and home visits in Dubai are not a service we sell anywhere in the UAE. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation. A family in Mirdif searching for a Cambridge Chemistry 0620 specialist is choosing from everyone we work with, not from whoever happens to be a 25-minute drive away at 5pm on a Tuesday. In a city where the school run and the evening traffic between Al Barsha and Dubai Silicon Oasis can eat 40 minutes each way, that pool difference is the whole decision.

What follows is the detail a parent actually needs before spending money: how the grading scales work and why your child's report may carry two of them, how the Core and Extended decision caps the grade before a single paper is sat, where marks go subject by subject, what the Dubai market charges in dirhams, how the exam calendar runs backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, and what the mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside IGCSE require. Every figure is attributed. Nothing here is a promise about a grade.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits in the middle of a longer route. Most Dubai British-curriculum schools run Key Stage 3 to Year 9, IGCSE across Years 10 and 11, then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. Tuition is only useful if it knows which of those destinations your child is heading for, because the subject choices diverge.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and the run-in to IGCSE
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE decide which tier a child is entered for. Year 9 maths sets in most Dubai schools are the mechanism by which a child ends up on Core rather than Extended, often without the family being told that the decision caps the grade at C or 5. Work in this window is about closing arithmetic and algebraic fluency gaps while they are still cheap to close, and about reading the sets data the school holds.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools frequently take in pupils mid-Key Stage from CBSE, American and other systems. A child arriving from a CBSE Year 8 into a British Year 9 has usually met more algebra and less statistical interpretation, and has rarely written extended prose answers under timed conditions. Six to ten weeks of targeted work before the IGCSE option forms are signed changes which tier the school offers.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally at the end. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series available in some regions. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Grades come as A*-G on most Cambridge syllabuses and as 9-1 on Pearson International GCSE and some Cambridge subjects, which is why a single report card can carry both.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a two-board city. A family can have one child at a school entering Cambridge 0580 Maths and another at a school entering Pearson 4MA1, and the papers are structured differently: Cambridge Extended maths is two papers, Pearson 4MA1 is two papers with a different formula-sheet policy. Tuition that does not establish the board in the first session is guessing at the paper your child will open.

programmes.name: A Level and the IB Diploma after Year 11
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is the entry ticket. Most Dubai sixth forms set a grade threshold per subject, commonly a 6 or B at IGCSE for the same subject at A Level, and higher for maths and the sciences. IB Diploma entry at Dubai IB schools usually looks for a spread of strong IGCSE grades rather than a single subject, plus evidence the child can write at length.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at grade no less than E or 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That rule shapes IGCSE subject choice for any family planning a UAE university route.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families ask about most, with the syllabus code where it matters and the specific place marks tend to disappear. The codes are Cambridge International unless a Pearson equivalent is named.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 is where the grade is won or lost. The recurring losses are premature rounding, missing units in mensuration, and non-calculator-style method marks thrown away because working was not written down. Bearings, similar-shape area and volume scale factors, and histogram frequency density account for a disproportionate share of dropped marks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 in stronger Dubai sets as A Level preparation. Calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities appear two years earlier than most pupils expect. The common failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than as a different paper with its own notation conventions.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism are the standing problem: series and parallel reasoning, potential dividers, and the direction conventions in electromagnetic induction. Paper 6 Alternative to Practical rewards the ability to spot a control variable and criticise a method, which is examinable skill, not lab access.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions are the three clusters that decide an Extended grade. Candidates lose marks writing ionic equations without charges balanced, and describing tests without the observation the examiner needs to see.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Marks go on precision of language rather than knowledge. Osmosis answers that say "water moves to the stronger solution" score nothing against a mark scheme asking for water potential. Genetics crosses, enzyme graph interpretation and transport in plants are the reliable trouble spots.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two or three papers. Pupils who did well in separate-science style teaching often over-answer, spending time on depth the mark scheme does not credit. Knowing the reduced content boundaries is worth several marks a paper.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990 and 0510 second language)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary carry heavy marks and are the most coachable components on any IGCSE timetable. Summary answers fail by lifting phrasing; directed writing fails by ignoring the stated audience and form. Both are fixable inside a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 / 0992)
subjects.description: Essay structure and quotation economy decide the band. Candidates write everything they know about a character rather than answering the question asked. Unseen poetry is where Dubai cohorts tend to be weakest, because it cannot be revised by memorising notes.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: The case-study paper is an application exercise, not a recall test. Marks follow from quoting the stimulus and giving a justified recommendation. Evaluation marks are routinely left unclaimed because answers stop at two advantages and two disadvantages.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation. Hexadecimal and two's complement conversions are mechanical marks that pupils drop under time pressure, and algorithm questions need a written plan before code. Highly suited to screen-shared teaching.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Area matters on this page for one reason only: it determines which schools your child's cohort comes from, which board they are entered for, and what time a session can realistically start once the school run and the evening commute are accounted for.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Dense British-curriculum catchment feeding several large Year 10 and 11 cohorts. Families here tend to want Extended-tier maths and separate sciences, and 5.30pm starts work better than 4.30pm once buses clear.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A mixed board area where Cambridge and Pearson entries sit side by side in the same friendship group. Establishing the exact syllabus code before the first session matters more here than almost anywhere in the city.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Long-established British schools with selective sixth forms, so IGCSE grade thresholds for A Level entry drive most tuition requests. English Literature and Additional Mathematics come up more often than in newer communities.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Villa communities with a heavy co-curricular load, which is why Saturday morning and post-prep slots fill first. Requests cluster around maths and the triple sciences in the spring term before the June series.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Jumeirah Lakes
regions.note: Apartment living with no spare study room, so a quiet one-to-one video lesson with headphones is often more practical than a visitor in the flat. Short, frequent sessions suit this cohort better than long weekend blocks.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Schools here run large IGCSE year groups with wide ability spreads, which makes Core versus Extended tiering the most common first conversation we have with families in this corridor.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Parents frequently travelling, so continuity matters: a tutor who keeps the same slot and writes notes a second parent can read on a flight is worth more than one who is flexible but undocumented.

regions.name: Al Furjan, JVC and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Fast-growing catchments with newer schools still building out their Year 11 results history. Families here ask more questions about past-paper availability and mock calibration than about anything else.

schoolClusters.city: Central and new Dubai
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum secondaries running IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, mostly Cambridge or Pearson entry, feeding both A Level and IB Diploma sixth forms. Named here as the schools our students attend, for context on cohort and board.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and outer Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Larger year groups, wider ability spread, and a higher proportion of Core-tier entries in maths and the sciences. Tiering reviews and Paper 6 practical-skills work are the most requested help in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Southern corridor and villa communities
schoolClusters.note: JESS Arabian Ranches and the schools around Sports City and Dubailand pull from spread-out villa catchments, which is why evening session timing is the practical constraint families raise first.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every IGCSE request we get in Dubai. All three are delivered as live one-to-one or small-group video lessons, so the choice is about frequency and intensity rather than about location.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-time
modes.description: One or two 60-minute lessons a week in the same slot, running alongside school. The tutor works a term ahead of nothing and a week behind nothing: each session takes the current school topic, the last marked assessment, and one older weakness that keeps resurfacing. This is the format that moves a grade over two terms rather than two weeks.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, written notes to the parent after each lesson

sections.heading: What IGCSE home tuition in Dubai buys, and what it cannot
paragraphs: IGCSE home tuition in Dubai buys three things: a diagnosis, undivided attention, and a feedback loop faster than a school's. A class teacher with 24 pupils in a Year 11 set marks a mock in a weekend and returns it with a grade and a sentence. A one-to-one tutor reads the same script in twelve minutes and can tell you that nine of the lost marks came from one habit. That is the entire value proposition, and it is a real one.

It cannot buy a grade. Nobody can, and any tutoring service in this city that implies otherwise is selling something it does not control. The variables that decide an IGCSE result include the paper your child happens to open, the grade boundaries set after the series, and how much work gets done between sessions. What good tuition changes is the number of marks reliably available to your child on a paper they have never seen, which is a different and more honest claim.

The format question is where Dubai parents most often get steered wrong. A tutor arriving at a family's address sounds like more attention, and in a classroom-versus-visitor comparison it is. Against live one-to-one video it is mostly a travel bill. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180-500 an hour partly because the tutor is being paid for a drive across the city. The tutor pool also shrinks to whoever is willing to make that drive, which is how a family needing Cambridge 0620 Extended ends up with a general science graduate.

So the position on this page is straightforward. We take the query seriously, answer the home-tuition question honestly, and then deliver the thing itself as live one-to-one video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. What a Dubai family gets instead is choice of specialist, a session that starts on time regardless of Sheikh Zayed Road, and a recording-free but fully documented lesson trail.

sections.heading: Why your child's report card may carry two different grading scales
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 11 report can legitimately show an A* in one subject and a 9 in another, and parents reasonably assume a mistake. There is none. Cambridge International reports most IGCSE syllabuses on the A*-G scale, and some on 9-1. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9-1. A school entering Cambridge sciences and Pearson maths will produce exactly that mixed report, every year, and rarely explains it in writing.

The practical consequence is that the two scales do not map one to one. The 9-1 scale deliberately spreads the top: 9 sits above the old A* standard, 8 straddles it, and 7 aligns broadly with an A. Sixth-form entry criteria in Dubai are usually written in one scale and applied to applicants holding the other, so a child with a 7 and a child with an A are not always treated identically by an admissions spreadsheet, even when they should be.

This matters for tuition planning because a target has to be set in the right currency. "We want a 7" means something different on a Pearson paper than "we want an A" does on a Cambridge one, and the mark distance from the current position differs accordingly. The first session on any maths or science subject starts by establishing the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the scale, in that order, before any teaching happens.

It also affects how you read grade boundaries. Boundaries are set per series, per paper, after the exam, and published by the board afterwards. A mock marked against last year's boundaries gives an indicative grade, not a predicted one. When a school says a child is "on a 6", ask which series boundaries were applied and what the raw mark was. The raw mark is the thing tuition moves.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that caps the grade before any paper is sat
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. Maths 0580, the separate sciences and Combined Science all run a Core route and an Extended route, with different papers and different content. A Core entry in maths caps the achievable grade. If your child's university or sixth-form target requires a grade above that cap, the tier decision has already decided the outcome, months before the exam.

In Dubai this decision is usually made by a set placement in Year 9 or early Year 10, based on internal assessment data. It is defensible as a judgement and frequently correct. What goes wrong is that it is communicated as a set change rather than as a grade ceiling, so families discover the implication in Year 11 when they read a sixth-form prospectus. If your child is in a lower set in a tiered subject, the question to ask the head of department in writing is simple: which tier are you entering my child for, and what is the highest grade that entry can award?

Moving tier is possible and is not rare. Final entries for a Cambridge series close months before the papers, so there is a real window. What it requires is evidence: Extended-standard work produced under timed conditions, not a parental request. Six to ten weeks of focused work on the Extended-only content, with marked papers to show the department, is the argument that actually moves an entry.

Not every tier move is in the child's interest. An Extended entry that collapses on Paper 4 can produce a worse grade than a confident Core entry would have. The honest version of this conversation looks at the marks currently available on an Extended paper, the time left before final entries, and the subject's weight in the child's post-16 plan. Sometimes the right answer is to keep the Core entry and spend the tuition hours on the two subjects where a grade move is genuinely reachable.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Ask a tutor where your child is losing marks and a vague answer is a warning sign. The information exists. Every IGCSE paper is marked against a published scheme, every mark has a reason, and a competent subject specialist reading a marked script can sort the losses into categories within a few minutes. The categories matter more than the total, because they have different cures and different costs in tuition hours.

Four categories cover nearly everything. Content gaps, where the child genuinely does not know the material; technique losses, where the knowledge is there but the answer does not meet the command word; process errors, which are arithmetic slips, rounding, units and transcription; and timing losses, where the last questions are blank or rushed. A script showing 14 marks lost splits very differently depending on the mix, and the fastest gains almost always sit in technique and process.

Technique losses are the cheapest marks on any IGCSE paper. A biology candidate who knows osmosis perfectly and writes "water moves to the stronger solution" is losing marks to vocabulary, not understanding. A maths candidate who writes only the answer loses method marks they had already earned. A business studies candidate who lists advantages without a justified recommendation forfeits the evaluation band. None of that requires new content. It requires being shown the mark scheme next to their own words, which is exactly what a one-to-one session does well.

Process errors respond to a different treatment: drilling under timed conditions, with a tally. We count rounding slips, unit omissions and sign errors across three papers and show the student the count. Fifteen-year-olds argue with advice and rarely argue with their own tally. Content gaps are the slowest and most expensive to fix, which is why diagnosing them accurately matters; spending eight weeks reteaching topics the child already knew is the most common way tuition money gets wasted in this market.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: the Cambridge and Pearson calendar
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an exam session, an entry deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the calendar is the single most actionable thing a parent can be given. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November each year.

The deadline that surprises families is the entry deadline, which sits months before the paper. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series are a worked example: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is more than two months. A tier change, a subject drop or a private-candidate entry has to happen inside that window.

One Cambridge rule deserves specific attention in the Gulf. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent printing a timetable found through a search engine, rather than the one the school issued, is taking a risk nobody needs to take.

On the Pearson side, the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which means any date on any tutoring website can be revised. Work from the live official timetable, always.
