sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for. This is a federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA sets the detail for Dubai, and its current requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arabs are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

For tuition this creates a practical point and a limit. The practical point is that these subjects sit on the same timetable and the same report card as IGCSE subjects, and a child struggling in Arabic as an additional language is carrying a load that affects everything else. The limit is that for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support here means working with the school's own material and the Ministry's framework, not importing an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule, and the competitor that got it wrong
paragraphs: Families planning a UAE university route need their child's school certificate recognised by the Ministry of Education. For the British track the published requirement is specific. Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule change IGCSE subject choices. The first is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a child counting them towards the total is short. The second is the number itself: one ranking competitor in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule says five. Getting this wrong by one subject is the kind of error that costs a family an exam entry fee and a term of work.

The American track has different requirements worth knowing if your child moves schools. English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to print, because none has been read on a Ministry source, and publishing an unverified number on a page a family acts on is worse than publishing nothing.

IB Gram does not perform, lodge or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anyone. It is a Ministry process and the Ministry is the only place to confirm the current rule before you act on it. What tuition can do is make sure the five subjects your child is entered for are the five that count, at grades comfortably above the floor, rather than discovering the arithmetic in Year 12.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to tutor in Dubai?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone, including us. The official route is MoHRE's own service, titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

There is a separate rule parents in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain should know, because families move between emirates. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. The practical implication is clear either way: do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for a fee.

An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A tuition centre needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit or accreditation of any kind, operates no premises in the UAE, and describes itself as neither approved nor endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board.

process.title: Send the last marked paper
process.description: Not the report card, the paper. A marked script with the examiner's or teacher's annotations tells a subject specialist more in ten minutes than a term of grades does. If there is no marked paper, we set one as the first task and mark it against the published scheme before any teaching begins.

process.title: Establish board, code, tier and scale
process.description: Cambridge or Pearson, which syllabus code, Core or Extended, A*-G or 9-1. Four facts, and they change what every subsequent session looks like. Dubai is a two-board city, so we confirm them from the school's own documentation rather than assuming.

process.title: Take the free first lesson
process.description: A full-length session with the proposed tutor, at no cost and with no card details required to book it. The point is to test whether your child talks to this particular adult. A tutor who is excellent on paper and silent in the room is the wrong tutor, and finding that out should not cost money.

process.title: Agree the target in marks, not adjectives
process.description: We convert the grade target into raw marks on the relevant papers, then into a ranked list of errors worth that many marks. The plan is the list, in order of marks available. Parents get it in writing before the first paid session.

process.title: Weekly notes, fortnightly recalibration
process.description: After each session you receive what was covered, what was set, and which error is currently being tracked. Every two weeks we check the error count against the previous fortnight. If it has not moved, the approach changes, or the tutor does.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: Teaching Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 as though they are the same chemistry course is how marks get lost on paper structure and formula-sheet policy. Every match we make is to a code the child is actually entered for, confirmed from the school's documentation before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: The specialist you need, not the one nearby
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, a family in Al Furjan and a family in Mirdif choose from the same set of specialists. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 are scarce in any single Dubai neighbourhood and reachable online from all of them.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can audit
whyPoints.description: Marked questions, a tracked error count, and written notes after every session. You should never have to ask whether tuition is working; the fortnightly count either moved or it did not, and the honest answer when it has not moved is a change of approach.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student produced. One competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger for the student and it is not something we will do at any price, for coursework, an IGCSE assignment or anything else.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band, regulator rule and exam date on this page is attributed to the organisation that published it, with the date. Nothing here is a self-reported statistic about our own results, because we cannot show you the underlying data for one.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for Dubai weeks
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around school hours, prep and co-curriculars, and can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. Travel between emirates or over a long summer does not break the slot, because the lesson follows the child.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE home tuition in Dubai mean a tutor comes to our villa?
faqs.answer: Not with IB Gram. We deliver IGCSE tuition as live one-to-one video lessons, and home visits are a service we run only in India. We use the phrase because it is what parents search for, and the underlying request is the one we answer: one specialist, one child, undivided attention. What changes is that you choose from every tutor we work with rather than from those willing to drive to your community at 5pm. For a scarce subject such as Additional Mathematics 0606, that difference decides whether a specialist is available at all.

faqs.question: Which tier has my child's Dubai school put them in, and who do I ask?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of department in writing for two things: the tier your child is entered for, and the highest grade that entry can award. Both are facts the school holds. Tiering in Dubai is usually decided by set placement in Year 9 or early Year 10 and communicated as a set change, so the grade ceiling rarely gets said out loud. Final entries for a Cambridge series close months before the papers, so there is a real window to move, provided you can show Extended-standard work produced under timed conditions rather than simply requesting it.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report show an A* in one subject and a 9 in another?
faqs.answer: Because Dubai schools enter different subjects with different boards. Cambridge International reports most IGCSE syllabuses on A*-G and some on 9-1; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9-1. A school entering Cambridge sciences and Pearson maths produces exactly that mixed report. The scales do not map one to one: 9 sits above the old A* standard, 8 straddles it, and 7 aligns broadly with an A. Set your target in the scale your child's board actually uses, because the mark distance to it differs.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates as of October 2026 run from AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, and AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits sit at AED 180-500 inclusive of travel, per Bestimate at 180-350 and independent tutors at 200-500. Specialists run AED 200-450 and above. Those are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram prices; ours depend on subject scarcity and tier, and the consultation after the free lesson is where you get the number.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as effective for IGCSE sciences as sitting beside a tutor?
faqs.answer: For the written papers, yes, and for one reason: the work being taught is written work. A shared screen with a marked script on it, annotated live, is closer to how examiners actually read an answer than two people looking at one piece of paper. Practical skills at IGCSE are assessed by a written component in most entries, which rewards method criticism and control-variable reasoning rather than lab access. What online cannot replicate is physically handling apparatus, which is the school's job and is why we work with the school's practical schedule rather than around it.

faqs.question: How many sessions will my child need before a grade moves?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which category the lost marks sit in. Technique losses, where the knowledge is there but the answer does not meet the command word, typically shift in two to four sessions. Process errors such as rounding or missing units take three to five with a tally kept. Timing responds to two or three full timed papers. Genuine content gaps are the slow ones, at six to ten sessions per significant topic. Any tutor who answers this question before reading a marked script is guessing, and the guess usually overstates how fast content gaps close.

faqs.question: Where is the line between helping with IGCSE coursework and doing it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the underlying skills, discuss the brief, explain the assessment criteria, question the student's reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves. A tutor may not produce assessed material, rewrite a draft into final form, or supply text for a student to submit. One site in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; that is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. We state the boundary in the first session so nobody is negotiating it later.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the exam must a Cambridge IGCSE entry be locked in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, which is the detail that catches families. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series give the shape: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, and results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. June and November series have their own dates. Any tier change, subject drop or private-candidate entry has to be settled inside that window, so the useful question in October is about entries, not revision.

faqs.question: My child's school issued a timetable and I found a different one online. Which do we use?
faqs.answer: The school's. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable found through a search engine may belong to another zone entirely. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that can be revised before a series, so the live official document or the school's issued copy is the only one to plan around.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor tells UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule says five. Confirm the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels before acting, and treat any tutoring site's version, including this one, as a prompt to check rather than as authority.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a licence to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated by the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified. Ask a prospective tutor for the permit reference.

faqs.question: Can my child start IGCSE tuition in the middle of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a lot of our Dubai work starts exactly there, usually after January mocks. What changes is the plan. Mid-Year 11 is too late to rebuild two years of content and exactly right for technique, process and timing, which is where most recoverable marks sit anyway. The first session reads the mock script, sorts the losses into categories, and spends the remaining weeks on the categories with the best marks-per-hour return. Starting late rules out some things; it does not rule out a grade move.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. Scarce combinations exist, and Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 at the top band, and some second-language subjects are the ones that most often have a wait. If no suitable specialist is free in the window you need, we tell you the wait rather than putting a near-enough tutor in the slot. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, we are explicit that the tutor teaching your child may be based elsewhere and delivering over video, because the alternative is a family discovering it in week three.

faqs.question: How do sessions work around Ramadan and the Dubai school calendar?
faqs.answer: Timings move. Sessions shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and we plan around the school's own revision and assessment weeks rather than on top of them. The Dubai academic year and the Cambridge June series interact awkwardly: the most useful revision window frequently lands across a holiday. We map that at the start of term so the intensive block sits where the family can actually sustain it, and we would rather pause a week than run a session nobody has the energy for.

faqs.question: What do we get in writing after each lesson?
faqs.answer: What was covered, what was set as independent work, which error is currently being tracked, and the count of that error across recent papers. It goes to the parent, not only to the student. Every fortnight we compare the count with the previous fortnight. That record is also the thing to ask for if you ever change tutors, because the diagnosis is the expensive part and it should not have to be redone. We keep marked work only while it is useful and delete it on request.

dubai/igcse-home-tuition.closingHeading: Start with a marked paper and a free lesson
dubai/igcse-home-tuition.closingBody: The useful first step is not a brochure call. Send the last paper your child sat with the marks on it, tell us the board and the syllabus code, and book the free first lesson with the specialist we propose. In that session your child works through real questions with the tutor while you see how the two of them talk to each other. Afterwards you get the diagnosis in writing: where the marks are going, which category they fall into, and what the first four weeks would target. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose someone else. Nothing is committed and no card details are needed to book it.

intro.heading: Four weeks in, and nobody can say whether it worked
paragraphs: This is the most common conversation in Dubai tutoring and it happens in late October. A family hired somebody in September. The sessions have been pleasant. The student says they are going better. The tutor says progress is being made. Nobody can name a single thing that has changed, because nothing was measured at the start, and so the family faces the same decision they faced in September with four weeks of spending behind them and no more information than they had then.

That is not usually a sign of a bad tutor. It is a sign that nobody set up the measurement, which takes about twenty minutes and almost nobody does. IGCSE is unusually well suited to measurement: there are published mark schemes, past papers with the marks allocated question by question, and components that can be timed. A student's position can be recorded with real precision at the start, and then recorded again at six weeks, and the difference is a fact rather than an impression.

The reason it does not happen is that measurement feels like paying for an assessment instead of teaching. It is also mildly uncomfortable: a recorded baseline makes failure visible, for the tutor and for the plan, and both parties have a quiet interest in vagueness. The families who get the most from tutoring in this market are the ones who insist on the uncomfortable version, and the providers worth hiring are the ones who offer it before being asked.

What this page gives you is a measurement system you can run yourself. Three numbers to record before the first session. What to look for on a marked paper, which is the single richest piece of evidence available and the one most often filed without being read. A way of ranking repairs by marks available rather than by how worried the student is. A term of checkpoints, each with an artefact attached, so that at any point you can ask what exists rather than how it is going. And an honest list of the things nobody can evidence at all.

A word on grade movement, because it is where expectations go wrong in both directions. Grade boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series and published afterwards, and they move between series. Nobody teaching your child knows where the line will fall. So the honest unit of progress is marks on a specific component, not grades, and a student three marks below a boundary is in a genuinely different position from one fifteen marks below, even though both are on the same grade in a report.

Finally the format, because this page answers a search containing the words home tutor. The market for a tutor who travels to a Dubai address is large and its published rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the journey folded in. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India, and we do not provide in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE. Every session described here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and a later section compares the two formats on the one thing this page cares about, which is what survives the session.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Measurement depends on knowing which papers a student is actually sitting, so the awarding organisation and the syllabus code come before the baseline. Dubai schools use both main boards, sometimes within one timetable.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes with several subjects tiered into Core and Extended on different papers and with different available grades. Past papers and mark schemes are published through official channels, which makes a precise baseline straightforward once the correct code is known.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Any Dubai revision plan should be dated against the right zone's live official timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes beginning with a 4, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher while most other subjects are untiered, and results are reported on the 9 to 1 scale rather than A* to G. Several subjects offer a coursework route in place of a second written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May or June and in November. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those windows matter to any evidence plan, because they set when a remark or a retake decision has to be made.

programmes.name: The post-16 destination
programmes.description: Not an IGCSE qualification, but the reason marks at sixteen matter. International A Level courses assume particular IGCSE content, most sharply in mathematics and the sciences, and a tier entry or a lighter science route can close a door without anyone announcing it.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Evidence looks different in different subjects, because the marks sit in different places. These are the subjects Dubai families most often ask about, with the measurable thing in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The easiest subject in the roster to measure, because marks are allocated per question and method marks are visible. The useful baseline is a timed paper with the marks recorded per question rather than as a total.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Measurable at topic level. Record separately the marks lost on electricity, on calculation questions and on unit handling, because those three fail independently and a single total hides which one is the problem.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry each produce a distinct error signature. The alternative-to-practical paper is separately measurable and often the component with the most recoverable marks in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject where a total mark misleads most, because candidates lose heavily on extended-response questions while scoring well on recall. Record the extended-response marks separately from the rest and the picture changes.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Measured by marking the student's own writing weekly against the published criteria. Progress shows first in reading questions, where selecting rather than summarising is a trainable habit, and only later in composition.

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.description: Evidence here is a marked essay a week, nothing else. Watch for quotation used as evidence rather than decoration, and for answering the question on the paper rather than the question that was revised.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: The measurable thing is application. Mark one paragraph a week on a single test: could any sentence in it only be true of this case material? Movement on that test precedes movement in the total mark by several weeks.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Harder to measure because three sciences sit inside two grades or one. Split the baseline by science rather than by paper, since a student can be solid in two and losing the whole margin in the third.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A short syllabus with concentrated difficulty, mostly in calculus and trigonometric identities. Baselines here are unusually informative because a single topic often accounts for most of the loss.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic rather than applied, and measurable through trace tables and pseudocode questions. Do not confuse it with ICT, 0417 or 4IT1, which is a different subject and a different baseline entirely.

regions.note: Villa communities where the 16:30 to 18:00 window is crowded with sport and activities. Sessions here tend to land late, and the record matters more because a tired student and a productive one produce the same attendance note.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Dubai Harbour
regions.note: Apartment towers where a quiet surface is the constraint rather than the schedule. Families here benefit most from the setup conversation, because a session recorded at a cleared table looks different from one at a kitchen counter.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Large established cohorts with multiple children in the same household sitting IGCSEs within two years of each other. Keeping separate records per child sounds obvious and is the most commonly skipped step here.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Jumeirah Village Triangle

sections.heading: The three numbers to record before the first session
paragraphs: Measurement at IGCSE is easier than at almost any other stage of schooling, because the material to measure against is published. Before anyone teaches anything, three numbers should exist on paper. Record them and the entire question of whether tutoring is working becomes answerable. Skip them and it stays a matter of opinion for the rest of the year.

The first number is a timed component mark, recorded question by question. Not a total, and not a practice sheet; one real past-paper component from the correct syllabus, sat under time, marked against the published mark scheme. The per-question breakdown is the part that matters, because a total of 42 out of 80 tells you nothing while a breakdown showing every calculation question lost and every recall question gained tells you what to do on Monday.

The second is the unfinished fraction: how much of the paper was left blank or obviously rushed at the end. This single figure separates two completely different problems that look identical in a grade. A student who answers everything and scores poorly has a knowledge or accuracy problem. A student whose last fifteen marks are blank has a pace problem, and pace is a cheaper and faster fix than content.

The third is the command-word error count: how many questions were answered at a lower command word than the one asked, where a candidate described when the question said explain, or explained when it said evaluate. This is the most transferable loss in the whole qualification. A student making it in one subject is almost certainly making it in eight, which means fixing it once pays nine times. Record all three, date them, keep them. They take one hour to produce and they are the foundation of everything else on this page.

sections.heading: What a marked paper shows that a school report cannot
paragraphs: A Dubai school report is written for a parent and a file, and it does a job neither of which is diagnosis. It summarises, it is positive by convention, and it describes a student rather than their script. A marked paper does the opposite: it is specific, it is indifferent to feelings, and it carries the evidence of exactly where the marks went. Of the two documents a family receives in a year, the report is the one they read and the paper is the one that is useful.

Read the script for pattern rather than for score. Four patterns cover most of what goes wrong at IGCSE and they lead to four different interventions. Marks lost at the end of the paper is pace. Marks lost on questions whose answers are nearly right is presentation and method. Marks lost on questions where the student clearly knew the material but answered a different question is command-word reading. Marks lost in clusters around one or two topics is content, and it is the only one of the four that needs teaching rather than training.

Two more signals are worth looking for and are routinely missed. The first is choice: in papers with optional questions, a candidate who consistently picks the question that suits them least is losing marks before they write anything, and that is correctable in a single session. The second is the crossed-out answer. A student who writes a correct answer, crosses it out and replaces it with a wrong one has a confidence problem rather than a knowledge problem, and that pattern is visible only on the paper itself.

Which is why the single most useful thing a Dubai family can do before hiring anyone is to ask the school for the marked scripts rather than the grades. Schools generally release them on request. Then put them in front of whoever you are considering hiring and watch what they do. A specialist will read them for pattern and name two or three components within ten minutes. Somebody who talks about the student's attitude instead has told you something useful about themselves.

sections.heading: Ranking repairs by the marks actually available
paragraphs: Once the baseline exists, the next decision is what to fix first, and the instinct is to fix whatever the student is most upset about. That is almost always wrong. The right ranking is by marks available divided by time required, and the ordering it produces is frequently counter-intuitive: the subject causing the distress is often fourth on the list, and the item at the top is something nobody had noticed.

Work it out explicitly. For each loss pattern identified in the baseline, write down roughly how many marks it accounted for across the paper and how long it would realistically take to address. Pace problems and command-word errors come out on top almost every time, because they account for a surprising number of marks and they take two or three sessions. Presentation and method come next. Topic content comes last, not because it does not matter but because it is the slowest and the most expensive per mark.

There is a second multiplier worth applying. Technique repairs transfer across subjects and content repairs do not. A student who learns to read command words correctly uses that in nine subjects; a student who learns electrolysis uses it in one. So on a ranked list, a technique item worth eight marks in Chemistry is really worth eight marks multiplied across the timetable, and that is usually enough to put it first even against a bigger single-subject content gap.

The practical form of this is a short written list with the marks beside each item, reviewed at six weeks and reordered. It stops a plan drifting into general revision, it makes the stop decision easy, and it gives a parent something concrete to ask about. The question to ask a tutor is not how is it going. It is which item are we on, and how many marks was it worth.

sections.heading: A term of checkpoints, each with something to show
paragraphs: Progress at IGCSE is not continuous and it is not smooth, which is why a parent checking in weekly learns less than a parent checking in at three fixed points with a defined artefact at each. The checkpoints that work in a Dubai school year are half term, the mock, and the period after the mock when there is still time to act. Each should produce a document rather than a conversation.

At half term the artefact is a repeat of the baseline component, marked the same way. Not a different paper and not a longer one; the same component so the comparison means something. The decision it supports is simple: are the marks on the targeted items moving. If they are, continue. If they are flat, change the target or change the tutor, and six weeks is early enough that either is still cheap.

At the mock the artefact is the school's own marked scripts, read for pattern rather than for grade. This is the richest single evidence point in the year and most families use only the headline number from it. The decision it supports is the ranked repair list for the remaining weeks, which should be shorter and more specific than the one made in September because there is now real data from a full set of papers under real conditions.

After the mock the artefact is a timed component on the highest-ranked item, done and marked within a fortnight. The decision it supports is whether the remaining weeks go to that item or to the next one. By this stage the arithmetic is unforgiving and honesty matters more than encouragement: some components cannot be recovered in the time available, and a provider who says so is more useful than one who sells the hours anyway. Dates everything against the live official timetable for your centre's zone or series, since entry deadlines and papers are both fixed well in advance.

sections.heading: Reading a mock against boundaries that have not been set
paragraphs: Mock results arrive in Dubai schools in the winter and produce more bad decisions than any other document in the IGCSE year. The problem is that a mock grade looks like a prediction and is not one. Grade boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each live series and published afterwards, and they move between series. A school marking mocks has to use some boundary, usually a previous year's, and that choice changes the grade without changing the script.

So read the marks, not the grade. A student who is three marks below a boundary and a student who is fifteen marks below are in completely different positions, and both appear in a report as the lower grade. The first is a technique and accuracy problem measured in a handful of marks and is the best value intervention available anywhere in this market. The second needs content work and more time. Treating them the same is how families spend a term on the wrong student.

Read across subjects too. A mock set is nine data points produced under the same conditions in the same fortnight, which makes it the only chance in the year to see whether a problem is subject-specific or global. If papers are unfinished in six subjects out of nine, no amount of Chemistry teaching addresses it. If one subject is far out of line with the others, that subject has a specific cause and the rest of the timetable is evidence that the student can work.

Finally, be careful about what a mock cannot show. It cannot show how a student performs after a proper revision period, because mocks usually fall before one. It cannot show resilience across a three-week examination series. And it cannot show the effect of a change made after it. A mock is a snapshot of a particular fortnight, and its value is diagnostic rather than predictive. Use it to build the repair list and then stop looking at the grade.

sections.heading: What a school report and a KHDA inspection band each answer
paragraphs: Dubai families hold several documents that look like evidence about their child and mostly are not. Separating them is worth doing once, because each answers a different question and using the wrong one leads to a confident wrong conclusion.

The school report describes your child in the school's own language, is positive by convention, and is written for a file as well as for you. It is useful for one thing in particular, which is attitude and engagement information a parent cannot otherwise get. It is not useful for diagnosis, because it summarises rather than specifies, and a comment that a student should develop exam technique names a problem without locating it.

The KHDA inspection report describes the school, not your child. Dubai private schools are inspected on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the report says a great deal about provision, leadership and outcomes across a cohort. It is genuinely valuable when choosing a school and irrelevant to the question of whether your particular child's Chemistry marks are moving. Families regularly conflate the two, and a strong inspection band reassures them about something it does not measure.

A fourth document, where the school produces it, is the most useful of all: the marked script. Ask for them. Dubai schools generally release marked papers on request, and a set of them is worth more than every report the school will ever issue. And where a school administers externally marked benchmark assessments, ask which ones and when, because that answer varies between schools in this emirate and it determines what comparative data exists at all.

sections.heading: What a parent who was not in the room can actually check
paragraphs: This page answers a search for a home tutor, so the format question is really a question about supervision. The case usually made for a tutor in the house is that a parent can see what is happening. The case is weaker than it sounds, because what a parent can observe through a door is tone and engagement rather than teaching quality, and both of those are poor predictors of whether marks move.

What is checkable is the artefact. A session that ends with a timed question marked against the published scheme, dated, with the marks visible, can be audited by anyone at any time. A session that ends with a pleasant atmosphere and a general sense that things were covered cannot be audited by anybody, including the tutor. That distinction does not depend on where the tutor was sitting, and it is the only distinction this page cares about.

The in-home market in Dubai is real and large, and its published rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the journey folded in, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher working online. In-home lessons here are usually sold at ninety minutes rather than sixty, because a tutor who has crossed the city needs the session to justify the drive. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and we run no in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE. Every session here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

The honest losses of the online format belong on the page. Nobody is in the room to notice a phone, close a door or tidy a desk, so the study space has to be arranged once, deliberately. Handwritten working needs a document camera or a phone propped over the page. And bench technique for a practical test needs a laboratory, which we do not have and will not pretend to. Against that, the format makes the evidence trail easier rather than harder, because the work is shared on screen and the record exists by default rather than by discipline.

sections.heading: What nobody can evidence, and three claims that should worry you
paragraphs: A page about evidence has to be clear about the limits, because the claims that cannot be evidenced are exactly the claims this market makes most often. Three of them should stop a conversation.

The first is a promised grade. Nobody can offer one. Boundaries are set after each series by the awarding organisation and move between series, so a provider promising a particular grade, a promised number of marks, or money back tied to a result is pricing something outside their control. The second is a statistic without its arithmetic. Any percentage of students achieving anything, any average score, any satisfaction figure should come with how many students, over what period, measured how. Competitors in this market publish figures like a 4.9 rating from several hundred reviews on pages where the underlying reviews cannot be found, and in one case publish two different review totals in the same document.

The third is a credential nobody will put in writing. No tutoring provider in this market holds KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation simply by operating, and a phrase implying regulator endorsement is the most dangerous sentence available in this sector. What can be evidenced is specific: a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service with a stated two-working-day completion time. Since it costs nothing, ask to see it.

What also cannot be evidenced is work that is not the student's own. Where an IGCSE subject carries a non-examined component, the submission has to be the student's, and a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A provider offering to supply content for an assessed piece is offering the student a malpractice finding, and that risk sits with the student rather than with the provider that sold it. Our session records keep the student's words and the tutor's feedback visibly separate, which makes the boundary checkable rather than merely asserted.

process.title: Send the board, the code and any marked papers
process.description: The awarding organisation and syllabus code decide which past paper the baseline uses, and marked scripts from the school are the richest evidence available. Ask the school for them; Dubai schools generally release them on request and most families never ask.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces the baseline
process.description: One trial lesson per family, nothing to pay and no card required. The hour produces a timed component marked question by question, the unfinished fraction, the command-word error count and a short written diagnosis. You keep the document whether or not you continue.

process.title: A ranked repair list with marks beside each item
process.description: Not a revision timetable. A short list ordered by marks available divided by time required, with technique items weighted because they transfer across the whole timetable. You can ask at any point which item we are on and what it was worth.

process.title: Weekly sessions that leave a dated marked artefact
process.description: Every session ends with a piece of the student's own work carrying the marks, dated, plus one line on what moved. Over a term that is a sequence you can lay out side by side, which is the only honest way to see whether the plan is working.

process.title: A six-week review with a stop recommendation
process.description: We repeat the baseline component, marked identically, and compare. If the targeted marks are flat we say so and recommend changing the target, changing the tutor, or stopping. There is no automatic rollover into another block.

process.title: A mock post-mortem when the scripts arrive
process.description: We read the full set of mock scripts for pattern rather than grade, because nine papers produced in one fortnight is the only chance in the year to see whether a problem is global or subject-specific. The output is a shorter, more specific repair list for the remaining weeks.

whyPoints.title: A baseline before any teaching
whyPoints.description: A timed component marked question by question, the unfinished fraction and the command-word error count, recorded and dated before the first teaching session. Without it, nobody can honestly say at week six whether the money did anything.

whyPoints.title: Marks, not grades, as the unit of progress
whyPoints.description: Boundaries are set after each series and move between series, so a grade is a moving target and a mark on a named component is not. Three marks below a boundary and fifteen below are different problems, and we treat them differently.

whyPoints.title: Repairs ranked by yield
whyPoints.description: Marks available divided by time required, with technique items weighted because they transfer across eight or nine subjects. The subject causing the most distress at home is frequently fourth on the list, and saying so is part of the job.

whyPoints.title: A dated artefact from every session
whyPoints.description: A marked piece of the student's own work, every time, so a parent who was not in the room can audit the sequence rather than rely on an impression. A session that leaves nothing behind cannot be judged by anybody.

whyPoints.title: An explicit stop recommendation
whyPoints.description: At six weeks we compare against the baseline and recommend continuing, changing or stopping. No automatic rollover. Spend that drifts because nobody set a review date is the most common quiet failure in this market.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated rather than talked around
whyPoints.description: No promised grades, no statistics without their method, no claimed regulator accreditation. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in Dubai and holds no centre or office anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I know whether an IGCSE tutor is actually working?
faqs.answer: Compare a measurement with an earlier measurement of the same thing. Before any teaching, record a timed past-paper component marked question by question, how much of the paper was left unfinished, and how many questions were answered at the wrong command word. At six weeks, repeat the same component and mark it identically. The difference is a fact. Without that baseline the question cannot be answered at all, which is why so many Dubai families reach half term having spent real money and learned nothing about whether it helped.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's Dubai school for before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: The marked scripts, not the grades, and a written list of subject, awarding organisation, syllabus code and tier. Schools here generally release marked papers on request and most families never ask, which means the richest evidence available sits in a cupboard. Put the scripts in front of anyone you are considering hiring and watch what they do with them. A specialist reads them for pattern and names two or three components within ten minutes. Somebody who talks about attitude instead has told you something useful about themselves.

faqs.question: How much can an IGCSE grade realistically move in one term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on how far below a boundary the student currently sits, which is why marks are the honest unit and grades are not. A student a handful of marks short, losing those marks to pace or command-word errors, can move within a few weeks because those are training problems. A student fifteen or twenty marks short with losses spread across topics is looking at content work over a longer period. Nobody can promise a grade, because boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series and move between series.

faqs.question: What does my child's mock grade actually predict?
faqs.answer: Less than it appears to. Schools must mark mocks against some boundary, usually a previous year's, and boundaries move between live series, so the grade is a function of that choice as much as of the script. Read the marks instead. Also read across the whole mock set, because nine papers produced in one fortnight is the only chance in the year to see whether a problem is global or subject-specific. And remember a mock usually falls before any real revision period, so it is a diagnostic snapshot rather than a forecast.

faqs.question: My child says the sessions are going well but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat that as information rather than as a contradiction. It usually means the sessions are addressing something other than what the marks are losing, which is a targeting problem rather than a teaching one. Go back to the baseline, check which items were ranked top, and ask the tutor which item the last four sessions were on and how many marks it was worth. If the answer is general revision, the plan was never targeted. Changing the target component is cheaper and faster than changing the tutor, and should be tried first.

faqs.question: Is unmarked practice worth anything at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Very little, and sometimes less than nothing. A student who completes a past paper without marking it against the published scheme has rehearsed whatever they already do, including the errors, and has reinforced them. Worse, they have used up a paper that could have produced a measurement. Marking is the part that converts practice into information: it identifies which components lost marks and which error types produced the loss. If a budget is tight, fewer papers properly marked beats more papers done and filed.

faqs.question: Which single fix usually recovers the most IGCSE marks?
faqs.answer: Command-word reading, in most cases, because it costs marks in every subject at once. A student who answers describe when the question says explain, or explain when it says evaluate, loses a few marks per paper across eight or nine papers, and the fix is three to five sessions bought once and used everywhere. Pace is the other strong candidate where a paper is unfinished, since the marks left blank at the end are often the largest single block available. Both are training rather than teaching, which is why they are fast.

faqs.question: Should we fix the subject my child is most worried about?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and usually not first. Rank the repairs by marks available divided by time needed, and weight technique items because they transfer across the whole timetable. On that ordering the subject producing the most distress at home frequently comes fourth, and the top item is often something nobody had noticed, like an unfinished paper or a pattern of poor question selection. Fix the distress eventually, because it matters, but fix the cheap marks first. That is also the fastest way to change how a student feels about the subject.

faqs.question: How often should a tutor send a written update?
faqs.answer: Every session, and one line is enough: the component worked on, what the student produced, and what to attempt before next time, with the marked work attached. A monthly report written in general language is worse than nothing, because it looks like evidence and contains none. The test to apply is whether a stranger could read the sequence of notes and say what changed. If the notes describe effort and attitude rather than components and marks, they are not an audit trail and the plan cannot be judged from them.

faqs.question: Does a strong KHDA inspection rating mean my child is doing well?
faqs.answer: No. Dubai private schools are inspected on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the report describes the school's provision, leadership and cohort outcomes. It says nothing about one student's marks in one subject. Families conflate the two constantly, and a strong band is genuinely reassuring about something it does not measure. The documents that describe your child are the report, which summarises, and the marked scripts, which diagnose. Only the second one will tell you where the marks went.

faqs.question: What evidence should exist by the time we reach the mock series?
faqs.answer: A dated baseline from before the first session, a sequence of weekly marked pieces, and one repeat of the baseline component at around six weeks marked identically to the first. If all three exist you can read the mock as the fourth data point in a series rather than as a verdict out of nowhere. If none exists, the mock becomes the baseline by default, which works but costs you a term of information you could have had for the price of one hour in September.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a non-examined component without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be visible in the record. A tutor can teach the skills the component assesses, discuss the requirements, question the student's choices and give feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor must not supply content that ends up in the submission. The work has to be the student's own, and a provider offering otherwise is offering the student a malpractice finding rather than a grade. Our session records keep the student's words and the tutor's feedback separate so the boundary can be checked rather than taken on trust.

faqs.question: What should make me suspicious of a Dubai tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Three things. A promised grade or money back tied to a result, which cannot be delivered because boundaries are set after each series. A statistic without its sample size, period and method on the same page, which several providers in this market publish and none can substantiate. And any implication of KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, which no tutoring provider acquires by operating. What can be evidenced is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid for two years, and therefore reasonable to ask to see.

faqs.question: Can a parent in the next room tell whether teaching is any good?
faqs.answer: They can tell whether it is pleasant, which is a weak predictor of marks moving. What is actually checkable is the artefact: a timed question marked against the published scheme, dated, with the marks visible. That can be audited by anyone at any time, and it does not depend on where the tutor was sitting. The in-home format does have one real advantage here, which is that an adult in the room can notice a phone or close a door, and an online session cannot. The study space has to be set up once instead.

faqs.question: Why is the lesson online when I searched for a home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because that is the phrase parents use, and we would rather answer it plainly than let you find out after an enquiry. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and we run no in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE. Every session is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home market rate in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside it; the online qualified-teacher band runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300. Both figures are other providers' published rates.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Buy the baseline first, then decide
dubai/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Ask the school for the marked scripts and a written list of subject, board, code and tier. Send both. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with nothing to pay and no card required, and it produces the three baseline measures and a short written diagnosis that you keep whether or not you continue. From there you get a ranked repair list with the marks beside each item and a review date six weeks out. If the marks on the targeted items are flat at that review, we will tell you to change the target, change the tutor or stop.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE one-to-one online, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications, Core and Extended tiers. Rates are quoted per subject after a free trial lesson, because a Core Maths hour and an Additional Mathematics hour are not the same product and pretending otherwise produces a useless number.

intro.heading: One number, six things inside it
paragraphs: A tuition quote in Dubai arrives as a single hourly figure, which is why comparing two of them is so unreliable. AED 200 from one provider and AED 320 from another may be the same teaching with different marking attached, or entirely different teaching with the same marking, or one with a cancellation policy that costs you a session a month and one without. The hourly rate is a summary of at least six decisions, and the only way to compare quotes is to ask what each decision was.

The six are teaching time, travel, marking between sessions, reporting to parents, materials, and the terms around cancellation and commitment. For a visiting tutor, travel is often the largest hidden share: a journey across Dubai in the afternoon peak can be most of an hour each way, and somebody pays for it. For an online tutor the travel line disappears, which is a large part of why the published online bands sit below the published in-home ones in this market.

The published figures are worth setting out plainly, because three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all and two of the ones that do quote US dollars. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors ranging to AED 500, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market rates, attributed to whoever published them. They are not IB Gram's price list, and this page does not publish one, because an hourly figure that ignores the subject, the tier and the series is the kind of number that has to be revised in a phone call anyway. What IB Gram does publish is the delivery model: tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India.

That is stated at the top rather than buried, because this page is about fees and the honest version of the comparison is part of the fee discussion. The in-home market in Dubai is real, it charges what it charges for good reasons, and a family that wants a person in the room has a legitimate preference. What this page does is show you exactly which lines of the bill exist because of that preference, so the choice is made on arithmetic rather than on a provider's sales pitch.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees differ by stage more than most quotes admit, because the work differs. These are the four stages a Dubai family pays for across a British-curriculum school career, and what drives the price at each.

programmes.name: Years 8-9, before the IGCSE course
programmes.description: The cheapest hours in the whole sequence and often the best value, because the work is foundational and does not need specification knowledge. Shorter sessions, fewer of them, no exam deadline forcing the pace. Market rates sit at the lower end of the qualified band here, and a strong general teacher is genuinely sufficient.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools take in new arrivals across the year, so Year 9 classes contain children who have come from CBSE, an American curriculum or a different British scheme of work. The gaps are specific rather than general, which means a short diagnostic block is usually cheaper than a term of weekly sessions. Paying for twenty hours when six would have done is the commonest avoidable cost at this stage.

programmes.name: Year 10, first teaching of the course
programmes.description: Mid-band rates, and the stage where weekly work costs least per grade moved, because the tutor is fixing this week's lesson rather than rebuilding a year. The tier decision also sits here, and an evidenced opinion on Core versus Extended is worth several sessions on its own if it changes the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai entries are submitted months ahead of the papers, Year 10 is when a fee spent on diagnosis changes the outcome rather than merely improving it. A family that establishes in October that Extended is reachable has a different two years ahead of them than one that discovers it in March, and the hours required are substantially fewer.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: The most expensive hours, for two reasons that have nothing to do with teaching quality. Demand peaks from January into the summer series, and the tutors who know a specific paper's mark distribution are scarce at exactly that moment. Specialist and exam-year rates in this market run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter candidates across Cambridge's March, June and November series and Pearson's May/June and November series, so the demand peak is not one season but two or three overlapping ones. Booking a named specialist in September for a May series costs less and gets a better match than booking the same person in March, which is the single largest saving available in the exam year.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: Priced at the scarce end, because the work includes sequencing that a school would normally do and because few tutors handle private-candidate logistics. Entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the examination centre rather than to a tutor, and that amount is set by the centre, so it must be confirmed with the centre directly.
programmes.countryNote: A resit decision in Dubai is partly a calendar decision. Cambridge runs a March series as well as June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a student can often sit sooner than families assume. Entry deadlines sit months ahead: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 for exams running 3 February to 4 March 2027.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Subject is the biggest single driver of an IGCSE tuition quote in Dubai, and it is driven by scarcity rather than difficulty. These are the subjects families ask about, with what moves the fee in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in Dubai and therefore the most competitive rates. Expect the middle of the qualified band for Extended and the lower end for Core. The fee rises in the exam term because demand does, not because the teaching changes.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Scarce, and priced accordingly near the top of the specialist band. Few tutors who teach 0580 also teach 0606 properly, and the honest question is not what it costs but whether anyone available teaches it at a workable hour.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Upper-middle of the qualified band. A tutor who has marked the practical paper's answers charges more than one who has taught only theory, and for a Year 11 candidate that difference is usually worth paying because the practical losses are patterned and fixable.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Similar to Physics, with the mole work driving the value. A tutor who can diagnose mole weakness in one session saves hours of general revision, which is the clearest case in the sciences for paying mid-band rather than budget rates.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Mid-band and a deeper pool than the other sciences. Much of the work is command-term discipline rather than content, which is highly teachable, so a shorter block often produces more movement per dirham than a full year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0510)
subjects.description: Mid-band, with a deep pool in Dubai. Before paying for anything, confirm which route your child is entered for: a child on the wrong one of the two is capped or stretched administratively, and that is a free conversation with the school.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with a thinner pool than the sciences. The value sits in long-question technique, so sessions built around marked written work are worth more than sessions built around content recap, and should be priced as such.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Scarce in the form that matters. Programmers are plentiful; tutors who teach to the published pseudocode conventions are not, and that is the distinction the fee should reflect. Ask directly whether they have taught Paper 2 answers to those conventions.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Scarce, and complicated by the fact that the two routes are different courses. Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and schools are required to ensure teachers of Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach it.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Priced as one subject but containing three, which makes a diagnostic that separates performance by discipline unusually good value. Families often pay for general science tuition when the actual deficit is in one of the three.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: For a visiting tutor, the community a family lives in is a cost input: the journey is inside the fee and the dead time is paid for. These notes price that reality by area, and explain what disappears from the bill when delivery moves online.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Bluewaters
regions.note: Central and well connected, so travel is not the constraint; parking and tower access is. Visiting tutors commonly add time for building entry, and sessions start late because school buses arrive late. Online removes both the access delay and the surcharge.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Journeys crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road double in the afternoon peak, so a visiting tutor's round trip can exceed the teaching hour. This is where the travel share of an in-home fee is largest and where it buys a parent nothing.

regions.name: Mudon, Town Square, Dubailand and Dubai South
regions.note: Outlying communities where the pool of tutors willing to drive is thinnest and the surcharge highest. Requests for scarce specifications from these areas are the ones most likely to go unmatched locally, whatever fee is offered.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Villa communities with schools close by, so children are home early and a 16:00 start is realistic. Travel from the city centre is moderate, which keeps in-home quotes nearer the bottom of the published band than JVC quotes are.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Long internal distances inside the communities themselves, so a visiting tutor's journey does not end at the gate. Families here often want two subjects in one evening, which multiplies the travel cost in-home and costs nothing extra online.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Short school runs and the earliest feasible session starts in the city. Travel is cheap for a visiting tutor here, which is why in-home quotes for these addresses sit closest to online rates and the comparison is tightest.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC
regions.note: Easy to reach, hard to work in: the binding constraint is a room with a door that shuts rather than a journey. Any quote should be tested against where the session will actually happen, because a session in a shared living room is not the product.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense older districts with strong IGCSE Maths and science demand and a reasonable local tutor supply, so in-home rates here are more competitive than in the outlying communities. Session timing is built around Maghrib and family dinner.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Marina, Al Barsha and Tecom
schoolClusters.note: Large IGCSE cohorts with post-16 routes splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. Each school's published fee sits on its KHDA profile, which is the figure to use when putting tuition costs in proportion. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: British and Indian-curriculum provision side by side, with early home times and heavy demand for Maths and the sciences. Fee sensitivity is higher here and the local tutor supply is better, which keeps in-home quotes closer to the published floor.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Dubai Hills, the Ranches and Al Qudra
schoolClusters.note: Wide catchments and long internal journeys, several campuses running both post-16 routes. Families here most often book two subjects together, which is the scenario where the in-home travel multiple is most visible on an invoice.

sections.heading: What IGCSE home tutor fees in Dubai actually cover
paragraphs: An hourly tuition rate in Dubai is paying for six things, and providers bundle them differently. Teaching time is the obvious one. Travel is the one that only exists if someone drives. Marking of written work between sessions is the line most often absent from cheap quotes and most responsible for whether the hours achieve anything. Reporting to parents, materials, and the terms governing cancellation and commitment make up the rest. Two quotes that differ by AED 100 usually differ on marking and cancellation rather than on teaching.

The published market figures give the shape of each band. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors reaching AED 500, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, and at that level the hour is supervision rather than marked teaching. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier.

When you take a quote, ask for it line by line. Not what is your rate, but: is marking of written work included between sessions, how long is the session, what notice do you need for a cancellation, what happens if we stop after three sessions, and does the figure include VAT. A provider who answers all five in one message is quoting a product. A provider who answers only the first is quoting a number, and numbers in this market have a habit of acquiring extras later.

sections.heading: The travel line, priced by Dubai community
paragraphs: Travel is the part of an in-home fee that parents accept without pricing, and it is often the largest avoidable share. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Jumeirah Village Circle at 16:30 is not making a twenty-minute journey; in the afternoon peak that round trip can approach the length of the teaching session. Nobody absorbs that for free. It appears either as a higher hourly rate, as a minimum session length that makes the trip worthwhile, or as a tutor who takes only clients within a narrow radius.

The minimum-session effect is the one families notice last. A visiting tutor who will not travel for less than ninety minutes has, in practice, raised your weekly bill by fifty per cent regardless of whether your child needs ninety minutes. For a Year 9 student, sixty minutes of focused work is often more productive than ninety, and paying for the extra half hour because of a journey is paying for the journey. Online, session length is set by the student's attention rather than by a drive.

The second effect is on the pool. A tutor pool defined by a twenty-minute radius around Mudon is a very different pool from one defined by who teaches Cambridge 0606 at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time. For common subjects the local pool is deep enough that this hardly matters. For Additional Mathematics, Computer Science pseudocode work, Arabic as a first language, or a private candidate who needs sequencing as well as teaching, the radius is the binding constraint and no fee overcomes it.

sections.heading: Monthly packages and what a lock-in actually costs
paragraphs: Packages look like a discount and sometimes are. Monthly arrangements seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. The arithmetic is worth doing before you agree, because the effective hourly rate inside a package is sometimes higher than the provider's own advertised hourly figure.

The real cost of a package is rarely the rate. It is what happens to unused sessions. Dubai school calendars contain half terms, long weekends, school trips, study leave and examination periods, and a package month with four scheduled sessions and two usable weeks hands the provider the difference. Ask three questions before signing: do unused sessions roll over, is there an expiry, and what notice cancels the arrangement. A package with rollover and a month's notice is a convenience; one with expiry and a term's notice is a commitment with a discount attached.

There is also a quieter effect on behaviour. A family inside a twelve-month package stops asking whether the tuition is working, because the decision feels already made. The arrangements that produce results are the ones with a review point: a date at which comparable marked work either moved or did not, and at which continuing is an active choice. If a package removes that date, the discount is being paid for with the thing that made the spending accountable.

sections.heading: The extras that appear on the second invoice
paragraphs: Most unexpected tuition costs in Dubai are not dishonest; they are simply not mentioned in the first conversation because nobody asked. A short list covers almost all of them. Late-cancellation charges, where a session cancelled inside the notice period is billed in full. Minimum session lengths that raise the weekly cost. Separate charges for mock marking or for reading a piece of written work outside session time. Rate increases at the start of the exam term. Charges for a second child in the same household. Materials billed separately.

Two of these deserve particular attention. The first is exam-term pricing. Several providers in this market charge more from January onwards, which is defensible given demand, but a family that budgeted in September on an autumn rate finds the number rising at exactly the point they are least able to change tutor. Ask in September what the rate will be in February and get the answer in writing. The second is the second-child question: families with two children at IGCSE often assume a household discount exists, and where the sessions are separate one-to-one hours, usually it does not.

The VAT question needs care rather than confidence. Whether and how tuition is treated for UAE VAT is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and depends on the provider's circumstances, so this page does not state a treatment. What a parent can reasonably do is ask whether a quoted price includes VAT, ask for an invoice that shows the amount charged, and ask for the provider's tax registration number where VAT is being charged. A provider unable to answer those three questions is worth a second look for reasons beyond tax.
