sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in Dubai, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal, and a parent comparing providers is entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Two further points are worth knowing. First, no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting you a specific penalty amount is quoting something unverified. Second, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs an educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority for a training institute. That is a specific permit issued to specific premises, and it is the thing providers are describing when they call themselves approved by the authority. IB Gram does not hold it, does not claim it, and has no office in the UAE.

In Abu Dhabi a further rule applies that Dubai parents should still know about, because families move between emirates: press reporting on the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules describes school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. The practical reading for any family is simple - never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately, however convenient it looks.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is deliberately short. Tell us the subject, the board if you know it, the tier if you know that, the year group and the evenings that suit a Jumeirah 3 schedule. We match a tutor who teaches that specification, and the first lesson is a free trial with that tutor, taught on real syllabus content so you can judge the teaching rather than the sales pitch. No schedule is agreed until afterwards, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than asking you to give it another fortnight.

Availability is where most providers go quiet, so here is the honest position. Mainstream IGCSE subjects can usually be covered within a few working days. A narrow combination, or a request in the fortnight before mocks or the weeks before a written series, can take longer. When the right specialist has no slot we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same tutor, a specialist outside the UAE teaching the same board on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start with the work resequenced around the deadline that matters. Putting a generalist in front of a Year 11 candidate to fill a gap serves nobody.

A last word on what to send. The single most useful document is your child's statement of entry or option sheet, because it carries the syllabus codes. The second most useful is the most recent marked assessment, ideally the paper itself rather than the grade. With those two things a tutor can plan the first three sessions before the first one starts, which is otherwise a fortnight of discovery that you paid for.

process.title: Send the subject, board and tier
process.description: A short message with the subject, the board if you know it, the tier if that is decided, the year group and the evenings that work. If you have the statement of entry or the option sheet, the syllabus codes on it answer most of our questions before we ask them.

process.title: We match on specification, not location
process.description: Tutors are matched to the exact syllabus - Cambridge 0580 Extended rather than maths in general - because the papers are not interchangeable. Distance from Jumeirah 3 plays no part in the match, which is what widens the pool of genuine board specialists.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One lesson, taught on real syllabus content, with no schedule agreed beforehand. You and your child judge the explanation and the pace, then decide. If it is not right, we change the tutor; the risk of a poor match sits with us rather than with your term.

process.title: A block with a target written down
process.description: Sessions are booked as a block aimed at something nameable: a tier decision, a paper to finish in the time, a topic never secured. A target makes the block reviewable at the end, which an open-ended weekly arrangement never is.

process.title: Audit it after four weeks
process.description: Four weeks in, compare the marked work against the diagnostic paper from week one. If the gap has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does. We would rather have that conversation in November than in April, and so would you.

whyPoints.title: Board-first matching
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subject differently, from paper structure to how practical work is assessed. Matching on the specification rather than the subject name removes the first month of mutual discovery that a cross-board tutor otherwise needs.

whyPoints.title: The same answer across the coast
whyPoints.description: Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Jumeirah 1 share gates, traffic and rate quotes, so a provider claiming a bespoke neighbourhood solution is describing marketing rather than a difference. What changes between these communities is the drive, and an online slot removes it.

whyPoints.title: Rates with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to a published provider page or a dated Dubai cost table, quoted as a market band. We do not present market rates as our own prices, and we do not publish an invented price list to look competitive.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice from marked evidence
whyPoints.description: Whether a student should sit Extended or Core is answered from past papers marked against the published scheme, not from encouragement. Sometimes the useful answer is the less flattering one, and a provider that never gives it is not giving you information.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the permit position
whyPoints.description: We explain the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime and the separate training-institute permit for premises, and we state plainly that IB Gram holds no regulator approval and has no UAE office. Providers implying otherwise are making a claim that is checkable.

whyPoints.title: Boards' materials referenced, not redistributed
whyPoints.description: Specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and live on their sites. We point you to them and teach from them rather than handing out a folder of other people's documents, which is both a copyright question and a sign of how a provider works.

faqs.question: Would the answer be different if we lived in Umm Suqeim rather than Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all, and that is the useful finding. These two communities share the same coastal road network, draw on overlapping school gates, and get quoted the same rates by the same providers. The afternoon traffic profile is near identical, so a visiting tutor faces the same unpredictable drive from either address. What decides whether tutoring works in both places is the same pair of factors: a slot that survives a busy week, and a tutor matched to the correct examination board and tier. Only one real difference exists on this coast, which is that tuition centres inland around Al Quoz are a shorter trip from Al Manara and Al Safa.

faqs.question: How do I find out which International GCSE board my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, subject by subject, and ask for it in writing. The definitive document is your child's statement of entry, which lists the syllabus code for every entry: four digits such as 0580 or 0625 for Cambridge, and codes such as 4MA1 or 4PH1 for Pearson Edexcel. Those codes let you find the correct specification and past papers on the board's own website, and they let a tutor confirm in one line that they teach the right course. Boards can differ between subjects within one school, so a single answer for the whole timetable is usually incomplete.

faqs.question: What actually differs between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Paper structure, practical assessment and tier naming, mostly. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended and assesses science practical skills through a separate practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson Edexcel examines practical understanding inside its written papers and splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Question stems, diagram conventions and mark-scheme wording differ enough that revising with the wrong board's past papers is actively unhelpful. The content overlap is large, which is why a cross-board tutor sounds convincing in a first lesson and then costs a student marks in a real paper.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for the Core tier or the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: The school decides, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11, from the evidence it has. The lower tier covers less content and caps the maximum grade; the upper tier covers more and leaves the full range available. The decision can be changed up to the board's entry deadline, which is why the mock period is the moment to raise it. A focused block on the topics that separate the tiers can move a borderline student up. A student who would not finish the upper-tier papers is better served by a secure result on the lower tier.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE tutor cost for a family on the Jumeirah coast?
faqs.answer: Market figures published by Dubai providers in 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, a visiting tutor at the home at roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed, and specialist examination-year tutors at AED 200 to 450 or more. Budget online options advertise from AED 45 to 65, and one premium named tutor is quoted at AED 650. Those are the market's numbers with their sources, not our price list. If a quote sits outside those bands, ask what explains it before you accept or dismiss it.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor who travels to the villa charge more per hour?
faqs.answer: Because the hour you book is not the only hour the tutor spends. A journey across this part of Dubai in the afternoon peak can take forty to ninety minutes each way, and that time has to be paid for somewhere. In the published Dubai bands it shows up as a higher hourly rate for in-home work than for the same tutor teaching online. The other place it shows up is the start time: a session scheduled at 4:30pm on a route with three stops often begins later than booked. Removing the journey removes both costs at once.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count for British-track equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market publishes six, which is the sort of error that leads a family to carry a subject it did not need. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry and the emirate attestation channels, so verify the current rule with them before planning around it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards those five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The reporting on the Ministry's requirements is explicit that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. They remain mandatory at school in Dubai under the published guidance from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which requires them regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so a child takes them and they occupy timetable periods. They simply do not count towards the equivalency total. That distinction is worth confirming with your school when option blocks are set, because it affects how many other accredited subjects your child needs to carry.

faqs.question: Does booking an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah 3 mean a tutor arrives at our villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We target the phrase because it is what parents in Dubai search, and we would rather answer it in the first screen than bury the answer. Our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and home visits in Dubai are not a service we offer; the visiting model is one we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The benefit is a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code your child sits, and an evening start that does not depend on the beach road clearing in time.

faqs.question: Can my child sit different subjects with different examination boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many Dubai schools do exactly that, entering maths with one board and the sciences with another. It is decided by the school rather than the family. The practical consequence for tutoring is that each subject needs its own board-specific preparation, including the right past papers, and that revision resources have to be checked individually rather than bought as a set. When you ask us for help in two subjects, we confirm the board for each separately, because assuming one answer covers the whole timetable is how the wrong papers end up in a revision folder.

faqs.question: When are International GCSE examinations actually held, and which series will my child sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also operates a March series: for March 2027 the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series your child sits is set by the school, so confirm it with them and use the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the choice is genuinely open. The content built in Year 10 is what Year 11 papers assume, and the tier decision is made on Year 10 and early Year 11 evidence, so support in that window influences which papers are available at the end. Starting in Year 11 is still worthwhile and is when most families actually begin, but the work becomes triage: choosing the components where effort converts into marks and accepting that some topics will not be rebuilt. The worst time to start is after the final entry deadline has fixed a tier nobody intended.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if lessons are taught online?
faqs.answer: Practical work itself happens at school, where the equipment and the supervision are. What a tutor can do online is prepare the examined element, and that differs by board: Cambridge candidates face either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards rehearsed technique, correct tabulation, graph plotting and uncertainty handling. Pearson Edexcel candidates meet practical understanding inside the written papers, which rewards knowing method and sources of error. Both are taught well through worked examples, past-paper practical questions and marking against the published scheme. Neither requires a tutor standing beside a bench.

faqs.question: What should I send so the first lesson is not spent on discovery?
faqs.answer: Two documents do most of the work. The statement of entry or option sheet, because it carries the syllabus codes and the tier, and the most recent marked assessment, ideally the script itself rather than the reported grade. With those, a tutor can plan the first three sessions before the first one begins. Add the school's next internal deadline and the mock window if you have them. Families who send nothing usually pay for a fortnight of the tutor working out what the school has already written down, which is the easiest waste to avoid.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingBody: You have the rate bands with their sources, the board differences with their syllabus codes, the tier decision and who makes it, the equivalency rule with the five-subject figure, and the permit position for every kind of tutor. The last comparison is the one only your child can make: does this tutor explain things in a way that lands. Send us the subject, the board, the tier and the evenings that work for a Jumeirah 3 week, and we will match a specialist and set up a free trial lesson taught on real syllabus content. Lessons run one-to-one online on Gulf Standard Time, and nothing is booked until after that first session.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects to Dubai students over live video. Each is listed with the syllabus codes they work on, because 0580 and 0607 are different courses and a tutor who has only taught one of them will tell you so.

intro.heading: The money question, answered before the sales pitch
paragraphs: A family on Palm Jumeirah deciding to hire an IGCSE home tutor is weighing a recurring cost against an uncertain benefit, usually in a hurry, usually with incomplete information. The incomplete information is not an accident. Of the best-ranking pages researched for this project, three publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. One agency's own frequently asked questions ask what tutoring costs and then decline to answer.

So here are the dirham figures, taken from providers' own public pages in October 2026 and attributed to each. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase lists AED 270. The Bestimate Dubai rate guide puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, with individual home tutors advertising up to AED 500. BartyED sits at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

Those numbers describe the market, not an IB Gram price list. We quote per student after a free trial lesson and a short diagnostic, because an hourly rate quoted before anybody has seen the child's marked work is a guess dressed up as a price. What this page can do is make the spread legible: why one hour costs five times another, which part of the higher number is teaching and which part is a car on the Palm trunk at 6pm, and where families routinely pay for something that was never going to move a grade.

The waste patterns are consistent and expensive. A group class bought for a diagnosed individual gap. Two hours booked because a travelling tutor has a two-hour minimum, when the child's concentration runs out at sixty-five minutes. A term of weekly sessions started without anybody establishing what was wrong, so the first six hours go on revisiting topics the student already had. Past-paper drilling with no marking against the published mark scheme, which teaches a student to be faster at the same mistakes. And the one nobody expects: paying for a tutor who does not know which board the school entered the child for.

The rest of the page works through all of it. There is a rate table by level and format, a breakdown of where the money inside a single hour actually goes, a Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel comparison with syllabus codes because the board changes the work, the cost of tuition set beside Dubai school fees and the KHDA fee freeze, a list of questions to ask before any money moves, and an honest account of how to buy fewer hours rather than more. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; Palm Jumeirah families are taught one-to-one over live video, which is also why no part of the hour you pay for is spent driving.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah families sit their children in schools that pick their own qualification routes, and the route decides both the work and the cost. These are the three stages where island parents most often start paying for support, with what each one demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by Cambridge International in a June series and a November series, with syllabus codes that identify the exact course: 0580 for Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 English as a First Language. Many subjects are tiered, so the school's decision between Core and Extended entry sets the grade ceiling. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the zone determines which version of the timetable applies.
programmes.countryNote: For a Palm Jumeirah family the cost consequence of tiering is the one worth understanding. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades whatever the tutoring spend, so money spent on a Core candidate buys security rather than a higher ceiling. The conversation with the school about tier, usually in Year 10, is worth more than a term of sessions and costs nothing.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international qualification, examined in May/June and November each year, with its own codes: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Papers, tiering and content differ from the Cambridge equivalent even where the subject name matches, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so dates can be revised before they are final.
programmes.countryNote: Island families with children in two different schools frequently have two different boards in the same house. That is a real budgeting issue: the same subject at the same level needs a tutor who knows the specific board's papers, and buying one tutor for both children only works if that tutor genuinely covers both. Ask for the code, not the subject name.

programmes.name: The post-16 decision and the year before it
programmes.description: The IGCSE year ends in a choice between A Levels and the IB Diploma, and the grades obtained decide which doors stay open. Several Dubai schools set subject-specific entry requirements for their own sixth form. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five.
programmes.countryNote: The cost argument for support in Year 11 rather than Year 12 is simple: a grade recovered at IGCSE is cheaper than a subject repeated or a sixth-form place lost. Families who spend in Year 11 tend to spend less in total. Equivalency rules should always be checked on the Ministry's own channels, and no IB points threshold should be relied upon from a secondary source.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Palm Jumeirah families most often pay for, with the syllabus code where it identifies the course and the specific thing that usually needs fixing. The code matters because it tells a tutor which papers your child will actually sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in Dubai and the one where tier choice decides the ceiling. Extended papers reward algebraic fluency and multi-step problems; marks go missing on method not shown and on questions that need a worded conclusion. A diagnostic on one past paper tells you more than three weeks of general revision.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606) and International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for a demanding post-16 maths route, often as a bridge to Higher Level. The content is substantially harder than 0580 and the tutoring market for it is thinner, so expect a smaller pool and plan earlier. Confusing 0580, 0606 and 0607 when booking is a common and expensive mistake.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits are where most Dubai students lose marks, followed by anything requiring a rearranged equation under time pressure. Practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory, which means they can be taught online with paper questions and graph work.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations and organic nomenclature account for a large share of dropped marks. Students who have learned definitions without practising calculation score inconsistently. Marking one paper against the published mark scheme usually reveals whether the problem is content or precision.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: High content volume tempts families into buying more hours than the subject needs. The marks are usually lost to command-word errors and to answers that describe when they should explain. Structured recall practice between sessions is what makes the paid hour worth paying for.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653, 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into fewer papers, often taken by students who will not continue sciences post-16. The budget question here is whether to hire one tutor across all three, which works only if the tutor genuinely teaches all three at this level rather than one well and two approximately.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension and directed writing carry the marks, and both are technique-led rather than knowledge-led. This is the subject where a small number of well-marked practice pieces outperforms a long weekly commitment, which makes it one of the cheapest grades to move.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: A different qualification from first-language English with different papers and a speaking component. Island households with more than one home language sometimes discover mid-year that the child has been entered for the wrong one of the two, which is worth confirming with the school before spending anything.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Definitions and diagrams earn the early marks; the longer responses need application to the case material and a judgement at the end. Most tutoring time is spent on content when it should be spent on structuring eight and twelve-mark answers against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Two very different subjects routinely confused when booking. Computer Science rewards algorithmic thinking and pseudocode discipline; ICT is practical and application-based. Paying for a tutor in the wrong one of the two is a mistake families usually notice at the second session.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsTitle: Palm Jumeirah by address, and what each part does to a tutoring budget
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: The island is not one place for logistics, and logistics are what a travelling tutor charges you for. Here is what each part of Palm Jumeirah means for the cost and the timing of support.

regions.name: The fronds
regions.note: Sixteen residential spurs reached one at a time from the trunk, with no through route between them. A tutor driving to a villa here adds the frond itself to the journey each way, which is exactly the time an in-home rate is built to recover.

regions.name: The trunk and Golden Mile
regions.note: Apartment living with the shortest run to the mainland and the easiest parking. Families here most often compare online sessions against a tuition centre in Al Sufouh or Dubai Marina rather than against a home visit.

regions.name: The Crescent
regions.note: The outer breakwater, furthest from the mainland by road and the slowest address to reach in evening traffic. Travel is the single largest hidden cost in any in-home quote taken here.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The first district off the trunk and the nearest concentration of tuition centres and campuses. Worth pricing as the realistic alternative to online if a family wants a room outside the house.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: A dense centre and freelance-tutor market immediately south of the trunk, which is why Palm families see a wide spread of advertised rates for apparently identical hours. Compare what is included, not the headline figure.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition actually costs around Palm Jumeirah
paragraphs: An IGCSE hour in Dubai sells for anything between about AED 33 and AED 650, and the spread is not mostly about quality. It is about who the tutor is, whether anybody is travelling, and how the provider has packaged the hour. The table below sets the bands out by what you are buying rather than by brand, with the published source for each figure and the month it was read.

Read the in-home line carefully. The Bestimate Dubai rate guide puts home visits at AED 180 to 350, and individual home tutors advertise up to AED 500, but those numbers include a journey, and on Palm Jumeirah the journey is long by Dubai standards: one road onto the trunk and then a single frond with no through route. A tutor pricing a Crescent villa at 6pm is pricing roughly ninety minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. Nobody absorbs that for free.

The monthly figures are the ones families misread most often. A package at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is roughly AED 100 a session. A package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour with travel inside it. Those are not competing offers for the same thing; they are eight hours against eight hours at very different prices, with different amounts of the fee going to teaching. The Bestimate guide's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Where the money goes inside a single hour
paragraphs: Two invoices for sixty minutes can contain completely different things, and the difference is where a family's budget leaks. The table below opens up the hour. It is the most useful comparison on this page, because once you can see what each format pays for, the headline rate stops being the number that matters.

The honest summary is that an in-home hour on Palm Jumeirah spends a substantial part of its value on logistics, and an unmarked online hour spends a substantial part of its value on nothing much at all. Marking is the part parents forget to ask about. A tutor who marks a student's written work against the published mark scheme between sessions has done the work that makes the next session useful, and that work costs them time whether or not it is itemised on your invoice. If it is not happening, you are paying for conversation.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so the first column is here as market context rather than as an offer. What we do sell is the online column: a specialist's hour with marking done outside it, no travel priced into it, and a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot that survives a busy term on the island. The reason for publishing this breakdown is that it is the argument against our own highest-margin option, and that tends to be the kind of comparison worth reading. Nothing in the breakdown is confidential, and any provider on the island could publish the same table. The ones that do not are usually the ones whose arithmetic does not survive it.

sections.heading: The five ways island families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: These are not hypothetical. They are the patterns that recur in conversations with families who have already spent a term's budget before they call. Each one is avoidable with a question asked earlier.

The first is buying a term before diagnosing a problem. Six weekly hours disappear into revisiting material the student already had, because nobody established what was actually missing. The second is buying group classes for an individual gap: a group is good value for coverage and poor value for a specific weakness, since the pace cannot bend to one student. The third is buying time instead of marking. A student who completes five past papers that nobody marks against the published scheme has practised their existing mistakes five times.

The fourth is paying for travel without meaning to. An in-home rate that looks like a premium for expertise is often a premium for the drive onto the frond, and the two-hour minimum attached to it buys a second hour the child's concentration cannot use. The fifth is the quiet one: paying for a tutor who does not know which board the school entered the child for. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different question styles, and a term of excellent teaching on the wrong one is a term of nearly useful work. Ask for the syllabus code at the first conversation, and if the tutor does not ask you for it, that is information too.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and why the board changes the bill
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised that "IGCSE Maths" is not one thing. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel run separate qualifications with separate codes, papers and tiering, and a school chooses per subject, which means one child can sit both boards in the same year. The cost consequence is direct: tutoring hours are only efficient when the practice material matches the papers the student will actually sit.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson's International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

There is a worked example of why entry deadlines sit months before the exams. For Cambridge's March 2027 series, the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. A family budgeting for support needs to plan against the entry deadline, not the exam date, because the tier a student is entered for is fixed at that point and no amount of later spending changes the grade ceiling. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and what a term of support is next to them
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment at 37 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. On 22 May 2026 KHDA confirmed there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate is adding seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment grew by 6 per cent.

That context matters for a budgeting conversation. School fees are the fixed cost and they are not rising this year; tutoring is the discretionary cost and it is the one families can size deliberately. A single weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at the market's AED 150 to 300 band is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 across a four-week month, which lines up with the Bestimate guide's own mid-band monthly estimate. An exam-year specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above lands nearer AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more.

Set against that, the cheapest intervention available to a Palm Jumeirah family costs nothing: a conversation with the school about which tier a child is entered for, and which board. A student moved from Core to Extended entry in Year 10 has had their grade ceiling raised without a dirham changing hands. A student left on Core while a parent spends AED 1,200 a month on tuition has paid for security, not for a higher grade. We would rather you spent the free thing first. On exam entry fees as a private candidate, ask the exam centre directly; those are set by the centre and we do not publish a figure we have not verified.

sections.heading: What to ask before any money moves
paragraphs: A short list of questions separates a priced service from a vague one, and all of them can be asked in a first conversation or a trial lesson. None of them require you to know the subject.

Ask which syllabus code the tutor will teach from, and whether they have taught that code before. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and what a lesson's length actually is. Ask whether marking of written work between sessions is included, and what you will see of it. Ask what happens if you stop after one session, and what happens if the match is wrong. Ask whether the figure quoted includes value added tax, and treat any general statement about the tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE with care unless it cites the Federal Tax Authority. Ask where the tutor is based and which time zone sessions run in.

Two more that are specific to this market. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit: it is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, so a tutor charging you for it is charging for something that costs nothing. And ask any provider claiming a regulator's approval to show the permit number. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and operates no premises in the UAE. A service that implies otherwise is making a claim, and a claim should be evidenced before you pay it.

sections.heading: Spending early is cheaper than spending late
paragraphs: The most expensive tutoring in Dubai is the kind bought in the last six weeks before a series. Not because rates rise, though specialist availability tightens and choice narrows, but because late support can only do technique work. Content gaps need weeks the calendar no longer has, so the same money buys a smaller result.

Counting backwards from a June series, the useful shape is a diagnostic in the autumn term, weekly work through the winter on whatever the diagnostic found, and a short block of timed paper practice in the final weeks. For a November entry the same shape compresses into a shorter window, which is why November candidates should start earlier in relative terms, not later. Cambridge's own worked March 2027 example makes the point: final entries closed on 27 November 2026 for exams beginning 3 February 2027, so the decisions that bound a grade were taken ten weeks before the first paper.

Ramadan sits inside the Dubai academic year and changes when revision realistically happens. Sessions move later in the evening, often after Iftar, and many families prefer shorter slots for the month. Planning for that in advance is free; discovering it in week two of the month costs you sessions. The same is true of the island's own rhythm: Palm Jumeirah households travel more than the Dubai average over long holidays, and a tutor who knows the plan can set independent work around it rather than billing for a slot nobody attends.

sections.heading: Starting small, and buying only what the diagnosis asks for
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing: tell us the subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the school and what the last marked piece of work said. That is enough to propose a named tutor who has taught that code, and to say honestly whether the problem looks like a content gap, a technique gap or a workload gap. Those three need different amounts of money spent on them.

The second step is the free trial lesson. Use it to ask the questions in the list above and to watch whether the tutor works from your child's marked paper or from a generic worksheet. If the fit is wrong, say so and the tutor changes; there is nothing to argue about, because the point of a free trial is that the decision is made before money moves. If the fit is right, start with the smallest sensible commitment rather than a term, and review it at six sessions against the written gap list.

The honest limits, stated here rather than discovered later. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; Palm Jumeirah lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Some subjects and codes, particularly 0606 and 0607 and the less commonly taken IGCSE options, have a thinner specialist pool and may take a week or more to match, and in the weeks before a series they may not be available at your preferred hour at all. We will tell you that before you pay rather than after, because a family that has bought the wrong thing has lost both the money and the weeks.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour around Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik for budget online platforms, from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists in the Bestimate Dubai guide, and AED 650 at BartyED at the premium end. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 in that guide, with listings up to AED 500, because the hour includes a journey. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices; ours follow a free trial lesson and a short diagnostic.

faqs.question: Why would one tutor charge five times what another charges for the same hour?
faqs.answer: Three things explain almost all of the spread. Who is teaching: a university student on a platform and a specialist who has taught the syllabus for a decade are not the same product. Whether anybody is travelling: an in-home rate recovers the drive, and on Palm Jumeirah that drive is long. And what is included beyond the hour: marking written work against the published mark scheme takes the tutor time outside your session, and a rate that does not fund it will not include it. Ask which of the three you are paying for.

faqs.question: Is an online hour genuinely cheaper than a home visit on the island?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is logistics rather than quality. The Bestimate Dubai guide puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and qualified online tutors at AED 150 to 300, and the in-home figure carries a round trip plus a frequent two-hour minimum. For a villa on a frond or the Crescent, a tutor is pricing something like ninety minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so for Palm Jumeirah the comparison is settled: lessons run one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way families here waste tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Buying a term before anybody has diagnosed the problem. The first six weekly hours then go on revisiting material the student already had, because nobody established what was missing. Two diagnostic sessions working through marked school assessments and a timed past-paper section tell you whether the gap is content, technique or workload, and those three need very different amounts of money. Families who buy the diagnostic first reliably buy fewer hours overall, which is the only honest reason for a tutoring service to recommend it.

faqs.question: Does the board my child sits change what tutoring should cost?
faqs.answer: It changes what the hours are worth rather than the headline rate. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different question styles and tiering, so practice material must match the code the school entered your child for. A term of excellent teaching against the wrong board's papers is a term of nearly useful work. Ask the school's exams officer for the code before you book anything, and if a tutor does not ask you for it in the first conversation, treat that as information about the tutor.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a group class or one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: Group classes are good value for coverage and poor value for a specific weakness, because the pace cannot bend to one student. If your child is broadly fine and needs structured revision alongside others, a centre-based group in Al Sufouh or Dubai Marina may be the cheaper sensible option. If a diagnostic has identified a particular gap, such as moles in 0620 or algebraic manipulation in 0580, a group will teach around it rather than through it. Pay for individual attention where the problem is individual.

faqs.question: Is marking of my child's written work included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer varies and it is the part families forget. A tutor who marks past-paper answers against the published mark scheme between sessions is doing the work that makes the next session useful, and that takes their time whether or not it appears on an invoice. If nobody is marking, your child is practising their existing mistakes repeatedly and getting faster at them. At IB Gram marking between sessions is part of the work rather than an itemised extra, and you should see the marked scripts.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: The published rates do not move much, but availability does, and that costs you in a different currency. In the weeks before a June or November series the specialists who have taught a given syllabus code for years are booked at exactly the hours Palm Jumeirah families want, which are weekday evenings. Choice narrows, and late support can only do technique work because content gaps need weeks the calendar no longer has. The same money buys a smaller result, which is the real late-booking premium.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and how should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the figure quoted is the figure you will pay, and get the answer in writing. We will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's opinion, and several competitor pages assert it anyway. The useful question for a parent is narrow: is this quote inclusive, and is there any other charge. Treat a provider that cannot answer that clearly as a provider whose invoices will also be unclear.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a tutor who comes to the villa instead?
faqs.answer: If having somebody physically in the room is what your child needs, that is a legitimate reason to pay the in-home premium, and the Dubai market serves it at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Be clear about what you are buying: a long drive onto a frond or the Crescent, often a two-hour minimum, and less flexibility when a school deadline moves. IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Dubai, so we are not the service for that preference, and we would rather say so than take the booking.

faqs.question: How many hours should I budget for one weak IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Most families settle at one hour a week on one subject for a term, which is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the Bestimate guide's mid band, and then taper. A diagnosed technique problem can need as little as four to six well-marked sessions. A genuine content gap across two years of a course needs longer and should start earlier. Anybody quoting a package before seeing marked work is quoting a guess, and more hours never substitute for independent practice between them.

faqs.question: Is a cheap platform tutor ever the right purchase?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, platform tutoring is a reasonable way to buy homework supervision, confidence and practice routine for a Year 9 or lower Year 10 student. It is the wrong purchase for an Extended-tier Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a paper, where you are paying for assessment-level knowledge of a specific syllabus code. Match the spend to the job: the error is not buying cheap, it is buying cheap for a problem that needs a specialist.

faqs.question: Are school fees in Dubai going up, and how does that affect this decision?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven private schools and 16,846 places. For a family, that means the fixed cost is stable this year and the discretionary tutoring cost is the one to size deliberately, rather than treating both as rising together.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing I can do that might actually change the grade?
faqs.answer: Talk to the school about the tier and the board. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however much tutoring is bought, so a tier conversation in Year 10 can raise a ceiling for nothing. Second cheapest: get one past paper marked properly against the published scheme, which usually reveals whether the problem is knowledge or technique. Both cost almost nothing and both change what you should spend afterwards. We would rather a family did these first and bought fewer hours as a result.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if we stop after one session?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is free and carries no obligation, so stopping after it costs nothing. Beyond that, start with the smallest sensible commitment rather than a term, and use the six-session review to decide whether hours go up, down or stop entirely. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and most providers never mention it. We would rather resize honestly at session six than keep a weekly slot running because it is already in the calendar and nobody has looked at it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The IGCSE specialists Springs families ask for most are Mathematics at Extended and Higher tier, the three separate sciences, English First Language and English as a Second Language, and Economics or Business Studies. Each is matched by board and syllabus code before anything else is discussed.

intro.heading: Nearby is easy to check. Knowing the paper is not.
paragraphs: There are a lot of people within fifteen minutes of The Springs who will teach your child maths. There are considerably fewer who can tell you, without looking it up, that Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended is examined on two papers with a calculator allowed on one of them, that Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 Higher tier splits the content differently across its two papers, and that a student entered for the wrong tier has a grade ceiling they cannot climb above no matter how well they perform. The gap between those two groups is the real subject of this page.

Proximity is a proxy, and it is a weak one. A parent in Springs 4 asking neighbours for a recommendation gets a shortlist of people who live nearby and are willing to drive at five in the afternoon. That is a perfectly sensible way to find somebody to supervise homework. It is a poor way to find somebody who has marked Paper 4, knows which command words carry method marks, and can look at a mock script and say which of the eight lost marks were content and which were technique.

The honest version of the answer is that IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Springs address. In-home visits in the UAE are not part of what we sell; that service exists only in our India operation. UAE tutoring is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the same tutor each week, work shared on screen, and sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason to prefer that is not the saved journey. It is that the shortlist becomes everyone who teaches 0580 Extended rather than everyone who teaches 0580 Extended and lives near Emirates Living.

First, though, you need to know what your child is actually entered for, and a surprising number of families do not. Two schools on the same bus route from The Springs can run different boards for the same subject. Some schools split boards by department, so maths is Pearson and the sciences are Cambridge. Tiering decisions are made by the school, sometimes without a conversation. The statement of entry, not the textbook cover, is the document that settles it.

So this page is built as a diagnosis rather than a sales pitch. How to find the syllabus code in ten minutes. What differs between Cambridge and Pearson for the same subject, with the codes side by side. The questions to ask a prospective tutor and what a weak answer sounds like. Where marks are actually lost, subject by subject. What the Dubai market charges, attributed. And what to do if your child is in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because the right plan is not the same.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: An IGCSE page needs three stages in view at once: the years that build the foundation, the two years that are examined, and the post-sixteen route the grades open. Springs families usually arrive at the middle one in a hurry and discover the first one mattered.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external grades, which is why this stage gets neglected and why so much IGCSE repair work traces back to it. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, sat in March, May and October, as an external read on where a cohort actually is. Algebra fluency, scientific notation, graph reading and extended writing are the four things that decide how hard Year 10 feels.
programmes.countryNote: A Springs household with a Year 8 child has the cheapest possible intervention available: one session a week on algebraic manipulation for two terms removes most of what later becomes a crisis in Year 11. It is also the stage where families discover whether their school will enter the child for Core or Extended, which is worth asking about well before the decision is made.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined in a June or a November series. Most subjects are tiered: Core covers grades C to G in the legacy scale, Extended reaches the top grades. Papers carry named components with fixed weightings, and the syllabus document for each code lists exactly what is assessable. Nothing outside it can be examined, which makes the syllabus the single most useful document a parent can read.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in before building a revision calendar from a PDF found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board several schools near The Springs use, with its own codes, its own paper structures and its own tiering. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November each year. Some Pearson qualifications are structured so that units can be sat in different series, which changes revision planning in a way Cambridge's structure does not.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for a Springs family is that a tutor who taught Cambridge for ten years is not automatically fluent in Pearson's mark schemes, and the reverse is equally true. We ask for the code before proposing anybody. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan from the live document on its site rather than from a date on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC afterwards
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the entry currency for whatever comes next, and the thresholds are set by the receiving school rather than by the board. Most Dubai sixth forms ask for a minimum grade in the subject a student wants to continue, often a 6 or a 7 for Higher Level or A Level sciences and maths. A grade 5 in Year 11 maths closes some doors quietly.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools near Emirates Living run IGCSE at sixteen and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. Families should find out which route their school offers before Year 11 subject conversations, because an IB Diploma entry needs a broader grade spread than three strong A Level subjects do.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Springs families request most, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes where both are commonly taught in Dubai. Ask a prospective tutor which of these they have actually taught, and notice whether they answer with a code or with a topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in Dubai and the one where tiering matters most. Extended and Higher tier questions in the last third of each paper demand multi-step reasoning rather than recall. Most lost marks sit in algebraic manipulation, bearings and vectors, and in failing to show the method a mark scheme is looking for before writing an answer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts as a bridge towards A Level or Diploma mathematics. It introduces calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities earlier than the standard syllabus. Students who coast through 0580 often meet their first real difficulty here, and it is a good predictor of how Higher Level maths will feel.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism generate most requests, closely followed by waves. Students can usually recite formulae and cannot explain the physics the formula describes, which is exactly what the longer questions test. Practical assessment arrangements differ by board and by centre, so check whether your child sits a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry are where grades are made and lost. The qualitative analysis and ionic-equation questions reward precision in wording that students treat as optional. Extended-tier content on electrolysis and rates of reaction needs deliberate question practice rather than re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the difficulty. Marks are lost through imprecise terminology and through answers that describe when the command word asked for an explanation. Data and graph interpretation questions carry a meaningful share of the paper and are routinely attempted without reading the axes or the units.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: The double or single award route taken where a school does not run three separate sciences. The content is a genuine subset of the separate syllabuses, which means a tutor must know exactly which sections are excluded. Teaching from a separate-science textbook wastes a student's time on material that cannot be examined.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing carry most of the risk. Students lose marks by summarising a passage rather than analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and by writing in a register the task did not ask for. The improvement here is technique rather than vocabulary, which makes it one of the fastest subjects to move.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language, with different expectations and a speaking component. Many Dubai students are entered for it appropriately and some are entered for it defensively, which can cap what a sixth form will accept later. Worth checking which one your child is sitting and why.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the hidden mark-earner: a correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram carries marks that a paragraph of prose cannot replace. Students lose marks by defining terms loosely and by giving evaluation that lists two views without weighing them. A strong subject for a student who writes clearly.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The case-study paper rewards application to the specific business in front of the student, not general business knowledge. Answers that could have been written about any company score poorly. Command words such as analyse, evaluate and recommend have precise mark implications that are teachable in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus skills questions on maps, graphs and photographs. The skills paper is learnable and is often where a grade is gained, because many students revise content and never practise the skills component. Fieldwork-style questions need a method vocabulary students are rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge 0470 / Pearson 4HI1)
subjects.description: Source evaluation technique separates grades more than knowledge does. Students who learn to interrogate provenance, purpose and audience outperform students who simply know more dates. The depth-study choices vary by school, so a tutor must teach your child's chosen options rather than the ones they know best.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before you look for anybody
paragraphs: Ten minutes of paperwork will save you a term of mismatched teaching. Your child's board and code appear in three reliable places: the statement of entry the school issues before a series, the subject information sheet most Dubai schools publish for Years 10 and 11, and the front of the examination paper from any school mock that used real past material. Ask the subject teacher directly if none of those is to hand. A textbook cover is not evidence, because schools regularly teach from one publisher's book while entering candidates with another board.

A code is four digits for Cambridge and an alphanumeric string for Pearson. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, Economics 0455 and History 0470. The Pearson International GCSE equivalents include 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology and 4EA1 for English Language. Two things travel with the code: the component structure and the tier. Both change what good teaching looks like.

Once you have the code, the search changes character. Instead of asking whether somebody teaches IGCSE maths, you are asking whether they have taught 0580 Extended, which components their students found hardest, and what they would do about a mock script that lost marks across the non-calculator paper. Those are answerable questions, and the answers tell you quickly whether the person in front of you has sat in these rooms. This is the single highest-value thing a parent in The Springs can do before spending a dirham.
bullets: Statement of entry, subject information sheet or mock paper front cover
Cambridge codes are four digits; Pearson codes are alphanumeric

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what actually differs for the same subject
paragraphs: Parents are often told the boards are interchangeable. They are not, and the differences are concrete enough to change a revision plan. The two boards divide content across papers differently, label tiers differently, and set questions in recognisably different house styles. A student who has practised one board's past questions all year and then sees the other board's paper will feel the difference within the first ten minutes.

Session structure is the other difference. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates centres to six administrative zones with zone-specific timetables. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series in advance. Neither board's dates should ever be copied from a tutoring page; both publish the live documents themselves.

The table below is deliberately about structure rather than difficulty, because claiming one board is easier is the kind of assertion that gets repeated for years without evidence. What a parent needs is simpler: know which board, know which tier, and make sure the person teaching your child has the matching mark schemes in their head. Where a school has split boards across departments, your household may need two tutors with two different specialisms, and that is a normal arrangement rather than a sign of something going wrong. Two tutors in one household sounds expensive until the alternative is priced, which is one tutor guessing at the half of the syllabus they were never trained on.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that identify a real syllabus specialist
paragraphs: You do not need to be a teacher to run this conversation. You need six questions and a sense of what a confident answer sounds like. The purpose is not to catch anybody out; it is to separate people who teach the qualification from people who teach the subject. Both exist in Dubai in large numbers, they charge similar rates, and only one of them can tell you what your child's mock script actually shows.

Listen for specificity and for willingness to say what they do not know. A tutor who says they cover all boards for all sciences at all levels is describing an availability calendar, not an expertise. A tutor who says they teach 0620 and 0625 well, have not taught Pearson chemistry recently, and would rather you found somebody who has, is telling you something far more useful about how they will handle your child's weak topic.

The second half of the conversation should be about evidence rather than promises. Ask what you will receive after each session. Ask how progress will be measured against the school's own assessments rather than an internal scale invented by the provider. Ask what happens if the match is wrong. And ask about the permit position, because private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, and a tutor who is vague about it is telling you something.

sections.heading: What a syllabus specialist is worth in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Rates in Dubai are public if you look, and the spread is wide enough that a parent should know where a quote sits before accepting it. Everything in the table below is a figure published by a named provider or by Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026, read in October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list. Three of the six competitor pages ranking for searches like this one publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in.

The useful way to read the table is by what the money buys rather than by the number. At the bottom of the range you are buying supervision: somebody present while homework happens. In the middle you are buying subject teaching. At the top you are buying board-specific examination technique, which is a narrower skill and the one that moves a grade in the final two terms. A family in The Springs paying a mid-range rate for supervision has not overpaid by much; a family paying a specialist rate for supervision has.

In-home arrangements sit higher on published rates than online ones, and the premium is the journey rather than the teaching. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Monthly packages circulating in the Dubai market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Ask what any package includes before comparing it with an hourly figure.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision with a ceiling
paragraphs: Tier entry is the most consequential administrative decision in an IGCSE, and in most Dubai schools it is made by the department rather than negotiated with the family. Cambridge tiered subjects offer Core and Extended routes; Pearson tiered subjects offer Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. That cap is not a judgement about potential, but it is a hard limit on an outcome, and it is set before the student sits anything.

The arguments on both sides are real. A student placed on Extended who cannot access the back third of each paper may finish with a lower grade than they would have achieved comfortably on Core, and will spend a year feeling lost. A student parked on Core who could have handled Extended loses access to sixth-form courses that specify a grade above the Core ceiling. Neither error is rare, and both are usually visible in Year 10 mock data if anyone looks.

What a parent in The Springs can usefully do is ask three questions by the middle of Year 10. Which tier is my child currently expected to sit, on what evidence, and when is the last date that decision can change? Tier decisions interact with entry deadlines, and once a centre has submitted entries, changes are not assumed to be possible. A tutor's job here is diagnostic rather than persuasive: establish from timed work which tier the student can actually access, and give you something concrete to take to the department.
bullets: Core and Foundation entries carry a grade ceiling

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 need different plans, term by term
paragraphs: The most common mistake in this market is buying the Year 11 product in Year 10 or the Year 10 product in Year 11. In Year 10 the problem is coverage: there are syllabus sections the student has met once and does not own. In Year 11 the problem is almost always conversion: the student knows more than the grade shows, and the lost marks are procedural. The same tutor can do both, but not in the same way, and a family paying for content delivery in the final term is buying the wrong thing.

Entry administration sits months ahead of the papers, which is why the planning column in the table matters. Cambridge's March 2027 series is the clearest published example of the lag: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027, with results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026.

Read the table as a planning instrument rather than a promise. Your school's internal deadlines will be earlier than the board's, and those internal dates are the ones that actually govern your child's autumn. Ask for them in writing at the start of the year, put them in a shared calendar, and treat any tutoring block as something scheduled backwards from them. Families in The Springs who do this find the final term far less dramatic than neighbours who did not.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: IGCSE has less assessed coursework than the IB, so the academic-honesty question takes a different shape here. It shows up around material rather than around authorship. Families ask for packs of past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents, and a certain kind of provider supplies them as downloads. That is somebody else's copyright being redistributed, and for unreleased material it is worse than a copyright problem.

The correct approach is simple and costs nothing. Past material, syllabus documents and specimen papers are published by the boards themselves, and your school has access to the secure materials that are not public. A tutor should reference and cite those official sources, teach from them in a live session, and point you to the board's own site rather than hand over a folder. If a prospective tutor offers a drive full of papers as a selling point, that is information about how they operate.

The authorship line still exists where coursework is assessed, and in a handful of IGCSE subjects it is. The rule is the same as anywhere: the student produces the work, and the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. No supplied text, no sections drafted on the student's behalf, no editing a piece until it is no longer theirs. A parent can test this easily by asking their child to explain a paragraph of their own work without notes. If the explanation comes back fluently, the work is theirs and the tutoring is doing its job. If it does not, the problem is not the mark; it is that nobody has learned anything worth keeping.
bullets: Boards publish syllabus and specimen material themselves; link, do not redistribute

sections.heading: Retakes, private candidates and the November series
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE story ends in June. A student who misses a grade threshold for sixth form, or who was entered at the wrong tier, has a second route, and the Dubai market handles it badly because almost nobody writes about it. Cambridge runs a November series as well as June; Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November. A November retake gives roughly five months of focused work and lands in time for most post-16 decisions to be revisited.

The administration is where families come unstuck. A student retaking may be entered by their own school, or may need to sit as a private candidate at a registered examination centre, which is a different arrangement with its own deadlines, fees and identification requirements. Entries close months ahead. The subject must be checked against the series, since not every syllabus is available in every series. All of this belongs on a calendar before any teaching is bought.

Teaching for a retake is also a different job from teaching the course. The student has already met the content once, so the work is diagnostic: find out precisely which components and which question types produced the lost marks, then rebuild those alone. A retake block that re-teaches the syllabus from the start wastes most of the available time. We ask for the breakdown by component before proposing anybody, because without it a retake plan is guesswork wearing a timetable. A Springs family deciding between a November retake and a full June resit should settle that question on the component breakdown alone, because the two routes cost very different amounts of time.

sections.heading: How to start from The Springs, and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: Bring three things to the first conversation: the subject and the syllabus code, the most recent mock or report with the component breakdown if you have it, and the evenings that genuinely work once school and activities are accounted for. With those we can usually name a specialist for your child's board in the same conversation. Without the code we will ask you to find it first, because matching on the subject name is how mismatched tutoring starts.

The first lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. It is a working session rather than a consultation: the tutor looks at where the understanding actually stops and teaches something, and you get a short written note afterwards. If the person is wrong for your child, say so and we will propose someone else. Nobody benefits from defending a bad match for three weeks out of politeness.

The things we will not pretend are worth stating plainly. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked for the certificate number. We do not promise a grade, because nobody honest can. And if no specialist for your child's board and tier is free in your preferred slot, we will tell you that and offer a different time, a short wait, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus, rather than quietly sending a generalist.
