faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board and syllabus code my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Three documents settle it. The statement of entry the school issues before a series lists every syllabus code. The subject information sheet most Dubai schools publish for Years 10 and 11 usually names the board. The front cover of any past paper used in a school mock carries the code directly. If none is available, email the subject teacher and ask for the code rather than the board, because some schools run different boards in different departments and a general answer can be wrong for one of your child's subjects.

faqs.question: For a Springs family, is Cambridge IGCSE equivalent to Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate qualifications from separate awarding bodies, with their own codes, paper structures, tiering labels and mark schemes. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended routes; the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers, and the content is divided across papers differently. Both are recognised by universities. What matters for tutoring is that past-question practice and mark-scheme familiarity must match the board your child is actually entered for, which is why we ask for the code before proposing anyone.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor visit our villa in Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in our India operation. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video with the same tutor each week and work shared on screen. The reason we prefer it is not the saved journey: it is that the shortlist for Cambridge 0620 Extended becomes everybody who teaches that syllabus on a compatible timezone, instead of everybody who teaches it and is willing to drive into the Emirates Living clusters at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IGCSE tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Ask which syllabus code they have taught and for how long, and listen for whether they answer with a code or a topic. Ask which paper your child loses most marks on and how they would find out; a strong answer asks to see the mock script first. Ask what you will receive in writing after each session, how progress will be measured against school assessments, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Vagueness on any of those is information.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended entry, and can it be changed?
faqs.answer: Core and Extended are different entry routes for the same Cambridge syllabus, and the Core route caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in the same way. The decision is usually made by the school department on the basis of classwork and mock performance. It can be revisited, but only up to the point at which the centre submits final entries to the board, which falls months before the examinations. Ask your school which tier is planned, on what evidence, and by when it can change.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE specialist cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: On figures published by named providers and read in October 2026: homework supervision runs around AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 and EdFlik from AED 45. Online subject teaching sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate and independent tutors. Board-specific examination technique in an exam year runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Those are their numbers, not ours.

faqs.question: My child studies Co-ordinated Science, not three separate sciences. Does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Significantly. Co-ordinated and Combined Science syllabuses cover a defined subset of the separate-science content, so a tutor must know exactly which sections are excluded from your child's code. Teaching from a separate-science textbook means spending sessions on material that cannot appear on the paper, which is the most common way time is wasted in this subject. Ask any prospective tutor which award your child sits, double or single, and whether they have taught that specific code rather than the three separate sciences.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 if the problem is coverage, Year 11 if the problem is conversion. In Year 10 there are syllabus sections a student has met once and does not own, and one weekly session across two or three terms closes them cheaply. By Year 11 most students know more than their grade suggests, and the lost marks are procedural: method not shown, command word misread, time mismanaged on the last question. Buying content delivery in the final term is the most common misallocation in this market.

faqs.question: Can my child retake an IGCSE in November rather than waiting a year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November, though not every syllabus appears in every series, so that has to be checked. A November retake gives roughly five months of focused work. The administration matters more than the teaching: entries close months ahead, and a student may need to be entered by a registered examination centre as a private candidate rather than by their former school. Put those deadlines on a calendar before buying any sessions.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us a folder of past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers that as a selling point. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to the boards, which publish them on their own sites, and schools hold the secure material that is not public. A tutor should reference and cite the official source and teach from it live in a session. Redistributing packs of board material is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is considerably more serious than that.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student in The Springs usually need?
faqs.answer: Two sixty-minute sessions a week in the subject causing the problem, through the term before the series, is the common pattern. Families supporting two subjects normally give each its own two slots rather than splitting one hour, because switching subject mid-session wastes the first ten minutes twice. If the diagnosis is narrow, such as electricity in Physics or moles calculations in Chemistry, a defined block of three to eight sessions with an agreed end date often does the job without an open-ended commitment.

faqs.question: Does my child's school decide which board, or can we choose?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and it decides campus by campus and sometimes department by department. That is why two children in the same Springs household can sit different boards for the same subject, and why an older sibling's experience at a different school tells you nothing reliable. Parents cannot usually pick a board, but they can and should find out which one applies to each subject, because every piece of past-question practice and every mark scheme a tutor uses needs to match it.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grades matter for UAE university entry and Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: They matter for both. For the British track, published equivalency requirements ask for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five. One ranking tutoring site tells UAE parents six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel before making subject decisions.

faqs.question: Our mock results were much worse than classwork. What does that usually mean?
faqs.answer: Most often it means technique rather than knowledge, and that is good news because technique moves faster. The usual culprits are showing no method on multi-mark questions, answering a different command word from the one printed, and spending too long on early questions so the last page is rushed. Ask the school for the component breakdown rather than the overall percentage. A tutor who sees which marks were lost, and where on the paper, can target that in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor for our exact board and tier is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so in the first conversation. Some combinations, particularly a specific board at Extended or Higher tier in a narrow evening window, are genuinely contested in a given week. The options we put forward are a different time, a short wait for the right specialist, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus on a compatible timezone. What we will not do is propose a general subject tutor for a board they have not taught and let you discover it in week three.

faqs.question: Does a private IGCSE tutor in Dubai need a licence to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, anyone giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any figure you read with scepticism.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Send us the code, not just the subject
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: The fastest way to get this right is to find your child's syllabus code before you contact anybody, ours included. With the code, the tier and a recent mock breakdown, we can usually name a specialist who has taught that exact paper in the same conversation, run one free lesson for you to judge, and give you a written note of what the next few sessions should target. Without it, every provider in Dubai will sell you a tutor for the subject and some of them will be teaching the wrong board's mark schemes. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week.

intro.heading: Three reasons families want a tutor in the house, and what each one really is
paragraphs: The home-tutor search is almost never about the house. Underneath it sit three distinct problems, and separating them is the difference between buying something useful and buying something expensive. The first is supervision: a thirteen or fifteen-year-old who will not open a book unless an adult is physically present. The second is logistics: a family unwilling to spend an hour in a car on a Tuesday evening for a sixty-minute lesson. The third is a belief, widely held and rarely examined, that proximity produces attention and attention produces marks.

Only the first of those is genuinely about presence, and even then it is usually about presence rather than about a tutor. The second is solved more cheaply by removing the journey altogether than by paying someone else to make it. The third is the one worth testing, because the evidence from marked papers does not support it: what moves an IGCSE grade is whether somebody reads the mark scheme against the student's own script and attacks the labelled losses. That happens equally well, and arguably more durably, on a shared screen.

The costs are public and worth stating before anything else. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included - Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate guide puts it at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200-500. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures as of October 2026, not our price list.

The gap between those two bands is mostly the car. A tutor crossing Dubai at five in the afternoon is spending forty to ninety minutes of their evening on the journey, and that time is in the rate whether or not it is itemised. It also constrains who can be in your shortlist: only tutors within a tolerable drive, which excludes the specialist in Extended-tier Chemistry or Additional Mathematics who happens to live on the other side of the city, or outside it.

IB Gram's position is unambiguous and worth having in the first screen rather than the fourth. We do not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutoring in the home is a service we offer only in India. For UAE families, tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The rest of this page is about whether that is the right answer for your particular version of the home-tutor problem, including the cases where it is not.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: The supervision argument for in-home tuition is strongest at the youngest stage and weakest at the oldest, which is worth knowing before a two-year commitment is made.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, where presence matters most
programmes.description: If any stage justifies an adult in the room, it is this one. Executive function is still developing, independent study habits are not established, and a twelve-year-old genuinely may not start without someone there. The content, assessed through Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, is also widely taught so the local tutor pool is deep.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai answer at this stage is often cheaper than hiring presence: a fixed desk in a shared room, a parent working nearby, and a video session with a tutor who holds the student to a visible task list. Presence turns out to be the parent's, not the tutor's, and that costs nothing.

programmes.name: Year 10, where the work becomes specification-specific
programmes.description: The point at which the balance tips. Content becomes board-specific, tiering decisions loom, and the value of a tutor shifts from supervision to specification knowledge. A nearby generalist who was perfectly adequate in Year 8 starts to be the wrong purchase, because the question is now which paper your child will sit.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically fix tier entries during or at the end of Year 10. A tutor chosen for geography rather than for specification experience is poorly placed to produce the marked evidence a tier conversation with a head of department needs.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam run
programmes.description: The stage where presence is worth least and specialism most. The work is mark-scheme reading, timed papers and attacking labelled error patterns. None of it depends on physical proximity, and all of it depends on whether the tutor has taught that paper. This is also the stage at which in-home rates peak, since demand concentrates between January and April.
programmes.countryNote: An in-home arrangement in a Dubai February also carries the highest risk of lost sessions, because a tutor stuck in traffic is a cancelled hour. A video slot is unaffected by Al Khail Road, which matters more in the exam run than at any other point.

programmes.name: Households with two or more children
programmes.description: The in-home economics change here, because one journey serves two students and the travel cost spreads. That is the strongest financial case for a home tutor in Dubai. The counterweight is that two siblings rarely need the same subject at the same tier, so one visiting tutor usually means one child gets a specialist and the other gets whoever came.
programmes.countryNote: Back-to-back video sessions solve this differently: two different specialists on one household evening, each matched to the right paper, with no shared journey to amortise and no compromise on either child's subject.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These notes say what each subject actually needs from a tutor, which is the test to apply rather than whether the tutor can reach your community.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Needs a shared working surface more than a shared room. Method lines, line by line, on the same page the tutor can annotate - which is exactly what a shared screen with a stylus provides, and what a kitchen table provides less durably because the page is gone by Thursday.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Needs a tutor who has taught the Alternative to Practical paper, which assesses experimental method in writing: variables named, instruments and precision stated, anomalies identified. That is a writing skill. Presence adds nothing to it; specification experience adds a great deal.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs equation and mole work drilled on a surface both parties can write on simultaneously. The cascade problem - one wrong coefficient removing later marks - is easiest to catch when the tutor can annotate the student's own working as it appears, rather than reading it upside down across a table.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Needs command-term discipline above all, because that is where the marks go. A question asking for an explanation and receiving a description loses most of its tariff. Training that is a matter of repeated question-shape prediction, which works identically in either format.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Needs mark-tariff counting on the summary and directed-writing tasks rather than general writing improvement. A tutor annotating a student's response on screen, with the scheme beside it, is doing the thing that moves this grade.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Needs recognition of each reading task's fixed shape within the first few seconds, which is pattern drilling. Students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course - common in Dubai's mobile school population - need targeted reading-paper work rather than conversational practice.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Needs case-study application and, in Economics, diagram convention drilled to the point of reflex: axes labelled, curves named, the new equilibrium marked. Two sessions of that usually recovers more marks than a term of content revision.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Needs the board's pseudocode convention and a ruled trace table, not programming fluency. This is the subject where a locally available 'IT tutor' is most often the wrong purchase, and where screen sharing is the natural working surface anyway.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Needs someone who has taught the specification, of whom there are very few in the UAE. No amount of willingness to travel produces one. This is the clearest subject-level case for abandoning a proximity search entirely.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Needs source interrogation and provenance use trained into a fixed reading order. The resource sits on screen with annotation over it, which is more legible for both parties than a photocopy between them.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Demand is structural, since KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The constraint is evening availability rather than distance, and the good slots are taken early in the term.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Needs scope clarification before anything else, because students on this route routinely revise content that is not on their papers. One session spent marking the specification against the revision list is the highest-value hour available, and it is a document exercise.

sections.heading: What in-home tuition in Dubai actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: A home-tutoring arrangement has more cost lines than its hourly rate, and most of them are discovered after the first month. The rate itself is public enough: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate guide puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200-500. Monthly packages of around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate in the market. Those are other providers' published figures, attributed and dated to October 2026.

Beneath the rate sit the structural terms. Minimum session length is the big one: a tutor making a forty-minute drive will not take a forty-five-minute booking, so the practical unit becomes ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes whether or not your child can concentrate for that long. Minimum weekly commitment often follows for the same reason. Late-cancellation terms tend to be stricter than online equivalents, because a cancelled visit costs the tutor the journey as well as the fee.

Then the household costs, which nobody prices at all. Visitor registration at a gated community or a tower's security desk. Parking, where resident bays are not available. The room that has to be cleared and kept quiet, which in an apartment usually means somebody else's evening is reorganised. And the simple social overhead of having a person in the house for two hours, which families in villa communities absorb easily and families in two-bedroom apartments do not.

The table sets these out against the online equivalent so the comparison is like for like. The point is not that in-home tuition is bad value - for a household that specifically wants an adult present, it is a reasonable purchase at a fair price. The point is that the comparison usually presented, hourly rate against hourly rate, leaves out most of what the arrangement costs.

sections.heading: The evening an in-home session consumes
paragraphs: Describe a weekly in-home session as a sixty-minute lesson and it sounds small. Describe it as an evening and it looks different. The tutor's arrival window is approximate, because Dubai traffic is approximate, so the household holds the hour either side of it. Someone waits at the gate or the security desk. The room is cleared. Dinner moves. Siblings are redirected. The lesson runs for ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes because that is the minimum the tutor takes. Then there is the departure, and the half-hour afterwards in which nothing much happens.

For a villa household in Al Barari or Arabian Ranches with space and staff, this is genuinely minor. For an apartment household in Dubai Marina or Al Wasl with two children and one quiet room, it is the whole evening twice a week, and it is the reason more of those families end up online than villa families do.

There is also the student's own state to account for. A session beginning at 4:30pm catches a Year 11 who left home at 6:40am and has been in school and traffic since. A session beginning at 7pm catches them after food and a shower. In-home arrangements tend to sit earlier, because the tutor has other visits to make and wants to be home; online arrangements sit later, because the tutor's evening does not contain a drive. The later slot is frequently the better lesson, and nobody chooses it for that reason.

None of this is an argument that families should not want a tutor in the house. It is an argument for pricing the arrangement in evenings rather than in hours, and then deciding. Several of the families who come to us after an in-home year say the teaching was fine and the logistics were what they stopped paying for.

sections.heading: Which home-tutor reasons online actually solves
paragraphs: Taking the three underlying reasons in turn: logistics, supervision and attention. Only one of them is genuinely about a tutor being in the room, and the other two have better answers than a visit.

Logistics is the easy one. If the objection is the drive, removing the drive from both sides is a more complete solution than paying a tutor to absorb it, and it costs less - the whole AED 180-500 to AED 150-300 gap is substantially that journey. Supervision is the real case, and the honest answer is that it is usually the parent's presence that works rather than the tutor's. A fixed desk in a shared room, a visible task list, a door open and someone within earshot delivers the supervision at no cost, and the tutor delivers the teaching.

The attention belief is the one worth testing against evidence. What demonstrably moves an IGCSE grade is that somebody marks the student's own script to the published scheme, labels the lost marks by cause, and attacks the largest cause. A tutor two feet away who does not do that will not move the grade. A tutor on a screen who does will. Proximity is neither necessary nor sufficient, and the mark scheme is indifferent to it.

There is a residual case where in-home is simply the right answer, and we should name it rather than argue round it: a younger student with significant additional needs for whom screen-based learning is genuinely inaccessible, or a household where the technology is unreliable. In those cases a local in-home tutor is the correct purchase and we are not the provider. We do not run home visits in Dubai, and we would rather say so in the first conversation than in the third.

sections.heading: What each format leaves behind
paragraphs: This is the part of the comparison that decides it, in our experience, and it is almost never discussed. The question is not what happens during the hour but what exists afterwards. A session that leaves nothing behind cannot be reviewed, compared or handed to a new tutor, and a parent has no instrument for judging it beyond their child's mood.

A good in-home session can leave a marked paper and a written note, and the better in-home tutors do exactly that. The practical difficulty is that paper degrades: the sheet goes into a school bag, the annotation is in one person's handwriting, and in six weeks nobody can find the first diagnostic to compare against the second. Online, the same artefacts are files with dates on them by default rather than by discipline.

The table below compares what each format typically produces. It is written honestly: the in-home column describes what usually happens, not what is possible, and a conscientious visiting tutor can match every row. The reason the typical case matters is that families buy the typical case.

Where this becomes concrete is at a tier conversation or a school transfer. A head of department weighing Extended entry, or a new school asking what support a student has had, responds to a folder of dated marked papers showing a trajectory. Dubai families move schools often enough that this is a real scenario rather than a hypothetical one, and the evidence travels only if it exists as files.

sections.heading: Vetting, permits and who is in your house
paragraphs: A family inviting a tutor into their home is making a safeguarding decision as well as an educational one, and the available checks are more concrete than most parents realise. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Because the permit is free and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time with no fees, there is no sound reason for a UAE-based tutor not to hold one. Asking to see it before a first visit is a normal request. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online is unverified and we will not repeat one.

Beyond the permit, the checks worth making are mundane and effective. Identity confirmed against a document, not a listing. A named platform or agency that holds that identity, rather than a marketplace profile. Contact with the student through the parent or a platform rather than through a personal messaging app. And a clear route to raise a concern that does not involve messaging the tutor. Those standards apply identically in either format, and an online session has the additional property that no unfamiliar adult is inside the house at all.

One rule to know specifically: teachers should not be tutoring their own enrolled students. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the ADEK position as press-reported and verify it against the current policy, but do not make the request.

sections.heading: Sitting beside your child, on a shared screen
paragraphs: The strongest version of the in-home argument is physical: a tutor can see the student's page, write on it, point at a line and watch a hand hesitate. It is a real advantage and it deserves a real answer rather than a dismissal. The answer is that the shared screen reproduces most of it and improves two parts.

What a well-run online session looks like: the past paper open as an image, the mark scheme beside it, a stylus or tablet so both parties can write on the same surface in different colours, the student's own script photographed and annotated live, and a visible countdown when timed work is running. The tutor sees the working appear rather than the finished answer. The student sees their own page corrected rather than a clean model answer, which is the difference between feedback and demonstration.

Two parts are genuinely better. First, the artefact: everything written is saved with a date on it, which paper is not. Second, resources: the official syllabus page, a specimen question and a diagram can be on screen in seconds without a bag of photocopies, and the links are to the boards' own published pages rather than to reproduced copies.

What online loses is small and worth stating. Reading body language is harder, though not impossible with cameras on. A very young or very distractible student is easier to hold in a room. And a poor connection ruins a session in a way that a car journey does not. Dubai's domestic connectivity is generally good enough that the last of those is rare, but it is the right question to ask before committing to a format.

sections.heading: Scheduling the household: siblings, fixtures and Ramadan
paragraphs: A Dubai school week is unusually constrained at both ends. Registers at 7:20 or 7:30am mean an early start and a hard limit on how late a session is useful. Co-curricular fixtures run into the early evening in many schools. The main road corridors are at their worst between about 4:30pm and 6:30pm, which is exactly when a visiting tutor would be travelling and when a student in an outlying community is still in transit.

That produces a narrow practical window, and it is the single biggest cause of in-home arrangements quietly failing. The tutor can offer 4:30pm because their next visit is at 6:30pm; the student cannot be home until 5:15pm; the session shortens, then shifts, then gets cancelled twice, and by March nobody is sure what happened to it. A video slot at 7pm is available precisely because nobody has to be anywhere.

Multiple children make this harder in person and easier online. One visiting tutor on one evening means both children are taught by the same person regardless of whether that person knows both specifications. Two video sessions back to back on the same evening means two specialists and one household block. For a family in Al Khawaneej or Dubai South, the second option is often the first time both children have had a tutor who actually taught their paper.

Ramadan reshapes the month. The school day shortens, routines move and a fixed afternoon slot becomes unusable. Sessions move to a post-Iftar window, run slightly shorter, and the fortnight either side of Eid is treated as consolidation rather than new content. Moving a video slot takes a message. Moving a visiting tutor's route takes a renegotiation, and in practice often takes a month off.

sections.heading: Closeness, coursework and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: A tutor who becomes part of a household's week becomes trusted, and trust is where the pressure around assessed work begins. The request is rarely crude. It is a parent asking whether the tutor could 'just tidy up' a coursework draft the night before it is due, or a student asking for a paragraph to copy because they do not know how to start. Both are the same request wearing different clothes.

The boundary does not move with familiarity. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has already produced, point out where a criterion is not met, and set further practice. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final state, or develop an investigation on the student's behalf. One site in this search landscape sells completed assessed work outright; that is malpractice and the penalty falls on the student rather than the seller.

The practical defence is timing, and it is easier to maintain with a documented relationship than with a familiar one. Criteria read before drafting starts. Method rehearsed before a write-up. Feedback on a genuine first attempt rather than a rescue in the final week. Schools publish internal deadlines months ahead of the board's, and those are the dates the plan should run on.

We also do not distribute board material. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge Assessment International Education and by Pearson, and should be read on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Referencing and linking them is proper practice; handing over a library of files is not, whatever the format of the lesson.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the trade we are asking you to make
paragraphs: Send the school, the subject with its board and syllabus code, the tier and two time windows that genuinely survive your household's week. If there is a marked mock script, send that as well; it will tell a tutor more than any description. Then take the free trial lesson, which costs nothing and takes no card details, and judge it by what it produced rather than how it felt.

Use the trial to test the two things that matter. Specification knowledge: what the papers are worth on that code, where candidates lose marks on the particular paper your child sits, what the first four weeks would attack. And the working surface: can both of you write on the same page, is the script annotated live, is there a saved file at the end. If the answer to the second is no, the format is not being used properly and you should say so.

Be explicit with us about the supervision question if that is the real reason you searched for a home tutor. The answer is usually a desk in a shared room, a visible task list and a parent within earshot, and we would rather build the session around that than pretend the issue does not exist. Where screen-based learning is genuinely inaccessible for your child, the right answer is a local in-home tutor and we will say so.

The trade, stated plainly: IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE - tutoring in the home is a service we provide only in India. You give up an adult in the room. You gain a tutor chosen for the paper rather than for the drive, an hour that is a full hour, a slot that traffic cannot cancel, and a dated written record of every session. For most Dubai families chasing an IGCSE grade, that is the better side of the trade. For some it is not, and knowing which you are is worth more than any argument on this page.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor cost in Dubai once travel is taken into account?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included - Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate guide puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200-500. Monthly packages of around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate in the market. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap between those bands is largely the journey. All of those are other providers' published figures as of October 2026.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange for a tutor to come to our villa or apartment in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutoring inside the home is a service we provide only in India. UAE tuition is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We put that in the first screen rather than the fourth because the alternative wastes your time, and because two ranking competitors in this search route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers while one displays a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. If presence in the room is non-negotiable, engage a local in-home tutor.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition as effective as a tutor sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: For moving marks, the evidence points to the work rather than the seating. What demonstrably shifts an IGCSE grade is somebody marking the student's own script to the published scheme, labelling the lost marks by cause and attacking the biggest cause. A tutor two feet away who does not do that will not move the grade; a tutor on a screen who does will. A well-run online session has both parties writing on the same page in different colours, the mark scheme beside it, and a saved dated file at the end. What it loses is body language and some ability to hold a very distractible younger child.

faqs.question: What does a weekly in-home session actually consume in a household evening?
faqs.answer: More than the lesson. The tutor's arrival window is approximate because Dubai traffic is approximate, so the hour either side is held. Someone meets them at the gate or the security desk. A room is cleared and kept quiet. Dinner moves and siblings are redirected. The session itself commonly runs ninety to a hundred and twenty minutes, because a tutor making a long drive will not take a forty-five-minute booking. For a villa household with space this is minor; for a two-bedroom apartment with two children it is the evening, twice a week.

faqs.question: My child will not concentrate unless an adult is physically present - what should we do?
faqs.answer: Separate the supervision from the teaching, because they do not have to come from the same person. The arrangement that works is a fixed desk in a shared part of the home, a visible task list the student ticks off during the session, the door open and a parent within earshot rather than in the chair. The tutor supplies the teaching and holds the student to the list; you supply the presence, which costs nothing. If the need is genuinely inaccessibility of screen-based learning rather than motivation, a local in-home tutor is the right purchase instead.

faqs.question: What minimum session length do in-home tutors in Dubai usually insist on?
faqs.answer: Commonly ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes, and the reason is the drive rather than the pedagogy. A tutor spending forty minutes each way will not make the journey for a forty-five-minute booking, so the session length is set by their travel economics. That matters because for drilling work - method lines, command terms, unit discipline - two shorter sessions a week usually outperform one long one. A format that permits forty-five minutes twice a week is teaching to the student's attention span rather than to the tutor's route.

faqs.question: How do I check a prospective tutor's permit and identity before letting them into our home?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible holders include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time with no fees. Then confirm identity against a document rather than a marketplace listing, keep contact with your child routed through you or a named platform, and establish how you would raise a concern.

faqs.question: What written evidence should I expect after a session in either format?
faqs.answer: A dated note saying what was taught, what was set and what changed, plus a marked piece of work roughly every third session with lost marks labelled by cause rather than merely counted. In an in-home arrangement that evidence is possible and the better tutors produce it, but it tends to live on paper that disappears into a school bag. Online it is a file with a date on it by default. The test comes six weeks later, when you want to put the second marked paper beside the first and see whether the error profile moved.

faqs.question: Can one tutor work with two of my children on the same evening?
faqs.answer: In an in-home arrangement, usually yes, and that is the strongest financial case for a visit because one journey serves two students. The catch is that two siblings rarely need the same subject at the same tier, so one visiting tutor generally means one child gets a specialist and the other gets whoever came. Back-to-back video sessions solve it differently: two tutors, each matched to the right specification, on one household evening, with a separate error log and session note for each child and no journey to amortise.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives nearby know my child's Dubai school better than a remote one?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the knowledge that matters is not geographic. What a tutor needs to know is which board the school enters for each subject, the syllabus codes, the tier, when its mock windows fall, whether it runs coursework components, and what its sixth form requires at IGCSE for a given A Level or Higher Level course. All of that comes from asking the family and reading the entry statement, not from living in the catchment. Ask any prospective tutor those six questions and see which ones they write down.

faqs.question: What happens to a fixed afternoon slot during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It stops working, which is why it should be moved rather than defended. The school day shortens, household routines shift and a 4:30pm session becomes the worst slot available. The practical pattern is to move to a post-Iftar window, shorten sessions slightly, and treat the fortnight either side of Eid as consolidation rather than new content. Moving a video slot costs a message. Moving a visiting tutor's route means renegotiating their whole evening schedule, which in practice often means losing the month.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a coursework deadline if they are not physically present?
faqs.answer: Within the same limits that apply in person, and the limits are not soft. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has already produced, point out where a criterion is not yet met and set further practice. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final state or develop an investigation on the student's behalf. Presence changes nothing about that line; familiarity is actually where pressure to cross it comes from, which is why the defence is engaging early rather than rescuing late.

faqs.question: How do we keep household privacy while still supervising the lessons properly?
faqs.answer: An online session is the easier of the two on this specific point, because nobody the family has not met is inside the house. The room is yours, the door can stay open and the audio is audible from the next room, so oversight does not require sitting in. Insist on a named platform rather than a personal messaging app, identity held by the provider rather than a listing, and contact with your child routed through you. Ask what personal data is collected about a minor, why, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted.

faqs.question: Are there cases where you would tell us to hire a local in-home tutor instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather say it early. Where a student has significant additional needs that make screen-based learning genuinely inaccessible, where domestic connectivity is unreliable, or where a much younger child simply cannot be held to a task without an adult in the room and no parent is available to be that adult, an in-home tutor is the correct purchase. We do not provide home visits in the UAE, so in those cases we are the wrong provider. Saying so costs us a booking and saves you a term.

faqs.question: What exactly is the trade-off we are being asked to accept?
faqs.answer: You give up an adult physically present in the room. In exchange you get a tutor chosen for the specification your child is actually entered for rather than for the drive, an hour that is a whole hour, roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour of travel premium removed from the published rate bands, a slot that traffic cannot cancel during the February exam run, and a dated written record of every session that survives a tutor change or a school move. For most Dubai families chasing an IGCSE grade that is the better side of the trade. For some it genuinely is not.

intro.heading: What IGCSE home tutors in Dubai are actually hired to fix
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry that reaches this page carries the same two sentences: my child is in Year 10 or Year 11 at a Dubai British-curriculum school, and the last paper came back lower than expected. The request is phrased as a search for IGCSE home tutors in Dubai. The underlying problem is nearly always narrower than the phrasing suggests — a tier chosen badly, a paper whose structure nobody explained, or four or five recurring mark-loss patterns that a marked script would show in twenty minutes. That is what this page is organised around, because fixing a named pattern is cheaper and faster than buying general tuition by the term.

The first thing worth establishing is which qualification your child is actually sitting, because Dubai parents routinely do not know. IGCSE is not one exam. Cambridge International runs its own syllabuses with four-digit codes — Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a First Language 0500 — and sits them in June and November series. Pearson Edexcel runs separate International GCSE specifications with different codes, 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology, 4EA1 for English Language A, available in May/June and November. The papers, the tiering and the practical assessment differ between the two. A tutor who has not asked which board your school entered your child for has not started work.

The second thing is the tier, which caps the grade before any revision begins. Cambridge separates Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A is tiered as Foundation and Higher, with Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher reaching 9. A Dubai student sitting the wrong tier is the single most common structural mistake we see, in both directions: a capable candidate held at Core who can never score above a C, and a fragile candidate pushed to Extended who loses marks across the whole paper rather than securing the accessible ones. This is a conversation to have with the school in Year 10, not in March of Year 11.

The third is where marks actually go. Across Dubai scripts the recurring losses are specific and dull: method marks lost to unshown working in 0580 and 4MA1; command terms misread, so a describe answer is given where explain was asked; units and significant figures dropped in 0625 and 4PH1; graph work done without reading the axis scale; and in the sciences, the practical component — Cambridge Paper 5 or Paper 6, worth 20 per cent of 0625 — treated as unteachable because there is no laboratory at home. Each of those is a trainable habit rather than a knowledge gap, and each one is worth more marks than another pass through the textbook.

On delivery, the honest position, stated before anything else: IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families work with a tutor one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the script or the past paper shared on screen so the marking happens in front of the student. For an exam-year subject that is usually an advantage rather than a compromise, because the tutor is selected for having taught 0580 Extended or 4PH1 rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive of your community.

The four bands below cover the two years before IGCSE, the IGCSE years themselves, and the two post-16 routes a Dubai cohort splits into.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where Dubai schools decide setting and, in effect, start deciding tier. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and many Dubai schools use the results to place students in Year 10 sets. Tutoring here is cheap, unglamorous and disproportionately effective: algebraic fluency, fraction and ratio security, and the habit of showing working are the three things that decide whether Extended is open two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in when they commit a student to Core or Extended, with some deciding in Year 9 and others leaving it until the entry deadline in Year 11. Ask your school directly which year the decision is taken and what evidence it uses, because a Year 9 Checkpoint result is a thin basis for a grade ceiling that lasts into university applications.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, and the first set of externally marked qualifications a Dubai student holds. Cambridge syllabuses are identified by four-digit codes and offer Core and Extended routes in many subjects; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications use codes beginning 4 and tier only some subjects. Both boards publish subject-specific assessment structures that differ paper by paper, and tutoring that ignores the structure wastes most of its hours.
programmes.countryNote: The UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, the largest single share across 227 schools and 17 curricula, which is why IGCSE provision in the emirate is deep and inconsistent at the same time. Two schools a few minutes apart may use different boards for the same subject, so a tutor matched by subject alone is a coin flip.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The commonest post-IGCSE route in Dubai British-curriculum schools and the one IGCSE tier choice most directly constrains. Further Mathematics and Physics at A Level assume Extended or Higher-tier algebraic fluency, and a Core candidate arriving in Year 12 has a genuine content gap rather than a confidence gap. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one accredited Advanced Level subject at a grade no lower than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, is required alongside the IGCSE count.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students applying to UAE universities need their certificates equivalated by the Ministry of Education, and the British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus the A Level or AS requirement. Treat the process as the Ministry's, not a tutor's, and verify current wording on the official channel before relying on it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other post-16 route, taken by a smaller Dubai cohort and chosen more often by families already in an IB continuum school. The IGCSE-to-Diploma step is sharper than the IGCSE-to-A-Level step in two places: Mathematics, where Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes a strong Extended or Higher-tier foundation, and the sciences, where the Internal Assessment demands independent experimental design that no IGCSE paper requires.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools creating 16,846 places. A Year 11 student considering the switch should look at the Mathematics route first, because that is the choice that is expensive to reverse in Year 12.

dubai/igcse-home-tutors.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the board codes, the papers and the specific place Dubai candidates drop marks. These are the subjects that account for the overwhelming majority of IGCSE tutoring requests in the emirate, and the descriptions are written to be useful before you book anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics — Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers in each route, one non-calculator and one calculator, each carrying half the marks in 0580 and in 4MA1. Dubai mark loss concentrates in unshown method on multi-step questions, mishandled surds and indices, and bearings and vectors left blank. Working written down is worth marks even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Physics — Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: Cambridge Extended candidates sit Paper 2 at 30 per cent, Paper 4 at 50 per cent and a practical component at 20 per cent. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Marks go on units, significant figures, prefix conversion, and explanations that describe what happens without naming the physics that causes it.

subjects.name: Chemistry — Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: Same three-component Cambridge structure as Physics. The recurring Dubai losses are mole calculations where the balanced equation was never checked, qualitative analysis tests recalled imprecisely, and organic mechanisms described in the wrong order. Six-mark extended responses need a structure, not more sentences.

subjects.name: Biology — Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: The subject where strong students most often plateau at a 6, because recall is good and command terms are read carelessly. Describe, explain, suggest and compare demand different answers, and a question asking for a comparison scores nothing for two separate descriptions. Data and graph questions carry more marks than students expect.

subjects.name: English as a First Language — Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, assessed in two papers. Dubai candidates lose reading marks by paraphrasing rather than analysing, and writing marks by producing fluent prose that ignores the audience, form and purpose set in the question. The fastest gains come from planning for three minutes before writing anything.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language — Cambridge 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with a different grade profile, and Dubai families regularly do not know which one their child is entered for. Support focuses on exam technique for the reading and writing components and on precision rather than range in the summary task.

subjects.name: Literature in English — Cambridge 0475 / Edexcel 4ET1
subjects.levels: Untiered · set texts vary by school
subjects.description: Marks depend almost entirely on using quotation to support a point about the writer's method rather than retelling the plot. Dubai centres choose different set texts, so tutoring must start from your school's actual texts. Unseen poetry is where the widest spread of marks appears.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics — Cambridge 0606 / Edexcel 4PM1
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Dubai sets as preparation for A Level Mathematics, and genuinely harder than the main syllabus. Calculus, trigonometric identities and series are the content that separates candidates, and most mark loss is algebraic slips carried through several lines rather than conceptual failure.

subjects.name: Business and Economics — Cambridge 0450 and 0455 / Edexcel 4BS1 and 4EC1
subjects.description: Content-light and technique-heavy. Marks are lost by answering with definitions when the command term asked for analysis or evaluation, and by ignoring the case study material the question is built on. A structured evaluation paragraph is a teachable formula and worth several grades across a paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT — Cambridge 0478 and 0417
subjects.description: Theory marks hinge on precise terminology, and the practical and pseudocode elements reward students who write out logic before coding anything. Trace tables and binary conversions are routinely dropped under time pressure despite being the most reliably scorable questions on the paper.

subjects.name: Geography and History — Cambridge 0460 and 0470
subjects.levels: Untiered · coursework option at some centres
subjects.description: Both reward structure and source handling over volume. In Geography the case-study detail is what distinguishes a 6 from an 8; in History, source questions need provenance used explicitly rather than content summarised. Where a school runs the coursework option, the rules on what support is permitted are strict.

subjects.name: Arabic — Cambridge 0508 and 0544
subjects.description: Two very different syllabuses sat by two very different cohorts in Dubai schools, and KHDA requires the Arabic first-language and additional-language classes to be organised separately. Matching a tutor to the wrong one of those two is the commonest avoidable error in Arabic tutoring requests.

dubai/igcse-home-tutors.regionsTitle: Dubai communities we book IGCSE sessions for, and what the Year 11 week looks like there
dubai/igcse-home-tutors.regionsIntro: IGCSE scheduling is governed by mock seasons, after-school commitments and the drive home. These are the Dubai communities that generate most of our Year 10 and Year 11 requests, with the practical detail that decides which slot actually survives a term.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
regions.note: British-curriculum heartland with large Year 10 and Year 11 cohorts. Sessions here cluster at 17:00 and 18:30 because school buses and sports fixtures occupy the late afternoon. Mock season in January produces the sharpest spike in Extended Maths requests of any Dubai community.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Several large British schools within a few minutes of each other, often using different boards for the same subject. Families frequently discover at the first session that a neighbour's child sits 4MA1 while theirs sits 0580. Early-evening slots are workable because commutes are short.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Al Safa
regions.note: Short school runs and a high proportion of students taking ten subjects, which makes timetable pressure rather than ability the limiting factor. Requests here skew towards two subjects at once, usually a science plus Extended Maths, and towards 45-minute rather than 60-minute sessions.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Apartment households where a quiet room matters more than travel time. Students often work at a desk with the past paper on screen and the script scanned in advance, which suits mark-by-mark feedback. Late slots to 20:00 are more common here than elsewhere.

regions.name: Mirdif, Uptown and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long bus runs mean many students are not home until after 16:30, so weekday sessions start late and weekend mornings carry an unusual share of the load. Families here most often ask for a single-subject block across the two terms before the exam series.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Dubai South and Jumeirah Village
regions.note: Newer communities with growing secondary cohorts and significant commutes against the morning flow. Holiday blocks in the December and spring breaks are the practical way to recover a term, and demand for those blocks here exceeds weekly bookings.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Mixed curriculum catchments where some students move into IGCSE from a different system in Year 10. Transition work — closing the algebra and scientific-notation gap left by a previous curriculum — is the dominant request rather than exam polish.

regions.name: Deira, Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Established schools with long-running IGCSE provision and a high proportion of Arabic first-language candidates. Requests split between Extended Maths and Arabic 0508, and early-evening Arabic slots fill before anything else on the timetable.

schoolClusters.city: Large British-curriculum secondaries, new Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Schools running full IGCSE option blocks into A Level, with Year 11 cohorts big enough that setting decisions are made early and are hard to move. Most requests from this cluster are Extended Maths and the separate sciences, triggered by a January mock rather than by a report.

schoolClusters.city: Established British-curriculum schools, central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Longer-standing secondaries where IGCSE provision is deep and some subjects run with the coursework option. Requests here include Literature set texts and the Geography and History coursework routes, where the rules on permitted support are strict and worth reading before any tutoring is booked.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools where students move into IGCSE from another system
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's turnover means a meaningful number of Year 10 students start IGCSE having come from a different curriculum. The work in this cluster is a content audit against the specific syllabus code rather than exam technique, and it is best done in the first term rather than the third.

dubai/igcse-home-tutors.modesIntro: Three formats cover nearly every IGCSE request from Dubai. All run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all begin the same way: a past paper the student has already sat, marked line by line, so the first teaching session starts at the real gap rather than at the start of the syllabus.

modes.title: Marked-script diagnostic, then weekly single subject
modes.description: The standard arrangement. The student sends a recent mock or past paper, the tutor marks it against the board's own mark scheme and names the four or five recurring loss patterns, and weekly sessions then work through them in order of marks available. Each session ends with a short timed question set, and the following session opens by marking it.
bullets: Board and syllabus code confirmed before the first session
Recurring loss patterns named in writing, not described vaguely
Timed question sets between sessions, marked at the next one
Progress tracked as marks recovered per paper section

modes.title: Two-subject exam-term block
modes.description: For Year 11 students in the two terms before a May/June or November series, usually Extended Maths plus one science. Sessions alternate subjects weekly, with full past papers sat under timed conditions every third week. The point is pacing and paper-sitting stamina as much as content, because most Dubai candidates lose more marks to timing than to gaps.
bullets: Alternating weekly subjects with a shared revision calendar
A full timed paper every third week, marked to the board scheme
Section-level mark tracking so revision time follows the marks
Explicit work on command terms and question-reading

modes.title: Tier and transition audit
modes.description: A short block for two situations: deciding Core against Extended or Foundation against Higher before an entry deadline, and auditing a student who has arrived in a Dubai IGCSE class from a different curriculum. Three or four sessions, a written content audit against the specific syllabus code, and a recommendation you can take to the school.
bullets: Topic-by-topic audit against the named syllabus code
Clear statement of the grade ceiling each tier imposes
Written recommendation for the school conversation
An honest answer where the recommendation is to change nothing

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Core candidate cannot be awarded above a grade C, and an Extended candidate is assessed across the full A* to E range. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A tiers the same way under different names, with Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher reaching grade 9. That single structural fact decides more Dubai outcomes than any amount of revision, and it is the first thing a tutor should establish — before content, before technique, before a timetable.

The decision is harder than it looks because it runs in both directions. A capable student parked on Core will produce comfortable marks and a ceiling that closes off A Level Mathematics and most science routes; the papers feel easy and the damage is invisible until Year 12. A fragile student pushed onto Extended will meet questions beyond reach across the whole paper, lose the accessible marks to time pressure and panic, and often finish below what the Core route would have given. Neither error announces itself in a Year 10 report.

Three pieces of evidence settle it in practice. The first is a marked Extended past paper under timed conditions: not a prediction, an actual script, which shows whether the accessible marks are being collected. The second is algebraic fluency, because Extended questions assume manipulation the Core route can avoid. The third is what the student intends to study at sixteen, since Core closes doors that are expensive to reopen. A tier audit that ignores the third question is not an audit.

The table sets out the comparison the way a parent needs it. Note that tiering varies by subject and by board — Cambridge offers Core and Extended in many subjects but not all, and Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics A while running most sciences untiered — so the right question to your school is subject-specific rather than general. Entry decisions sit with the school and the final entry deadline, and a change after the deadline is not always possible.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, two different exams
paragraphs: Dubai schools choose boards subject by subject, and a single student can reasonably sit Cambridge Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel Physics in the same series. Parents are rarely told this explicitly, and tutors who do not ask will teach the wrong paper structure for a term. The difference is not cosmetic: the number of papers, their length, the weightings and the treatment of practical work all vary between the two boards for the same named subject.

The clearest divergence is in the sciences. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each carry a separate practical component — Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical — worth 20 per cent of the qualification, with the theory papers at 30 and 50 per cent for Extended candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills within the written papers instead, with no separate practical paper. A student moving between schools mid-course can therefore gain or lose a whole component.

Mathematics diverges differently. Cambridge 0580 splits Core and Extended with two papers each, one non-calculator and one calculator, each carrying half the marks. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 sits two papers of two hours, each worth half the qualification, tiered as Foundation and Higher. Pearson also runs Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 and Cambridge runs Additional Mathematics 0606 as the stretch options, and the two are not interchangeable in content.

The practical consequence for a Dubai family is simple. Find the syllabus code on your child's exam entry statement or ask the examinations officer, then check the board's own published syllabus for that series — syllabuses are revised, and a 2027 series may differ from the version a tutor last taught. Nobody should be reproducing or supplying board syllabus documents, mark schemes or past papers; the correct move is to read them on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com and teach from them.

sections.heading: Where Dubai IGCSE candidates actually lose marks
paragraphs: Mark loss at IGCSE is far more patterned than families expect. A marked script from a Dubai Year 11 mock usually shows the same four or five behaviours repeating across every section, and the total they cost is almost always larger than the total lost to genuine ignorance. This is the most useful section on the page, because every item in it is trainable in weeks rather than terms.

Unshown method is the biggest single loss in mathematics. Both 0580 and 4MA1 award method marks, and a student who works in their head and writes one line has forfeited them before the answer is even wrong. The habit is worth retraining explicitly, with the tutor refusing to accept bare answers in session. Command terms are the biggest loss in the sciences and in business subjects: describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate ask for structurally different answers, and a comparison answered as two descriptions scores close to nothing however accurate it is.

Then there are the quiet ones. Units and significant figures in 0625 and 4PH1, where a correct calculation presented wrongly loses the final mark. Prefix conversion — kilo, milli, micro — mishandled under time pressure. Graph questions where the axis scale was never read. Six-mark extended responses written as a stream of sentences rather than a structured sequence. And timing: a student who spends eighteen minutes on a six-mark question has lost the marks at the end of the paper, which are usually the easiest ones left.

The table below is the diagnostic we run on a first marked script. Each row is a loss pattern, the papers it shows up on, roughly what it costs across a full paper, and the specific drill that closes it. Figures in the cost column are typical ranges observed on scripts rather than a measured study, and they vary by subject and candidate — they are there to show the order of priority, which is the point.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Dubai: the honest comparison
paragraphs: This page targets a phrase Dubai parents genuinely type, so the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home IGCSE tutoring in Dubai is a real and sizeable market. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, independent listings run from AED 200 to AED 500, and published monthly packages for four two-hour visits sit at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799. Families choose it because it removes the organisational load, and that is a legitimate reason.

What it costs beyond the rate is the tutor pool. A family in Dubai South or Mirdif choosing a visiting tutor is choosing from the IGCSE specialists willing to drive to Dubai South or Mirdif at 17:00 on a weekday, and the specialists most in demand — 0580 Extended, 4PH1, Additional Mathematics 0606 — are the ones least likely to be on that list. Travel is inside the price whether itemised or not, and a cancelled session is a wasted journey somebody pays for. In an exam year, the scarce resource is the right tutor, not the convenience.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families work one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the script on screen and the marking visible as it happens. For IGCSE work this has one concrete advantage that in-home tutoring cannot match: the student's own past paper can be annotated live, mark by mark, against the board's published scheme, and both parties keep the annotated copy. It also means a Year 11 candidate in Al Furjan and one in Jumeirah draw on the same pool of syllabus specialists.

Two limitations worth stating. A student without a quiet room and a reliable connection will do better with someone in the room, and we will say so at the trial rather than afterwards. And no format compensates for a student who will not do the timed question set between sessions; that is the single strongest predictor of whether IGCSE tutoring moves a grade, in any delivery mode.

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a session, an entry deadline or a results date, which is remarkable, because the calendar is what makes tutoring urgent or not. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year.

Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and Cambridge's own published key dates for the March series make the point better than any explanation. For the March 2027 series the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results are released on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry deadline is therefore more than two months before the first paper, and a tier change after it may not be available.

There is one Cambridge administrative detail that catches international centres and costs real candidates real exams. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. If you are holding a printed timetable found online, check it is the zone version your school sits.

For Pearson, the published pattern is equally usable: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so any plan should work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date. We publish no IB session or results dates anywhere on this site that have not been confirmed against the IB directly.

sections.heading: What IGCSE grades have to show for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: A Dubai family planning on a UAE university needs the Ministry of Education equivalency rules in mind from Year 10, because the requirement is about which subjects were taken as much as how well they went. Four of the ten query clusters we researched contain no mention of equivalency at all, and one ranking competitor publishes a subject count that does not match the published rule. This is one of the few places where a tutoring page can simply be more accurate than the pages above it.

On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is the one most often got wrong, and it changes which IGCSE options a student should keep.

For comparison, the American track requires English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics evidenced by at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold has been verified on the Ministry's own pages, so no figure is published here — check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly rather than relying on any tutoring site, including this one.

Two boundaries matter. Equivalency is a Ministry process: IB Gram does not perform it, submit it or influence its outcome, and nobody should tell you otherwise. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression — anyone framing it that way is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. What tutoring can legitimately do is protect the five-subject count by stopping a borderline grade from falling below the threshold.
