sections.heading: Coursework, feedback and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects offer a coursework option that Dubai centres may or may not run — Geography, History, English and others — and where a school does run it, the rules on permitted support are strict and the consequences of breaching them fall on the student. It is worth knowing exactly where the boundary sits before any tutoring is arranged, because the commercial pressure in this market runs the other way.

What a tutor may legitimately do: teach the skills a task demands, explain the assessment criteria, ask questions that expose a weak argument, read what the student has written and say where it is unclear or unsupported, model structure on a different example, and mark a timed practice piece. What a tutor may not do: supply content to be presented as the student's own, hand over text, or take a draft away and return it rewritten. The work and the words stay the student's. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach and precisely the behaviour these rules exist to stop.

The same principle governs materials. Board syllabuses, mark schemes, past papers and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or supplying them is copyright infringement. The correct practice is to reference them, cite the official page, and teach from the student's own copy issued by the school or downloaded by the family from the board's site. Any site offering bundles of past papers as downloads is telling you something about how it operates.

For Dubai parents there is a second, local dimension. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify current wording before relying on it — but the direction is clear, and no reputable arrangement markets your child's own teacher privately.

sections.heading: How many hours a grade actually takes
paragraphs: The question every Dubai parent asks second, after price, is how long this will take. There is no honest single answer, and anyone offering one is selling. What can be said usefully is how the variables interact: how far the current mark sits from the target, whether the gap is technique or content, how many weeks remain before the series, and whether the student will do the work between sessions.

The technique-versus-content distinction does most of the explanatory work. A student losing twelve marks a paper to unshown method, misread command terms and timing collapse is holding the content and leaking marks, and that leak closes in roughly eight to fourteen sessions with between-session practice. A student who has not secured a third of the syllabus is in a different position entirely, and no number of technique sessions substitutes for the content. The marked diagnostic script tells you which case you are in, which is why it comes first.

The second variable is weeks remaining, and it behaves non-linearly. Starting in September of Year 11 for a May/June series gives roughly thirty usable weeks and allows content and technique to run in parallel. Starting after the January mocks gives perhaps fourteen, which forces a choice: secure the accessible marks and the technique, and accept that the hardest extended topics will not be built from nothing. Starting six weeks out is not pointless, but it is triage — paper-sitting discipline, command terms and the four highest-cost loss patterns, in that order.

The third variable is the only one entirely outside the tutor's control. Across every delivery format, the strongest predictor of whether IGCSE tutoring moves a grade is whether the student completes the timed question set between sessions. We build short sets precisely so completing them is realistic for a Dubai student carrying nine or ten subjects, and the following session opens by marking them, so the loop closes. Where sets stop being done, we say so in writing rather than continuing to bill a slot that has stopped working.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in Dubai, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a Dubai parent arranging a tutor independently is the one who carries the checking burden. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated with scepticism; the ministry has not specified amounts. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

A separate permit governs anything that operates as a business with premises and staff. A training institute in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That distinction matters because claims of KHDA endorsement for individual tutors circulate freely in this market and usually describe something the seller does not hold. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or endorsement, and makes no such claim anywhere on this site.

What a Dubai parent can practically do: ask any independent tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit and under what category, ask whether the student is enrolled at the tutor's own school, and ask which syllabus code they are teaching to. Three questions, and they filter out most of the risk in this market without requiring you to become an expert in it.

Every third week in an exam-term block, a full paper is sat under timed conditions and marked, which is also the only reliable way to build paper stamina.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE home tutors in Dubai still travel to the villa, or is it all online now?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in Dubai. Visiting tutors are a real market priced by Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, with monthly packages for four two-hour visits published at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai — that is a service we offer only in India. Dubai families work one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with past papers annotated on screen mark by mark. The practical trade-off is specialist access against physical presence: online reaches the 0580 Extended or 4PH1 specialist regardless of which community you live in.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor charge per hour in Dubai, and what is inside that figure?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online IGCSE tuition at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, visiting tutors at AED 180 to AED 350 per Bestimate's 2026 table, and independent listings reaching AED 500. Budget platforms start far lower — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — and generally buy homework supervision rather than syllabus-level teaching. For visiting tutors, travel is inside the figure whether or not it is itemised. Those are market bands, not an IB Gram price; our quote follows a free 30-minute trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended in Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Decide it on a marked Extended past paper sat under timed conditions, not on a prediction. Core is capped at grade C and Extended spans A* to E, so the choice sets a ceiling before revision begins. Three questions settle it: are the accessible marks on an Extended paper actually being collected, is algebraic manipulation fluent, and does the student intend A Level Mathematics or a science at sixteen? Core closes those doors and reopening them in Year 12 is expensive. Audit it in Year 10, because entry decisions sit with the school and a change after the final entry deadline may not be possible.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my school uses Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code is on the exam entry statement the school issues, and the examinations officer will confirm it in one email. It is worth asking subject by subject rather than once, because Dubai schools commonly mix boards: a student can sit Cambridge Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel Physics in the same series. Once you have the codes, read the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com for the series your child will sit, since specifications are revised and a 2027 version may differ from the one a tutor last taught. Any tutor who has not asked for the code has not started work.

faqs.question: Does Paper 6 alternative-to-practical work mean lab skills can be taught over video?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board, which is why the code matters. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 carry a separate practical component worth 20 per cent — Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical — and the school decides which route candidates sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers with no separate practical paper. The laboratory work itself happens at school in either case. What tutoring covers is the written assessment of practical skills: apparatus description, variable control, tabulation, graph work, uncertainty and the specific phrasing those questions reward.

faqs.question: My child is predicted a 5 in Extended Maths. What actually moves that to a 7?
faqs.answer: On most Dubai scripts at that level, three things: method shown on every multi-step question, timing discipline so the final third of the paper is reached, and the four or five topics that are genuinely absent rather than shaky. The first two are habit work and typically recover six to twelve marks a paper within three or four sessions. The content gap is the slower part and needs identifying precisely, which is what a marked script does. What will not move it is another pass through the textbook from page one — that is the commonest way an exam year is spent without the grade changing.

faqs.question: When is the final entry deadline for the Cambridge March 2027 series?
faqs.answer: Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series give final entries as due 27 November 2026, with the examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June. The entry deadline therefore sits more than two months before the first paper, which is the practical reason tier decisions have to be made in the autumn term. Deadlines are set by Cambridge and administered through your school, so confirm the specific dates for your series with the examinations officer rather than relying on any third-party page.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable depend on which administrative zone our school is in?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable so that papers are sat within an acceptable window across time zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a Dubai family this is a genuine risk, because a timetable found through a search engine may well be another zone's. Ask your school which zone it sits in and work only from the version it issues.

faqs.question: Is the equivalency subject count five or six, and which figure should I trust?
faqs.answer: Five. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one page ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is the Ministry's process and nobody else's: verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel before making a subject decision on it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted among the five equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count on the British track. That has a practical consequence for option choices in Year 9 and Year 10: a student needs five accredited subjects outside those two at grade E or grade 3 or better, so dropping a sixth academic subject to lighten a timetable can quietly put the count at risk. The subjects remain mandatory at school under KHDA requirements regardless of the curriculum your school is licensed to teach, so this is about the equivalency count specifically, not about whether they are studied.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework, or does that break the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task needs, explain the assessment criteria, question a weak argument, read what the student has written and say where it is unsupported, model structure using a different example, and mark timed practice. A tutor cannot supply content, hand over text, or take a draft away and return it rewritten. The work and the words stay the student's own, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student rather than the tutor. Materials matter too: board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes should be read on the official sites, not redistributed by a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 11 with two terms left?
faqs.answer: Two terms is enough for a meaningful change if the diagnosis is honest about what will fit. Roughly fourteen usable weeks after January mocks forces a choice: secure the accessible marks and close the technique leaks, rather than building the hardest extended topics from nothing. In that order the work is paper-sitting discipline, command terms, method shown on every question, and then the two or three content gaps that cost the most marks. What does not work in two terms is starting at chapter one. Six weeks out is triage rather than tutoring, and we will describe it that way instead of selling it as a programme.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Maths with Cambridge and Physics with Edexcel in the same year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it is common, because schools choose boards subject by subject. It has one consequence worth planning for: the paper structures, command-term conventions and practical assessment differ between the boards, so revision technique does not transfer cleanly from one subject to the other. A student who has learned Cambridge six-mark answer structure will not automatically produce the right shape for a Pearson extended response. Tutoring should therefore be matched per code rather than per student, which is why we ask for every code on the entry statement rather than just the subject list.

faqs.question: What does a marked diagnostic on a past paper actually tell you?
faqs.answer: It separates leakage from absence, which is the only distinction that matters for planning. A script marked against the board's published scheme shows whether marks are being lost to unshown method, misread command terms, units and significant figures, graph reading and timing collapse — all habit problems that typically close in eight to fourteen sessions — or to topics that are genuinely not there, which is slower work. It also shows where in the paper the marks go, so revision follows the marks rather than the student's preferences. You get it in writing with the cost of each pattern estimated, and it is useful at a parents' evening whether or not you book tutoring.

faqs.question: How many hours per subject does a Dubai IGCSE student usually need?
faqs.answer: The honest answer is that it depends on four things and anyone quoting a single figure is guessing: how far the current mark sits from the target, whether the gap is technique or content, how many weeks remain before the series, and whether the between-session timed sets get done. A technique leak with thirty weeks available is often eight to fourteen sessions. A third of a syllabus missing with fourteen weeks left is a different problem that no session count fixes. That last variable — work completed between sessions — is the strongest single predictor of grade movement in any delivery format.

dubai/igcse-home-tutors.closingHeading: Send a marked paper before you book anything
dubai/igcse-home-tutors.closingBody: The useful first step costs nothing and is not a sales call: send the exam board, the syllabus code from the entry statement, and a recent mock or past paper your child has already sat. You get back a written diagnostic marked against the board's published scheme, naming the recurring loss patterns, roughly what each costs per paper, and which to attack first. Then one free 30-minute trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the subject — one per family, no card details — over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If the honest reading is that the tier is wrong rather than the technique, the note will say so and you can take it to the school.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-e.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE Mathematics to Year 10 and Year 11 students across Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches, Motor City and the wider Dubailand belt. Each is matched to a syllabus code and a tier rather than to a general subject label.

intro.heading: Why the neighbourhood matters less than the syllabus code
paragraphs: Search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate and the results try to sell you proximity. Proximity is the least useful variable in this decision. Two households a four-minute drive apart, one in Dubai Hills Estate and one in Arabian Ranches, routinely have children sitting different mathematics qualifications: one on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, the other on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A 4MA1 Higher, and a third child nearby on Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 because their school routes students towards the IB Diploma. Those are three different papers, three different grading scales and three different sets of examiner habits.

That is the comparison this page is built on, and it runs through every section: what differs between these communities, what differs between the syllabuses their schools use, and why the practical answer ends up the same in each case. The answer is a specialist matched to the code on the front of the paper, delivered online so that the pool of specialists is not limited to whoever lives within a short drive of your villa and has Tuesday evening free.

The second thing that differs by community is time, not content. Dubai Hills Estate sits between Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street, so its buses run to Al Quoz, Al Barsha South and Meydan. Arabian Ranches has its own primary school on site but sends secondary students further. Arabian Ranches 3, Town Square and Mudon have the longest runs of this group, and a Year 11 student getting home at 16:20 has a different evening from one home at 15:40. A tutor who has to drive loses part of the window to the road. A tutor on video does not, and the slot holds at the same time every week regardless of which of these communities you live in.

The third difference is what families worry about. In Dubai Hills Estate the common question is tier: a Year 10 student placed on Core who wants a grade above a C, or a Year 11 student on Higher losing marks they clearly understand. In the Ranches, with a longer-established cohort, the question is more often the step from IGCSE into the Diploma or A Level. In Motor City and Sports City, where the apartment population turns over faster, the question is mid-year transfer: a student arriving from a CBSE or American school into Year 10 of a British curriculum, three months behind on a syllabus nobody has mapped for them.

All four of those problems have the same shape. Identify the exact qualification, identify the tier, identify which papers carry which marks, then work the published past papers against the published mark scheme until the gap between what the student knows and what the student scores closes. What follows sets out the syllabus differences, the real entry and results dates from Cambridge and Pearson, the Dubai market rates in dirhams with sources, and the five-subject rule that the UAE Ministry of Education actually applies when a certificate is submitted for equivalency.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-e.programmesIntro: IGCSE mathematics is one rung of a British-curriculum route, and the rungs either side change what the tutoring should aim at. These are the stages we support around Dubai Hills Estate.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The two years before an IGCSE course starts are where tier placement is effectively decided, because schools set groups on Year 9 performance. Work at this stage is fluency: fractions, negatives, index laws, rearranging formulae and straight-line graphs. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which some schools use as an external marker before setting groups.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches families often meet this stage without realising it is a decision point. A Year 9 student who is comfortable but slow usually gets placed on the lower tier, which caps the grade available two years later. A term of fluency work in Year 9 is cheaper and less stressful than a tier appeal in Year 11, and it is the most under-used intervention in this market.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: A two-year course sat at the end of Year 11, tiered in every version. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher; Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics splits into Core and Extended and adds an investigation component that suits IB-bound students. The tier caps the grade, so it is the single most consequential administrative fact about your child's mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Schools used by Dubai Hills Estate families run different combinations of these. Repton Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, GEMS Metropole Motor City and Dubai Heights Academy are all British-curriculum routes, and the board and specification are a school-level choice that can change between cohorts. Ask the department which code is on this year's entry rather than assuming last year's applies.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma, the two exits
programmes.description: An IGCSE mathematics grade is a gatekeeper twice over: schools set minimum grades for A Level Mathematics and for IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, commonly a 7 or an A, and the content gap is real in both directions. A* and 9 students still meet calculus, proof and vectors as new material in the first term after IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Around Dubai Hills Estate both exits are available within a short bus ride, which is unusual. GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai run IB Diploma routes; Repton Al Barsha and Kings' School Al Barsha run A Level routes. A Year 11 student choosing between them should look at the mathematics requirement for each before the option form, not after.

programmes.name: Mid-year transfer into a British-curriculum Year 10 or 11
programmes.description: Students joining from CBSE, American, French or MoE curricula meet the same mathematics in a different order and with different assessment conventions. The gap is rarely ability; it is coverage and command terms. A mapping exercise against the syllabus content list identifies exactly which sections have not been taught, which is faster than general revision.
programmes.countryNote: Motor City, Dubai Sports City and Town Square see the most of this because their rental populations turn over more often. A student arriving in January of Year 11 has roughly two terms, which is enough if the missing content is identified in week one and not discovered in a March mock.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-e.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics divides into content strands and into paper skills, and a first lesson usually finds the problem in one rather than both. These are the areas students around Dubai Hills Estate most often need.

subjects.name: Number and index laws
subjects.description: Standard form, surds at the higher tier, upper and lower bounds, percentage change in reverse, and compound interest. Bounds questions are the clearest tier marker: lower-tier students usually have never met them, and they appear reliably on higher-tier papers.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations including one linear and one quadratic. This strand is the strongest predictor of whether a student will cope with A Level or IB Mathematics, and it is where higher-tier marks are most often thrown away.

subjects.name: Quadratics and the function toolkit
subjects.description: Solving by factorising, formula and completing the square, plus turning points, roots and sketching. Students who only know the formula lose the questions that ask for a minimum value or a vertex, because those need the completed-square form.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle rules, similarity, congruence and the circle theorems at the higher tier. Marks here depend on naming the reason, not just the number: an unjustified angle in a 'give reasons' question scores part of the available credit at best.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, then the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems at the higher tier. Three-dimensional trigonometry is the single most avoided topic in Year 11 revision in our experience.

subjects.name: Graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Straight lines, gradients, parallel and perpendicular lines, quadratic and reciprocal curves, and gradient of a chord or tangent at the higher tier. Sketches lose marks for missing intercepts and asymptotes in exactly the same way they do at IB level.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, and tree and Venn diagram probability. Histograms with unequal widths are the most reliable source of lost marks at the higher tier, because frequency density is rarely taught twice.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and rates
subjects.description: Direct and inverse proportion, best-value comparison, compound measures and exponential growth and decay. These are the questions dressed as real-life contexts, where students lose marks by answering the arithmetic and ignoring the units asked for.

subjects.name: The investigation component
subjects.description: 0607 includes an investigation paper, which is unusual at this level and valuable for students heading to the IB, because it rehearses the kind of extended reasoning the Diploma exploration demands. Schools that run 0607 are usually IB continuum schools and choose it deliberately.

subjects.name: Paper technique and command terms
subjects.description: Show that, work out, explain, give a reason, hence. Each instruction has a mark-scheme consequence, and a student who writes the answer to a 'show that' question without the intermediate lines loses the method marks. This is taught separately from content and usually changes a grade boundary faster.

sections.heading: Dubai Hills Estate against Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Town Square
paragraphs: Start with the comparison, because it decides the schedule. Four communities within fifteen minutes of each other produce four different evenings for a Year 11 mathematics student, and the differences are entirely about distance to school and household shape rather than about anything academic.

Dubai Hills Estate families mostly bus into the Al Quoz and Al Barsha South school belt, with returns clustered around 15:40 to 15:55. Arabian Ranches has a primary school inside the community, so younger siblings are home early while secondary students travel further; the net effect is often more than one pick-up in the same afternoon. Motor City and Sports City are apartment-heavy, with some students walking to school and others on long runs, so two children in the same building can need slots two hours apart. Town Square, Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3 sit furthest out with the longest bus journeys of the group.

The academic picture varies too, in a way that follows the housing rather than the geography. Established villa communities have settled cohorts, so the questions are sequential: tier placement in Year 10, then the A Level or Diploma choice in Year 11. Faster-turning rental areas generate mid-year transfers, where the issue is coverage rather than ability, and a student may be three chapters behind through no fault of their own.

What does not vary is the remedy. In each case the work is to establish the exact syllabus code, the tier, the papers and their weightings, then close the measurable gap with past papers marked against the published scheme. Because that work is identical across all four communities, the only thing that should change by address is the time the lesson starts. Online delivery is what lets the specialist stay the same while the clock moves.

sections.heading: Which mathematics qualification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that should be asked before any tutor is hired, and it is answered on the front of a past paper or on the school's entry information rather than by guesswork. Across the schools Dubai Hills Estate families use, at least three distinct mathematics qualifications are in circulation, and they are not interchangeable.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most widely sat. It is tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped below the top grades and Extended reaching A*. Cambridge revised the specification, and the paper structure differs between the older and the current version, including how calculator and non-calculator assessment is split. Check which syllabus year your child is entered for on the Cambridge syllabus page for their examination series, because past papers from the wrong version drill the wrong paper shape.

Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is the quieter one and worth knowing about. It is also tiered, and it adds an investigation component, which is why IB continuum schools often prefer it: the extended reasoning rehearses what the Diploma exploration later demands. A student on 0607 who is given 0580 past papers by a tutor who did not check will practise a paper they are not sitting.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, is tiered into Foundation and Higher, with two papers of two hours at each tier and a 9 to 1 grade scale. Specification B, 4MB1, is a different structure again. A grade 9 and an A* are not the same statement about a student, and a tutor should be able to explain which they are aiming at without looking it up.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the last moment it can be changed
paragraphs: Tier is the most consequential administrative fact in IGCSE mathematics and the least discussed. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available. A student entered on Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, which means a Year 10 placement made on a single set of Year 9 results can quietly decide what a sixth-form application looks like two years later.

Schools place students for defensible reasons. A student who would be swamped by the higher tier scores better on the lower one, and a safe grade on Core is worth more than a scattered one on Extended. The problem is that placement is often treated as settled when it is still movable, and parents in Dubai Hills Estate frequently discover the cap in Year 11 when the sixth-form entry requirement is published.

The practical test is whether the student can handle the content that only appears at the higher tier. For Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher that means bounds, surds at the appropriate level, the sine and cosine rules, circle theorems with reasons, histograms with unequal class widths, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations with a quadratic. A student who can be taught those six to eight areas to a reliable standard across two terms is a candidate for a tier conversation. A student who is still insecure with negatives and index laws is not, and saying so early is kinder than agreeing with the ambition and failing in June.

Timing matters because entries are made months before the examination. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. The gap between entry and exam is the point: by the time revision feels urgent, the tier has already been submitted. Ask the department in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, with evidence from marked higher-tier papers rather than a general sense that your child could do better.

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam calendar with real dates, and why zones matter in Dubai
paragraphs: No competitor page we examined for these queries names an examination series, an entry deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because these dates are published, they are the dates that constrain everything, and they are the reason a January decision is worth more than an April one.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March 2027 key dates are a useful worked example of the distance between entry and examination: examination period 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read your own series on cambridgeinternational.org rather than borrowing another series' dates.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The zone point is specific to being in Dubai and almost nobody mentions it. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A family in Dubai Hills Estate downloading a timetable found through a search engine may well be reading a different zone's version. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that document.

sections.heading: Where a grade 6 becomes a grade 7, and where it does not
paragraphs: Most families hiring an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate are asking for one or two grades, not a transformation, and the work that delivers that is narrower than general revision. Across the students we see, the same handful of areas separate a 6 from a 7 or an A, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan against.

The first is algebraic fractions and the harder simultaneous equations, where one linear and one quadratic equation are solved together. These appear reliably on higher-tier papers, carry several marks each, and are routinely skipped in revision because they look unpleasant. The second is histograms with unequal class widths, which require frequency density and are taught once, early, and then never revisited. The third is circle theorems where the question asks for reasons: the angle is often right and the justification missing, which costs the communication marks.

The fourth is three-dimensional trigonometry, which students avoid because it needs a diagram drawn before any calculation starts. The fifth is not content at all. It is method recording: writing down enough intermediate working that the method marks survive an arithmetic slip at the end. Students at this level frequently lose two or three marks a paper to answers presented without the lines that earned them.

The useful consequence is that a seven or eight week block aimed at those five areas is a realistic and measurable plan, which a general promise to improve at maths is not. We mark two recent papers in the first lesson, count the losses by category, and name the three areas worth the time. Anything that is not costing marks comes off the list, including topics the student finds uncomfortable but is not actually being examined on heavily.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and why in-home costs more in these communities
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this query publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency these households transact in. Here are the Dubai bands in dirhams with the organisation that published each one, read in October 2026.

Budget online tuition, typically university students or generalist platforms, runs from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors pricing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and the Bestimate Dubai rate survey putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, and independent home tutors ask AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages visible in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The in-home premium is a travel charge, and the comparison this page is built on makes it concrete. A tutor driving to Dubai Hills Estate from Al Barsha at 16:15 may lose twenty to thirty minutes each way; the same tutor reaching Town Square or Arabian Ranches 3 at the same hour can lose closer to fifty. Somebody pays for that time, and it is not the tutor. It buys no additional teaching, which is the whole point of the comparison.

Two further cautions on price. An hourly rate is not a product: a session that includes marked work between lessons, written notes and a plan against the school's own deadlines is a different purchase from an hour of conversation at the same price. And a figure quoted without a source and a date is not a market rate, it is a claim. Every number in this section carries both. We publish no IB Gram rate card here because the right figure depends on tier, specification and weeks remaining; the first lesson is free and the quote arrives with the written plan.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same in every one of these communities
paragraphs: The comparison that runs through this page ends in one place. Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Town Square differ in commute, housing and the questions families ask first, and none of those differences changes what good IGCSE mathematics tuition consists of. It is a specialist in the specification your child is entered for, working the right tier's past papers against the published mark scheme, at an hour the student can actually concentrate in.

IB Gram delivers that online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated on every UAE page on this site, and it is stated here rather than buried because the alternative is letting a family discover it after a phone call.

The case for it is the comparison itself. Hiring within driving distance of Dubai Hills Estate means choosing among mathematics teachers who live nearby and have that evening free. Online, the same family chooses a Cambridge 0607 specialist, or a Pearson 4MA1 Higher specialist, or someone who has taught the revised 0580 paper structure from the year it changed. For a narrow requirement, specialism beats proximity, and the narrower the requirement the bigger the gap. The honest trade-offs are real too: a video lesson needs a quiet corner and a charged laptop, younger students need a parent within earshot for the first few sessions, and a tutor on screen cannot take a phone away.

On the legal position, which the competitor set covers in a single heading at best: an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two working day completion time through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts is published, treat any page quoting a specific fine figure as unverified.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: what the UAE actually requires at equivalency
paragraphs: Families on a British curriculum around Dubai Hills Estate eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency, usually when a UAE university application is being prepared, and the published rule is narrower than the rumour. For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details are routinely reported wrongly. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which changes the arithmetic of a Year 11 option choice. And the number is five: one page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects, which is not what the published clarification says. Getting the count right is a small thing that changes real decisions, because a family planning a sixth subject purely for equivalency may not need it.

For completeness, the American track is assessed differently: English proficiency via a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics via at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB there is no points threshold we have been able to read on an official source, so this page publishes none. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any specific IB figure found elsewhere as unverified until you have seen it on the Ministry's own page.

Alongside all of this, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects occupy real timetable space in a Year 11 week, and a revision plan that ignores them is a plan the student cannot keep. Equivalency itself is a process completed with the Ministry; no tutoring service performs it, influences it or is required for it.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school in Dubai Hills Estate use for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and it can differ between year groups and between subjects in the same school. The fastest way to find out is the front page of a recent past paper or assessment, which carries the board name and the syllabus code, or the entry information the examinations officer issues. Around Dubai Hills Estate all three of Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are in circulation. Ask before booking any tutoring, because practising the wrong board's papers drills a paper structure your child will not sit.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 harder than Pearson Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are differently shaped rather than ranked. The content overlaps heavily, but the paper structures, timings and grade scales differ: Cambridge reports A* to G with the available range capped by tier, while Pearson reports 9 to 1 with the same kind of cap. Cambridge has also revised 0580, so the paper split differs between syllabus versions. What matters for a student is familiarity with the examiner's conventions on their own specification. A tutor who has taught the specific code will see the recurring question styles that a general maths tutor will not.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607 International Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Both are tiered Cambridge IGCSE mathematics qualifications, but 0607 includes an investigation component and is often chosen by IB continuum schools because the extended reasoning rehearses what the Diploma exploration later requires. The content emphasis differs as well, with 0607 leaning more on graphical and technology-supported work. A student on 0607 needs 0607 past papers; being given 0580 material is one of the more common tutoring mismatches around schools in the Al Barsha corridor, and it is avoidable by checking the code once.

faqs.question: My son is on the Core tier and wants a top grade. Can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the window closes earlier than families expect because entries are submitted months before the examination. Cambridge's own key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 for exams starting 3 February 2027, which is the general shape across series. Raise it in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, with marked higher-tier papers as evidence. The content test is whether bounds, circle theorems with reasons, histograms with unequal class widths and algebraic fractions can be taught to a reliable standard in the time left.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE maths exams actually sat by students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Results dates differ by board and series: Pearson sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable for your series, since provisional versions are revised.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE maths tutoring cost more in Dubai Hills Estate than in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Online, no, because there is no travel in the price. In-home tutoring does vary by community, and that is the whole in-home premium: a tutor reaching Dubai Hills Estate from Al Barsha at 16:15 loses twenty to thirty minutes each way, while reaching Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square at the same hour can cost closer to fifty. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors, against AED 200 to 450 and above for online specialists. The teaching is identical; the driving is not.

faqs.question: Do you travel to homes in Arabian Ranches or Motor City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own working on camera and written notes afterwards. The gain is the pool you choose from: instead of the mathematics teachers who live near Motor City and have Tuesday free, you choose someone who teaches your child's exact specification and tier, and the lesson starts the moment the student sits down.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is more efficient and Year 11 is more common. Starting in Year 10 means fluency and algebra can be fixed while they are still cheap to fix, and it means a tier conversation can happen with two terms of evidence behind it rather than a rushed appeal. Starting in Year 11 works, but the available work narrows to the areas that measurably cost marks, and the exploration of alternatives is gone. The least useful timing is the term of the examination, when only paper technique and method recording can still move.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE searches states six subjects, which the published clarification does not support. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is their process rather than a school's or a tutor's.

faqs.question: Can my daughter sit different subjects with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Many schools do exactly that, choosing Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson Edexcel for others, and a student can also sit a subject as a private candidate at an approved centre. The practical consequences are administrative: two sets of timetables, two results release dates, and two sets of entry deadlines to keep track of. For tutoring it means confirming the board subject by subject rather than assuming the school uses one throughout. Ask the examinations officer for the entry list, which shows the board and code against each subject.

faqs.question: What does modular mean with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Modular structures let components be sat in different series rather than all at the end, which some Pearson qualifications allow and others do not. Whether it applies to your child depends on the specification the school has entered them for, so check the specification document on qualifications.pearson.com rather than relying on a general answer. Where a modular route is available it changes revision planning substantially, because an earlier component needs to be examination-ready while the rest of the course is still being taught. The examinations officer can confirm which structure is in use.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable zone matter for a school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable you read may not be the one your centre is using. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent in Dubai Hills Estate who downloads a timetable from a search result can easily be reading another zone's document. Ask your examinations officer which zone the centre is in and plan from that version only.

faqs.question: Will a grade 7 in IGCSE maths be enough for IB Maths Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: It usually meets the school's entry requirement, and it is not the same as being ready. IGCSE mathematics stops short of the calculus, proof and vector work that Analysis and Approaches opens with, so even strong IGCSE students meet genuinely new material in the first term of DP1. The students who cope are the ones whose algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than merely correct. A bridging block in the summer between Year 11 and DP1, aimed at differentiation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities, is the most useful few hours available at that point.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE maths tutor start after we get in touch?
faqs.answer: For the common specifications, usually within a few days, because the pool is not limited to tutors living near Dubai Hills Estate. Narrower requests take longer: a Cambridge 0607 specialist at Extended tier, or Further Pure Mathematics, can need a week or more to match properly. If no specialist is available for a specific code and tier, we will say so rather than assigning a general mathematics tutor and hoping. A free first lesson with the proposed tutor comes before any payment, so a poor match costs you an hour and nothing else.

With that and the school's assessment dates we can say whether a specialist is free, which papers the lessons will use, and what the weeks remaining can realistically move. dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hill.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Mathematics to Emirates Hills families online. Tell us the specification code on your child's exam entry and the series they are sitting, and we match on that rather than on the word maths, because Cambridge and Edexcel tier differently and reward different exam habits.

intro.heading: Work out the date first, then decide what tutoring can realistically do
paragraphs: Most parents arrive at IGCSE mathematics tutoring with a grade in mind and no date in mind. The date is the more useful of the two. A student eleven weeks from a terminal paper and a student eleven months from one need entirely different work, and the mistake families in Emirates Hills make most often is buying the eleven-month programme with eleven weeks left, or the eleven-week crash course when there was time to fix the foundations properly.

So start with the series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series available at some centres; Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and again in November. Your child's school has already chosen, entered them, and in most cases decided the tier. Those three facts constrain everything. A Cambridge candidate in a March series centre has a final entry deadline in the preceding November and forecast grades due in late February; a Pearson November candidate sits papers through late October and into November and waits until the following January for results.

The second thing to establish is the tier, because in mathematics the tier sets a ceiling on the grade before any revision happens. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Edexcel 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. A Core or Foundation candidate cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and the decision is normally made by the department during Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments. If that decision looks wrong to you, the window to discuss it closes long before the exam, and it closes at the entry deadline, not at the paper.

Third, find out which administrative zone your child's centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. The guidance for exams officers is unambiguous about this and states that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version of the timetable was used. Parents very rarely check this; it costs nothing to ask the exams officer which zone the school is in and to work from that timetable rather than from a version found online.

Once those three facts are on the table, the planning becomes concrete. Count backwards from the paper to the mock, from the mock to today, and allocate the weeks. The sections below do that arithmetic in public: what each milestone is, who sets it, what a student should have finished by then, and what a tutor should be doing in the weeks between. Everything here is built around the calendar because for an IGCSE mathematics candidate the calendar is the binding constraint, not the syllabus.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hill.programmesIntro: Around Emirates Hills a child reaches IGCSE mathematics through one of a few routes, and each arrives with a different amount of exam experience. The stage your child is at changes whether this term is about building content, choosing a tier, or rehearsing papers under time.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins, taught against a school scheme rather than an external specification. There is no external examination, so gaps accumulate invisibly. Algebraic fluency, fraction and index work, and confidence with negative numbers are the three things that decide how comfortable Year 10 feels.
programmes.countryNote: In Emirates Living the Key Stage 3 years are when tier outcomes are quietly decided. A child who leaves Year 9 shaky on algebraic manipulation tends to be placed in Core or Foundation in Year 10, and that placement sets a grade ceiling two years early. Tutoring at this stage is cheap, unhurried, and the single highest-leverage intervention available.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: A two-year course examined in the Core tier or the Extended tier. Core candidates sit a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of ninety minutes each; Extended candidates sit a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of two hours each. There is no coursework component, so the whole grade rests on terminal papers.
programmes.countryNote: The Cambridge calendar is what shapes the year for most British-curriculum schools near Emirates Hills. Entries close months before the papers, forecast grades are submitted weeks before them, and results reach the centre before certificates follow. Ask the exams officer for the zone timetable and the internal mock dates in the same email; both drive the revision plan.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Examined in two papers of two hours each, both with a calculator permitted, tiered as Foundation or Higher. Foundation covers the lower grade range and Higher the upper, with an overlap band. The absence of a non-calculator paper changes revision priorities noticeably compared with Cambridge.
programmes.countryNote: Families sometimes discover mid-year that their child is on Edexcel rather than Cambridge, or the reverse, because the two are discussed interchangeably in conversation. They are not interchangeable: tier names differ, paper counts differ, and calculator rules differ. Read the specification code on the exam entry confirmation and tell your tutor that code, not the word IGCSE.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or IB Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The destination that gives IGCSE mathematics its weight. A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches Higher Level both assume secure algebra from the Extended or Higher tier. Students who scraped a pass at the top of a lower tier routinely struggle in the first term of either.
programmes.countryNote: This is the argument for taking IGCSE mathematics seriously in a household where the child is heading for engineering, medicine or economics. Schools near Emirates Hills split after sixteen between A Level and the IB Diploma, and both routes assume the Extended or Higher content as a starting point rather than as an achievement.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hill.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is a single qualification assessed through two terminal papers, but the work splits into distinct blocks that reward different revision. The list below names the blocks and what each one costs a candidate who leaves it alone until April.

subjects.name: Number and the non-calculator paper
subjects.description: Fractions, ratio, percentages, standard form, surds at Extended, bounds and accuracy. Cambridge candidates face this without a calculator, which turns a routine topic into a technique topic. Marks go on upper and lower bounds, on percentage change in reverse, and on rounding too early in a multi-step calculation.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, simultaneous and quadratic equations, inequalities, sequences, and function notation at Extended. This is the block that decides the tier and the block where a weak Key Stage 3 shows up. Factorising a quadratic with a leading coefficient above one separates grades reliably.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry and transformations
subjects.description: Gradients, intercepts, parallel and perpendicular lines, and the four transformations with their full descriptions. Students lose marks by describing a transformation incompletely: a rotation needs angle, direction and centre, and two of the three earns nothing if the third is missing.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, arcs and sectors, similar shapes and the circle theorems at Extended. Circle theorems are learnt as diagrams and tested as reasoning chains; candidates who cannot name the theorem they used lose the justification marks even with the right angle.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, with the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems at Extended. The reliable failure is a non-right-angled triangle attacked with basic ratios, and bearings questions where the diagram is never drawn.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability at Extended. Histograms with unequal class widths cost more marks per question than any other statistics topic because frequency density is taught once and tested in context.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic, magnitude, position vectors and geometric proofs using vectors. The proofs are the sticking point: students compute correctly and then do not write the sentence that makes the result a proof, which is where the final marks sit.

subjects.name: Calculus at Extended level
subjects.description: Differentiation of simple polynomials, gradients of curves, and stationary points where the specification includes them. Light in volume and heavy in marks, and frequently the last topic taught, which means it is the topic most often met for the first time in a mock paper.

subjects.name: Exam technique and command words
subjects.description: Show that, work out, calculate, give an exact answer, write down. Each licenses different work and each has a marking consequence. A candidate who writes an answer with no working on a show-that question has scored nothing, and this single habit costs more marks across a paper than any content gap.

modes.description: A weekly session running alongside the school's scheme of work across two years or the better part of one. sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in Emirates Hills can do depends on the weeks left
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Emirates Hills is most useful when the work is planned backwards from a known date. Establish three facts before the first lesson: which series your child is entered for, which tier, and which administrative zone the centre sits in. Those three answers determine whether the next period of work is about building content, repairing a tier decision, or rehearsing papers under the clock.

With a year or more in hand the work is content and fluency, and it is unhurried. Algebraic manipulation gets rebuilt properly, the non-calculator habits get established before they are urgent, and tier placement stays a live conversation with the department rather than a fact the family receives. This is also the only window in which a Core or Foundation placement can realistically be revisited, because once the entry is submitted the tier is fixed.

With a term in hand the work is the mock script. A marked mock is a better curriculum than any revision guide because it is specific to this student. Every lost mark gets a topic label and an error type, the clusters get taught, and the same questions get reattempted cold two weeks later. Eight to ten sessions handled this way typically shifts more than twenty sessions of general revision, because nothing is spent on material the student already holds.

With six weeks left the work changes character again and becomes rehearsal. No new content, timed sections rather than whole papers so that review happens while the attempt is fresh, the two papers practised separately because a calculator paper and a non-calculator paper reward different instincts, and attention moved to pacing and the discipline of writing working down. Parents often resist this because it feels like less teaching. It is where the last grade boundary is crossed.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards, with the dates the boards publish
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes an exam calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is the first thing a parent needs. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables for future series ahead of time.

The useful thing about those series is not the exam week. It is how far ahead of the exam week everything else sits. Take the Cambridge March 2027 series as the worked example, because the published key dates make the point plainly: the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results arrive on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. A family that starts thinking about tier in January 2027 is two months past the only decision that mattered.

The Pearson pattern has the same shape with different numbers. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January gap is the one families forget: a November candidate waits roughly two months, which matters if a sixth-form application depends on the grade.

Because provisional timetables can be revised, work from the live official timetable rather than from a date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. Ask the exams officer for the current zone timetable in writing and keep it. The table below sets the milestones out in the order they happen, with the authority that sets each one.

sections.heading: Administrative zones: the timetable error that cannot be undone
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a separate version of each timetable per zone. The exams officer guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version was used. That sentence should be read twice by any parent building a revision plan from a timetable found through a search engine.

The practical consequence is small to fix and large to get wrong. A paper that sits on a Tuesday morning in one zone may sit on a Wednesday afternoon in another. A student who has rehearsed a two-paper sequence in the wrong order has rehearsed the wrong thing, and a family who has booked travel around the wrong dates has a genuine problem that no amount of tutoring resolves.

So the first email of the examination year goes to the exams officer, not the mathematics department, and it asks three questions: which administrative zone is the centre in, which series are my child's mathematics papers in, and what are the internal mock dates. Those answers are administrative facts the office holds and will give you. Everything a tutor plans sits on top of them.

There is a second zone-related point about retakes. If a student misses a paper or performs far below the forecast, the next available series may be months away and in a different part of the academic year, which changes whether a retake fits around a sixth-form start. Ask the exams officer what the next available series for that specification is at that centre before you decide anything about a resit.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: when the ceiling gets set
paragraphs: In IGCSE mathematics the tier decision sets a ceiling on the grade before revision begins, which makes it the most consequential academic decision of Year 10. Cambridge 0580 offers a Core tier and an Extended tier. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 offers Foundation and Higher. In both cases the lower tier covers the lower part of the grade range and the upper tier the upper part, with an overlap band in the middle.

Departments make the decision on internal evidence, usually across Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, and they make it conservatively because entering a student for a tier they cannot access produces a worse outcome than entering them for a tier they can. That logic is sound in aggregate and occasionally wrong for an individual, particularly for a student who arrived mid-course from a different curriculum and whose early internal assessments measured unfamiliarity rather than ability.

If you think the placement is wrong, the conversation has to happen before the final entry deadline, which for a Cambridge March 2027 candidate was 27 November 2026. Bring evidence rather than an opinion: a timed upper-tier paper attempted under supervision, with the script, is worth more than any number of conversations about potential. A tutor can supervise exactly that and hand you the marked script to take to the department.

One honest caveat. Moving a student to the higher tier is right when the content gap is closable in the time left and wrong when it is not, and a tutor who always recommends the move is not giving you advice. The table below sets out what each tier actually involves so the conversation can be about papers rather than about ambition.

sections.heading: The eight weeks after a mock, week by week
paragraphs: A January mock script is the most valuable document an IGCSE mathematics candidate will produce, and in most households it is looked at once and filed. The eight weeks after it arrive with a structure already built into them if the script is used properly, and the structure is the same whether the target is a grade 5 or a grade 8.

The first week is analysis, not teaching. Every lost mark gets two labels: a topic and an error type, where the types are content, method, arithmetic, reading and time. The totals tell you what the next six weeks are for. A script with twenty marks lost to arithmetic and six to content needs a different programme from the reverse, and the grade alone cannot distinguish them.

Weeks two to five are teaching the two or three largest content clusters, with the deliberate decision to ignore the smaller ones. Trying to fix everything in six weeks fixes nothing. Weeks six and seven are reattempts, cold, of the same questions that were lost, which is the only evidence that the teaching held. Week eight is timed rehearsal on fresh material, both papers separately.

The table sets this out as a plan you can run with or without a tutor. The one thing that does not work is reading through a revision guide front to back, because it spends most of its time on material the student has already demonstrated they hold.
