dubai/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The evidence method is the same across the British-curriculum ladder, but what counts as evidence changes with the qualification. These four bands cover what a Dubai family is most often asking about, including the two most mispriced situations in the emirate: crossing into IGCSE from another system, and a retake series.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Externally marked papers with published mark schemes, which makes IGCSE the easiest qualification in the ladder to evidence properly. Every lost mark has a scheme line behind it, so a script can be sorted into method, command term, content, arithmetic and timing losses with no interpretation required. Section-level tracking works cleanly here because papers are structured consistently from series to series.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical obstacle is knowing which board. Schools choose subject by subject, so a student can sit Cambridge Mathematics and Pearson Physics in one series, and the mark schemes use different conventions. Evidence work starts with the syllabus code from the entry statement, because marking a 4MA1 script against a 0580 scheme produces a confident, useless report.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still run by a number of Dubai schools alongside or instead of IGCSE, with its own syllabus codes and paper structures. The evidence approach is identical — mark to the published scheme, sort the losses, track by section — but the papers are not interchangeable with IGCSE papers of the same subject name, so past-paper practice has to match the qualification the student is actually entered for.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between Dubai schools sometimes move between O Level and IGCSE mid-course without anyone flagging the difference. A baseline paper against the correct code is the quickest way to find out whether the content covered so far maps onto the qualification the new school will enter the student for.

programmes.name: AS and International A Level
programmes.description: The same evidence structure with higher stakes and longer papers, so the full-paper checkpoints matter more and the section-mark table carries more rows. Mark-scheme conventions carry over from IGCSE, which is one reason a student who has learned to read a mark scheme at sixteen has a durable advantage at eighteen. Written feedback shifts from technique towards argument and extended structure.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, is required alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Equivalency is the Ministry's process; verify current requirements on the official channel.

programmes.name: MYP crossover into IGCSE
programmes.description: Students arriving in a Dubai IGCSE class from the IB Middle Years Programme have usually been assessed against criteria out of eight rather than against mark schemes, and the first IGCSE paper is a genuine shock in form rather than in content. The baseline paper is especially valuable here, because it separates unfamiliarity with the paper from an actual content gap — two problems with very different costs.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's school turnover makes this crossover common, and it runs in both directions. The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, so most movement is from MYP into IGCSE rather than the reverse, and the autumn term of Year 10 is when it is cheapest to fix.

dubai/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject produces a different kind of evidence, because each paper structure fails in a different place. The entries below name the codes and then state what is actually measurable in that subject — the number the section-mark table will track and what a fortnightly note can honestly say.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The cleanest subject to evidence. Mark schemes award method and accuracy marks separately, so a script shows precisely how many marks were lost to unshown working rather than to wrong answers. The tracked number is method marks recovered per paper, which usually moves inside four weeks.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Evidence here is about where in a long solution the error enters, since one algebraic slip propagates through several marks and follow-through rules decide whether they are lost. The tracked number is marks lost after the first error, which is a measure of presentation discipline rather than ability.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Three tracked numbers rather than one: calculation marks lost to units, prefixes and significant figures; explanation marks lost to describing instead of explaining; and practical-paper marks, which in Cambridge carry 20 per cent of the qualification. The three move at different speeds and should be reported separately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations give a crisp measurable: marks lost because the equation was not balanced before the arithmetic started. Alongside it, extended-response marks against the structure the scheme rewards. Both are countable per paper, which makes a six-week comparison meaningful rather than impressionistic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject where the section-mark table is most revealing, because recall sections often sit high while data-handling and application sections sit low. A single overall percentage hides that completely, which is why strong biology students plateau at a 6 for a year without anyone identifying the reason.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Harder to evidence and still possible. Reading responses are marked against assessment criteria rather than point-scored, so the tracked artefact is a criteria grid with the band for each strand, plus a count of analytical comments per response versus paraphrase. Both change visibly across a block.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different criteria, frequently confused in Dubai enquiries. The measurable is precision in the summary task — content points captured against content points available — which is one of the few English numbers that behaves like a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.description: The tracked evidence is the ratio of quotation used to support a point about method against plot retold, scored on the student's own essays. Set texts differ between Dubai centres, so the baseline essay has to be on a text the school actually teaches rather than a generic one.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Evidence is almost entirely about command-term compliance. Count the marks lost where a definition was given for an analyse or evaluate command, and the number falls sharply once an answer skeleton is practised against real mark schemes. Fast-moving and easy to demonstrate in writing.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Two separate trackable strands: theory terminology precision, measured as marks lost to imprecise definitions, and algorithmic work, measured by whether a trace table was completed before coding. Both are countable, and the second is the single highest-yield habit on the paper.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: In Geography the measurable is named case-study detail present in an answer; in History it is provenance used explicitly in source questions rather than content summarised. Where a Dubai centre runs the coursework option, support stays inside the permitted boundary and is documented as feedback on the student's own drafting.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Two distinct syllabuses and two distinct cohorts, and KHDA requires the first-language and additional-language classes to be organised separately. Evidence differs accordingly: reading-rate and extended-writing bands for 0508, vocabulary coverage and accuracy counts for 0544. Matching the wrong stream makes the evidence meaningless.

dubai/igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what an online session needs to work there
dubai/igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery has its own geography: connection quality, a quiet room, and the gap between the bus arriving and the student being able to concentrate. These are the Dubai communities we schedule most often, with the practical constraint that actually decides each one.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: High-rise living where the limiting factor is a quiet room rather than bandwidth. Students usually work at a dining table or a bedroom desk with a second device as a document camera for handwritten working. Late slots to 20:00 are more workable here than in villa communities.

regions.name: Emirates Living, The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa households with reliable connections and a study room, which makes these the easiest sessions to run technically. The constraint is the activity timetable: swimming and football occupy 16:00 to 18:00 for most Year 10 and 11 students, pushing sessions late.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Dense mid-rise communities with very large secondary cohorts. Sessions here are frequently booked in pairs for siblings an hour apart, which works well online because no travel sits between the two and the tutor keeps both section-mark tables open.

regions.name: Mudon, Town Square and Tilal Al Ghaf
regions.note: Outlying villa communities where a visiting tutor would spend forty minutes each way. Online removes that entirely, and these are the clusters where families most often move to video after failing to book a specialist locally. Weekend morning slots are popular.

regions.name: Dubai Investment Park and Al Furjan
regions.note: Long bus runs mean many students are not settled before 16:45, so a 17:15 start holds better than an earlier one. Families here use the December and spring breaks as intensive blocks more than any other Dubai cluster, which suits full-paper checkpoints.

regions.name: Al Barari, Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Low-density communities with strong connections and little scheduling competition, where the main constraint is simply how late a Year 11 student can usefully work. We cap evening sessions at 20:00 because a full timed paper after that produces unreliable evidence.

regions.name: Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Established communities with a high proportion of Arabic first-language candidates and a mix of O Level and IGCSE entries. Confirming the qualification and code before the baseline paper matters more here than in the newer British-curriculum catchments.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Uptown
regions.note: Weekend-heavy timetables because weekday evenings are compressed by commutes. Saturday morning is the most requested slot, and it is also the best time to sit a full timed paper, so checkpoint weeks are usually scheduled here on a weekend.

schoolClusters.city: Large British-curriculum secondaries with published mock cycles
schoolClusters.note: Schools running formal mock seasons in November and January, which gives an evidence block natural checkpoints to align with. The useful pattern here is a baseline in September, a block to January, and the school's own mock as the external comparison rather than a tutor-set paper.

schoolClusters.city: Schools running O Level alongside or instead of IGCSE
schoolClusters.note: Dubai still has significant O Level provision, and the papers are not interchangeable with IGCSE papers of the same subject name. Establishing the qualification and code before any baseline paper is sat is the whole of the setup work in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: IB continuum schools with students crossing into IGCSE
schoolClusters.note: Students moving from MYP criterion marking to externally marked papers, where the baseline separates unfamiliarity with the paper format from a genuine content gap. Cheapest to address in the autumn term of Year 10 rather than after a first mock.

sections.heading: The first ninety minutes: what the baseline actually produces
paragraphs: Before any teaching happens, one paper gets marked properly. Either the student sits a past paper under timed conditions on video, or a recent school mock is supplied and scanned. The tutor then marks it question by question against the board's own published scheme — not against a general sense of whether the answer was good — and itemises every lost mark with the scheme line that explains it. That process takes roughly ninety minutes of tutor time and produces four artefacts, listed in the table below.

The categorisation is where the value sits. Every lost mark is assigned to one of five categories: method not shown, command term misread, content genuinely absent, arithmetic or transcription slip, or time ran out. The distribution across those five is the plan for the whole block, and it is usually surprising. A student described by everyone as weak at mathematics commonly turns out to be losing more marks to unshown method and timing than to absent content, which is a four-week problem rather than a two-term one.

The second surprise is the section distribution. An overall mark of 58 per cent tells you nothing useful; the same script broken into paper sections frequently shows 80 per cent in two sections and 25 per cent in another, which is a completely different instruction for how to spend the next ten weeks. Tracking by section rather than by total is the single change that makes tutoring evidence legible, and almost no provider does it because it requires marking rather than conversation.

All four artefacts belong to you. The annotated script, the itemised loss table, the section-mark baseline and the written recommendation are sent as files and are yours whether or not any teaching follows. That is deliberate: a Dubai parent who takes a properly annotated script to a parents' evening is in a much stronger position than one who takes a worry, and that holds true even if the conclusion is that no tutoring is required this term.

sections.heading: One online session, minute by minute
paragraphs: Sessions in this market are described in adjectives. Here is one described in minutes, because the shape of the hour is what determines whether anything is produced. The structure below is what a sixty-minute IGCSE session looks like in practice, and the last column of the table is the part most arrangements skip entirely.

The opening ten minutes are spent marking the timed set from last week, in front of the student, against the scheme. This is not administration. It is the most instructive ten minutes of the hour, because the student watches marks being awarded and refused and learns what the scheme actually rewards. It also produces a number, which goes into the section-mark table, which is how a fortnightly note is able to say something specific rather than encouraging.

The middle forty minutes are teaching aimed at the highest-cost category from the baseline, and they are governed by one rule: no bare answers. A student who works mentally and writes a single line has forfeited method marks before correctness is even in question, so the tutor refuses to accept unshown working in session for the first four weeks. That habit is worth six to twelve marks a paper in mathematics and transfers to the sciences unchanged.

The closing ten minutes set the next timed question set — short, specific, sized for a student carrying nine or ten subjects — and record what was covered. The set is deliberately small because the purpose is a measurement next week, not volume. Where the sets stop being completed, the evidence trail says so plainly in the next fortnightly note, and we will recommend pausing rather than continue billing a slot that has stopped producing data.

sections.heading: Reading a mark scheme: the notation that explains your child's grade
paragraphs: Examination mark schemes are published documents written in a compressed notation, and almost no Dubai parent has ever had it explained. That is a shame, because the notation answers the question families ask most often — why did a correct-looking answer score two out of four — faster than any amount of discussion. The table below sets out the conventions you will meet on Cambridge and Pearson schemes for mathematics and the sciences.

The most important distinction is between method marks and accuracy marks. A method mark is awarded for a correct approach even when the final number is wrong. An accuracy mark requires the right answer. The consequence is immediate and under-appreciated: a student who writes down their working can score most of a question while getting it wrong, and a student who works mentally and writes only an answer can score zero for the same thinking. This is the single most profitable thing to teach a Dubai Year 11 candidate, and it takes about three weeks of refusal to accept bare answers.

Follow-through is the second convention worth understanding. Where a scheme allows follow-through, an error early in a long solution does not necessarily cost every subsequent mark, provided the later work is correct in the context of the mistake. That is why presentation discipline matters so much in Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics: the marks lost after the first error are a measure of how clearly the solution was laid out, and they are recoverable by habit.

Where this becomes practical is in what we do and do not supply. Mark schemes, syllabuses, past papers and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites and belong to them. We read them there and teach from your child's own school-issued or family-downloaded copies; we do not redistribute them, and any site offering bundles of them as downloads is telling you something about how it operates. Grade boundaries, in particular, are set per series after the papers are marked, so no fixed boundary should ever be quoted to you as a target.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, week by week: what the trail looks like
paragraphs: A block has a shape, and publishing it in advance is the simplest way to make the arrangement accountable. The table sets out a standard twelve-week evidence block: what the focus is each week, what artefact exists at the end of it, and what a parent should look for. If week five arrives and the artefact for week four does not exist, you have an answer about the arrangement without needing to interpret anything.

The pattern is front-loaded towards habit and back-loaded towards content, for a specific reason. Habit losses — method, command terms, units, timing — are the cheapest marks in the paper and they move fastest, so attacking them first produces a measurable change by week four and buys the student confidence that the rest of the block rests on. Content work is slower and benefits from the extra weeks, and the week-six paper tells you whether there is enough time left for the content that remains.

The two full timed papers are the backbone. A full paper at week six, marked against the scheme and broken into sections, compared against the baseline, is the only honest mid-block judgement available. Short sets show whether a specific habit changed; a full paper shows whether it survives ninety minutes of pressure, which is the condition the real exam imposes. Where a school's own mock falls inside the window, that becomes the checkpoint instead, because an externally administered paper is better evidence than a tutor-administered one.

What the closing summary must do is name what did not move. Any report that lists only improvements is a marketing document. A twelve-week block typically closes two or three loss categories convincingly, moves one partially, and leaves one largely untouched — and the untouched one is the most useful line in the summary, because it is what the next decision should be made about.

sections.heading: What it is honest to claim about grade movement
paragraphs: This is the section most competitor pages replace with a statistic. We are not going to, and the reasoning is worth setting out because it also tells you how to read everyone else's numbers. A claim such as a given percentage of students improving by a grade is only meaningful with the sample size, the period, the subjects, the starting grades and the method of measurement stated on the same page. Without those, the figure is unfalsifiable, and an unfalsifiable figure on a commercial page is a marketing choice rather than evidence.

What can be said honestly is narrower and more useful. Specific loss categories move at observable speeds: method-mark losses in mathematics typically fall substantially within three to four weeks of refusing bare answers; command-term losses fall within two to three weeks of drilling answer shapes against real schemes; timing collapse takes longer, usually four to six weeks, because it requires full-paper practice rather than question practice. Those are patterns we see on scripts, described as ranges, not a measured study with a published method — and they are stated that way deliberately.

Grade movement itself is not fully in a tutor's control, and anyone implying otherwise is selling. Grade boundaries are set per series after papers are marked and published by the boards afterwards, so the same raw mark can land differently in different series. A student's final grade also depends on the tier they were entered for — Cambridge Core is capped at grade C, Pearson Foundation at grade 5 — on whether they sat the paper well on the day, and on work done outside tutoring. The defensible claim is about marks recovered in specific paper sections, which is why that is what gets tracked.

There is one more number worth stating plainly: the strongest predictor we observe of whether tutoring moves marks is whether the between-session timed sets get completed. Not the rate paid, not the format, not the tutor's qualification tier. That is why the sets are small, why each session opens by marking them, and why the fortnightly note records completion. If a provider never mentions what the student has to do, the arrangement is being sold as something that happens to your child rather than something they do.

sections.heading: The room, the kit and the connection: making online work in Dubai
paragraphs: Online tuition fails for mechanical reasons more often than pedagogical ones, and all of the mechanical reasons are fixable in an afternoon. The requirements are modest, and being explicit about them before the first session is the difference between a block that produces evidence and one that produces frustration.

The connection comes first and is rarely the problem in Dubai. A stable connection carrying live video both ways plus a shared screen is comfortably within a standard home package in every community we schedule, and the practical failure mode is contention rather than bandwidth — three other people streaming in the same apartment during a 19:00 session. Wired where possible, and a session time chosen when the household is not at peak, solves nearly all of it.

The second requirement is a way for the tutor to see handwritten working as it happens, because for mathematics and the sciences a conversation about an answer is worth very little next to watching the working appear. Three arrangements work: a graphics tablet, which is best and costs least in the long run; a phone or second device angled over the page as a document camera, which is free and works well; or writing on paper and photographing each question as it is finished, which is slowest but adequate. We will tell you which one suits the subject at the trial.

The third is the room, and it matters most for younger students. A desk with the door shut beats a sofa, a second screen for the paper beats scrolling on one, and a bedtime that the session finishes well before beats a late slot squeezed in after activities. We cap evening sessions at 20:00 for IGCSE students because a full timed paper after that produces unreliable evidence, and unreliable evidence is worse than none — it leads to the wrong decision about the next ten weeks.
bullets: Wired connection where possible; pick a slot when the household is quiet
Graphics tablet, a second device as a document camera, or photograph each question
Two screens if possible: one for the tutor, one for the paper
A desk and a closed door, not a sofa and a television
No full timed papers after 20:00; the evidence is not reliable

sections.heading: Formats compared on the evidence they leave behind
paragraphs: Families usually compare tutoring formats on price and convenience. Comparing them on what documentation survives the arrangement is more revealing, because that is what you will have in March when a decision has to be made about the final term. The table does exactly that, and the result is not a clean win for any one format — it is a clean loss for arrangements that produce nothing written at all.

In-home visiting tuition in Dubai is priced by Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, and it can produce excellent evidence; the obstacle is practical rather than inherent. Marking happens on paper that stays in the student's room, notes are written in a book that gets left at school, and nothing is dated or collated unless the tutor is unusually disciplined. Six months later there is no trail. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai — home visits are a service we offer only in India — so this is offered as market comparison rather than as a choice we sell.

Group classes and centre enrolment have a structural limit on evidence: marking is per class, feedback is per topic, and the artefact that matters most — your child's own script annotated against the scheme — generally does not exist. That is a reasonable trade at AED 70 to 150 a student for topic revision where the group is genuinely at the same level. It is not a reasonable trade if the question you need answered is why a specific candidate lost nineteen marks on a specific paper.

What online one-to-one does well is specific and unglamorous: everything is a file. The annotated script is a file, the section-mark table is a file, the fortnightly notes are dated files, the two full papers are files. In March, a parent holding that set can make an informed decision in ten minutes, and if a tutor changes, the new tutor starts from the trail rather than from zero. That is the honest case for the format, and it has nothing to do with convenience.

sections.heading: When online is the wrong choice, and what we say instead
paragraphs: A page selling online tuition should be able to name the cases where it is the wrong answer, so here they are. Four situations, and in each one we will say so at the trial rather than take the booking and discover it in week five.

The first is a student who will not engage with a screen under any circumstances. This is less common than parents fear and more common than providers admit, and it shows up clearly in a thirty-minute trial: no written working, no questions, monosyllabic answers. Some of those students work well with someone physically present, and for a Dubai family that means a visiting tutor at Bestimate's published AED 180 to 350 band. We will say that plainly, because an arrangement that produces no evidence is worse than no arrangement.

The second is a household with no quiet space available at any usable hour. Online tuition requires a door that shuts for an hour, and in a crowded apartment at 19:00 that may not exist. Sometimes the fix is a time rather than a format — a 07:00 weekend session is genuinely better than a contested evening one — and sometimes it is not. The third is a student whose problem is not academic at all: a motivation, attendance or wellbeing issue dressed as a content gap. Tutoring is the wrong instrument, the baseline paper usually reveals it, and the right move is a conversation with the school rather than a block of sessions.

The fourth is a timetable with no room in it. A Year 11 student carrying ten subjects, three fixtures a week and a bus that arrives at 16:45 does not have capacity for two tutoring subjects plus between-session sets, and adding them produces incomplete work and unreliable evidence. The honest recommendation there is one subject, chosen by where the marks are, and we would rather make that recommendation than sell two slots that both underperform.

sections.heading: Mocks, forecast grades and what happens after results
paragraphs: The evidence trail has to connect to the official process at three points, and families are rarely told how any of them work. The first is the mock, which is set, marked and standardised by the school and is not an examination board judgement. A mock grade is useful as a comparison against the baseline and as paper-sitting practice; it is not a prediction with any external standing, and Dubai schools differ considerably in how harshly they mark them.

The second is the forecast grade, which is a centre obligation rather than a student task. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series list forecast grades as due 27 February 2027, with final entries having fallen on 27 November 2026 and the examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. The forecast is submitted by the school based on its own evidence. A tutor does not set it and should not imply influence over it, though a well-documented section-mark trail is a reasonable thing to share with a subject teacher before they submit.

The third is what happens after results. Results dates and post-results processes are set by the boards and administered through the centre: Cambridge released March 2027 results on Direct on 13 May with certificates in late June, and for Pearson, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Enquiries about results and any remark route run through the school to the board, within deadlines the board publishes for each series. Check them with your examinations officer rather than any tutoring site.

One boundary to restate here. No IB session or results date appears anywhere on this site that has not been confirmed with the IB directly, because the IB's own pages block automated checking and a date restated from a secondary source is not a verified date. Cambridge and Pearson dates above are from the boards' own published key dates and timetables, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should work from the live official timetable rather than from a restatement — including this one.

process.title: Confirm the qualification, board and code
process.description: Before anything else, the exact qualification: Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE or Cambridge O Level, with the code from the entry statement. Marking a 4MA1 script against a 0580 scheme produces a report that is confident and wrong, and in Dubai a single student frequently sits two different boards in one series.

process.title: Sit or supply a baseline paper
process.description: Either the student sits a past paper under timed conditions on video, or a recent school mock is scanned and sent. Timed conditions matter, because a paper done casually measures knowledge while the real paper measures knowledge under ninety minutes of pressure, and those produce different scripts.

process.title: Receive the four baseline artefacts
process.description: An annotated script, an itemised loss table sorting every lost mark into five categories, a section-mark baseline, and a written recommendation. All four are files and all four are yours, whether or not teaching follows. The recommendation sometimes says no tutoring is needed this term.

process.title: One free 30-minute trial lesson
process.description: With the tutor who would run the block, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. One per family, no card details. The trial works on the highest-cost category from the baseline, and we use it to tell you which handwriting setup the subject needs — graphics tablet, document camera or photographed pages.

process.title: Run the block with fortnightly notes
process.description: Ten teaching sessions across twelve weeks, full timed papers at weeks six and twelve, and a dated written note every fortnight updating the section-mark table. Each session opens by marking last week's timed set in front of the student, which is where most of the learning about the scheme happens.

process.title: Close with a summary that names what did not move
process.description: The closing document compares both full papers against the baseline section by section and states explicitly which loss categories closed, which moved partially and which did not move at all. The untouched one is the most useful line in it, because that is what the next decision should be made about.

whyPoints.title: Marking comes before teaching, every time
whyPoints.description: The first deliverable is a script annotated against the board's published scheme with every lost mark sorted into five named categories. A tutor who has not seen a marked script is guessing at where the marks went, which is the default in this market and the reason so many arrangements produce nothing measurable.

whyPoints.title: Marks tracked by paper section, not by overall score
whyPoints.description: An overall 58 per cent hides a script sitting at 80 per cent in two sections and 25 per cent in another, which is a completely different instruction for the next ten weeks. Section-level tracking is the change that makes tutoring evidence legible, and it requires marking rather than conversation.

whyPoints.title: Everything is a dated file you keep
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts, loss tables, section-mark tables, fortnightly notes and two full marked papers, all sent as files. If the tutor changes, the next one starts from the trail rather than from zero, and in March you can make an informed decision about the final term in ten minutes.

whyPoints.title: No statistics we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No improvement percentage, no satisfaction score, no star rating, no grade promise. A statistic needs its sample size, date and method on the same page, and several pages ranking for these searches publish review figures that contradict each other within one page.

whyPoints.title: Official process explained, not implied
whyPoints.description: Mocks are the school's, forecast grades are the centre's, boundaries are set per series by the board, and results and remark deadlines run through the examinations officer. We explain each and claim influence over none, and we publish no IB date that has not been confirmed with the IB directly.

whyPoints.title: The cases where online is wrong, named on the page
whyPoints.description: A student who will not engage with a screen, a household with no quiet hour, a problem that is not academic, and a timetable with no capacity. We say so at the trial rather than take the booking, because an arrangement that produces no evidence is worse than no arrangement.

faqs.question: How will I actually see, week by week, that online IGCSE tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Through four documents that exist whether or not anyone feels positive about the sessions. A baseline script annotated against the board's published scheme with every lost mark itemised; a section-mark table showing marks by paper section rather than overall; a dated written note every fortnight recording what moved and what recurred; and two full timed papers, at weeks six and twelve, compared against the baseline section by section. All are files and all are yours. If week five arrives and the week-four note does not exist, you have your answer without needing to interpret anything.

faqs.question: What do M1 and A1 mean on a mark scheme, and why should a parent care?
faqs.answer: M1 is one method mark, awarded for a correct approach even when the final number is wrong. A1 is one accuracy mark, which requires the right answer. The practical consequence is large: a student who writes out working can score most of a question while getting it wrong, and a student who works mentally and writes only the answer can score zero for identical thinking. On Dubai Year 11 mathematics scripts this habit alone is commonly worth six to twelve marks a paper, and it changes within about three weeks of a tutor refusing to accept bare answers in session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really mark my child's handwritten working over a video call?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better than marking it afterwards, because the tutor sees the working appear rather than reading a finished product. Three setups work. A graphics tablet is best and cheapest over a year. A phone or second device angled over the page as a document camera is free and works well. Writing on paper and photographing each question as it is finished is slower but adequate for essay subjects. At the trial we tell you which suits the subject — for mathematics and the sciences the live view matters considerably more than it does for English.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics tablet for online IGCSE maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Not essential, but it is the setup that produces the best evidence for mathematics and the sciences, because the tutor watches each line appear and can intervene at the line where the error enters rather than at the end. A basic tablet is a modest one-off cost and removes the friction of photographing pages every few minutes. The free alternative is a second device angled over the page as a document camera, which works well enough that we never make a tablet a condition of starting. Essay subjects need neither; a shared document is better for those.

faqs.question: What connection quality does a live video IGCSE lesson need in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. Live video both ways plus a shared screen sits comfortably inside a standard home package in every Dubai community we schedule. The practical failure is contention rather than bandwidth: three other people streaming in the same apartment during a 19:00 session will degrade the call when the line itself is fine. Wired where possible, and a slot chosen when the household is quieter, resolves nearly all of it. If the connection genuinely cannot hold a session, we will say so after the trial rather than persist and produce unreliable evidence.

faqs.question: Is a school mock grade a reliable prediction of the real IGCSE result?
faqs.answer: It is useful evidence and not a prediction with external standing. Mocks are set, marked and standardised by the school, and Dubai schools differ considerably in how harshly they mark them — some deliberately mark down to motivate, others use real past papers and real schemes. What a mock does well is measure performance under pressure across a full paper, which short question sets cannot. Use it as the week-six checkpoint in a block, because an externally administered paper under proper conditions is better evidence than one a tutor administers at home.

faqs.question: Who decides the forecast grade my child's school submits to the board?
faqs.answer: The school does, on its own evidence, and it is a centre obligation rather than a student task. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, forecast grades were published as due 27 February 2027, with final entries having closed on 27 November 2026. A tutor neither sets the forecast nor should imply any influence over it. What is reasonable is to share a documented section-mark trail with the subject teacher before they submit, because a teacher forming a judgement on limited classroom evidence may find a marked script and a mark-by-section record genuinely useful.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the percentage of your students who improve?
faqs.answer: Because a figure like that is only meaningful with the sample size, the period, the subjects, the starting grades and the measurement method stated on the same page, and without them it cannot be checked. An unfalsifiable number on a commercial page is a marketing choice, not evidence. Several pages ranking for these searches publish review and outcome figures that contradict each other within the same page, and one marks up questions that do not appear on the page at all. What we publish instead is what each loss category typically does, described as a range observed on scripts rather than as a study.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grade boundaries change from one series to the next?
faqs.answer: Yes. Boundaries are set for each series after the papers have been marked and are published by the boards afterwards, so the same raw mark can land on different grades in different series. That is why a target expressed as a raw mark from a previous series is unsafe, and why we track marks recovered by paper section instead. It is also why nobody should be sending you boundary tables as downloads — those documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson and should be read on their own sites, alongside the syllabus for the specific series your child sits.

faqs.question: What exactly do I receive at the end of a twelve-week block?
faqs.answer: Eleven documents. The annotated baseline script, the itemised loss table in its final state, the section-mark table maintained across the block, six dated fortnightly notes, the two full timed papers marked by section, and a closing summary comparing both papers against the baseline. The summary states which loss categories closed, which moved partially, and which did not move at all. That last line is the most useful one, because it is what the decision about the next term should be based on, and a report that lists only improvements is not a report.

faqs.question: How does tracking marks by paper section differ from tracking an overall score?
faqs.answer: An overall score averages away the information you need. A Dubai Year 11 script at 58 per cent commonly turns out to be 80 per cent in two sections and 25 per cent in a third, and those two scripts imply completely different work for the next ten weeks. Section tracking puts the marks next to the sections so revision time follows the marks rather than the student's preferences, which is usually the inverse. It also makes the week-six comparison honest: a two-point rise in a total can hide a strong section slipping while a weak one improved.

faqs.question: Can the online sessions be recorded so my child can rewatch them before exams?
faqs.answer: Session recording is agreed case by case before a block starts, and it is worth thinking about properly rather than defaulting to yes. Recordings of a minor's lessons are personal data, so the purpose, the storage location, who can access them and how long they are kept all need to be settled in writing first, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection is the relevant backdrop. In practice most students use the annotated script and the worked examples far more than they rewatch a session, so we usually suggest making the written artefacts good rather than making a video archive.

faqs.question: When is online tutoring the wrong choice for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Four cases, and we say so at the trial rather than take the booking. A student who will not engage with a screen at all, which shows up clearly in thirty minutes as no written working and monosyllabic answers. A household with no quiet hour available at any usable time. A problem that is not academic — motivation, attendance or wellbeing presenting as a content gap, which the baseline paper usually reveals. And a timetable with no capacity for between-session work, where the honest recommendation is one subject chosen by where the marks are rather than two that both underperform.

faqs.question: What happens if my child stops doing the timed sets between sessions?
faqs.answer: The fortnightly note records it, and we raise it rather than working around it. Completion of between-session sets is the strongest predictor we observe of whether marks move — stronger than the rate paid, the format or the tutor's qualification tier — because each session opens by marking last week's set and that is where most of the learning about the mark scheme happens. If sets stop getting done we first make them smaller, since an over-sized set is usually the cause. If they still do not get done, we recommend pausing rather than billing a slot that has stopped producing data.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai student work with a tutor who is in a different time zone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most do, which is the reason online delivery widens the specialist pool so much. Every session is scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and the tutor works to your child's clock, not the reverse — if a 17:15 Dubai slot is right, that is the slot. The practical consequence is positive: a student in Mudon or Dubai Investment Park can work with a specialist in 0606 Additional Mathematics or Cambridge 0508 Arabic who would never have driven to their community. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the baseline before you ask for the rate
dubai/igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Send the qualification, the board and the syllabus code from the entry statement, plus a recent paper your child has sat. You will get back an annotated script marked against the board's own published scheme, every lost mark sorted into five named categories, a section-mark baseline and a written recommendation — four files, yours to keep, whether or not any teaching follows. Then one free 30-minute trial lesson with the tutor who would run the block, over live video in Gulf Standard Time, one per family and no card details. If the recommendation is that no tutoring is needed this term, it will say so.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below carries a rate band rather than a slogan, set by subject scarcity, syllabus code and session length. The band is confirmed in writing before the free trial lesson, with the session length it is built around and anything that is charged on top stated in the same message.

intro.heading: What IGCSE private tuition in Dubai actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: Ask five Dubai providers for a price on the same Year 11 Extended Mathematics brief and you will get five numbers between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour. That fourteen-fold spread is not a market failing to settle; it is five different products sold under one phrase. One is a university student supervising homework. One is a tuition centre putting six students in a room. One is an agency placing a qualified subject teacher online. One is an independent tutor pricing in a forty-minute drive across the emirate. One is a named premium tutor with a waiting list. Comparing their headline rates tells you almost nothing, and that is the problem this page exists to solve.

Start with what the market publishes. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both read October 2026 — the budget online band. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200, which is roughly where a qualified subject tutor working online sits. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Then look at what the published rate leaves out, because this is where Dubai families are most often caught. Registration or placement fees charged once. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged before teaching starts. Material and past-paper charges, which are sometimes charges for documents the board publishes free. Travel surcharges by community, or travel priced inside an hour so that a sixty-minute visit delivers forty minutes of teaching. Cancellation windows of forty-eight or seventy-two hours that quietly convert a missed session into a paid one. Rescheduling limits per term. Report or progress-report fees. Peak-season premiums in the weeks before a series. Minimum commitments of ten or twenty sessions. Sibling rates that evaporate if session lengths differ. And the one nobody mentions until the invoice: whether the quoted figure is before or after VAT.

The third layer is contract shape, which matters more than the rate for most families. An hourly arrangement is the most expensive per session and carries almost no risk. A twenty-session package is cheaper per session and transfers the risk to you, because the exposure sits in the cancellation terms, the expiry date and who holds unused sessions if the match turns out to be wrong. A monthly subscription is the easiest to forget about, which is precisely why it is the model most likely to still be running in June for a student who stopped needing it in February. None of the three is wrong. Choosing one without reading the cancellation clause is.

On our own position and on delivery, plainly. IB Gram publishes no price list on this page, because an honest quote depends on subject scarcity, syllabus code and session length, and because a figure given before anyone has met your child is a figure about nothing. What we publish is the market with its sources attached, then one free 30-minute trial lesson — one per family, no card details — after which you get a written quote in AED naming the tutor, the session length and anything charged on top. Dubai lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.programmesIntro: Price behaves differently at each stage, because scarcity does. These four bands cover the stages a Dubai family buying IGCSE tuition is usually pricing across, including the one most providers never mention: entering a subject again, or for the first time, as a private candidate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two years that generate most tuition spend in Dubai. Pricing within IGCSE varies more by subject than by year: Extended Mathematics, the separate sciences and Additional Mathematics command the top of the qualified-tutor band, while Business, Economics and ICT sit below it because the tutor pool is wider. Year 11 spend typically runs 20 to 40 per cent above Year 10 for the same subject, driven by mock season and entry deadlines rather than by difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's scale is what creates the spread. The UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of enrolment across 227 private schools, so there are enough buyers to support a genuine budget tier and enough demand in exam term to support a premium one. Both tiers advertise with the same words, which is why comparing the included items matters more here than in a smaller market.

programmes.name: AS Level
programmes.description: Rates step up at AS, typically by 20 to 50 per cent over the same subject at IGCSE, because the pool of tutors competent at AS Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry is materially smaller. Families who have budgeted an IGCSE rate for two years are routinely surprised in Year 12. The step is worth planning for in the Year 11 budget rather than discovered in September.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at a grade no lower than E can substitute for one Advanced Level subject. That makes AS a route decision as well as an academic one, and it is the Ministry's process rather than a tuition provider's — verify the current wording on the official channel.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: The highest band in the British-curriculum ladder, where premium and named-tutor pricing concentrates. Published figures in this market reach AED 650 an hour at the top end. The practical question for a Dubai family is whether the premium is buying scarce subject competence — Further Mathematics, Physics, Economics at the top grades — or simply reputation, and the test is whether the tutor can diagnose from a marked script in the trial.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's post-16 cohort splits between A Level and the IB Diploma, and the two markets price differently for the same hour of a tutor's time. A family holding quotes from both should compare what is included rather than the rates, because Diploma quotes often bundle Internal Assessment feedback time that A Level quotes do not.

programmes.name: Retakes and private candidate entry
programmes.ageRange: Any age · November and March series
programmes.description: The least-discussed and most often mispriced situation: a student retaking a subject, or entering one their school does not offer. Tuition for a retake is usually shorter and more intensive than a first attempt, because the content exists and the loss patterns are known from a real script. The separate cost is the examination entry itself, which is set by the centre and the board rather than by any tutor.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of licensed centres in Dubai accept private candidates, and each publishes its own fee schedule and deadlines. No entry-fee figure is quoted on this page because none has been verified from a centre's own current schedule — ask the centre directly, in writing, and confirm the series deadline at the same time.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: Rates inside IGCSE are set by how many people in Dubai can teach the subject well, not by how hard it is. Each entry below names the syllabus codes and explains where that subject sits in the local price band and why, which is the part of pricing no provider explains.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Extended and Higher tier)
subjects.description: The single most demanded IGCSE subject in Dubai and consistently at the top of the qualified-tutor band. Extended and Higher-tier competence is a narrower skill than it appears, and Year 11 demand concentrates in the eight weeks after January mocks, which is exactly when the premium appears.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Priced above standard Mathematics because the tutor pool is small. Taken by stronger Dubai sets heading for A Level Mathematics, and the content — calculus, identities, series — is genuinely a different teaching job. Expect this to sit near the ceiling of the qualified-tutor band rather than the middle.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Top of the science band in Dubai, partly because competent physics teaching is scarce everywhere and partly because the practical component adds a second thing to teach. Rates for 0625 with the practical paper routinely exceed rates for the same tutor teaching Chemistry.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mid-to-upper science band. Supply in Dubai is better than physics, so rates sit slightly lower for equivalent experience. Demand peaks later in the year than mathematics, because chemistry problems tend to surface in the second mock rather than the first.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The widest supply of the three sciences and therefore the most competitive pricing. Worth noting that a cheaper biology rate does not mean a weaker tutor here — it reflects a larger pool rather than lower quality, which is the opposite of the assumption most families make.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Priced in the middle of the band, with a wide quality spread because almost anyone will offer it. The discriminating question for a Dubai family is whether the tutor marks to the board's own criteria rather than to a general sense of good writing, and that is testable in a trial.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English and frequently confused with it in Dubai enquiries. Specialists in the second-language syllabus are scarcer than general English tutors, so a correctly matched tutor often costs more than the first quote a family receives.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Among the scarcest specialisms in the Dubai market and priced accordingly, at or above the science band. KHDA requires Arabic first-language classes to be organised separately from the additional-language group, so the two are not interchangeable and should never be quoted as if they were.

subjects.name: Arabic as a foreign language
subjects.description: Better supplied than the first-language syllabus and priced closer to the middle of the band. The most common pricing error in Dubai Arabic enquiries is a first-language quote for an additional-language need, or the reverse, which is a difference of well over AED 100 an hour.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Below the science and mathematics bands because supply is wide. Technique rather than content drives the grade, which means short, cheap blocks are often genuinely sufficient — one of the few places in this market where the low quote and the right answer coincide.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Unusual pricing: wide supply of people who can code, narrow supply of people who can teach the specific theory terminology and pseudocode conventions the papers reward. The cheap end of this subject is cheap for a reason, and the trial lesson is where the difference shows.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Mid band, with a premium where a Dubai centre runs the coursework option, because support for coursework has to be delivered inside strict rules and fewer tutors will take it on. Always establish whether your school runs the coursework route before comparing quotes.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what they do to a quote
dubai/igcse-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Where you live changes the price of in-home tuition and, less obviously, the price you are first quoted for online tuition. These are the Dubai communities where that effect is clearest, with the market behaviour we actually see from each.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: High-rise households where travel surcharges are low but parking and building access slow a visiting tutor down, so sixty-minute visits often deliver less teaching. Online quotes here start higher than the emirate average simply because providers assume a higher budget.

regions.name: The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense apartment communities with large Year 10 and 11 populations, which makes this one of the few parts of Dubai where group classes genuinely find students at the same level. Group pricing of AED 90 to 150 a student is realistic here rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens, The Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Price-sensitive, high-volume demand and the most competitive quoting in the emirate. It is also where the budget tier is most likely to be sold as something it is not, so the included-items comparison matters more here than anywhere else.

regions.name: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Established communities with strong Indian and British curriculum demand side by side. Independent tutors dominate and quote directly, often below agency rates, which puts the permit and syllabus-code checks squarely on the parent.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Hills

regions.note: Long drives from where most Dubai tutors live, which shows up as a travel surcharge of AED 50 to 150 an hour or as a flat refusal. The gap between the in-home and online quote is wider here than in any other cluster.

sections.heading: What each provider model charges in Dubai, and what is inside the figure
paragraphs: A Dubai family holding five quotes is usually comparing five different products. The table below separates them by model, states the AED band each publishes, names the source and the month it was read, and lists what is typically inside and outside the figure. That last pair of columns is where the real comparison happens, because two quotes 40 per cent apart can represent identical value once travel, materials and cancellation terms are accounted for.

The budget online tier is real and has a legitimate use. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, which is where Tutopiya and EdFlik publish their entry rates, you are buying supervision and reassurance: somebody sitting with a student while they work, keeping them on task, answering questions as they arise. For a Year 10 student who simply does not start homework, that can be exactly the right purchase. What it does not buy is diagnosis against a syllabus code or marking to a board scheme, and families who expect that from a budget rate are disappointed by the product rather than cheated by it.

The qualified-tutor band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online, is where most genuine IGCSE teaching sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270. Above that, the premium tier reaches AED 650 at the top of the published Dubai market. The honest observation about the premium tier is that it buys scarcity reliably and competence only sometimes — a named tutor with a waiting list is priced by demand, and demand is not a measure of teaching.

In-home visiting rates look higher than online rates and are often the same thing with travel inside them. Bestimate's 2026 table gives AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, and independent listings run from AED 200 to AED 500. When you strip the travel out, the teaching component of a AED 300 visit is frequently in the same band as a AED 200 online session. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai — home visits are a service we offer only in India — so the comparison here is offered as market information rather than as an option we sell.

sections.heading: The eleven extras that change the real hourly cost
paragraphs: The gap between a quoted rate and what a Dubai family actually pays per hour of teaching is typically 10 to 35 per cent, and almost all of it sits in items that are perfectly legitimate and simply were not mentioned. None of the eleven below is a scam. Each is a real cost somebody has to carry. The problem is that they are disclosed at different points in the sales process by different providers, which makes the quotes incomparable unless you ask.

Two of them deserve particular attention because they are the largest. The first is travel inside the hour: a visiting tutor booked for sixty minutes who arrives late from Downtown and leaves on time has delivered forty-five minutes, so the effective rate is a third higher than quoted. Ask whether the hour starts at the agreed time or on arrival. The second is the cancellation window. A seventy-two-hour cancellation policy, applied to a Year 11 student with a changing fixture list and a mock timetable, converts several sessions a term into paid absences. Both are negotiable before signing and immovable afterwards.

The material charge is worth a separate warning. Board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites and should be read there; a charge for supplying them is a charge for something the board already provides, and redistributing those documents is a copyright matter. A charge for a provider's own written notes or question banks is a different and reasonable thing. Establish which one you are being billed for.

On VAT, the only statement this page will make is a narrow one. UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is not something a tutoring site should assert without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and this page has none. What you can and should insist on is clarity about the specific quote in front of you: ask whether the figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and ask for the answer in the same written message as the rate. A provider that will not put that in writing has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Hourly, block or term: three contracts and what each exposes you to
paragraphs: Most Dubai families think they are choosing a tutor. They are also choosing a contract, and the contract decides what happens in the two situations that actually arise: the match is wrong, or the need ends earlier than expected. Both are common. Neither is a failure. A sensible contract makes both cheap.

Paying per session is the most expensive per hour and the correct default for a first arrangement. Nothing is held in advance, stopping costs one session's notice, and the provider carries the risk of being good enough to be rebooked. The reason families move away from it is a discount, and the discount is real — but it is the price of accepting the risk transfer, and that trade only makes sense once the match has proved itself.

A package transfers risk in three specific places, and all three are readable before signing. Who holds unused sessions if you stop, whether the package expires on a date or on completion, and whether sessions are transferable between siblings or subjects. A twenty-session package at a 15 per cent discount that expires in ninety days, bought in October for a student whose need closes in January, is a bad purchase at a good rate. The version with no expiry and transferability is a good purchase at the same rate.

Monthly subscriptions are the most comfortable and the most likely to overrun. The failure mode is simple and we see it constantly: nobody cancels. A plan bought in October for a Year 11 mock problem is still billing in June, long after the problem closed, because reviewing it requires an awkward conversation. Our own answer to that is a written half-term review with an explicit stop recommendation, and we say stop when stopping is right. Any model can be run honestly; the subscription is the one that needs a review date built in.

sections.heading: Tuition spend against a Dubai school-fee year
paragraphs: Tuition is easier to judge next to the school bill than on its own, and 2026-27 is an unusually clean year in which to do it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most Dubai families this is the first flat fee year in some time, which makes a tuition decision a decision about new money rather than about a rising baseline.

The arithmetic below converts the market mid-band into the spend patterns Dubai IGCSE families actually choose. It assumes AED 220 an hour, a thirty-four-week academic year, and no extras, and it is arithmetic rather than an IB Gram price. The striking thing when it is laid out is how much cheaper a targeted block is than a year-long weekly slot, and how rarely families choose the block. Two subjects weekly across Year 11 is roughly AED 15,000; two targeted blocks that close the actual loss patterns are roughly a fifth of that.

The pattern that gives the best return in our experience is not the cheapest or the dearest. It is a marked diagnostic, then a short block against the named patterns, then a stop, then a second short block in the term before the series. Total spend lands near the middle of the table and the hours sit where the marks are. The pattern that gives the worst return is the open weekly slot with no named target, which is also the easiest to sell and the hardest to end.

One more line in the budget that most families miss entirely: examination entry for any subject taken outside the school's own entry. Private candidate entry is priced by the centre, not the tutor, and each Dubai centre publishes its own schedule and deadlines. No figure appears here because none has been verified from a centre's current schedule. If a retake or an extra subject is in your plan, get that number in writing early, because the entry deadline usually falls months before the paper.

sections.heading: Does paying more buy a better IGCSE grade?
paragraphs: Not reliably, and the market data makes that unusually easy to see. Published Dubai rates for the same described service span fourteenfold. If price tracked outcome, the AED 650 tutor would be roughly fourteen times as effective as the AED 45 one, which nobody believes. What price tracks in this market is scarcity, demand and overhead — and scarcity is only sometimes a proxy for competence.

Three things do correlate with grade movement, and none of them appears in a rate. The first is whether the tutor works from the correct syllabus code and the board's own mark scheme. A tutor teaching 0580 content to a 4MA1 candidate will be pleasant, expensive and off-target. The second is whether a marked script came before the teaching, because that is the only way the hours get aimed. The third is whether the student completes the work between sessions — the single strongest predictor we see, in every format and at every price point.

There is one legitimate reason to pay the top of the band, and it is scarcity rather than quality. Arabic as a first language, Additional Mathematics, and physics at the top grades have genuinely thin supply in Dubai. If your need is one of those, the premium is the market clearing and there is no clever way around it. If your need is Business Studies technique or English exam structure, paying premium rates is paying for availability you do not need.

What this means practically is that the trial lesson is worth more than the rate card. In thirty minutes a competent tutor will ask for the syllabus code, look at a marked script, and name a loss pattern with the marks it costs. One who talks about motivation and potential for thirty minutes has shown you something too. That test costs nothing and discriminates better than any price signal in this market.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask five Dubai providers for a quote
paragraphs: Most quotes in this market are vague because the brief was vague. A provider given a subject and a year group has to price the uncertainty, and prices it upwards. A provider given a precise brief can price precisely, and the quotes you receive become comparable with each other for the first time.

Send seven things in one message: the exam board and the four-digit or alphanumeric syllabus code from the entry statement; the tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher; the exam series you are working towards; the current mark or grade and the target; a recent marked paper if you have one; the session length you want and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time; and the format, which for Dubai families means online one-to-one. That single message removes most of the ambiguity that inflates a quote.

Then ask five questions and compare the answers rather than the rates. What is inside the hourly figure and what is billed on top. What is the cancellation window and how many reschedules a term. Is the figure inclusive or exclusive of VAT. What happens if the match is wrong — specifically, is there a replacement arrangement and what happens to anything prepaid. And who exactly will teach the session, by name and subject background, because an agency quoting a rate and matching later is quoting a rate for an unknown tutor.

One last filter that costs nothing. Ask whether the provider holds any regulatory approval and listen carefully to the answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years; a business with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. Those are specific, checkable things. A provider implying a regulator endorses its teaching has either a permit number to show you or a problem. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none.
bullets: Send the board, the code, the tier and the series in the first message
Send the current mark, the target and a marked paper if one exists
Ask what is billed on top, and get the VAT position in writing
Ask who will teach, by name and subject background, before agreeing a rate
Ask about the replacement arrangement before you need it, not after

sections.heading: When the match is wrong, and what should happen to the money
paragraphs: Roughly one arrangement in six does not work, in any market and at any price. The student does not engage, the tutor's pace is wrong, the subject turns out to be a different problem from the one described. This is normal and it is the situation most tuition contracts handle worst, because the commercial incentive runs towards keeping the slot rather than fixing the match.

What a reasonable arrangement looks like: the problem is raised after two sessions rather than endured for a term, a different tutor is offered without a new registration fee, nothing prepaid is lost, and the written diagnostic travels with the student so the new tutor does not restart from zero. What an unreasonable arrangement looks like: a package expiring on a date, no replacement without a fresh fee, and prepaid sessions locked to a tutor you have decided against.

This page does not offer a refund tied to a grade outcome, and you should be sceptical of any page that does. Published grade promises either come with refund terms nobody honours or with conditions that make them unreachable, and either way the provider is selling certainty it does not have. No tutor can promise a grade; what can be promised is a named target, written feedback, and an honest statement when the arrangement has stopped producing anything.

Our own practice, stated so you can hold us to it: the trial is free and takes no card details; nothing is prepaid unless you choose a block; a block has an end condition rather than an expiry date; if a match is wrong we change the tutor and the written diagnostic goes with the student; and at every half-term review we say whether to continue, reduce or stop. Saying stop is part of the service, not a loss of business, and the alternative is billing a Dubai family through June for a problem that closed in February.

sections.heading: The Dubai tuition year: when demand and prices move
paragraphs: Tuition pricing in Dubai is seasonal, and knowing the shape of the year is worth real money. Demand has three peaks and two troughs, and both the rate you are quoted and the availability of a scarce specialist move with them. Buying in a trough and holding the slot is a legitimate strategy that almost nobody uses.

The first peak follows the first set of school assessments in the autumn term, when reports arrive and families act. The second and largest follows January mocks, which is when Extended Mathematics and physics specialists disappear and premiums appear. The third is the short, intense window immediately before a May or June series, which is largely triage buying at the worst prices. The troughs are the long summer and the weeks either side of the December break, when availability is widest.

Ramadan sits across this pattern and changes the shape of the week rather than the price. School hours shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a fixed late-afternoon slot that worked in February often stops working. Families either move to a post-Iftar slot, shift to late-morning weekend sessions, or pause for the month and use the spring break as a block. A provider that cannot accommodate the move will quietly cost you four weeks of continuity, which is a real cost even if no invoice shows it.

The table maps the year as a buying calendar. Use it the way a Dubai family actually can: book scarce specialisms in the trough before you need them, avoid committing to a long package at a peak rate, and plan Ramadan and the long summer explicitly in the contract rather than discovering how they are billed.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor in Dubai, and what that costs them
paragraphs: Permit status belongs in a pricing conversation because it is part of what a parent is buying, and because the market contains a persistent myth that the permit is expensive and therefore baked into high rates. It is not. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. Any rate justified to you by permit costs is justified by something that does not exist.

Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists the process as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the one to point an independent tutor towards rather than around.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — the ministry did not specify amounts — so treat any figure circulating online with scepticism rather than repeating it. A separate and much heavier regime applies to a business with premises and staff, which requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

Two Dubai-specific consequences for a buyer. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school; that is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it before relying on the exact wording, but no reputable arrangement markets your child's own teacher privately. And no provider in this market, including IB Gram, should be describing itself as regulator-endorsed. We hold no permit, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and nothing on this site should be read as claiming one.
