faqs.question: What is the real hourly cost of IGCSE private tuition in Dubai once extras are added?
faqs.answer: Take the quoted rate and add 10 to 35 per cent for most arrangements. The published bands read in October 2026 run AED 33 to 65 for budget online platforms, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 350 for a visiting tutor including travel, and up to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. On top sit registration or diagnostic fees, material charges, travel inside the hour, community surcharges, cancellation windows that convert absences into paid sessions, peak-season premiums, weekend rates, report fees and the VAT position. Ask for all of them in the same written message as the rate.

faqs.question: Is a twenty-session package genuinely cheaper than paying by the hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per session, yes, usually by 10 to 20 per cent. In total, only if you use it. A package transfers risk to you in three readable places: whether unused sessions remain yours if you stop, whether it expires on a date or on completion, and whether sessions transfer between siblings or subjects. A discounted package expiring in ninety days, bought in October for a need that closes in January, costs more than paying hourly. Start by the session for three or four weeks, then convert to a block with an end condition rather than an expiry date if the need is genuinely sustained.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai tuition quote include VAT, and how do I get that confirmed?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for the answer in writing in the same message as the rate. This page will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we have none to offer; what matters practically is whether the specific figure quoted to you is inclusive or exclusive, which only the provider can tell you. A difference of up to five per cent on a year of weekly sessions is real money. A provider unwilling to put the VAT position in writing alongside the rate has told you something useful about how the rest of the billing will work.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are dearest to tutor in Dubai, and is that about difficulty?
faqs.answer: It is about supply, not difficulty. Arabic as a first language, Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, Extended and Higher-tier Mathematics, and physics at the top grades all sit at the ceiling of the Dubai band because the pool of people who teach them well is thin. Biology sits lower with the widest supply of the three sciences, which reflects availability rather than weaker tutors. Business Studies, Economics and ICT sit lower still. If your need is one of the scarce subjects, the premium is the market clearing and there is no clever way around it.

faqs.question: Do Dubai tutoring rates rise in the weeks before a May or June series?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically by 10 to 25 per cent, and the scarce specialists disappear entirely. The pattern is predictable: demand rises after autumn assessments, peaks sharply after January mocks, and spikes again in the short window before the papers. Availability is widest in the long summer and the weeks either side of the December break, when rates are at their lowest and tutor choice at its widest. A Dubai family that books a scarce specialism in a trough and holds the slot through the peak pays less and gets a better tutor, which is a straightforward strategy almost nobody uses.

faqs.question: What should I include when I ask several Dubai providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: Seven items in one message: exam board; syllabus code from the entry statement; tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher; the exam series you are working towards; the current mark and the target; a recent marked paper if you have one; and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time with the session length you want. A provider given a subject and a year group has to price the uncertainty and prices it upwards. A precise brief produces precise quotes, which is the only way five quotes become comparable with one another rather than five different products.

faqs.question: What happens to my money if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the contract you signed, which is why it is worth asking before you need the answer. A reasonable arrangement replaces the tutor without a new registration fee, loses nothing prepaid, and passes the written diagnostic to the new tutor so nothing restarts from zero. An unreasonable one locks prepaid sessions to a tutor you have decided against and charges a fresh fee for a replacement. Raise a mismatch after two sessions rather than enduring a term — roughly one arrangement in six does not work, in every market and at every price point, and it is not a failure.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE in Dubai as a private candidate, and what does entry cost?
faqs.answer: A small number of licensed centres in Dubai accept private candidates, which is the route for a retake or for a subject the school does not offer. Entry fees are set by the centre and the board, not by any tutor, and each centre publishes its own schedule and deadlines. No figure appears on this page because none has been verified from a centre's current schedule, so ask the centre directly and in writing. Confirm the entry deadline in the same message: Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries at 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper.

faqs.question: Is a Dubai tuition centre group class better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: At AED 70 to 150 a student against AED 150 to 300 for one-to-one online, the arithmetic looks obvious and the condition attached is not. A group only works when the students are genuinely at the same point, because the pace is set by the group rather than by your child. In dense apartment communities with large year groups that condition is often met; in low-density villa communities it usually is not. Factor in the second commute on top of the school run, any registration fee and term minimum, and whether written feedback on your child's own work is included at all.

faqs.question: Why is an independent Dubai tutor sometimes more expensive than an agency?
faqs.answer: Because the independent is pricing one person's scarce time while an agency is pricing a pool. An independent with a full timetable in a scarce subject has no reason to discount, and listings in this market run from AED 200 to AED 500 an hour. What the higher independent rate does not usually include is a replacement arrangement if the match fails, written progress reporting, or anyone to escalate to. That is the real trade: a direct relationship at a direct price, with the permit check, the syllabus-code check and the recovery plan all sitting with you.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget for a full IGCSE year across two subjects?
faqs.answer: At the market mid-band of about AED 220 an hour, two subjects weekly across a thirty-four-week year is roughly AED 15,000 before extras. The same money spent differently buys considerably more: a marked diagnostic, a ten-session block against the named loss patterns, a stop, and an eight-session block before the series comes to roughly AED 4,400. That is the pattern with the best return we see, because the hours sit where the marks are. The worst return is the open weekly slot with no written target, which is the easiest arrangement to sell and the hardest to end.

faqs.question: Are the monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 good value?
faqs.answer: Published monthly packages in this market include AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Per hour of teaching those are roughly AED 200 to 225 and AED 100 respectively, so the comparison depends on what the hour contains. Travel is inside the visiting figure whether itemised or not, and a sixty-minute visit that starts late delivers less than sixty minutes of teaching — ask whether the hour starts on arrival or at the agreed time. For scarce subjects the deciding factor is usually not price but which specialists will travel to your community at that hour.

faqs.question: Does paying a higher hourly rate actually move an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Published Dubai rates for the same described service span fourteenfold, and nobody believes the top tutor is fourteen times as effective. Price tracks scarcity, demand and overhead. Three things do track grade movement: whether the tutor works from the correct syllabus code and the board's own mark scheme, whether a marked script came before the teaching so the hours are aimed, and whether the student completes the work between sessions. Test the first two in the free trial by watching whether the tutor asks for the code and names a loss pattern from the script.

faqs.question: Can we pause during Ramadan and the summer without losing paid sessions?
faqs.answer: That depends on the contract, and it is worth settling before either arrives. Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than the price: school hours shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a fixed late-afternoon slot often stops working. Families move to a post-Iftar slot, switch to late-morning weekend sessions, or pause and use the spring break as a block. Our own practice is that holiday and Ramadan weeks are agreed in advance rather than invoiced by default, and a fixed block carries an end condition rather than an expiry date, so pausing does not consume prepaid value.

faqs.question: Should a diagnostic assessment be free, or is paying for one reasonable?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in Dubai and some providers charge AED 100 to 300 for an initial assessment. Paying is not unreasonable where the output is substantial — a marked script against the board's published scheme, the loss patterns named with the marks each costs, and a written tier recommendation you can take to the school. Paying for a twenty-minute conversation that produces a sales quote is unreasonable. Ask what document you receive and whether it is yours to keep regardless of whether you book. Our own written diagnostic and the thirty-minute trial lesson are free, one trial per family, with no card details taken.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.closingHeading: Send the brief, collect five comparable quotes
dubai/igcse-private-tuition.closingBody: Write one message containing the exam board, the syllabus code, the tier, the series, the current mark, the target and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time, and send it to us and to anyone else you are considering. You will get back a written diagnostic if you include a marked paper, a free 30-minute trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the subject, and a quote naming that tutor, the session length and everything billed on top including the VAT position. One trial per family, no card details. Dubai lessons run one-to-one over live video, and if the honest answer is a short block rather than a year, that is what the quote will say.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below works to one named syllabus and marks against the published scheme rather than from memory. Where a subject is tiered, the tutor states on day one which tier the papers they are preparing for belong to, because Core and Extended reward different answers to the same question.

intro.heading: The question to ask a tutor is not how experienced they are, it is what they can show you
paragraphs: Most tutoring conversations in Dubai start in the wrong place. A parent asks about qualifications and years of experience, gets reassuring answers, books a block of ten hours, and then has no way to tell in week six whether the money is working. Experience is a weak predictor. What a tutor produces each week is a strong one, and it can be inspected by a parent with no subject knowledge at all.

This page is built on that idea. An IGCSE private tutor working properly generates artefacts: a marked script with annotations tied to the mark scheme, a named error with a count attached, a timed paper with the time stamps written on it, a draft with comments that ask questions rather than supply answers. Those things either exist after three sessions or they do not. If they do not, no amount of rapport explains the gap.

The reason this matters more at IGCSE than at almost any other stage is that IGCSE marks are unusually legible. Every paper is marked against a published scheme. Every command word has an agreed meaning. "State" takes one line, "describe" takes the what, "explain" takes the why, and "suggest" takes a reasoned answer to a situation the examiner has not seen before. A specialist reading your child's script can sort fourteen lost marks into categories in minutes and tell you which three are cheapest to recover. A generalist tells you the child needs to revise more.

There is a second reason evidence beats reputation in this particular market. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school pupils as of 2024-25, with 37% of that enrolment on a UK curriculum, so the IGCSE cohort here is large and the tutoring supply that serves it is uneven. Plenty of people in this city will teach maths competently. Far fewer can read a marked Paper 4 and tell you that nine of the fourteen lost marks were technique and process, which recover in weeks, while only three sat in content, which takes months. The two tutors look identical on a profile page and produce completely different terms.

IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a Dubai address; home visits are something we offer only in India. For evidence-led work the online format is actively better, not a compromise: the script sits on a shared screen, annotated live, with both the answer and the mark scheme visible at once. That is nearer to how an examiner reads a paper than two people leaning over one piece of A4.

Below is the machinery. How a marked script gets read, which command words cost Dubai cohorts the most marks, what a twelve-week ledger looks like, what a predicted grade actually rests on, where the line sits on coursework feedback, what the market charges in dirhams and which published source says so, and what the evidence looks like when the right decision is to change tutor or stop. Nothing on this page promises a grade, because no tutor controls one.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage. In Key Stage 3 it is fluency data; across IGCSE it is marks against a scheme; after Year 11 it is whether the grade cleared a published threshold. A tutor should be able to say which of the three they are producing.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the entries are set
programmes.description: The evidence that matters here is fluency, measured rather than described. Timed arithmetic and algebra checks, a reading-comprehension score, and a written piece marked for structure. These produce a baseline that the Year 9 set placement can be argued against later, which is the only stage at which a tier decision can be influenced cheaply.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools take pupils in mid-Key Stage from CBSE, American and other systems most years. A child arriving from CBSE Year 8 has usually met more algebra and fewer extended written answers. Three timed baseline tasks in the first fortnight tell you which of those two gaps you are dealing with, instead of a term of impressions.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11, the two examined years
programmes.description: Evidence becomes marks. Each paper is marked against the board's published scheme, so a lost mark has a documented reason. A tutor's weekly output across these two years should be a marked question, a running error count, and periodically a full paper sat to time. Mock results are useful only when the raw mark is recorded alongside the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a two-board city, with Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel entries sitting in the same friendship group. Evidence is board-specific: a mark scheme for Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 does not describe Pearson 4MA1 Paper 2. Any tutor producing evidence against the wrong scheme is producing a convincing-looking document that means nothing.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry after Year 11
programmes.description: The evidence here is the published threshold. Dubai sixth forms set subject-level entry criteria, commonly a 6 or B in the same subject for A Level and a spread of strong grades plus writing stamina for the IB Diploma. Tuition in Year 11 should be aimed at a stated number rather than at general improvement, because the number is what the admissions spreadsheet reads.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Families planning a UAE university route should check the five counted subjects before Year 11 entries are locked.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, what evidence of progress actually looks like. A tutor who cannot name the artefact they produce in a subject is unlikely to be producing one.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The artefact is a marked Paper 4 with method marks circled separately from answer marks. The useful count is process errors: rounding mid-calculation, missing units, sign slips. Three papers with a tally produce a number that a fifteen-year-old will argue with far less than they argue with advice.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Evidence here is a circuit question marked twice, before and after a fortnight of potential-divider work. Electricity and magnetism are where the marks sit and where the recall decays, so a cold retest two weeks later is the only honest check that teaching landed.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis half-equations are countable. The artefact is a sheet of ten equations with balanced charges checked, dated, and repeated cold. Progress is the drop in unbalanced equations, not the student's reported confidence.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Almost all recoverable marks are vocabulary precision. Evidence is the student's own sentence rewritten next to the mark-scheme wording, kept and compared a month later. Water potential, enzyme graph description and genetics notation are the three reliable sources of lost marks.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, 0510 second language)
subjects.description: The summary task and directed writing are both marked against clear criteria, which makes them the most auditable components on the timetable. Evidence is a summary scored twice: once as written, once after the lifting of phrasing has been removed.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 / 0992)
subjects.description: Evidence is an essay plan next to the band descriptors, with the quotations counted. Candidates who write everything they know about a character can see the problem immediately when the plan is scored against the question actually set.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study evaluation marks are the ones routinely left unclaimed. The artefact is an answer with the stimulus quotations highlighted and the justified recommendation marked separately, so the student sees which half of the answer earned the band.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the explicit link from diagram to argument. Evidence is a marked diagram with axis labels and shifts checked, then the same diagram reproduced from blank a week later, which is where the real retention gap shows.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Trace tables are self-marking, which makes them ideal evidence. A student who completes a trace table correctly has demonstrably understood the algorithm. Hexadecimal and two's complement conversions are mechanical and should reach near-perfect accuracy under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 in stronger Dubai sets. Evidence is notation discipline: calculus written correctly, not just answered correctly. The common failure is treating 0606 as harder 0580, and a marked script makes that visible in one session.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai should be able to show you after three sessions
paragraphs: After three sessions with an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai you should hold four things. A marked piece of your child's work with annotations that reference the mark scheme. A named error, stated specifically enough to count. A number: how often that error occurred across the work seen so far. And a sentence about what happens next, in which the error is the subject rather than the child's attitude.

If those four things exist, the tuition is auditable. You do not need to understand chemistry to look at a sheet that says "unbalanced ionic equations: 7 of 10 in week one, 4 of 10 in week three" and know what is going on. If they do not exist, you are buying company. Pleasant company, often, and sometimes useful for confidence, but not something that can be shown to have moved marks.

The reason tutors avoid this is that it creates accountability in both directions. A tracked count that does not fall after four weeks is an argument the tutor has to answer. Most will prefer to report that your child is improving in confidence, which may even be true, and which cannot be checked. Our position is that the count gets shown to the parent whether it moved or not, and a flat count triggers a change in approach rather than a reassurance.

A note on what three sessions is not enough for. It is not enough to move a grade, and anyone presenting it that way is overselling. Genuine content gaps need six to ten sessions per significant topic. Three sessions is enough to produce a diagnosis you can trust and to see whether your child actually talks to this tutor, which are the two things that should be settled before you commit money to a block.
bullets: A marked script with scheme-referenced annotations, not a grade and a sentence
One error named precisely enough to be counted
The count itself, across all work seen so far

sections.heading: Reading a marked script: command words and the marks hiding behind them
paragraphs: The single most common reason a Dubai IGCSE candidate who knows the material scores below their understanding is that they answer a different question from the one the command word asked. This is not a vague risk. It is countable, it is visible on any marked script, and it is the cheapest category of mark to recover because no new content has to be learned.

Command words are specified. "State" or "give" wants a short factual answer with no reasoning; writing a paragraph wastes time without adding marks. "Describe" wants what happens, in order. "Explain" wants why, and a description scores nothing against an explain mark scheme no matter how accurate it is. "Suggest" signals an unfamiliar context and is marked on reasoning rather than recall, which is why candidates who leave it blank are leaving the most forgiving marks on the paper. "Calculate" wants working, because the method marks are awarded before the answer is reached.

The session technique is simple and it works on fifteen-year-olds. Put the student's own answer on one side of the screen and the published mark scheme on the other. Ask them to award themselves the marks. Nearly every student is stricter than the examiner on content and far more generous than the examiner on form. Watching themselves fail to award a mark they thought they had earned does more in ten minutes than a term of being told to read the question carefully.

This is also where board differences bite. A Cambridge mark scheme and a Pearson mark scheme for the same topic credit different wording, and the number of marks per question differs. A tutor marking Pearson work against a Cambridge scheme produces a document that looks like evidence and is not. Establishing the board before the first marking exercise is not administrative tidiness; it determines whether the evidence means anything.

sections.heading: The first session, and how a mock paper gets taken apart
paragraphs: A first session that teaches content is a wasted session. Nobody yet knows which content to teach. The first hour reads evidence, and the most useful evidence is the most recent mock with the marks on it. If the script is not available, we set a past paper and mark it ourselves before any teaching happens, because a plan built on a report card grade is a plan built on a summary of a summary.

The reading happens in a fixed order. First, total marks lost and where on the paper they sit, because a cluster at the end is a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem. Second, each lost mark gets a category: technique, process, timing or content. Third, the categories get a mark total. Fourth, the totals get ranked. The resulting list is the plan, in order, and it frequently surprises the family because the topic they were worried about is rarely the one costing the most marks.

A worked example from a typical 0580 Extended Paper 4 script. Fourteen marks lost: five to rounding and unit errors spread across the paper, four to two blank questions in the final section, three to a genuinely unlearned topic, and two to method marks forfeited by writing only answers. The family had asked for help with the unlearned topic, which is worth three marks. Process and timing together are worth nine, and both respond faster. Starting with the unlearned topic would have felt responsive and returned the least.

The output of the first session is written, goes to the parent, and is short: the ranked category list with mark totals, the single error we will track first, a target count, and the fortnight by which we expect it to move. Everything after that is execution against a document you can check. If a tutor cannot produce that document after reading a script, the diagnosis did not happen.
bullets: Marked script read before any content is taught
Every lost mark assigned to technique, process, timing or content
Categories ranked by marks available, not by parental concern
A written one-page diagnosis with a target count and a review date

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, measured: the ledger a Dubai parent can audit
paragraphs: A term of tuition should leave a document behind. Not a folder of worksheets, a ledger: what was marked each week, what the tracked count was, and what changed. The point of writing it down is that memory is kind to tuition. Everyone remembers the session where something clicked. Nobody remembers the four weeks where a count sat still.

The shape below is what a maths or science term typically looks like. Weeks one to two diagnose and set the baseline. Weeks three to six attack the highest-value error category, usually process or technique, because those return marks fastest. Weeks seven to nine move to content gaps, which are slower. Weeks ten to twelve run full timed papers, which test whether the earlier gains survive under pressure. They often do not at first, which is exactly why that block exists.

What a parent does with the ledger is ask one question every fortnight: did the number move. If it did, continue. If it did not, the conversation is about why, and the honest answers are a narrow set. The error was misdiagnosed. The independent work between sessions is not happening. The tutor's explanation is not landing with this particular child. Or the gap is genuinely content-shaped and needs more weeks than estimated. Each of those has a different response, and none of them is "keep going and hope".

The ledger also solves a problem families do not anticipate: tutor changes. Tutors move cities, change jobs, and occasionally turn out to be the wrong fit in week five. When the record exists, the next tutor starts from the diagnosis rather than redoing it, which saves two to three sessions. We keep the record with the family's file and hand it over on request, and we delete marked work when asked.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, mocks and raw marks: what the school's number rests on
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a professional judgement, not a measurement, and it is produced under constraints parents rarely see. Dubai schools generate them from internal assessment data, set placement and teacher judgement, usually in a short window and for a whole cohort at once. They are frequently accurate. When they are not, the family needs to know what evidence sits underneath before challenging anything.

The question that cuts through is about raw marks. A mock grade is a raw mark converted using some set of grade boundaries, and boundaries are set per series, per paper, after the exam. A mock marked against last year's boundaries produces an indicative grade, not a prediction. So the useful request to a head of department is not "can the prediction change", it is "what raw mark did my child score, out of what total, and which series boundaries were applied". That is a factual question with a factual answer.

Raw marks also make progress legible in a way grades do not. A child who moves from 94 to 112 out of 130 has gained eighteen marks and may still be sitting in the same grade band, which looks like no progress on a report card and is in fact substantial. The reverse happens too: a one-mark move can cross a boundary and flatter a term of work that achieved very little. Tracking marks protects a family from both illusions.

For forecast grades there is a hard date in the calendar. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, with final entries having closed on 27 November 2026 and the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. The implication is that the conversation about a prediction belongs in the autumn term, not in the spring. By the time the forecast is submitted, the evidence that would have changed it needed to already exist.

sections.heading: Coursework and assignment drafts: what feedback may do, and where it stops
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry a component the student produces outside an exam hall. Wherever that exists, there is a line, and the line is not negotiable. A tutor may teach the skills the component needs, explain the assessment criteria in plain language, discuss the student's chosen approach, question their reasoning, and respond to a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not produce assessed material, rewrite a draft into a submittable state, or supply sentences for a student to hand in.

The practical test we use is whether the feedback could be read aloud to the student's teacher without anybody being uncomfortable. "Your second paragraph asserts a conclusion your data does not support; which figure would you need to show to support it?" passes. Handing over a corrected paragraph does not. The first builds the skill the criteria are actually assessing. The second transfers the mark to the tutor and exposes the student to a malpractice finding they, not the tutor, will carry.

This market has a specific problem that makes the boundary worth stating loudly. One site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. Families encountering that offer sometimes assume it is normal and that everyone does a version of it quietly. They should not. It is an academic-integrity breach, it is the kind of thing boards investigate, and the student is the one who faces the consequence.

Our process makes the boundary auditable rather than merely asserted. Feedback is logged, so the trail of advice can be read in order. Sessions on a coursework component are scheduled against the school's internal deadlines so the work is produced over time rather than assembled at the end. And the boundary is written down and sent to the parent before the first draft session, because the moment to agree it is before anyone is under deadline pressure.

sections.heading: What a private tutor costs in Dubai, and what the extra dirhams actually buy
paragraphs: The Dubai market publishes rates unevenly, so here are the bands with their sources, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 inclusive of travel, per Bestimate at 180-350 and independent home tutors at 200-500.

Above that, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-badged tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, 600-1,200 mid-range and 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

What the extra dirhams buy, in evidence terms, is mark-scheme literacy. A tutor at the bottom of the range usually knows the subject and not the scheme, which means they can explain content and cannot tell you that nine of fourteen lost marks were technique. That is a real distinction and it is most of the price gap. The upper bands exist because syllabus-specific marking experience is scarce, and scarcity in a small market prices accordingly.

A note on the in-home premium. The AED 180-500 band for visits is partly a travel bill, and travel is the one component of a tutoring fee that produces no teaching. IB Gram prices against the online bands rather than the in-home bands because nobody is driving anywhere. We do not publish a rate card on this page: the figure depends on subject scarcity, tier and session length, and the consultation after the free first lesson is where you get it. Any page quoting you a specific dirham figure as our price is not ours.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands, and what a school report tells you about tuition
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The report is public, it is detailed, and most families read only the headline band. The useful part sits further in, in the subject-level and phase-level judgements, because a school can be Very Good overall and have an inconsistent department in exactly the subject your child is struggling with.

That is the connection to tuition, and it is a practical one. If the inspection report flags attainment in a subject as acceptable while the rest of the school sits higher, a child in that subject is being taught in a department under scrutiny. Tuition in that subject is more likely to be worth the money than tuition in a subject where the department is strong and the child's problem is attitude or organisation.

The band also tells you something about how to read the school's own predicted grades. A department with inconsistent internal assessment produces predictions with wider error bars, which makes raw marks and external past-paper evidence more valuable. A strong department's prediction is usually well calibrated, and a parent who disputes it with a tutor's opinion rather than with marks will get nowhere, correctly.

One thing an inspection band is not is a statement about any individual child or any tutor. We name KHDA here because it is the regulator and because its reports are a free, public, well-evidenced source that families underuse. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, endorsed or licensed by KHDA, holds no permit from it, and operates no premises in the UAE. An operation with premises here would require a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific thing issued to training institutes, and we do not hold one or claim to.

sections.heading: When the evidence says change the tutor, change the plan, or stop
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement has to be willing to produce an unwelcome answer, or it is not evidence-led. The count either moved or it did not, and when it has not moved after four to six weeks of consistent work there are only a few honest explanations. Confronting them is cheaper in week six than in month five.

The first is misdiagnosis. The error being tracked was not the one costing the marks, which happens most often when a family's stated concern overrode the ranked list. The fix is re-reading the script and re-ranking, and it costs one session. The second is independent work not happening between sessions, which no amount of tutoring hours compensates for; a child who does nothing for six days and sits a lesson on the seventh will plateau. That is a scheduling and expectation conversation, not a teaching one.

The third is personal fit, and it is more common than the industry admits. A tutor can be technically excellent and simply not land with a particular fifteen-year-old. The signal is a student who answers in monosyllables, does not bring questions, and performs better on independent work than in sessions. When we see that, we propose a different tutor and the ledger transfers, so nothing is restarted from zero.

The fourth answer is the one nobody advertises: sometimes the right decision is to stop. A child carrying nine subjects, a coursework backlog and three tuition slots a week is not short of teaching. Dropping a session and sleeping is occasionally the intervention with the highest return. We would rather say that and keep a family's trust than sell hours into a timetable that is already full. If a subject's marks are genuinely secure, the honest recommendation is to spend the money elsewhere or not at all.

process.title: Send the marked script, not the report
process.description: The most recent paper with the marks and annotations on it is worth more than a term of grades. If none exists, the first task is a set past paper, marked by us against the published scheme, before any teaching is planned. A diagnosis built on a report card is a summary of a summary.

process.title: Confirm board, code, tier and scale from school documents
process.description: Cambridge or Pearson, which syllabus code, Core or Extended, A*-G or 9-1. Dubai runs both boards inside the same neighbourhood, and evidence marked against the wrong scheme looks convincing and means nothing. We take these four facts from the school's own paperwork.

process.title: Free first lesson, then a written diagnosis
process.description: A full session with the proposed tutor at no cost, with no card details needed to book. Afterwards you receive the ranked category list with mark totals, the first error to be tracked, a target count and the review date. That page is the contract the rest of the term is measured against.

process.title: Weekly marked work, fortnightly count review
process.description: Every session returns a marked question and updates the count. Every two weeks the count is compared with the previous fortnight and sent to you whether it improved or not. A flat count is information, and it changes the plan rather than producing a reassuring email.

process.title: Decide at the review point
process.description: At week six and week twelve there is a decision, taken from the ledger: continue, change approach, change tutor, or stop. We put the recommendation in writing with the numbers that support it, including when the recommendation is that further sessions in this subject are not the best use of your money.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published scheme, every week
whyPoints.description: Work is marked to the board's own scheme rather than from a tutor's memory of what good looks like. That is what makes a lost mark explainable, and it is the capability that separates a subject-knowledgeable tutor from one who can tell you which fourteen marks went where.

whyPoints.title: One error, counted, until it stops
whyPoints.description: Fortnightly counts rather than termly impressions. A student who sees their own rounding-error tally fall from seven to two argues with it far less than with advice, and a parent who sees a flat tally has grounds to ask for a change of approach without any subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: The specialist you need, not the one within driving distance
whyPoints.description: Live video means a family in Mirdif and a family in Dubai Hills choose from the same specialists. Additional Mathematics 0606 and top-band Computer Science 0478 are scarce in any single catchment and reachable from all of them, which is the practical advantage of not sending anyone anywhere.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on coursework we put in writing first
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, questions and feedback on the student's own draft. Not replacement text, not a rewrite to submission standard. One competitor in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; the student carries that risk, not the seller, which is why we set the line before the deadline pressure starts.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, no figures about ourselves
whyPoints.description: Market rates carry the provider and the date. Regulator rules carry the authority. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no average grade gain and no star rating, because we cannot show you the underlying data for any of them and a number without its method is worth nothing.

whyPoints.title: Records that transfer and delete on request
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis is the expensive part of tuition and it should not be redone when a tutor changes. The ledger stays with your file and moves to the next tutor on request. Marked work is kept only while it is useful to the plan and deleted when you ask.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai hand over after the first three sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things. A marked piece of your child's work with annotations tied to the published mark scheme. One error named precisely enough to count, such as unbalanced ionic equations or rounding mid-calculation. The count of that error across the work seen so far. And a next step whose subject is the error rather than the child's effort. Those four exist after three sessions or they do not. Three sessions is not long enough to move a grade, and anyone implying otherwise is overselling, but it is long enough to produce a diagnosis you can check.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but the marks do not show it. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually command words. IGCSE schemes credit specific forms of answer, and a correct description scores nothing against an explain mark. "State" wants one line, "explain" wants a causal link, "suggest" wants reasoning about an unfamiliar context, and "calculate" wants working because method marks come before the answer. The fastest diagnostic is to put your child's answer beside the mark scheme and ask them to award their own marks. Most students are stricter than the examiner on content and far more generous on form, and seeing that happen is more persuasive than being told.

faqs.question: How do I check a mock grade rather than just accepting it?
faqs.answer: Ask for the raw mark and the boundaries. A mock grade is a raw mark converted using some set of grade boundaries, and boundaries are set per series after the exam, so a mock marked against last year's boundaries gives an indicative grade rather than a prediction. The precise request is: what mark did my child score, out of what total, on which paper, and which series boundaries were applied. Raw marks also show progress a grade band can hide, since eighteen extra marks can look like no movement on a report card.

faqs.question: Can tuition change a predicted grade, and when is it too late to try?
faqs.answer: Tuition cannot change a prediction; evidence can, and the timing is tight. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, with final entries closed on 27 November 2026. For any series, the evidence that would revise a judgement has to exist before the school submits. That makes autumn the right term for this conversation. The evidence that works is marked work at the target standard under timed conditions, handed to the department, not a letter explaining that your child is trying hard.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with my child's coursework draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the skills, explain the criteria in plain words, discuss the approach, question the reasoning, and respond to what the student has written. Not produce assessed material, not rewrite a draft to submission standard, and not supply sentences to be handed in. Our working test is whether the feedback could be read aloud to the class teacher without discomfort. "Your conclusion asserts more than your data supports; which figure would you need?" passes that test. A corrected paragraph does not, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Is it normal for tutoring sites in Dubai to offer finished assessments?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it is not normal practice; it is an integrity breach. At least one site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Boards investigate this, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller. If any provider offers to supply work for submission, that is the point to stop the conversation. We put the boundary in writing before the first draft session and log every comment, so the sequence of advice given can be read in order by anyone who asks.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for an evidence-led IGCSE tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands as of October 2026 put budget online tutoring at AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The practical difference along that scale is mark-scheme literacy rather than subject knowledge. Those are the providers' own figures, not ours; our rate depends on subject scarcity and tier and comes after the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Why do in-home rates in Dubai sit so much higher than online ones?
faqs.answer: Travel is inside the fee. Published in-home bands run AED 180-500 an hour, per Bestimate at 180-350 and independent tutors at 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online. The difference is largely a car on Al Khail Road, which produces no teaching. It also shrinks the pool to whoever will make the drive at 5pm, which is how a family needing Cambridge 0620 Extended ends up with a general science graduate. We price against the online bands because nobody is driving anywhere.

faqs.question: How does a KHDA inspection report help me decide about tuition?
faqs.answer: Read past the headline band to the subject and phase judgements. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school can sit at Very Good overall while one department is flagged as inconsistent. If that department teaches the subject your child is struggling in, tuition there is more likely to pay than in a subject where the department is strong and the real problem is organisation. The reports are public and free, and most families use only the first page.

faqs.question: What do I do if the tracked count has not moved in six weeks?
faqs.answer: Treat it as information and ask for a review. There are four honest explanations and each has a different fix. The error was misdiagnosed, which costs one session to re-rank. Independent work is not happening between sessions, which is a scheduling conversation rather than a teaching one. The tutor is not landing with this particular child, in which case we propose someone else and the ledger transfers. Or the gap is content-shaped and needs more weeks than estimated. The wrong response is another month of the same with encouragement.

faqs.question: Will we have to start from scratch if we change tutor?
faqs.answer: No, provided the record exists. The diagnosis is the expensive part of tuition, typically two or three sessions of reading scripts and ranking error categories. We keep the ledger with your family's file, so a new tutor opens with the ranked list, the tracked error and the count history rather than rebuilding it. That usually saves two to three sessions. Marked work is held only while it is useful to the plan, and we delete it when you ask, including the scripts and the session notes.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor actually see enough to mark my child's work properly?
faqs.answer: More than in a shared-desk arrangement, in practice. The script sits on screen with the mark scheme next to it, annotated live, so both the answer and the criteria are visible to tutor and student at once. Written work is photographed or shared before the session and marked beforehand, which means session time goes on the conversation rather than on reading. The part online cannot do is handle apparatus, which belongs to the school; we plan around the school's practical schedule rather than pretending to replace it.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and nothing is wrong yet. Is tuition premature?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest point to act, for a specific reason: tier entries are not locked. In tiered Cambridge subjects a Core entry caps the achievable grade, and the decision usually follows set placement rather than an explicit conversation. Evidence produced in Year 10, meaning Extended-standard work under timed conditions, is the argument that moves a department before final entries close. Waiting until a Year 11 mock looks wrong means arguing after the window. A diagnostic in Year 10 is also genuinely allowed to conclude that nothing needs doing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. Maths and physics overlap enough that one specialist often covers both well, and the shared algebra and graph-work diagnosis saves time. Chemistry and biology are less interchangeable than families expect, because the recoverable marks sit in different places: calculation discipline in one, vocabulary precision in the other. We would rather put two specialists on two subjects than stretch one tutor into a subject where they can explain the content but not the mark scheme.

faqs.question: What does the free first IGCSE lesson include, and what is the catch?
faqs.answer: A full-length session with the proposed tutor, working on real questions from your child's own board and tier, followed by a written diagnosis if a marked script was supplied. No card details are needed to book it and there is no obligation afterwards. The condition is simply that it is one lesson per family, with the tutor we propose. The purpose is to test two things money should not be spent discovering later: whether your child talks to this adult, and whether the tutor can read a script.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Send a marked paper and see what comes back
dubai/igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to judge any tutor, including ours, is to hand over a marked script and read what they produce from it. Send the last paper your child sat with the marks on it, tell us the board, syllabus code and tier, and take the free first lesson with the specialist we propose. Afterwards you get one page: the ranked list of where the marks went, which category each loss falls into, the first error we would track, and the fortnight by which we expect its count to fall. If that page does not convince you, nothing has been spent. If the tutor is not right for your child, say so and we propose someone else.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE science at Core and Extended tier across Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Combined Science and Coordinated Sciences. Each one works one-to-one over live video with Dubai families, holds the subject at degree level, and teaches the specific paper your child is entered for rather than a generic syllabus summary.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Dubai actually costs, and why two quotes for the same child differ by 300 per cent
paragraphs: Ask five providers in Dubai what IGCSE science tuition costs and you will be quoted anything from AED 45 an hour to AED 650 an hour. Both ends are real. EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 for budget online lessons and Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 for its lowest tier, while BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Between those poles, Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a specialist exam-year subject tutor at AED 200 to 450 and above. Nothing is wrong with any of those numbers. They are prices for different things, and the whole purpose of this page is to let you work out which thing your child needs before you pay for a thing they do not.

The first variable is the tutor, not the subject. A university student who finished IGCSE Biology four years ago can run a vocabulary drill competently and will sit near the bottom of the band. A teacher who has marked Extended Chemistry scripts knows that question 6 on Paper 4 is where the mark scheme refuses to accept a correct answer written in the wrong units, and that knowledge is what the top of the band is buying. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from the June series, the cheaper option often costs more in the end because it spends six of those eight weeks re-teaching content instead of fixing exam technique.

The second variable is the structure your child's school has chosen, and in Dubai that varies school by school. A student taking Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 sits one set of papers covering all three disciplines and can usually be supported by one tutor. A student taking Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate subjects is sitting nine components, and the honest answer is that no single tutor is equally strong across all three at Extended tier. That decision, taken at the end of Year 9, is the single largest driver of a Dubai family's science tuition bill two years later.

The third variable is timing, and it is the one families control. Rates in Dubai firm up from January onwards as Year 11 cohorts across the emirate start booking the same evening slots. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run from AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A family that starts in October pays the lower end of their chosen tier and gets the slot they want. A family that starts in March pays the upper end and takes whatever slot is left, which in practice means 8pm on a school night.

The fourth variable is what the hour actually includes. Some rates are for contact time only. Others include marked past-paper questions returned between sessions, a running record of which syllabus points are secure, and contact with the parent once a month. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, because the number depends on tier, subject count and session length, and a figure invented for a landing page would be worse than no figure. What you can see for free is the tutor: a 30-minute trial lesson, no card details required, after which you know whether the Extended Physics explanation lands with your child or not.

Everything below is organised around that one question. There is an AED band table with its sources named, a structural comparison of Coordinated Sciences against three separate subjects, a practical-paper section that explains why Paper 6 exists, a side-by-side costing of online against in-home against group, the June and November series counted backwards from results day, and a plain account of what the MoHRE private tuition permit is and why you should ask about it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai families arrive at IGCSE science from three directions: a Cambridge Lower Secondary route inside the same school, an Indian or American middle-school programme, or the IB Middle Years Programme. Each leaves a different gap, and the first session is usually spent working out which gap you are actually looking at.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Science
programmes.description: The three-year run-up to IGCSE, finishing with Checkpoint tests that Cambridge offers in March, May and October. Science is taught as one subject with strands in biology, chemistry and physics, and the assessment is diagnostic rather than certificated. Most Dubai British-curriculum schools use the Checkpoint result to stream Year 10 into Core or Extended, which makes Year 9 the cheapest year in which to buy tutoring.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Checkpoint result frequently decides whether a child is entered for Coordinated Sciences or three separate subjects, and that entry decision is harder to reverse than parents expect. A family spending AED 200 an hour on Year 11 Extended Chemistry is often paying to undo a Year 9 streaming decision that a term of Year 9 support would have changed. Schools publish their streaming criteria in the Year 9 options evening pack; ask for it in writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE Science
programmes.description: Two years ending in externally marked papers in the June or November series. Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 each split into a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, with separate question papers for Core and Extended candidates. Pearson runs the same subjects as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 with a different practical model and a modular entry pattern.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a June-series city. Most British-curriculum schools in the emirate enter their main cohort for June and use November for resits and for students who arrived mid-year. That matters for scheduling: the revision peak in Dubai falls in Ramadan and the hottest weeks before the summer exodus, which is why online evening slots in February and March are the first to disappear across the emirate.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma and the science route after IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE science grades are the entry gate to A Level Biology, Chemistry and Physics and to IB Diploma science at Higher Level. Most Dubai sixth forms ask for a grade 6 or B at IGCSE before accepting a student onto the matching A Level, and IB Diploma coordinators look at the Extended tier result rather than the Core one when placing a student at HL.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has both routes in volume, often on the same road. A student finishing IGCSE at a British school in Al Barsha can walk into A Level at the same school or cross the city to an IB Diploma. Families making that choice in Year 11 should know that IB Diploma science at Higher Level assumes the Extended tier content, so a Core tier grade 5 is a weaker platform for HL Chemistry than the same grade from the Extended papers.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Science at IGCSE is not one subject, and the tuition a child needs depends on which of these combinations their school entered them for. Each entry below names the paper structure and the place where Dubai students most reliably drop marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Multiple choice, a theory paper and a practical component. Extended candidates lose marks less on recall than on the long-answer questions about transport in plants and homeostasis, where the mark scheme wants a causal chain in order. Learning the chain as a sequence rather than a list is the single highest-yield drill in this syllabus.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The Extended theory paper rewards precision with state symbols, charges and units. Organic chemistry and electrolysis are where Dubai cohorts most often stall, because both require a method rather than a fact. Mole calculations carry method marks, so a student who sets out working legibly still banks marks after an arithmetic slip.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism produce the widest mark spread of any topic in the syllabus. The Extended theory paper asks students to rearrange formulae under time pressure and to read a graph gradient as a physical quantity. Practice should be timed from the start, because the mark loss here is as much about pace as about understanding.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single award covering all three disciplines at reduced depth, usually taken where a student needs science on the certificate but is heading for humanities or business post-16. The risk is that revision spreads thinly across three subjects; a tutor's job here is to ration time by paper weighting rather than by how interesting a topic is.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Two IGCSE grades from one set of papers covering biology, chemistry and physics. Popular across Dubai because it protects curriculum time for a sixth or seventh subject. Supporting it well means working across all three disciplines in one hour, which is why availability of genuinely cross-trained tutors is tighter than for single subjects.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than through a separate practical test. Students moving from Cambridge mid-course are often surprised by the question style: longer stems, more data to interpret, and a stronger emphasis on describing an experimental method in enough detail to be repeated.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry the full syllabus with no tiering decision to make, which simplifies entry but removes the safety net of a Core paper. Calculation-heavy sections and the required practicals are the two places where a student who was comfortable at Cambridge Core needs several weeks of catch-up.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: The formula list and the expectation that students quote and rearrange relationships accurately drive most of the mark loss. Radioactivity and waves reward diagram-based answers. A tutor working on this specification should be marking against the Pearson mark scheme, not the Cambridge one, because the credit patterns differ.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Pearson's answer to Coordinated Sciences, awarding two grades from papers that cover all three disciplines. Useful for students who need breadth plus a strong overall grade profile. The content overlap with the separate sciences is substantial, so a tutor can support a sibling pair on different specifications without starting from scratch.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680
subjects.description: Taken in a handful of Dubai schools as a science-adjacent option, with a strong case-study element that suits students who write well but find equations hard. Marks concentrate in data interpretation and in the extended-response evaluation questions, both of which respond quickly to structured practice.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor.regionsIntro: IGCSE science tuition demand in Dubai is not spread evenly. It follows the British-curriculum school clusters, and the school-run timetable in each of those clusters decides what time a session can realistically start. These are the areas families book from most often.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Dense with British-curriculum secondary schools and the most competitive 5pm to 7pm slot window in the emirate. Families here are usually choosing between separate sciences and Coordinated Sciences, and book earliest in the academic year.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Apartment living, no spare study room and long lift waits at school pick-up. Sessions here start later than in the villa communities, and headphone-based online lessons are the practical format rather than a compromise.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: A long school run on the Emirates Road corridor means a child is rarely home before 4.30pm. Science sessions land well at 6pm, after a break, and parents here commonly take a Saturday morning slot for past-paper work.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Newer schools, growing Year 10 cohorts and a high rate of mid-year arrivals who are switching specification. Catch-up work on specification differences is the most common first request from this area.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A mix of British and Indian-curriculum families, which makes CBSE-to-IGCSE science transitions common here. The content gap is smaller than parents fear; the question-style gap in practical and data questions is larger.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Established British schools with long-standing Extended tier cohorts and high expectations in Chemistry and Physics. Requests from this area skew towards grade 8 to grade 9 refinement rather than remediation.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to the universities, with families who often want the IGCSE science grade framed against A Level and university entry from the first session. Evening availability is easier here than in the Marina cluster.

regions.name: Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Older residential districts where Combined Science and Coordinated Sciences entries are proportionally higher. Budget sensitivity is real, and the honest recommendation is often fewer, longer sessions concentrated in the ten weeks before the series.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai school cluster
schoolClusters.note: The schools along the Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah corridor run the largest Extended tier science cohorts in the emirate. All are inspected annually by KHDA, and their published inspection reports include a subject-level comment on science that is worth reading before you book anything.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and new-community Dubai school cluster
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving Mirdif, Nad Al Sheba, Sobha Hartland, Dubai Hills and Academic City. Several opened within the last decade and have Year 11 cohorts smaller than their Year 7 intake, which means science sets are often mixed-ability and private support is more common.

sections.heading: The AED bands for IGCSE science tuition in Dubai, with every figure attributed
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Dubai is quoted somewhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour as of October 2026, and the spread is explained almost entirely by who the tutor is and what the hour includes. That range is not a marketing device. It is five different products sold under one word.

The table below collects the published rates we could verify from provider pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. Where a provider states a starting price, it appears as a floor rather than a typical price, because a floor rate is almost always for the shortest session with the least experienced tutor. None of these figures is an IB Gram price. We publish them because three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in.

Read the table with one question in mind: what does the hour include? A rate at the bottom of the band typically buys contact time only. A rate in the middle usually includes a marked question set between sessions. At the top it includes a written record of syllabus coverage, timed papers marked against the official scheme and a monthly conversation with the parent. The difference between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour is rarely the tutor talking more impressively; it is whether anything happens between Tuesday and the following Tuesday.

One figure deliberately absent is a VAT statement. The UAE treatment of tuition fees depends on the provider's registration status and is not something a landing page should assert, so ask any provider whether the number they quoted you includes VAT, and ask for it in writing.

sections.heading: Five things that move the number on a Dubai science quote
paragraphs: Parents often assume the price difference is negotiation. It is not. Five concrete variables set the figure, and four of them are inside your control before you ask anyone for a rate.

Tier comes first. Core and Extended are different papers with different ceilings, and Extended tier work is quoted higher because the theory paper goes further and the mark scheme is less forgiving. If your child is entered for Core, say so when you ask for a rate, because being tutored at Extended depth for a Core paper is a way of spending money on content that will never be examined.

Subject count comes second, and it is the big one. Three separate sciences at Extended tier is three syllabuses, nine components and in practice more than one tutor. A double-award entry is one set of papers and usually one tutor. A family can halve a science tuition bill by recognising which of those two situations they are in before they start booking.

The remaining three are session length, proximity to the series and what the hour includes. Ninety minutes is better value than sixty for Extended tier work, because a timed paper section plus feedback does not fit into an hour. Rates firm up across Dubai from January as Year 11 cohorts book the same evening slots. And an hour that produces marked work is a different product from an hour that produces a conversation, even when the two are priced the same.
bullets: Core or Extended: ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for
One double award or three separate sciences, which decides tutor count

sections.heading: Coordinated Sciences, Combined Science or three separate subjects, costed properly
paragraphs: This is the decision most Dubai families make without being told it has a price tag. At the end of Year 9 the school presents three science routes, usually framed around curriculum time and university aspiration. Nobody mentions that one route can cost three times as much to support privately.

Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award: one set of papers covering biology, chemistry and physics, producing two IGCSE grades. Combined Science 0653 is a single award covering the same three disciplines at lower depth, producing one grade. Separate Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 produce three grades from three full syllabuses. Pearson mirrors the structure with Science Double Award 4SD0 alongside the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1.

The tutoring consequence is arithmetic. A double-award student can be supported by one cross-trained tutor across all three strands in a single session, with time rationed by paper weighting. A student taking three separate sciences at Extended tier needs genuine depth in each, and the honest position is that very few tutors are equally strong across all three at that level. That means two or three tutors, two or three hourly rates, and two or three sets of homework landing on a Year 11 timetable that is already full.

None of this means the double award is better. A student heading for Medicine or Engineering needs the separate sciences, and the extra cost buys something real. The point is to make the decision knowing what follows from it, in Year 9, when a term of targeted support can still change which route the school offers.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: the practical decision that quietly costs tutoring hours
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade sits in the practical component, and that component comes in two forms. Paper 5 is a practical test sat in a laboratory. Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, a written paper about experimental method, apparatus, tables of results and sources of error. Your child's school chooses which one to enter, and many Dubai parents do not know which it is until results day.

The distinction matters for tuition because the two papers reward different preparation. Paper 5 rewards hands under running water: measuring accurately, reading a thermometer at eye level, recording to a consistent number of decimal places. Paper 6 rewards the written grammar of experimental work, which is learnable without a bench. Describing how to control a variable, identifying why a reading drifted, drawing a results table with units in the headers and plotting a line of best fit are all skills a tutor can build over live video with a shared screen and a scanned past paper.

This is where online delivery is a straightforward advantage rather than a trade-off. Paper 6 is a written paper, and the drilling it needs is annotation, marking and redrafting of written answers. A tutor sharing a screen can mark a results table in real time, show the mark scheme alongside it and make the student rewrite the error-analysis sentence twice. The laboratory work itself belongs in school, where the equipment and the supervision are, and no private tutor in Dubai should be presenting a home bench as a substitute for it.

Pearson handles practical skills differently again, assessing them inside the written papers rather than through a separate component. A student moving between the two systems mid-course needs this explained once, carefully, because the question style changes more than the content does.
bullets: Ask the school, in writing, whether your child is entered for Paper 5 or Paper 6
Paper 6 technique is written technique and responds quickly to marked practice

sections.heading: Online, in-home and small-group science tutoring in Dubai, side by side
paragraphs: The phrase most Dubai parents search is a home tutor, and it is worth answering that properly rather than deflecting it. In-home tuition in Dubai is a real market with real prices: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with monthly packages of four two-hour visits advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The premium over online is travel, and in Dubai travel is not a rounding error. A tutor crossing from Al Quoz to Arabian Ranches at 5pm is committing ninety minutes to a sixty-minute lesson, and that time is inside your rate whether or not it appears as a line item.

The second cost of in-home tuition is less visible and more important. It restricts your choice to tutors who live within driving distance of your villa. For a Year 11 student who needs Extended Chemistry specifically, the pool of people within a twenty-minute drive who have actually marked 0620 Extended scripts may be nobody. Families solve this by accepting a generalist who is nearby, which is a geography decision dressed up as an academic one.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing and scanned past papers annotated live. The case for it is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is. The case is that your child gets the right specialist for the paper they are sitting rather than the nearest available person, and that nothing in the fee is paying for Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm.

Small-group tuition is the third option and it is genuinely cheaper per student, but it works only when the group shares a tier, a specification and a weak topic. A group of four where two sit Core and two sit Extended delivers half a lesson to everyone.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost, subject by subject
paragraphs: A quote is only useful if you know what you are buying hours to fix. Across Dubai cohorts the mark loss in science is strikingly patterned, and most of it is not a content gap.

In Biology, the long-answer questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance want a causal chain in the right order. Students who know every term still score two out of four because they list facts instead of linking them. The fix is structural: a sentence frame that forces cause, mechanism and consequence, practised on six past questions until it becomes automatic.

In Chemistry, the mark loss sits in precision rather than knowledge. State symbols, charges, units and significant figures carry marks, and the Extended theory paper awards method marks in mole calculations, which means a student who writes out working legibly still banks credit after an arithmetic error. Organic chemistry and electrolysis both need a procedure rather than a memory, and both respond to being taught as a flowchart.

In Physics, electricity and magnetism produce the widest spread in the whole syllabus, and the second problem is pace. The Extended theory paper asks for formula rearrangement under time pressure, and students who can do the physics untimed lose marks they would otherwise have. Timed practice from the first session, not the last month, is what closes that. Across all three subjects, the practical component is the most ignored twenty per cent on the paper, and a single session on results tables and error analysis frequently moves a grade boundary.

Chemistry: state symbols, units and legible working that earns method marks
