sections.heading: Starting without overspending, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence that wastes the least money is short. Ask the school what support is already included. Get the board and syllabus code for each science, and the tier entered. Collect the last two marked scripts. Then buy a diagnostic rather than a term, and let the diagnosis name the component and the hours. A free trial lesson - one per family, with no card details taken - is the right place to test whether a tutor can read those scripts and say something specific about them.

What a diagnostic should produce is a written plan naming the component, the number of sessions, what the student will do between them and how progress will be measured. If the output is a vague promise about confidence, that is a sign the sessions will also be vague. Paper scores are the measurement that matters, and they are available because official past papers exist and the schemes are published by the boards on their own sites.

Availability is the part most providers conceal, so here it is plainly. Specialist cover is not uniform across subjects and hours. Chemistry and Physics at Extended tier in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest slots in the week, because every family in Dubai wants them. If no specialist is free for the hours a family in The Views needs, the honest answers are a different time slot, a short wait, or a tutor whose specialism is adjacent rather than exact - and the family should be told which of the three applies before paying anything.

Finally, review on a timetable rather than on a feeling. Four sessions in, look at the paper scores and the marked work. If the target component has moved, extend. If it has not, change the component, change the tutor, or stop. A plan that cannot be stopped at a review point is not a plan, it is a subscription, and subscriptions are how a reasonable AED 200 an hour becomes a number nobody examined.

process.title: Confirm board, code and tier
process.description: Before anything is priced, find out which board each science is entered with, which syllabus code, and whether the entry is Core or Extended. The school's head of science can confirm all three in one message. This single step prevents the most expensive mistake in the market, which is buying past-paper practice for the wrong board.

process.title: Send the last two marked scripts
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it tells a specialist more than an hour of conversation. It shows which component is leaking, whether the losses are knowledge or technique, and whether the candidate is finishing. Scripts and the school report comments are the whole of the useful input.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Use it as an interview rather than a lesson: ask the tutor to name the component that is costing marks and to say what the first four sessions would target. A specific answer is the thing being tested.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic block, not a term
process.description: Two or three sessions whose output is a written plan with a component, a session count and a measurement. This costs less than a month of weekly sessions and it is the step that decides whether the eventual spend is four hours or forty. Families who skip it almost always buy more hours than they needed.

process.title: Work between sessions and mark it
process.description: The variable that halves or doubles the total hours is whether written work gets done and marked between lessons. Set it, do it, return it marked to the scheme. A student completing timed questions each week needs roughly half the sessions of one who only turns up, and no discount available anywhere matches that saving.

process.title: Review on paper scores at session four
process.description: At the fourth session compare paper scores on the target component against the starting point. Extend, change or stop on that evidence. A review point that is written into the plan in advance is what separates a costed intervention from an open-ended monthly payment nobody audits.

whyPoints.title: The price is on the page, in AED
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published here with the provider that quoted each one and the month of the quote. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A family in The Views comparing offers should be able to see the range before making a call.

whyPoints.title: No drive inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so none of the hour is spent on Sheikh Zayed Road and none of the rate pays for it. From Emirates Living the school-run drive to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is twenty to forty minutes each way, which is the premium in-home pricing exists to cover.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a component, not a postcode
whyPoints.description: The useful question is not who is nearby but who has marked the paper your child is losing marks on. Choosing by component rather than by distance widens the pool to every specialist free at that hour, which is the practical argument for the online format in a subject with three distinct mark schemes.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0610, 0620, 0625, 0653 and 0654 and Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 behave differently in question stems and mark schemes. Work is planned against the code the candidate is entered for, and past papers come from that code, which is the difference between practice and busywork.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains, sets practice and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing assessed is produced for a student, ever. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is a malpractice trigger for the candidate, and the boundary is worth saying out loud rather than leaving implied.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Specialist cover varies by subject and by hour, and the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window is the tightest in the week. If no exact specialist is free for the slot a family needs, that is said before anything is paid, with the alternatives named. Concealed coverage limits are a cost that arrives later.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor for The Views cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates reaching The Views run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, as published by providers in October 2026. Most families transact between AED 150 and 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a subject specialist. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with the drive inside the rate. Those are market bands rather than an IB Gram price list. What varies inside a band is whether the hour contains marked written work or only conversation, and that difference matters more than the number.

faqs.question: Is one tutor for all three sciences cheaper than three specialists?
faqs.answer: It is usually cheaper per hour and often more expensive per mark. Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Extended tier are three syllabuses with three mark schemes, and few tutors mark all three to examiner standard. Where a candidate has one narrow problem in each subject, a single tutor on alternating weeks can work and halves the weekly cost. Where one science has a broad problem, that subject needs its own specialist. The honest test is to ask the tutor to name the component costing marks in each of the three. A tutor who can do that for all three is rare and worth keeping.

faqs.question: Do triple-award candidates need more tutoring hours than double-award?
faqs.answer: Yes, roughly in proportion to the papers sat. Three separate sciences means three multiple-choice papers, three theory papers and three practical components, so there is simply more assessed material. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 produces two grades from the same three strands and Combined Science 0653 produces one, which concentrates the work. With a combined award the efficient approach is diagnostic: identify which strand is dragging the single grade and spend the hours there. Buying three subjects' worth of support for one combined grade is one of the commonest overspends in this market.

faqs.question: Is a group science class in Barsha Heights better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly yes. Per problem, usually not. A group class is sold at a lower per-student rate and delivers a shared pace across a syllabus, which suits broad revision before a series. It does not suit one candidate's specific weakness, because the weakest topic for your child is rarely the topic the group needs that week. A reasonable sequence is a group class for syllabus coverage if the school is not already providing it, plus a short one-to-one block aimed at the component the mock paper identified. Paying group prices to solve an individual problem is a false economy.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix electricity and magnetism?
faqs.answer: For a candidate who understands the rest of Physics and loses marks on circuits, six sessions is a realistic block: roughly one per sub-topic, plus retrieval practice and two timed papers. At the mid market band of AED 200 an hour that is around AED 1,200 of indicative arithmetic, not a quoted price. The variable that changes it most is whether the student completes and submits the written work between sessions. A candidate who does needs about half the hours of one who does not, which is a bigger saving than any rate negotiation will produce.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour buy a better science tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The published spread in Dubai is roughly fourteenfold for what is advertised as the same service, and a high rate can reflect scarcity in a subject at a particular hour rather than method or experience. The checkable signals are different: can the tutor name the component your child is losing marks in before being booked, will they mark written work against the published scheme rather than discuss it, and do they know the syllabus code rather than just the subject. Those three questions separate tutors more accurately than price does, and all three can be tested in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: When in Year 10 is the cheapest time to start science support?
faqs.answer: The cheapest intervention is usually the earliest small one. A short diagnostic in the first term of Year 10, once the tier entry is known, costs a few hours and prevents a weak strand becoming a whole-subject problem by the mocks. Waiting until the spring of Year 11 does not raise rates formally, but it narrows availability sharply, and a family looking for a specialist in April chooses from whoever is left. Early also means the work can be spread, and spread hours are both cheaper per month and more effective than the same hours compressed.

faqs.question: Do science tutoring rates in Dubai rise before the June series?
faqs.answer: Published rates do not generally move, but effective cost does. As a series approaches, demand concentrates in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window, specialists in Chemistry and Physics fill first, and families accept adjacent rather than exact specialisms or less convenient slots. That is a quality cost rather than a price rise. Some providers do sell intensive exam-term packages at higher monthly totals because the session count is higher. The practical conclusion is to book the specialist and the slot early, even if the sessions themselves start later in the year.

faqs.question: What should I ask about price before the first science lesson?
faqs.answer: Six questions settle it. Is the rate per clock hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? Is marking of written work between sessions included or extra? Is there a minimum block, and can we stop at a review point? What happens to unused sessions? Is the rate per subject if two sciences share a slot? And does the quoted figure include VAT? Ask them in writing and keep the reply. Most disputes in this market come from the gap between an hourly rate and what the hour included, not from the rate itself.

faqs.question: Are the AED rates quoted per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both conventions exist in Dubai, which is exactly why comparison is hard. Some providers quote a clock-hour rate; others quote per session, where a session may be fifty, sixty or ninety minutes. A few quote monthly packages with a stated session count, such as the AED 799 a month for eight online sessions visible in the market. Convert everything to a cost per sixty minutes of teaching before comparing, and ask separately whether marking between sessions is inside that number. Two quotes that look twenty per cent apart are sometimes identical once normalised.

faqs.question: Can the alternative-to-practical paper be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of an online hour. The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper: read a method, complete a results table, plot and interpret a graph, spot an anomalous point, name a source of error, suggest one improvement. All of that is paper technique and responds to marking. Where a school enters the practical test instead, the hands-on work belongs to the school, and tutoring supports the surrounding decisions - table layout, precision, how many readings and at what intervals. Those are made before any apparatus is touched.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge or Pearson science cheaper to get tutoring for?
faqs.answer: The rate is the same; the availability is not. Cambridge syllabuses are more widely entered in Dubai, so the pool of tutors who know 0610, 0620 and 0625 well is larger and easier to fill at awkward hours. Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 need a tutor who works from the Pearson specification and Pearson past papers, and that pool is smaller. The real cost difference appears if a family buys the wrong board's practice. Confirm the board per subject rather than per school, because some schools enter a mixture.

faqs.question: How do I check a private science tutor may legally teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Ask any individual tutor whether they hold the permit and check the official page yourself. Anyone quoting you a fee for it, or a fine amount, is working from something that is not published.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if the first science tutor is the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Ask before you pay, in writing, and prefer arrangements with a review point rather than a long prepaid block. A sensible structure is a free trial lesson first, then a short diagnostic block, then a review at the fourth session against paper scores on the target component. If the component has not moved, the right move is to change the tutor or the target, not to extend. Avoid any arrangement that ties a refund to an exam outcome; outcomes depend on the student's own work and no honest provider prices them.

faqs.question: What if no Physics specialist is free for the hours we need?
faqs.answer: That happens, most often in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window during an exam term, and the honest answer is one of three. A different slot, sometimes a morning at a weekend, which is usually the best of the three. A short wait for the right specialist, which is reasonable in autumn and risky in April. Or an adjacent specialism - a Chemistry teacher strong on quantitative work covering the calculation side while Paper 6 technique waits. Which one applies should be said before any payment, not discovered afterwards.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Price the problem, then buy the hours
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: The useful order is cheap first: ask the school what is already included, confirm the board, code and tier for each science, collect the last two marked scripts, then test a tutor on a free trial lesson by asking them to name the component that is costing marks. Buy a diagnostic rather than a term, write down the component, the session count and the measurement, and review on paper scores at the fourth session. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which keeps the drive out of the rate and widens the choice to every specialist free at that hour. The market bands on this page are published so a family in The Views can compare offers before anyone picks up a phone.

intro.heading: What a Dubai summer actually buys you
paragraphs: The Dubai school year closes in the first week of July and opens again in the last days of August or the first week of September, depending on whether a school runs a British or an IB calendar. That leaves roughly eight to nine clear weeks. For an IGCSE student the arithmetic is unusually favourable. A two-year course taught at four or five lessons a fortnight loses nothing in that window, while a student who uses thirty of those hours properly can arrive in Year 11 having already closed the three topics that would otherwise sit unresolved until the February mock.

Summer tuition is not term tuition moved sideways. During term a tutor is permanently one week behind a school scheme of work, patching whatever was taught on Tuesday afternoon. In July nothing is being taught, so the agenda belongs entirely to the student. That changes what a session can be. A whole hour can go on simultaneous equations with no competing deadline. A second hour can revisit the same topic two days later, which is the spacing that moves recall rather than comprehension, and term-time scheduling almost never allows it.

The second thing the break buys is a clean read on where the marks went. Most Dubai families arrive in July holding a June report card with a letter on it and no information underneath. A report says grade 5. It does not say that the 5 came from scoring well on routine calculation and badly on anything beginning with the command term explain. One timed paper, marked against the published mark scheme in front of the student, produces that split inside ninety minutes and turns a vague worry into a list.

Travel is the constraint everyone underestimates. Dubai empties in July. Families move between the UAE, the United Kingdom, India, Egypt, Lebanon and Pakistan, often more than once, and a tutor who can only meet in a Dubai living room loses the student for five of the nine weeks. Lessons delivered over live video follow the student instead. A session booked for 17:00 Gulf Standard Time becomes 13:00 in London and 18:30 in Mumbai, and the schedule holds because the fixed points are the tutor and the student, not a car.

The last thing to settle before July is whether the summer is remedial, preparatory or a resit campaign, because those are three different plans. A Year 10 student closing gaps works topic by topic. A student entering Year 11 works forward into the first term's content so that September becomes revision rather than first contact. A student entered for the Pearson November series is on a fixed countdown and needs past-paper volume from week one. Mixing the three is the most reliable way to watch a summer dissolve into pleasant, undirected conversation.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.programmesIntro: Summer work splits by where a student sits on the British curriculum ladder, not by age. These are the four entry points Dubai families book in July, with what each should have produced by the last week of August. A Year 9 student choosing options needs something different from a November resit candidate, and the only reason the two get planned identically is that nobody asked the question in June.

programmes.name: Pre-IGCSE: the options summer
programmes.description: Year 9 ends with a subject-choice form and very little information behind it. A July block here is diagnostic rather than remedial: enough algebra, enough chemical calculation and enough extended writing to tell whether triple science and Extended maths are a sensible load or an expensive mistake. The output is a short written view on each candidate subject, with the specification content the student has not yet met named topic by topic.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai complicates this because option blocks differ sharply between schools in the same community. A Jumeirah school may run triple science against a second language, while a school ten minutes away runs them in parallel. Settling the question in July, before the form is returned in September, is cheaper than discovering in Year 11 that Chemistry 0620 was never going to fit alongside Additional Mathematics 0606.

programmes.name: Year 10 gap closure
programmes.description: The most common July booking. One year of the course has been taught, roughly half the specification is covered, and the June report has produced a grade nobody can explain. Work runs topic by topic against the published subject content, with a timed section of a past paper every second session so that progress is measured in marks rather than in how the student felt about the hour.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Year 10 students lose a disproportionate number of marks in the first half of the specification because it is taught in Year 9 and never revisited. Number, units and the mole, and the practical-skills paper content all fall into that trap. A summer block that goes back to the earliest taught topics, rather than forward, usually produces more mark movement than any amount of new content.

programmes.name: The September bridge into Year 11
programmes.description: This block runs forward. Four or five weeks of work on the content a school will teach in the autumn term turns September from first contact into revision, which matters enormously in a year where the February mock sets predicted grades for university applications. It suits a student who is already reasonably secure and whose risk is volume rather than understanding.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set their Year 11 mocks earlier than UK schools do, often in January or early February, because UCAS and UAE university deadlines arrive sooner for the cohort sitting A-Levels or the IB Diploma afterwards. A student who spent the summer four weeks ahead walks into that mock having seen the material twice. One who did not sees it once, three weeks before.

programmes.name: The November resit campaign
programmes.description: A fixed countdown with no room for topic tourism. Past-paper volume starts in week one, marked and logged, and the plan is built from the error log rather than from the syllabus order. The student needs to know which paper, which tier and which board before the first session, because the Cambridge and Pearson versions of the same subject award marks differently.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE exams in May or June and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry is made through a centre, and private candidates in Dubai need to secure one early. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the realistic point at which a Dubai sixth-form place can be confirmed on a repaired grade.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.subjectsIntro: Nine subjects account for most July bookings in Dubai. The syllabus code matters more than the subject name, because Cambridge and Pearson split content, papers and tiers differently for the same nominal course. Send the code from your child's exam entry or statement of entry and the planning starts from the right document rather than from an assumption.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tiers
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in algebraic manipulation, trigonometry beyond the right-angled triangle, and the long multi-step questions at the back of Paper 4. Summer work normally starts with indices, surds and rearranging formulae, because nearly every later topic quietly depends on them and the dependency is invisible in a school report.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure (0606, 4PM1)
subjects.description: Calculus, matrices, logarithms and kinematics arrive with no gentle introduction, and students who coped with 0580 by pattern-matching run out of patterns. July is the natural moment for this subject because it rewards uninterrupted blocks of practice rather than one lesson a week squeezed against everything else.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism produce the widest spread of marks, and the practical-skills questions produce the most avoidable losses: axes unlabelled, a line of best fit drawn through the origin for no reason, a conclusion that restates the data. Both are fixable in a summer with no competing homework.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: The mole dominates. Students who cannot move confidently between mass, moles, concentration and volume lose marks across half the paper, not just in the calculation questions. Organic chemistry and the qualitative-analysis tables are the other two reliable gaps, and both reward memorisation with structure behind it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance carry most of the lost marks, usually because an answer describes when the command term asked the student to explain. Summer work here is as much about answer construction as about recall.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science (0653, 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two GCSE grades, which means the specification cuts content unpredictably and students revise topics they will never be asked about. The first useful summer hour is spent mapping what the double award actually includes, against the single-science syllabus the online revision sites assume.

subjects.name: English Language (0500, 0990, 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry the marks, and both are assessed on a band descriptor rather than a tick list. A student who has never read the band descriptors is guessing. Summer work pairs one timed response a week with line-by-line marking against the published criteria.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475, 0992, 4ET1)
subjects.description: Closed-text examination means quotation accuracy matters, and Dubai students who changed school mid-course sometimes carry notes on a text they are no longer being examined on. July is the moment to confirm the set texts for the series and build a quotation bank around the assessment objectives.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455, 0450, 4EC1, 4BS1)
subjects.description: Both subjects are lost on evaluation rather than knowledge. A definition earns one mark; a judgement supported by a chain of reasoning earns four. Summer sessions here work almost entirely on paragraph structure, with the content treated as raw material rather than as the thing being learned.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and Additional Language (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Dubai students sit Arabic alongside an international curriculum because KHDA requires the subject regardless of the licensed curriculum. The IGCSE version is a separate examination with its own specification, and summer support has to distinguish between school Arabic lessons and the Cambridge assessment they do not automatically prepare for.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.regionsIntro: Area matters less for delivery than it used to, because the sessions run over live video, and more for scheduling. These are the seven Dubai communities that generate the most July enquiries, with what the summer actually looks like in each. The pattern of who leaves and when decides whether a thirty-hour block fits into six weeks or nine.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Heavy British-curriculum catchment and the earliest July departures, with many families away for the whole of August. Blocks here usually compress into the first five weeks, running three sessions a week rather than two, and finish before the family travels.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Dubai Harbour
regions.note: Apartment living and shorter trips. Students are often in Dubai for most of the break but share a desk with a sibling and a parent working from home, so sessions are timed to the quietest part of the day rather than the conventional late afternoon.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Dubailand
regions.note: Villa communities where a tutor visit once meant a thirty-minute drive each way from the city. Online delivery removes that entirely, which is why mid-morning sessions are common here in July, a slot that was never practical during term.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Large family households with several IGCSE-age children and a strong preference for consecutive sessions. Two students back to back on the same subject at different tiers is the usual pattern, with one on Core and one on Extended.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: The densest cluster of British-curriculum schools in the city, which produces the widest spread of exam boards in a single community. Confirming Cambridge against Pearson before the first session matters more here than almost anywhere else.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai, Business Bay and DIFC
regions.note: Short breaks and working parents, so July bookings skew towards evening sessions and towards resit candidates rather than Year 10 gap closure. Students here are often already in a sixth form elsewhere and repairing one grade.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Price-sensitive and well informed, with families who have already compared four providers before making contact. Published market rates and a clear statement of what a block excludes matter more to this group than any other.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum schools running IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A-Levels or the IB Diploma. Families in this cluster usually know their exam board but rarely know the tier their child has been entered at, which is the first thing a July diagnostic settles.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Al Quoz
schoolClusters.note: The highest concentration of British-curriculum provision in Dubai, with a mix of Cambridge and Pearson entries across schools a few minutes apart. Students who move between these schools mid-course are the ones most likely to be revising the wrong specification.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Larger year groups and a broader attainment spread, so Core and Extended entries sit side by side in the same household. Summer plans in this cluster more often involve two children than one, on different tiers of the same subject.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes of summer booking cover almost every enquiry. The difference between them is not the number of hours but what the hours are pointed at, and choosing the wrong shape is why some summers produce a visible grade shift and others produce a pleasant set of conversations and no mark movement at all.

modes.title: The thirty-hour block
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week across six to nine weeks, planned as one course rather than as separate lessons. Week one is diagnostic. Weeks two to seven work the error log in priority order. The final week is a timed full paper under exam conditions, marked and returned with a written handover for the autumn term.

modes.title: Resit countdown
modes.description: For a student entered for a November or later series. Past papers from week one, worked under timed conditions, with the plan rebuilt every fortnight from what the marking shows rather than from the syllabus order. The board and tier are confirmed before the first session, because Cambridge and Pearson reward different answer structures for identical content.

modes.title: September bridge
modes.description: Four to five weeks spent forward of the school, covering the content the autumn term will teach. Suits a secure student whose risk is volume rather than understanding, and it changes the February mock from a first full encounter with the specification into a second one. Pace is deliberately brisk and the material is revisited in September anyway.

modes.title: Two students, one timetable
modes.description: Common in Dubai villa communities where two or three siblings sit IGCSE in consecutive years. Sessions run back to back with separate plans, separate diagnostics and separate reporting, which keeps the convenience of one timetable without the compromise of teaching two different tiers in the same hour.

sections.heading: What IGCSE summer tuition in Dubai costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six agency pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. Here is the market in dirhams. Budget online tutoring, usually a university student working straight from the textbook, sits around AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150.

An in-home visit is the expensive option, and the premium is travel rather than teaching. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts home tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A tutor who drives from Mirdif to Arabian Ranches for a 17:00 session has spent ninety unpaid minutes in a car, and that time is priced into the hour whether or not anyone itemises it. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Summer moves the number in one direction only: volume. A thirty-hour block bought in July almost always carries a lower effective hourly rate than six single lessons bought in February, because the tutor is planning one course rather than six separate rescues. Monthly packages visible across the Dubai market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages: the free trial lesson and the conversation after it are where a quote comes from, and the figures above are the market you are quoting against.

sections.heading: The eight-week plan, written backwards from the September return
paragraphs: A summer plan written forwards fills the available hours. A summer plan written backwards from the first week of September decides what has to be true on the last Sunday of August and works out what each week must deliver to get there. The difference shows up in week six, when the forward plan is still working through the syllabus in order and the backward plan has already spent two weeks on the three topics that were costing the most marks.

The sequence below assumes thirty hours across eight weeks at two sessions a week, which is the most commonly booked shape in Dubai. It survives interruption reasonably well. A family that disappears for a fortnight in the middle loses weeks four and five, and the plan absorbs that by compressing the consolidation block rather than by abandoning the final timed paper, which is the one component that must not move.

Two outputs make this plan auditable rather than aspirational. The first is the error log, a running list of every dropped mark classified by topic and by command term, which replaces the tutor's memory as the planning document and is shared with the family rather than kept in a notebook. The second is the weekly named deliverable in the right-hand column of the table below. If a week ends and the deliverable does not exist, the plan has slipped, and the next session opens with that rather than with new content. Both are deliberately boring, which is the point: a summer plan that can be checked halfway through is the only kind that gets corrected in time.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Almost nobody loses IGCSE marks because a topic was never taught. Marks go missing because an answer does the wrong thing with the content it has. A student who knows the mechanism of osmosis perfectly and writes a description when the paper asked for an explanation has lost two marks on knowledge they possess. Repeat that across a paper and a grade 7 becomes a grade 5 without a single genuine gap in understanding.

Command terms are the mechanism. Each one has a mark-scheme shape behind it, and the shapes are not interchangeable. Calculate wants working and a unit. Explain wants a causal chain, usually two linked statements. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence, not two paragraphs side by side. Suggest wants a plausible application of principle to an unfamiliar context and is marked generously if the reasoning is visible. None of this is secret and none of it is on the specification.

The second mechanism is arithmetic about time. A Cambridge Extended paper allocates roughly one mark a minute, and a student who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has borrowed eight minutes from somewhere later. The fix is not speed, it is triage, and it is learned by sitting timed sections with a clock visible and reviewing what the clock cost rather than only what the answers scored. July is the only time of year with room to practise that properly, because a timed section costs an hour of a session that is not also carrying this week's homework.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision Dubai families leave too late
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is examined at two tiers. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and can be awarded grades C to G. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can be awarded grades A* to E. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10 and sometimes as late as the autumn of Year 11, and it sets a hard ceiling on what the student can be awarded no matter how well the paper goes.

Families frequently discover the tier only when the statement of entry arrives. By then a student capable of a grade 6 may be entered for Core, where a grade 6 does not exist, and a student who is genuinely struggling may be entered for Extended, where the paper is written for a different attainment range and the experience is demoralising rather than instructive. July is the right moment to look at the question honestly, because a tier change requested in September is a conversation and one requested in January is a problem.

The right-fit signal is not the report grade. It is how the student performs on the harder half of the tier above, under time. A student who scores respectably on Paper 4 questions from the first half of the specification belongs on Extended even if the school is hesitant. A student who finds Paper 2 uncomfortable and Paper 1 straightforward is better served by a Core entry with a secure grade C than by an Extended entry and a grade E. Both conversations are easier with a marked script in hand.

sections.heading: Resit routes, and why the entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Dubai family can learn in July is that exam entry is a separate process from exam preparation, with its own calendar and its own failure mode. Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE in a May or June series and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge International runs June and November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, plus Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March series key dates make the lead time concrete: for March 2027 the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The same shape applies to the series a Dubai centre uses. Entry closes months before anyone sits anything.

One operational detail catches private candidates every year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the only safe reference is the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one.

sections.heading: How the lessons are actually delivered, and why nobody arrives at a Dubai address
paragraphs: Every session on this page is one-to-one and runs over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is true in July as it is in term time. The reason is not logistics. It is that the pool of people who can teach Cambridge 0620 organic chemistry to a grade 8 standard and who also happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Arabian Ranches in August is close to empty, while the pool who can teach it over a shared screen is not.

What the video session gives up is physical presence. What it gains is specification match. A Dubai family choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from whoever is available locally and free at 17:00; a family choosing an online specialist is choosing from everyone who teaches that paper. In a subject where the difference between a Cambridge and a Pearson answer structure is worth a grade, that trade is not close.

Practically, a session uses a shared whiteboard, a document camera or phone stand so handwritten working is visible both ways, and the actual past-paper PDF annotated live. Sessions are recorded, which turns the summer into a revision archive the student still has in February. Handwritten scripts are photographed and returned marked. None of this requires anyone to be in a car during a Dubai August, which is its own argument.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai calendar and the mandatory subjects that do not pause
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The scale is worth knowing before you plan a summer: Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of that enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent.

Two KHDA facts shape a July plan. The first is money: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is therefore being added to a flat school-fee base this year rather than a rising one, which changes how a thirty-hour block looks in a household budget. The second is capacity: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places, four of them UK curriculum.

The third thing that does not pause is the mandatory UAE subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. A summer that ignores these subjects ignores part of the September timetable.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule that decides which summer subjects matter
paragraphs: If your child will apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules decide which IGCSE grades count, and the British-track requirement is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that changes summer planning is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student holding seven IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has five that count, with no margin. One ranking competitor publishes the claim that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the rule says, and a family planning around that number is planning around an error.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs and verifies, not something a tutoring service performs, promises or accelerates, and nothing on this page should be read as a route around it. And no IB points threshold for equivalency is published here, because the figure circulating online could not be verified against moe.gov.ae. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own page or with the attestation authority in your emirate before you plan a subject load around it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a summer with no teacher watching
paragraphs: July is when the boundary gets tested, because school coursework deadlines sit in the autumn and the person supervising is on holiday. The position here is not negotiable. A tutor teaches, questions, models technique and gives written feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not author assessed work, does not supply finished answers for submission, and does not edit a draft to the point where the voice and the judgements are no longer the student's own.

This is a live problem in this market rather than a theoretical one. One site ranking for these queries sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's own certification at risk, and no amount of tutoring hours makes it a sensible purchase. The honest version of coursework support is narrower and more useful: teaching the skill the task assesses, reading a draft the student wrote and naming what the criteria would reward, then handing it back.

The same boundary applies to materials. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and they are referenced and linked rather than reproduced or redistributed. Where a session works through a past paper, it works through the official document on screen. That is both the lawful position and, incidentally, the only version in which the student is looking at the real thing rather than at somebody's retyped approximation of it.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work

Board materials are cited and linked, never reproduced as downloads
Feedback is written down, so what was said can be checked later

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and the June report
process.description: Three things make the first session useful: the statement of entry or exam timetable showing the board and tier, the June report card, and one piece of recent marked work. Without the codes, planning starts from an assumption about which specification your child sits, and in Al Barsha that assumption is wrong about as often as it is right.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a timed diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a real lesson, not a sales call, and no card details are needed to book it. If the match works, session one is a timed section of a past paper from the correct tier, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches. That produces the error log everything else is planned from.

process.title: A written plan with one named output a week
process.description: You receive the sequence before the hours are booked: which topics, in which order, with what existing at the end of each week. A plan with named weekly outputs can be audited mid-summer. A plan that says revision and consolidation cannot, which is how six weeks disappear without anything measurable changing.

process.title: Fortnightly marked paper and a short note to you
process.description: Every second session ends with timed questions, marked and annotated. The note that follows is short and specific: what moved, what has not, and what the next fortnight targets. It is written so a parent who does not teach the subject can still tell whether the block is working.

process.title: Handover into September
process.description: The final session is a full paper under exam conditions, followed by a one-page handover naming the topics that are now secure, the ones still at risk and the command terms to watch. It is written for the student to take into the autumn term and, if the school asks, to show a teacher.

whyPoints.title: The diagnostic comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: No topic is taught in week one. A timed section of the correct paper is sat and marked first, because the gap a parent describes and the gap the marks show are different often enough that starting from the description wastes the first fortnight of a nine-week window.

whyPoints.title: Specification, not subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are not the same course, and 0625 Physics is not 4PH1. Tutors are matched to the paper your child sits, and the first session confirms it from the statement of entry rather than from what the school is assumed to use.

whyPoints.title: Marked to the published mark scheme wording
whyPoints.description: Scripts are marked against the board's own criteria rather than a private rubric, and the mark scheme language is shown to the student. A student who has read what the examiner is paid to reward stops guessing what a four-mark answer looks like.

whyPoints.title: The schedule follows the family
whyPoints.description: July in Dubai means travel. Sessions run over live video anchored to Gulf Standard Time, so a block booked in June survives three weeks in London and a fortnight in Kerala without being rescheduled into nothing. The only fixed points are the tutor and the student.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on what a tutor touches
whyPoints.description: Coursework and assessed work stay the student's own. Teaching, questioning and written feedback on a draft the student wrote are inside the line; authoring, supplying or finishing assessed work is outside it, and saying so plainly is a genuine difference in this particular search result.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed, including the fallback
whyPoints.description: Some subject and tier combinations have thin availability in a UAE time zone during August. Where that happens you are told before booking, offered a specialist in another time zone with the session times that implies, or told to wait. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE summer tuition does a Dubai student actually need?
faqs.answer: Thirty hours across the break is the most commonly booked block, which is two sessions a week for eight weeks with a little slack for travel. For a single weak topic, eight to ten hours is enough. For a student repairing two subjects, sixty hours is realistic and needs three sessions a week from the first week of July. The number that matters more than the total is the spacing: two sessions a week on one subject beats four sessions in one weekend, because the gap between them is where retention happens. Any provider quoting a fixed package without seeing a marked script is guessing.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in July if my child only goes into Year 10 in September?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, but for a different reason than most families expect. A pre-Year 10 block is diagnostic rather than remedial. The useful question is whether the subject combination on the options form is a sensible load, and that is answered by seeing how the student handles early algebra, chemical calculation and extended writing under time. The output is a short written view on each candidate subject. That is worth more in Year 9 than content teaching, because the subjects chosen in September decide two years of work and the form is usually returned before anyone has tested the assumptions behind it.

faqs.question: We leave Dubai for six weeks in summer. Can the lessons continue from London or Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the main practical reason the sessions run over live video rather than in person. The schedule is anchored to Gulf Standard Time and converted for wherever the student is, so a 17:00 Dubai slot becomes 13:00 in London or 18:30 in Mumbai. What the student needs is a laptop, a stable connection and about forty minutes of quiet, which a hotel room supplies as well as a villa study. Sessions are recorded, so a week genuinely lost to a family event is recoverable rather than simply gone from a block you have already paid for.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE in November rather than waiting a whole year?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE in a May or June series and again in November, so a November resit is a real route. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the point a sixth-form place can be confirmed on a repaired grade. The constraint is entry, not teaching: entries go through a centre and close well ahead of the papers. Confirm the live timetable and the entry deadline on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are revised and a date restated on any tutoring page can be out of date.

faqs.question: What does summer IGCSE tuition cost per hour in Dubai this year?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market in October 2026 runs roughly like this. Budget online tutoring sits at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, and Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced into the hour. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are market figures from published sources, not an IB Gram price list; a quote follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry or the exam timetable the school issues carries the board name and the syllabus code, and that document is the only reliable source. School websites often name the board for the whole key stage while individual departments enter differently. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0625 for Physics. Pearson codes start with a digit and two letters, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1. The distinction is not cosmetic: the papers differ in structure, tiering and the answer shapes the mark schemes reward, so revising the wrong one costs real marks in a real examination.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Core to Extended over the summer?
faqs.answer: The decision belongs to the school, but the summer is when the evidence for it can be gathered. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 awards grades C to G at Core and A* to E at Extended, so a Core entry caps the outcome regardless of how well the student prepares. The signal to look for is performance on Paper 4 questions drawn from topics already taught, under time. Respectable marks there argue for Extended even when the school is hesitant. Difficulty with Paper 2 alongside comfort on Paper 1 argues the other way, and a secure Core grade C beats an Extended grade E on any application.

faqs.question: Does summer tuition cover the IGCSE science practical papers?
faqs.answer: It covers the assessment, which is what carries the marks. Cambridge and Pearson both examine practical skills through a written paper rather than through observed laboratory work for most international candidates, and the lost marks are predictable: axes without units, a line of best fit forced through the origin, a conclusion that restates the readings instead of interpreting them, an evaluation that names an error without saying what it does to the result. All of that is teachable over a shared screen using the real past paper and real data. What a session cannot replace is the school laboratory time itself.

faqs.question: My child got a grade 4 in the June mock. Can that realistically move by next June?
faqs.answer: A two-grade movement over a full year is common when the starting point is technique rather than absent knowledge, which a marked script shows within one session. A grade 4 built on reasonable content knowledge and poor answer construction moves faster than a grade 4 built on three untaught topics. No honest tutor promises a specific grade, and anyone who does should be asked how they propose to control an examination they do not mark. What can be promised is measurement: timed questions every fortnight, marked to the board's criteria, so the trajectory is visible by October rather than guessed at in May.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai families book most often in July?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then Chemistry, Physics and English Language in roughly that order, with Biology and Additional Mathematics behind them. The pattern reflects where the specifications are least forgiving rather than where teaching is weakest. Mathematics punishes gaps from two years earlier, Chemistry punishes anyone shaky on the mole, Physics punishes weak algebra in disguise, and English Language punishes students who have never read a band descriptor. Economics and Business Studies arrive later in the year, usually in the term before the examination, because their problem is evaluation technique and that can be fixed faster.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach my child over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, with its own service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with my child's coursework while school is closed?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses, explains what the published criteria reward, reads a draft the student has produced and names what is missing in writing. A tutor does not author assessed work, supply finished answers for submission, or edit a draft until the judgements stop being the student's own. That line matters in this market because at least one site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments, which is an integrity breach that puts the student's own certification at risk. Written feedback on the student's own work is the version that is both lawful and useful.

faqs.question: For a UAE university application, how many of my child's IGCSE grades actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which catches families out, because a student with seven certificates of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has exactly five that count. One competitor page states that six subjects are required, which does not match the rule. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before planning a subject load.

faqs.question: Is online summer tuition genuinely as useful as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE work it is a straight trade, and the trade favours video. What you lose is physical presence. What you gain is the specification match: instead of choosing from whoever lives nearby and is free at 17:00 in August, you choose from everyone who teaches that exact paper. Sessions use a shared whiteboard, a document camera so handwritten working is visible both ways, and the real past paper annotated live. They are recorded, which turns July into a revision archive the student still has in February. For a subject where a Cambridge answer differs from a Pearson one, that is not a close call.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session, and what should we send beforehand?
faqs.answer: Send three things: the statement of entry or exam timetable showing board and tier, the most recent report, and one piece of marked work. The first paid session is then a timed section of a past paper from the correct tier, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches, which produces an error log classified by topic and command term. That log, not the report card, is what the written plan is built from. The free trial lesson sits before all of this and is a real lesson with a real tutor, booked without card details.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.closingHeading: Book the July block before the calendar fills
dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.closingBody: Dubai summers are short and awkwardly shaped: nine weeks on paper, five once travel is subtracted, and the specialists for Extended Mathematics and Chemistry 0620 are committed by the middle of June. Send the syllabus codes, the June report and one marked script, and the free trial lesson can be sat the same week. You will get a written plan with a named output for each week, a timed diagnostic marked against the board's own mark scheme, and a one-page handover in late August that tells your child exactly what September needs to address. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, from wherever the family happens to be.

intro.heading: Two boards, one subject name, and the mistake that follows
paragraphs: A Dubai parent who asks for IGCSE Maths tuition has given a tutor roughly half the information needed. Cambridge International runs Mathematics as syllabus 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with its own paper structure and its own house style of question. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE Mathematics as specification 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with a different paper split and a different relationship between the formula sheet and the recall expected. Both appear on Dubai school reports as IGCSE Maths. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong one will teach correct mathematics and waste a term.

This happens more in Dubai than in most cities, for a structural reason. The emirate licenses 17 different curricula across its private schools, and British-curriculum provision is the largest single block by enrolment. Within that block, schools choose boards subject by subject. A single Year 11 can be entered for Cambridge sciences, Edexcel Mathematics and a Cambridge first-language English, and nothing on a termly report makes that obvious. The information lives on the options form and the exam entry letter.

So the first job of this page is to make the board map legible. The second is to translate it into the two decisions that follow: which tier to sit, and which subjects to count. Both have consequences well beyond the exam. Tiering sets a grade ceiling that sixth-form admissions read. Subject selection interacts with the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule, which on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and which excludes Arabic and Islamic education from that count.

The third job is to be clear about what tuition can and cannot do inside that structure. It can teach a specification properly. It can convert a score into a cause and attack the cause. It cannot change a tier the school has entered, it cannot promise a grade, and it cannot shortcut an equivalency process run by a ministry. Any service that suggests otherwise is selling something other than teaching.

IB Gram arranges this as one-to-one tuition delivered live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and scheduled around a Dubai school week. We do not operate home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India. The practical consequence for a family is that board specialism beats proximity: a Cambridge 0620 Chemistry teacher is matched to a household in Al Qusais on exactly the same terms as one in Jumeirah, because nobody is driving anywhere.

What follows is arranged as a reference rather than a pitch. There is a table comparing the two boards across the subjects Dubai schools enter most, a table separating the three different grade thresholds a family has to track, and a table setting out retake windows against the deadlines that govern them. Between them sit the sections on subject count, on arriving mid-course from another system, and on what a tutor may and may not do with a coursework component. If you read only one part, read the first section, because knowing which board your child is entered for changes every decision after it.
bullets: Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are both 'IGCSE Maths' and need different preparation
Dubai schools mix boards by subject; the entry letter is the authoritative document

dubai/igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: Three programme structures account for nearly every IGCSE entry in Dubai. They differ in how units are banked, when retakes are possible, and how much of the grade is decided on a single morning.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, linear entry
programmes.description: All papers in a subject sat in one series, with the grade decided across that set. Subjects carry four-digit codes and most sciences and mathematics are tiered Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available. Cambridge offers a June series and a November series, plus a March series in some regions, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres sit June as the main series, with November used chiefly for retakes and private candidates. Because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, the school's own published timetable is the only version a Dubai family should plan against.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, including modular routes
programmes.description: Identified by codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with Mathematics tiered Foundation and Higher. Several specifications are available in a modular structure, so units can be sat and banked across series rather than everything resting on one window. Exams run in May/June and November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Modularity is the practical argument for Edexcel in a transient city. A student arriving in Dubai mid-course, or one whose first attempt at a unit went badly, can bank a result and re-sit a component without re-sitting the subject. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is a real window for a Dubai Year 12 needing one grade lifted.

programmes.name: Mixed-board entry across one student's subject set
programmes.description: Not a programme the boards publish, but the arrangement many Dubai schools actually use: Cambridge for the separate sciences, Edexcel for Mathematics, and either board for English depending on the cohort. It is a reasonable choice by a school optimising for each department's strengths, and it creates a planning problem for the family because two sets of entry deadlines, two grading conventions and two timetables apply at once.
programmes.countryNote: The fix is administrative rather than academic: one page listing each subject, its board, its code, its tier and its series, taped inside a folder. Most of the avoidable chaos in a Dubai Year 11 comes from nobody having written that page down.

programmes.name: What IGCSE grades are for: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: Dubai sixth forms set subject-specific IGCSE bars, commonly a grade 6 or 7 in the same subject before A Level, with IB Diploma Higher Level pitched similarly. Those bars are published by the school rather than by the board, and they are the reason tiering matters: a capped grade can be a perfectly good result and still fall below an entry requirement.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More sixth-form capacity does not loosen subject bars; it widens the choice of where to meet them.

dubai/igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: The subject notes below are written around the board difference, because that is where Dubai families lose time. Each one names what changes between Cambridge and Pearson and what a tutoring hour should therefore be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier names differ and so do the papers. Cambridge Extended runs two papers with a heavier emphasis on structured multi-step questions; Edexcel Higher splits across two papers with its own formula provision. Working shown line by line earns method marks on both, and that single habit is worth more than any topic revision in either specification.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge tiers the subject and sets an Alternative to Practical paper; Edexcel's structure handles practical skills differently and weights its papers differently. Electromagnetic induction and circuit analysis are where marks go in both. A tutor should be able to say which paper carries what percentage before the first session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations with limiting reagents and percentage yield sit in the Extended and Higher content rather than the Core. The qualitative-analysis tables differ in presentation between boards, which trips students who revise from the wrong board's notes - a common failure in Dubai, where sibling sets often sit different boards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Very similar content, materially different question style. Cambridge rewards precision against its own syllabus statements; Edexcel asks more extended-response application. A student revising from the other board's past papers will meet unfamiliar phrasing in the exam and read it as unfamiliar content, which costs confidence as well as marks.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Both assess reading and directed writing, with mark tariffs attached to content points on the summary tasks. Cambridge 0500 and the Edexcel specification differ in text provision and coursework options, and some Dubai schools enter a coursework route while others do not. Timing discipline moves these grades faster than vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate specification with its own mark profile, entered by Dubai schools according to the cohort rather than the individual. Students moved from 0510 to 0500 part-way through a course - frequent in a city with this much school transfer - meet a reading paper that assumes practice they have not had, and that gap is the whole tutoring brief.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Data-response and case-study questions carry the marks on both boards. The standing loss is a correct definition applied to no particular firm. Evaluation marks need a judgement with a reason attached, which is a writing habit rather than knowledge, and it is teachable inside a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the quiet mark-earner: axes labelled, curves named, the shift shown and the new equilibrium marked. Students who can explain the economics verbally and draw it loosely lose marks they never notice losing. Gulf-relevant examples make the application marks easier to reach.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The written papers test pseudocode to the board's own convention, trace tables and data representation rather than coding fluency. A student fluent in Python will still drop marks writing pseudocode the wrong way. Dubai schools sometimes enter Computer Science and ICT with different boards, which changes the practical component entirely.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is necessary and insufficient. The top band requires the source or figure interrogated and a conclusion that answers the question set. Fieldwork and skills components differ between boards, so a tutor needs to know which paper your child sits before promising anything about preparation.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. IGCSE Arabic is a separate examination sitting alongside that requirement, and the two are regularly confused on a report.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.levels: Single tier, entered by a minority of schools
subjects.description: Calculus and series arriving two years early, taken by students heading for A Level Maths or Further Maths. This is the clearest case where the pool of tutors who have actually taught the specification is small in any one part of Dubai, and where matching over video rather than by neighbourhood is the only way to reach one.

dubai/igcse-tuition.regionsTitle: Where the families asking about IGCSE tuition in Dubai live
dubai/igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: These districts are listed because their school mix shapes which board questions come up, not because a tutor sits in any of them. Delivery is over video, so the match is made on the specification.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Muhaisnah
regions.note: A dense mixed-curriculum belt where British, Indian and Ministry-curriculum schools share the same streets. Households here frequently have children on two different boards at once, which is where the mixed-entry confusion is most acute.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Views
regions.note: Established villa communities feeding a small number of long-standing British-curriculum schools. Requests here cluster around tier decisions in Year 10 rather than emergency Year 11 work.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Short distances but severe single-road congestion at school-run times. Families here are unusually willing to schedule late evening sessions, which suits tutors working from other time zones.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Apartment districts with a high proportion of mid-year arrivals. Students joining a two-year IGCSE course in its second year are the typical case, and board familiarity rather than content is usually the gap.

regions.name: Town Square and Remraam
regions.note: Newer outlying communities where the school commute is the longest part of the day. Sessions realistically start after 6:30pm, and Friday morning blocks are more popular here than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: International City and Al Nahda
regions.note: Price-sensitive districts where the published market range for tutoring matters most. Families here ask about session length and frequency before they ask about tutor credentials, which is a reasonable order.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Schools and universities adjacent to each other, with households already comfortable with screen-based learning. Computer Science and ICT board differences come up here more than elsewhere.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mirdif
regions.note: Villa districts on the eastern edge, where the drive to a tutor in central Dubai was historically the deciding objection. Removing the journey changes the economics of weekly tuition entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Al Qusais and the eastern districts
schoolClusters.note: A long-established schooling belt with the widest board mix in the emirate. Students we support from these catchments most often arrive with a Cambridge science entry and an Edexcel mathematics entry, and no clear record of which is which.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living, Motor City and Sports City
schoolClusters.note: Villa and townhouse communities built around their schools, with settled cohorts and published sixth-form entry bars. Tier conversations in Year 10 dominate the requests from this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: High residential turnover and a steady flow of students joining courses part-way through. Board familiarity, past-paper style and mark-scheme convention are the recurring requests rather than new content.

dubai/igcse-tuition.modesIntro: Three session patterns cover the board-specific work families ask for. All of them run as live video lessons; none involves a tutor attending a UAE address.

modes.title: Specification-matched weekly tuition
modes.description: One or two fixed slots a week on a single named specification. The tutor works from the board's published syllabus and past papers for that code, not from a generic subject plan, and the session note records which syllabus statements were covered. This is the format for a student on a two-year course who wants the grade secured rather than rescued.
