modes.title: Board-transfer catch-up
modes.description: For students who have changed school, country or board mid-course - the single most common Dubai scenario. The work is a mapping exercise first: what the new specification contains that the old one did not, which topics are assessed differently, and which revision material the student now has to stop using.
bullets: Gap map between the two specifications, written down
Question-style retraining on the new board's past papers
Explicit list of old material to set aside
Realistic timeline, including when a series change is the better answer

modes.title: Retake and modular planning
modes.description: Where a single grade needs lifting for a sixth-form condition, the planning question comes before the teaching question: which series, which board, which components, and what the entry deadline is. Pearson's modular routes sometimes allow a component re-sit rather than a whole-subject repeat, and that distinction changes the workload completely.

Component-level rather than subject-level planning where the board allows it
Private-candidate entry route explained, with the centre's own rules checked
Honest assessment of whether the available weeks are enough

sections.heading: How to find out which board your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Three documents answer this, and the school report is the least reliable of them. The options form signed in Year 9 names the subjects but often not the board. The termly report usually says 'IGCSE Mathematics' and stops there. The document that settles it is the exam entry statement issued before final entries close, which lists each subject with its code, its tier and its series. Ask the exams officer for it by name; every Dubai centre produces one.

Failing that, the codes are recognisable on sight. Cambridge uses four digits: 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500, 0510, 0450, 0455, 0460, 0478. Pearson Edexcel uses a digit, two letters and a digit: 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1, 4BS1, 4EC1, 4GE1. If a textbook cover, a worksheet header or a past paper in your child's folder carries one of those strings, you have your answer for that subject - though not necessarily for the others, because mixing boards across a subject set is normal in this emirate.

It is worth doing this before you book anything. A tutor who is told 'IGCSE Physics, Year 11, Dubai' will prepare competently for whichever board they know best. A tutor told '0625 Extended, June series, mocks in February' will plan the term around the right papers. The difference between those two briefings is the difference between a useful term and a pleasant one, and it costs one email to the exams officer.

The same document resolves the tier question, which parents often do not realise has already been decided. Entries are made at a tier, and by the time the entry statement exists the school has committed. If you want that revisited, the conversation has to happen before the final entry deadline - for the Cambridge March 2027 series, for instance, final entries are due 27 November 2026, more than two months before the exam period opens on 3 February 2027.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: The two boards are not harder or easier than one another in any way a parent can act on, and anyone who tells you otherwise is guessing. What they are is different in structure: in how many papers a subject carries, in how tiering is named and handled, in how practical skills are assessed, and in whether components can be banked across series. Those differences change what a tutoring hour should contain.

The table below compares the subjects Dubai schools enter most. Read it as a planning document rather than a league table. The useful column is the last one, because it names the thing a tutor should be doing differently depending on which paper your child will open in the exam hall.

One structural difference deserves emphasis for Dubai specifically. Pearson's modular availability in some specifications means a unit can be sat, banked and re-sat without repeating the whole subject. In a city where families relocate mid-course and students arrive in Year 11 having done Year 10 somewhere else, that flexibility is worth real money. Cambridge's linear structure, by contrast, concentrates everything into one series, which is simpler to plan for and less forgiving of a bad fortnight.

The second difference worth a parent's attention is how practical skills reach the paper. Cambridge sets an Alternative to Practical paper in the tiered sciences, which assesses experimental method in writing: naming the independent and dependent variables, identifying controls, reading instruments, spotting anomalies and proposing improvements. That is a distinct skill with its own vocabulary, and it is taught explicitly or not at all. Pearson distributes practical assessment differently across its science papers. A tutor who has prepared students for one and not the other will teach the right science in the wrong register, and the marks will show it.

Tiering is the third. Cambridge's Core and Extended split applies across several subjects and caps the grade available at Core; Pearson tiers Mathematics as Foundation and Higher and runs most other International GCSE subjects at a single tier. A family comparing two children, or comparing a current report with an older sibling's, is often comparing a tiered entry with an untiered one and reading a difference in grades that reflects structure rather than ability.

sections.heading: Reading the grade: 9-1, A*-G and what a Dubai sixth form asks for
paragraphs: Two grading scales are in circulation and Dubai families see both. Several specifications report on a 9 to 1 numeric scale; others still report A* to G. A school may use one scale for some subjects and the other for the rest, depending on board and specification. Parents comparing a sibling's results from three years ago to a current report are frequently comparing two different scales without realising it.

What matters practically is the entry bar on the other side. Dubai sixth forms publish subject-specific IGCSE requirements - commonly a grade 6 or 7, or the equivalent letter, in the same subject before A Level, with IB Diploma Higher Level pitched similarly. Those bars are set by the school, not by the board, and they are the only figure that should drive a tiering decision. Ask for them in writing before Year 10 entries are finalised.

The third number in the picture is the Ministry of Education's equivalency threshold, which is far lower than people assume and serves a completely different purpose. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced rule says five.

So a student can clear equivalency comfortably and still miss a sixth-form entry bar by two grades. These are separate processes with separate purposes, and conflating them is how families end up either complacent or panicked for no reason. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry; verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel rather than through any tutoring service.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects, and which ones actually count
paragraphs: Dubai schools typically enter students for somewhere between seven and ten IGCSE subjects, and parents routinely ask whether more is better. For equivalency purposes the answer is no: the published rule counts five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and a sixth or seventh pass adds nothing to that specific test. For sixth-form admission the answer is also usually no, because the bars are subject-specific rather than cumulative.

Where subject count does matter is in risk and workload. A student carrying ten subjects into a June series is sitting more papers in a tighter window, with less revision time each. A student carrying seven has slack. Schools balance this against breadth and university narrative, and they are generally right, but a family looking at a struggling Year 11 should know that reducing the load is a legitimate conversation with the school rather than an admission of defeat.

The composition matters more than the count. A student intending A Level Economics needs strong mathematics regardless of whether they take IGCSE Economics. A student heading for IB Diploma Higher Level Chemistry needs the separate-science route rather than Combined Science in most sixth forms. These dependencies are published by the receiving school and are worth collecting a year before they bite.

One Dubai-specific wrinkle: the mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside the IGCSE set and consume timetable space. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. None of that reduces the IGCSE workload; it simply explains why the week is full.

sections.heading: Retakes, the November window and the private-candidate route
paragraphs: The retake conversation in Dubai usually starts in late August, after results, and by then some of the options have closed. Pearson's International GCSE November series runs from late October to 19 November in a typical year, and the entry deadline for it falls well before the autumn term is under way. Cambridge's November series and, where available, its March series work the same way: the decision point precedes the information that would have made the decision easy.

The practical answer is to agree the retake framework in advance, in June, while the exams are still being sat. If a sixth-form offer is conditional on a grade 6 in Mathematics, write down now what happens if a 5 arrives: which series, which board, whether the current school will enter the candidate, and what the fallback course is. Families who do that treat results day as administration. Families who do not spend August discovering that an entry deadline passed in July.

Where a school will not enter a former student, the private-candidate route exists and is used regularly in Dubai. It means finding a centre willing to accept external candidates, meeting that centre's own deadlines and fees, and accepting that some components - certain practical or coursework elements - may not be available to a private candidate at all. That last point is the one that catches people, and it is specification-specific, so check it against the board's own documentation before planning a subject.

Pearson's modular routes change the arithmetic where they apply, because a single unit can sometimes be re-sat and banked rather than the whole subject repeated. That can turn a four-month project into a six-week one. It is not available on every specification, so it is a question to ask rather than an assumption to make.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes the conversation
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. That is not the whole UAE picture, and it matters for families who move between emirates - a common enough event that the differences are worth knowing before they arrive.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae says plays a central role in supervising private schools in those three emirates. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits with the emirate regulator there.

For a tutoring decision, the regulator matters in two ways. First, the inspection report is a readable document and the subject-level judgements inside it are more useful than the headline band: a school rated strongly overall can have one weak IGCSE science department after a staffing change, which is exactly when outside subject support earns its place. Second, the regulator sets the mandatory-subject rules that shape the timetable your tuition has to fit into.

To be explicit about our own position: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. The regulators are named here to help you read your own school's paperwork.

sections.heading: Coming into IGCSE from another system mid-course
paragraphs: Dubai absorbs students from everywhere, and a large share of the IGCSE tuition requests we receive are transition problems wearing the costume of a subject problem. A student who has 'suddenly gone backwards in Chemistry' has often not gone backwards at all: they have met a different assessment convention and are answering a question that was not asked.

The commonest transitions have predictable gaps. From CBSE or ICSE into IGCSE, the content is usually ahead but the command-term discipline and the extended-response expectations are behind. From an American middle-school programme into Year 10 IGCSE, the opposite: comfort with projects and discussion, unfamiliarity with terminal written examinations and with the mark-tariff logic they run on. From the IB Middle Years Programme into IGCSE, strong inquiry habits and a shock at how specifically the syllabus statements are assessed.

The useful first session in any of these cases is a mapping exercise rather than a lesson. Which topics does the new specification assume? Which of the student's existing revision materials now belong in a drawer? Which question types have they genuinely never seen? Write that down, and the next eight weeks have a purpose. Skip it, and tuition becomes general practice at whatever the student happens to mention that week.

Timing changes the answer too. A transition arriving in Year 10 has room to rebuild habits. The same transition arriving in the second term of Year 11 is a triage problem, and the honest advice is sometimes to narrow the subject set with the school, or to plan for a November or March series, rather than to buy more hours into a window that cannot hold them.

sections.heading: What tuition may do with coursework, and what it must never do
paragraphs: Some IGCSE specifications carry coursework or controlled-assessment components, and Dubai schools differ in whether they enter them. Where they do, the component is assessed work and the rules around it are not soft. A tutor may explain the criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has already produced and point out where a criterion is not yet met. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final state, or develop the investigation on the student's behalf.

This boundary is worth stating bluntly because the Gulf tutoring market contains businesses that cross it openly. One site in this search landscape advertises finished Internal Assessments for sale. That is malpractice, it is detectable, and the penalty falls on the student rather than the vendor. A family paying for tuition should expect a tutor to refuse a request of that kind and to say why.

The practical defence is timing. Almost all pressure to cross the line comes from lateness: a deadline in five days and a blank document. Tuition that engages with a coursework component early - criteria read before drafting begins, method rehearsed before a write-up, feedback on a genuine first attempt - never arrives at that pressure point. Schools publish internal deadlines months before the board's, and those are the dates to work from.

We also do not distribute board material. Syllabuses, specimen papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge Assessment International Education and by Pearson, and they should be reached through cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Referencing and linking them is proper practice; handing them out as a download is not.

sections.heading: Getting started on the right specification
paragraphs: Begin by getting the entry statement from your child's school and writing one page: subject, board, code, tier, series. That page is the brief. With it, matching a tutor is straightforward and usually quick. Without it, the first two sessions are spent discovering what should have been known before booking.

Then take the free trial lesson, and use it to test specification literacy rather than rapport. Ask the tutor what the papers are worth on that code, where candidates typically lose marks on the specific paper your child will sit, and what they would attack first. A tutor who knows the specification answers in particulars. A tutor who knows only the subject answers in generalities, and generalities are exactly what the mark scheme does not reward.

Be prepared for an honest answer about coverage. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English, Business Studies and Economics are well covered on both boards at both tiers. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics and the less commonly entered languages are thinner, and in those cases we would rather name a short wait or recommend a different approach than put a willing generalist in front of a specification they have never taught.

On delivery there is no ambiguity to manage. These are live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. The trade is deliberate: the household gives up a tutor in the room and gets a tutor who has actually taught the specification on the entry form.

process.title: Get the entry statement
process.description: Ask your child's exams officer for the exam entry statement, which lists each subject with its code, tier and series. It is the only document that settles the board question, and it takes one email. Everything that follows is planned from it.

process.title: Specification-matched introduction
process.description: A free trial lesson with a tutor who has taught that specific code. It includes a short timed question from the correct board's past papers, so the first evidence comes from the right examination rather than a close relative of it.

process.title: Gap map, where a transition is involved
process.description: For students who changed board, school or system mid-course, the first substantive session is a mapping exercise: what the new specification assumes, which question types are unfamiliar, and which old revision material should be set aside.

process.title: Weekly sessions against the syllabus statements
process.description: One or two fixed slots a week, with session notes that reference the board's own syllabus wording rather than a generic topic list. That makes coverage auditable and stops the same ground being revisited by accident.

process.title: Series and deadline review each term
process.description: Entry deadlines, tier decisions and any retake framework are revisited termly, not in August. Cambridge final entries for a March series fall in the preceding November, and decisions taken late are decisions taken badly.

whyPoints.title: The board comes before the subject
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched against the specification code on the entry form. A Cambridge 0620 and an Edexcel 4CH1 student get different preparation, because they will open different papers.

whyPoints.title: Mixed-board entries are handled as normal
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools frequently enter Cambridge sciences alongside Edexcel mathematics. Planning around two sets of deadlines and conventions at once is the usual case here, not an exception we are surprised by.

whyPoints.title: Transitions are mapped, not guessed
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from CBSE, an American system or the IB Middle Years Programme get an explicit gap map first. It is cheaper than eight weeks of general practice and it shortens the catch-up considerably.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson timetables and deadlines are referenced from their own published sources, with the caution that Pearson revises provisional timetables and Cambridge timetables are zone-specific.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Dubai school entered Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for a subject?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the exam entry statement, which lists every subject with its code, tier and series. The termly report usually will not tell you, and the options form often does not either. Failing that, the codes are recognisable: Cambridge uses four digits such as 0580, 0620 and 0500, while Pearson Edexcel uses a digit, two letters and a digit, such as 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4EA1. Check each subject separately, because entering Cambridge sciences alongside an Edexcel mathematics entry is a normal arrangement in Dubai schools rather than an oddity.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE harder than Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Neither board is harder in any way a parent can act on, and claims to the contrary are usually marketing. They differ structurally: paper counts and splits, tier naming, how practical skills are assessed, how much recall the formula provision assumes, and whether components can be banked across series. Those differences change what preparation should contain, not how difficult the subject is. The practical risk is not board choice but board confusion - a student revising from the other board's past papers meets unfamiliar phrasing in the exam hall and interprets it as unfamiliar content.

faqs.question: Why do both my children sit IGCSE Maths but use completely different textbooks?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because they are on different specifications, either because they are at different schools or because a school changed board between cohorts. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are separate examinations with different paper structures and different tier names - Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. The textbooks are written to one specification each and are not interchangeable for past-paper practice. Keep the two sets of revision material physically separate, and check which code each child is entered for before buying anything else.

faqs.question: Can a tutor switch my child from the Core tier to the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: No. Tier is set by the school when entries are made, and no tutor has standing in that decision. What tuition can do is produce the evidence for a conversation with the head of department: marked papers showing whether the student can access extension questions, and how far the mark falls when the same questions are timed. That conversation has to happen before the final entry deadline. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, for example, final entries are due 27 November 2026, well before the exam period opening on 3 February 2027.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need to pass for a UAE certificate to be recognised?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which does not match the sourced rule. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process - check your own case through the Ministry's own channel rather than relying on any tutoring provider's summary, including this page.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count Arabic and Islamic Studies towards the five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published equivalency guidance for the British track states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That is a separate matter from KHDA's requirement that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum - the subjects are compulsory at school and simply do not count towards that particular equivalency total. Families often conflate the two rules, which leads them to believe a subject set is sufficient when it is one countable pass short.

faqs.question: My child is joining a Dubai school in the second year of an IGCSE course - what should the first tutoring session cover?
faqs.answer: A mapping exercise rather than a lesson. Which topics does the new specification assume have already been taught? Which question types has the student genuinely never seen? Which of their existing revision materials now belong in a drawer because they were written for another board or system? Writing that down turns the next eight weeks into a plan. Skipping it turns tuition into general practice on whatever the student happens to mention. Mid-course arrivals are among the most common situations in Dubai, and the gap is usually convention rather than content.

faqs.question: If results day goes badly in August, what retake options still exist?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, because the key deadlines precede results. Pearson's International GCSE November series ran from late October to 19 November 2026 in its final timetable, with entry closing well before the autumn term settles. Cambridge runs a November series and, in some regions, a March series - final entries for March 2027 are due 27 November 2026. The practical answer is to agree the retake framework in June, while exams are still being sat: which series, which board, which components, and whether the current school will enter the candidate.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE as a private candidate in Dubai rather than through their school?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is used regularly in the emirate, but with three caveats. You need a centre willing to accept external candidates, you work to that centre's own deadlines and fees rather than the board's headline dates, and some components may not be available to private candidates at all. That last point is specification-specific and is the one that catches people out, particularly in subjects with practical or coursework elements. Check it against the board's own documentation for the exact code before planning a subject around this route.

faqs.question: Which is better for a student who moves countries often, a linear or a modular specification?
faqs.answer: Modular, where it is available, for exactly that reason. Pearson offers several International GCSE specifications in a modular structure, so a unit can be sat and banked across series rather than everything resting on one window. For a family likely to relocate mid-course, that turns a potential repeat year into a component re-sit. Cambridge's linear structure concentrates a subject into one series, which is simpler to plan and less forgiving of a disrupted term. Modularity is not available on every specification, so treat it as a question for the school rather than an assumption.

faqs.question: What does KHDA actually require alongside my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. None of this reduces the IGCSE workload; it explains why the timetable is full.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a tutor to attend our home in Dubai for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. UAE tuition runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that works in your favour here is specification specialism: the person who has actually taught Cambridge 0478 Computer Science or Edexcel 4EC1 Economics may live nowhere near your community, and over video that stops mattering. You also keep the whole hour rather than losing thirty minutes each side to Dubai traffic.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Dubai legal, and should I be checking anything?
faqs.answer: It is legal and it is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure you see quoted has not been verified.

faqs.question: Should my child take the separate sciences or Combined Science for a Dubai sixth form?
faqs.answer: It depends on where they are going, and the receiving school publishes the answer. Most Dubai sixth forms expect the separate-science route before A Level or IB Diploma Higher Level in a science, and Combined Science or the double award is generally aimed at students heading for non-science options. Combined is not a lesser choice in itself - for a student taking humanities and economics at A Level it is efficient and sensible. The mistake is choosing it in Year 9 and discovering the Higher Level requirement in Year 12, so collect the entry bars in writing early.

faqs.question: How quickly can board-specific IGCSE tuition be arranged for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Where the subject is well covered - Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English, Business Studies, Economics - a match on the correct specification is normally possible within a few working days once you supply the code, tier and two workable time slots. Thinner specifications take longer: Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics and the less commonly entered languages have genuinely small pools of tutors who have taught the actual paper. In those cases we will give you a wait, a different session pattern, or a straight recommendation to look elsewhere, rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

dubai/igcse-tuition.closingBody: Before you book IGCSE tuition in Dubai, get the exam entry statement and write down five things for every subject: name, board, code, tier and series. That page answers most of the questions this article raised, and it turns a vague request for help into a brief a specialist can act on. Then take the free trial lesson and test whether the tutor knows the specification rather than merely the subject. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, planned around your child's school week and the board's own published deadlines.

Each works from your child's own paper, mark scheme and statement of entry rather than a generic revision plan.

intro.heading: Distance is a proxy for something else, and in Dubai it is a poor one
paragraphs: When a parent searches for IGCSE tuition near me in Dubai, the word doing the work is not 'near'. It is 'me'. Proximity is standing in for a set of entirely reasonable demands: I want to know who this person is, I want to know what happened in the hour I paid for, I want to see something my child has written and someone has marked, and I want to know whether any of it is changing the grade. A tutor three streets away appears to satisfy all four because you can open the door and look. That instinct is sound. The mechanism is weak.

It is weak for a specific Dubai reason. The emirate had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment. Those students are not distributed the way housing is. A family in Dubai Marina may have a child at a school in Al Barsha; a family in Mirdif may be running two children to two different boards. The pool of tutors who live within a twenty-minute drive of your villa and the pool of tutors who have taught Cambridge Physics 0625 Paper 4 to the standard your child needs are two different sets, and they overlap less than anybody wants them to.

The honest alternative is not to argue that online is more convenient. It is to replace the thing proximity was standing in for. If what you wanted was visibility, then visibility is the product: a written diagnosis after the first lesson that names components rather than topics, a session note for every hour that references the paper and the question numbers, marked work in your child's own handwriting kept as a dated folder, and a stated next step specific enough that you could tell six weeks later whether it failed. Those are artefacts. You can read them at the kitchen table. You cannot read a drive time.

This page is built around those artefacts. There is a table on what proximity is a proxy for and what actually answers each demand. There is a table on reading an IGCSE grade, because Dubai reports now carry two live scales - Cambridge IGCSE grades A* to G and Pearson International GCSE grades 9 to 1 - and parents comparing siblings across boards are frequently comparing nothing. There is a table on what a usable session note contains against a useless one. There is a table of the documents that actually govern your child's exams, most of which never reach the parent. And there is a term-by-term table of what should be in the folder by when.

A word on delivery, stated early because it changes how you read the rest. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is not a workaround. It is the reason the evidence exists at all: a shared screen can be recorded, a marked document can be filed, and a session note written against a visible paper is easier to produce than one written in a car on the way to the next appointment.

What follows is deliberately unglamorous. There are no promises about grades on this page, no satisfaction percentages and no star ratings, because none of those can be checked by the person reading them. There are documents, deadlines, grade scales, a regulator map and a permit rule, each with its source named. If you finish this page knowing which four pieces of paper to ask for and what a good one looks like, it has done its job, whether or not you ever book anything.

dubai/igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits at one point in a longer sequence, and what counts as evidence changes either side of it. The notes below describe each stage from the point of view of a Dubai parent trying to see what is happening, because the documents available to you are different in Year 9 than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 (Years 7-9)
programmes.description: The years before any external entry exists. Reporting is internal, there is no statement of entry, no mark scheme and no board, which means the only evidence a parent can hold is the school's own assessment and whatever a tutor produces. This is the stage where the habit of filing marked work either forms or does not, and the stage where parents most often accept a verbal progress update because nothing else is on offer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage is where board allocation is quietly decided. Schools choose Cambridge or Pearson entries subject by subject, and a Year 9 parent who asks which board each department intends to enter will get a clearer answer than a Year 11 parent asking the same question under deadline pressure. Ask early; it is written down somewhere and it costs nothing to see.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: Two years, external papers, and the first point at which real documents exist: a statement of entry listing syllabus codes and components, a zone-specific timetable, mark schemes published after each series, and a results statement. Grades arrive as A* to G from Cambridge or 9 to 1 from Pearson. This is where evidence-led tutoring is most measurable, because every claim can be checked against a marked paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Year 11 cohort is unusually mobile, with mid-year arrivals from several systems, so a child's own folder is often the only continuous record anybody has. Families who keep the diagnosis, the session notes and the marked papers in one place find that it survives a school change intact, which the school's internal data does not.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma and the sixteen-plus fork
programmes.description: After IGCSE a Dubai student usually moves to A Level or the IB Diploma, and the entry requirements are stated in IGCSE grades. The evidence accumulated in Years 10 and 11 therefore does something beyond reassurance: a sixth form admissions tutor reads grades, and a department deciding whether a borderline student can take Higher Level mathematics reads the papers behind them.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai sixth forms set their own IGCSE thresholds and those thresholds differ by subject and school, the useful question in Year 10 is not 'is my child doing well' but 'what grade does the course she wants in Year 12 actually require'. That number is published by the school and reframes every tutoring decision that follows.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: The federal process that converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers recognise. For the British track students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.
programmes.countryNote: This is the evidence trail that outlasts the tutoring, and almost nobody in this market mentions it. One competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, because equivalency is a regulatory process no tutoring provider performs on your behalf.

dubai/igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: Evidence looks different in each subject, because each is assessed by a different combination of components. The notes below say what a marked piece of work should show you per subject, which is more useful to a Dubai parent than a list of topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The cheapest subject to audit, because the marks are itemised. A properly marked paper shows method marks separated from accuracy marks, which immediately distinguishes a student who cannot do the maths from one who loses marks for unshown working. Ask for the mark breakdown by question, not the total; the total hides the diagnosis.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Evidence should show the practical and data-handling components separately from the recall questions. Dubai students commonly hold the content and lose marks on graph work, units and the six-mark extended responses. A marked paper that does not distinguish those three is not telling you anything you can act on.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Look for whether the loss is in moles calculations, in organic mechanisms or in the practical paper, because the three need entirely different session plans. A tutor who reports 'chemistry is improving' without naming which of the three has moved is describing a feeling rather than a result.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: The subject where command-term discipline shows up fastest in evidence. Describe, explain, compare and suggest earn different marks for different answers, and a marked paper annotated with the command term beside each loss is the single most useful artefact a biology tutor can produce for a Dubai parent.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Marked against assessment objectives rather than right answers, which makes evidence harder to read and more important to keep. Ask for two drafts of the same response with the objective named beside each piece of feedback; movement between those two drafts is the proof, not the final mark.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Where coursework exists, the evidence boundary matters most: a tutor may question, teach and comment on the student's own draft and may not supply text for it. Keep every draft dated. The sequence of drafts is both the proof of teaching and the proof of authorship.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Data-response and extended-writing marks behave differently and should be reported separately. Dubai students often perform well on definition and diagram marks and lose the evaluation marks entirely, which a total score conceals and a question-level breakdown exposes immediately.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole subject and the usual failure is generic answers that ignore the stimulus. Useful evidence is a marked answer with the case-study detail that should have been used highlighted in the margin. That is a two-minute annotation and almost nobody does it.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by a minority of Dubai students, usually alongside Extended Mathematics and usually with a sixth-form target already in mind. Evidence should be tied explicitly to that target: the grade the intended A Level or Higher Level course requires, and the distance to it, in marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory papers and practical assessment pull apart sharply, and a student can be comfortable in one and lost in the other. Ask which paper the marked work came from. A folder of theory questions tells you nothing about the practical component and vice versa.

dubai/igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: These notes are not about which tutors live where. They are about what each part of Dubai does to a weekday evening and therefore to the evidence a term can realistically produce, since a session that keeps getting moved produces no folder at all.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Early school finishes make a 4pm start workable, which is the slot most likely to survive a whole term. Families here often have a sixth-form target already named by the school, so the useful evidence is the gap in marks between the current paper and that threshold.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Later sessions, apartment living, and a high share of families who moved mid-year. The first artefact worth paying for here is a diagnosis that establishes which board and which tier the child is actually entered for, because a mid-year arrival's paperwork is frequently incomplete.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and Mudon
regions.note: Long bus runs mean many Year 11 students are not at a desk before 4.45pm. One sustainable weekly hour produces a better folder than two sessions that are repeatedly rescheduled, so the honest advice in these communities is to buy less and hold it.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Siblings across different schools and sometimes different boards. The grade-scale table on this page matters most to families here, because a 6 from one child and a B from another are not the comparison most parents assume they are making.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: A dense cluster of British-curriculum schools entering both Cambridge and Pearson papers. Because the same mock papers recur across the cluster, a tutor who has already marked that paper can produce a question-level diagnosis in the first session rather than the third.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Good supply at the lower price tiers thanks to the universities nearby, and therefore the part of Dubai where asking about the MoHRE private tuition work permit is most worth doing before any money changes hands.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartments, late finishes and frequent travel. Recorded or screen-shared sessions matter more to these households than to any other in the emirate, because a parent who is away on the Tuesday still wants to read what happened on the Tuesday.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Settled communities where a fixed weekly slot holds for the whole term, which is the condition under which an evidence folder actually accumulates. Twelve dated session notes and twelve marked pieces are a record; four are an anecdote.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: A concentration of British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge and Pearson papers side by side, often within one school. Families from this cluster usually arrive with mock papers already marked by the school, which shortens diagnosis to a single session and makes the first week's evidence unusually strong.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: A mixed belt where British, Indian and IB-continuum schools sit within a few kilometres. Households here frequently run two children on two grade scales, which is why the 9-to-1 against A*-to-G comparison is the question that comes up most often from this part of Dubai.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Marina, JLT and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: Apartment communities with a high rate of mid-year arrivals from other systems. The common first job here is establishing the documentary basics: which board, which tier, which components, and whether the student is entered as a school candidate or privately.

dubai/igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three shapes of support, each producing a different kind of record. Pick the one that matches what you need to be able to see, because the evidence a format produces is part of what you are buying.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with a written record
modes.description: One fixed hour a week across a term, with a session note after each and a marked piece of the student's own work every two or three sessions. This is the format that produces a folder: twelve dated notes and a trail of marked papers by the end of a term, which is enough to tell whether a grade moved and why. It suits Year 10 and the first half of Year 11.

modes.title: Marked-paper cycles before a series
modes.description: A concentrated run in the weeks before a mock or an exam series, built around whole papers sat under timed conditions and then marked question by question. The output is the most legible evidence available to a parent: a sequence of papers with marks per question and a visible pattern of which losses closed. It costs more per week and runs for fewer weeks.

modes.title: Diagnostic block for a new arrival
modes.description: A short defined block for a student who has just joined a Dubai school mid-year, where nobody yet knows which board, tier or component set applies. The work is documentary before it is academic: find the statement of entry, confirm the syllabus codes, establish the tier, then sit one paper to produce a baseline. It ends with a written baseline rather than a course.

sections.heading: What a search for IGCSE tuition near me is really asking
paragraphs: Four demands sit inside the word 'near', and none of them is actually about distance. The first is identity: who is this person and can I verify them. The second is accountability: what happened in the hour I paid for. The third is proof of work: show me something my child produced and someone marked. The fourth is movement: is the grade changing. Proximity feels like an answer to all four because you can look at the person, and looking has always been how parents checked things.

In Dubai the substitution breaks down in a specific way. Your child's school is frequently nowhere near your home, the board your child is entered for is decided by department rather than by postcode, and the tutor who has marked the exact paper your child is about to sit is unlikely to live in your community. The practical result is that a local search returns availability rather than fit. Availability is easy to buy and hard to notice you have bought.

The table below takes each of the four demands and separates what distance appears to deliver from what actually delivers it. Every item in the right-hand column is something you can ask for by name before you pay anyone, including us. Most of them cost nothing and none of them requires trusting a claim. If a provider cannot supply the artefact in the third column, that is information, and it is better to have it in week one than in week eleven.
bullets: Identity: ask for the permit position and a straight answer about who teaches the session
Accountability: ask what the session note contains before the first session, not after
Proof of work: ask to see a marked sample in another student's anonymised hand
Movement: agree the baseline paper and the review date in writing on day one

sections.heading: Reading an IGCSE grade on a Dubai report: A* to G against 9 to 1
paragraphs: Dubai schools enter both Cambridge IGCSE, which reports grades A* to G, and Pearson International GCSE, which reports grades 9 to 1. Both scales are current, both appear in the emirate, and a household with two children in two schools can easily be holding one of each. Parents comparing a 6 with a B, or deciding whether a 5 is a problem, are frequently comparing nothing at all. This is the most common unforced error in reading IGCSE evidence in Dubai, and it takes one table to fix.

The approximate alignment below is the one used across the sector for comparison purposes and it is useful for exactly that: comparing siblings, reading a sixth-form entry requirement written in the other scale, and judging how far a grade has to move. It is not a conversion rule set by any board, and no grade boundary should be inferred from it. Grade boundaries are set per series per syllabus and are published by the boards after each series; ask your child's school for the ones that applied to the paper in front of you.

What the table adds, and what no competitor page in this market provides, is the third and fourth columns: what each band is usually telling you about the student's work, and what typically moves it. A grade is a summary of a pattern, and the patterns are consistent enough to be useful. A student sitting at a C or a 4 across several subjects almost never has a knowledge problem in all of them; what they usually have is an exam-technique problem that presents identically everywhere.

sections.heading: The session note: the smallest artefact, and the one most often missing
paragraphs: If you buy one thing from this page, buy the session note. It is five lines, it takes a tutor four minutes, and it is the difference between a term you can audit and a term you have to take on trust. Most providers in this market do not produce one. Several produce something worse: a cheerful paragraph that names no paper, no question and no next step, which reads like accountability and functions as its opposite.

A usable note names the document the session worked from, the specific questions or components covered, what the student got wrong and why, what was set for next time, and the one thing a parent could usefully do. That last line is the one that gets dropped, and it is often the most valuable, because a Dubai parent who knows to check that a past paper was actually attempted under timed conditions can enforce something no tutor can enforce remotely.

The table below contrasts a usable entry with a useless one, field by field. Ask for the template before the first session rather than after the third. A provider who can show you an anonymised example has a system; a provider who says notes are sent 'as needed' does not, and the hours will not leave a record. This is also the test to apply to a tuition centre in your own neighbourhood, which is no more likely to produce a note than an online tutor and is often less likely, because the parent is physically present and the note feels redundant.

sections.heading: The four documents that actually govern your child's exams
paragraphs: Most of the paperwork that determines what your child sits never reaches the parent. It reaches the exams officer, and it sits in a drawer. Four documents matter, and all four are available to you by asking the school. Knowing they exist is most of the benefit; a parent who asks for a statement of entry by name is immediately a different kind of customer to both the school and any tutor.

The statement of entry is the important one. It lists the syllabus codes your child is actually entered for, the components within each, and the tier where tiering applies. Parents routinely discover from it that a child they believed was on Extended Mathematics is entered for Core, or that a science is being sat with a different board from the one the tutor assumed. Everything downstream of a wrong assumption here is wasted, including the tutoring.

The zone timetable is the one with the sharpest consequence. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is the board's own language. The practical instruction for a Dubai family is to get the timetable from the school's exams officer rather than from a search result, and to check it against the statement of entry rather than against a revision plan.

sections.heading: A Dubai Year 11 counted forwards, and what should be in the folder by when
paragraphs: Evidence accumulates on a calendar, and the calendar is set by the boards rather than by the tutor. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is why a plan written in January is already working inside decisions made the previous autumn.

The Cambridge March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of that gap: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Pearson's pattern is comparable: its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Because provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, the only safe practice is to work from the live official timetable your centre holds rather than from any date restated on a web page, including this one. The table below is therefore built around school events and evidence milestones rather than around board dates, so it stays usable whichever series your child is entered for. Check every date against the exams officer and the board's own published timetable.

sections.heading: Hours delivered against hours paid: the ledger nobody keeps
paragraphs: The least glamorous piece of evidence is an attendance ledger, and it is the one most likely to reveal a problem. Over a twelve-week term, a weekly slot should produce twelve sessions. In practice it produces nine or ten, because of travel, illness, school events and the two or three weeks where something else took priority. That gap is normal. What is not normal is nobody counting it, and then a parent wondering in April why a plan built on twenty-four hours delivered sixteen.

Keep the count yourself if nobody offers to. Date, duration, whether it ran, and if it did not, who cancelled and whether it was made up. Four columns in a notes app. The value appears at the six-week review: a term where seven of nine sessions ran and the grade did not move is a teaching problem, while a term where four of nine ran is a scheduling problem, and those two have completely different fixes. Most families diagnose the first when they are looking at the second.

This is also where a Dubai household's geography shows up in the data rather than in anecdote. Villa communities with long bus runs lose sessions to late arrivals; apartment households with two commutes lose them to the 7pm crush; travel-heavy families lose whole weeks. The fix is almost always to move the slot earlier or to Saturday morning rather than to buy more hours, and the ledger is what makes that obvious. Ramadan deserves its own line: agree before the month begins whether sessions move to late morning or after Iftar, and record the decision, because the alternative is losing four consecutive weeks by default.

sections.heading: Annotated drafts, and the point at which evidence of teaching must stop
paragraphs: Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework, the evidence a tutor produces and the evidence of authorship are the same documents, which makes the boundary a practical matter rather than a legal footnote. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires. A tutor may question a plan until the student can defend it. A tutor may comment on the student's own draft, name the assessment objective the comment relates to, and teach the student to self-assess against the criteria. A tutor may mark a practice piece.

A tutor may not supply any part of the assessed work: not a sentence, not a restructured paragraph handed back as a replacement, not a worked answer the student then submits. The distinction that matters in practice is between a comment and a rewrite. 'This paragraph asserts and does not evidence; find the quotation that supports it' is teaching. Handing back a paragraph with the quotation inserted is not, and the sequence of drafts in the folder will show which happened.

That is why dated drafts are worth keeping even when nothing is wrong. They are the student's own record of authorship, in their own hand, with the teaching visible beside it as comment rather than substitution. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum; buying that is not a shortcut, it is an academic malpractice exposure that sits with the student rather than with the seller. We do not sell assessed work at any price, and the draft trail is how a family demonstrates that nobody did.

sections.heading: After the grades: the evidence trail that outlasts the tuition
paragraphs: IGCSE grades do one more job after sixth-form placement, and it is the one nobody mentions on a tutoring page. For UAE recognition, the Ministry of Education runs an equivalency process, and for the British track the requirements are specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details inside that are worth holding on to. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which changes the arithmetic for a student carrying both as mandatory school subjects. And one page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the sourced requirement. Publishing the correct count is not a competitive flourish; it is the difference between a family planning around five subjects and a family planning around six.

No IB points threshold for equivalency appears in the source material available for this project, so none is published here, and no equivalency figure for the IB should be taken from a tutoring page. Equivalency is also not something any tutoring provider performs, guarantees or expedites. Describe it, verify it on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority, and keep the results statement filed. Tutoring is also not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and anybody implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

Verify directly - no figure published here

sections.heading: Who may legally teach your child privately in Dubai
paragraphs: Identity was the first demand hiding inside 'near me', and there is a documentary answer to it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody, including a provider using it as a scare tactic. Ask the question plainly and accept a plain answer. A tutor who holds the permit will say so; a tutor who does not should not be telling you the permit is optional, because it is not.

Two related points, because they are routinely blurred. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval first and annual renewal. That is a document about premises, and it is not something an online provider holds or should claim. Separately, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document; the practical reading is that your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to hire.
