sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, and how a Jumeirah 1 week is actually scheduled
paragraphs: Two practical matters to close on. The first is boundaries. Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or controlled assessment, and where they do, the work is assessed as the student's own. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, question a weak argument and show a student how to reference properly. A tutor may not supply text that becomes part of a submitted piece. The test is whether every word on the page was generated by the student, and this market contains operators who fail that test for money.

Nor should any tutoring provider claim regulatory approval it does not hold. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises; individual private tutoring runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no regulator's approval and does not describe itself as approved, licensed or accredited by one. Ask any provider who does to show the number.

The second matter is the week itself. A Jumeirah 1 family's realistic constraint is the afternoon: the school-gate congestion on Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road runs well past 15:00, and students living on Pearl Jumeira or coming back from inland schools arrive home later than the map suggests. Because lessons are delivered over video, a slot at 18:30 or 19:30 starts at that minute and does not depend on anybody completing a journey. The slot holds through school holidays, shifts for travel, and moves to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan rather than being cancelled.

If you are weighing areas as part of a school decision, the companion pages for Dubai Marina, JBR, JLT, Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows, The Lakes and The Greens cover the same ground for those catchments, and the Jumeirah 1 area page sets out the wider local picture.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the board and the syllabus code for each subject, and write them down. Students often do not know, and the two boards differ in ways that change revision entirely: Cambridge grades A* to G and Pearson grades 9 to 1, Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator paper from 2025 while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, and the sciences handle practical assessment differently. Some Dubai schools split by subject, entering Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics, so one answer for the whole timetable may not exist.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 1 need to teach the same board as the school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this matters more than distance. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry knows the practical component and the question styles that go with it; a tutor who has taught Pearson 4CH1 knows a different paper structure. Preparing a student against the wrong specification produces confident revision and a disappointing result. Because IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, the pool is selected on specification experience rather than on who can reach a Jumeirah 1 address, which is what makes board-specific matching possible at all.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between a Core and an Extended entry?
faqs.answer: The tier sets the highest grade available before the paper is sat. Core covers the shared core content with shorter, more structured papers and makes only the lower part of the grade scale reachable. Extended adds the extended content, runs longer papers with more multi-step questions, and makes the top grades available. The decision should be arithmetic rather than aspirational: a student who can attempt most of an Extended paper competently will usually score better there, while one still shaky on core content will hand in a script with blank spaces.

faqs.question: Which command words cost my child the most marks?
faqs.answer: Usually explain, evaluate and compare. Explain wants a causal chain with each link stated, and students write a description with the word because attached. Evaluate wants both sides plus a supported judgement, and students stop before the judgement, which is where the final marks sit. Compare wants both items addressed against the same criterion in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. The diagnostic habit that fixes all three is reading the mark allocation as an instruction about how many distinct scoring points to produce.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge non-calculator maths paper a real change for my child?
faqs.answer: It is, and it catches students who have had a calculator in hand since Year 7. From 2025, Cambridge 0580 candidates sit a non-calculator paper alongside the calculator one, which puts genuine weight on fraction work, indices, surds and mental estimation. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 candidates face the opposite pressure: a calculator on both papers raises the expectation of longer multi-step modelling questions. Either way, the first fortnight of useful tutoring is arithmetic fluency drills, which feels unglamorous and recovers marks faster than anything else available.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used so they actually teach something?
faqs.answer: Sit the questions under time with everything closed, then mark against the published scheme, then record the type of error rather than the topic, and only then go back and teach the gap. Marking before teaching is what makes the practice diagnostic. Most students do the reverse, work through a paper with the scheme open, feel broadly fine and learn nothing. Pair that with per-question timing practice, because running out of time is not a content problem and cannot be fixed by revising more content.

faqs.question: Can practical science skills be taught if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer depends on the component. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper tests reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, identifying variables and suggesting improvements, and all of that is paper work that transfers perfectly to a shared screen with real data sets. Where a laboratory practical test applies, the school's own practical programme is irreplaceable, and a tutor's job is to make sure the student can analyse and write up what they did. No tutor on video substitutes for a school laboratory.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects count towards UAE equivalency, and are Arabic and Islamic education included?
faqs.answer: The sourced rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited A Level subject at E or two AS Level subjects at E. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor page states that six subjects are needed, which does not match the published guidance. Check the current rule against the Ministry of Education's own material before acting on any version of it, including this one.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held, and how far ahead is the entry deadline?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and a March series used in some regions. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Always work from the live official timetable for your centre's zone, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones.

faqs.question: My child joined a Dubai school mid-year and the board changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Do a syllabus audit in the first fortnight, before anything else. A board change alters content coverage, tiering, grade scale and sometimes the practical component, and the topics taught in a different order elsewhere leave gaps that nobody has flagged. Map the new specification's content list against what your child has actually been taught, mark the unmatched items, and work through them in the order the new school's scheme of work will need them. Mid-year arrivals are common in Al Wasl and City Walk, and this audit is what makes the first term survivable.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if the exams are three months away?
faqs.answer: Not too late to matter, but the plan has to change. Three months is enough to fix technique, command-word discipline, timing and a short list of high-frequency topics, and that can move a grade. It is not enough to teach two years of missing content, and any provider implying otherwise is selling something. The first lessons should therefore be spent identifying the few topics that appear most often in the paper and are most recoverable, and then drilling them under timed conditions rather than attempting full syllabus coverage.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with IGCSE coursework or a controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, question reasoning that does not hold and show the student how to reference properly. A tutor may not supply text that becomes part of a submitted piece, or return a draft rewritten into a finished state. The test is whether every word on the page was generated by the student. Providers in this market do sell finished work, and a student who submits it risks a malpractice finding, so the boundary is worth stating to any tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Do you cover both tiers of maths, and can you help us decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the decision is settled with evidence rather than opinion. Two lessons with diagnostic questions drawn from both tiers show whether a student completes core-level questions reliably and can attempt harder ones, which is the real signal. We set out the grade range each tier makes available and the progression consequences for Year 12, then leave the entry decision to the family and the school, since the school submits it. We will not push a higher tier for its own sake.

faqs.question: How are the AED rates for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai set, and what do families pay?
faqs.answer: Published market figures as at October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300 an hour, with one provider advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 once travel is included, and specialist exam-year support at AED 200-450 and above. Budget online options are advertised from around AED 45. Those are other providers' published rates with their own dating, not an IB Gram price list; our arrangement begins with a free trial lesson at a time you choose, with no card taken.

intro.heading: The real question behind "does anyone near me know this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Families in The Views are usually one or two years into a British-curriculum school before they discover that "IGCSE" is not one qualification. It is a family of specifications issued by competing awarding bodies. Cambridge International runs its own suite, identified by four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSEs with codes like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. OxfordAQA runs a third suite. Two children in neighbouring apartments in Panorama or Turia can both be sitting IGCSE Maths next summer and be preparing for papers that differ in tier structure, calculator rules and grade range.

That is why the honest answer to "is there an IGCSE tutor near me" is a question back: which code does your child sit? A tutor who taught Cambridge Extended Mathematics for a decade is a strong match for a 0580 candidate and a weaker one for a Higher tier 4MA1 candidate until they have worked through that specification's own past papers. The mismatch rarely shows up in the first session, because the content overlaps heavily. It shows up in the mock, when the student meets a paper structured differently from the one they practised.

The supply problem follows from that. The Views is a compact community of apartment clusters overlooking the Emirates Golf Club fairways. Its secondary students travel out to schools in Emirates Hills, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and The Meadows, and between those schools you will find Cambridge centres, Pearson centres and some that enter candidates with both depending on the department. Finding a specification-matched specialist for Chemistry, Economics and Second Language English inside a twenty-minute radius, free at 7pm, is not a realistic expectation of any neighbourhood.

IB Gram answers it by removing distance from the equation. Every lesson for a UAE family runs live, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying that in the fourth paragraph rather than the fortieth is deliberate, because the alternative is a parent assuming someone is coming. What replaces the drive is a tutor chosen for the code on the statement of entry, with the past paper, the mark scheme and the student's own script on a shared screen.

The rest of this page is written to make you dangerous in a parents' evening. It shows how to read the specification code off your child's own documents, what Core and Extended and Foundation and Higher actually cap, where marks go on each paper type, how far ahead the entry deadline sits, what the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule really requires, and what the Dubai market charges for an IGCSE hour in dirhams, with each figure attributed to whoever published it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects The Views families ask for most, with the code in each of the two main suites and the part of the course where marks go missing. Sessions are built from your child's own marked scripts against the published mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The current 0580 assessment design separates a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper, which catches out students who have practised everything with a handheld. Pearson 4MA1 sits two papers of equal weight. Most lost marks are arithmetic fluency, incomplete working on method marks, and algebraic manipulation that was never secured in Year 9.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 candidates sit either a practical test or a written alternative to practical, and the alternative is a technique in its own right: reading apparatus diagrams, spotting control variables, and explaining a method without having performed it. Electricity and the equations of motion are where most students in this catchment lose marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are the recurring failures. The practical or alternative-to-practical component asks for precise observation language, not general description. Students who can recite the reactivity series still drop marks explaining why a particular displacement happens.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A terminology subject that punishes approximation. Marks are lost on command terms, on describing where an explanation was asked for, and on data questions where a trend is stated without reference to the figures. Work usually starts by annotating the student's own script against the published mark scheme wording.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of an unseen passage reward structure over style. Strong talkers underperform because they narrate instead of analysing, and because they do not budget the time the paper actually gives them. Sessions drill a repeatable reading method and a timed writing plan.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A large entry across Dubai schools and a different skill set from First Language English. Listening and speaking components carry real weight, and the written tasks are assessed against format conventions as much as language. The commonest avoidable loss is ignoring the register and audience the task specifies.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the mark. Unlabelled axes, shifts drawn in the wrong direction and evaluation paragraphs that repeat the analysis account for most dropped marks. The data-response question rewards students who quote the figures given rather than recalling general theory.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Easy to learn and hard to apply under timed conditions. Students lose marks by describing a business tool rather than applying it to the case study in front of them, and by skipping the justification that higher-tariff questions require. Case-study drill with a stopwatch moves grades faster than more content.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB Higher Level course, and often taught in a thin slot alongside the main maths option. Calculus and trigonometric identities are where the course gets steep. A tutor here is usually filling the time the school timetable could not give the subject.

Schools must also ensure teachers of these subjects hold the appropriate KHDA approval, which is worth knowing when comparing in-school and private provision.

sections.heading: How to read your child's specification code in five minutes
paragraphs: Before buying a single hour, establish what your child is actually sitting. There are four reliable places to look. The statement of entry the school issues before each series lists the awarding body, the syllabus or specification code and the component numbers. A school report or subject handbook usually prints the code next to the subject name. The department head will confirm it in one email. And the student's own past-paper practice carries the code in the header, which is often the fastest route of all.

Once you have the code, the awarding body's own site gives you the rest free of charge. Cambridge publishes the full syllabus for each four-digit number, including the assessment structure, the component weightings and which papers a Core or Extended candidate sits. Pearson does the same for its International GCSE specifications. Nothing on this page should be taken in preference to those documents for your child's own exam year, because specifications are revised and a structure that applied two years ago may not apply now.

The table below lines up the two main suites side by side for the subjects this catchment takes most. Its purpose is not to say which body is better. It is to show you that the difference is real, so that a tutor who shrugs when you say 4MA1 can be ruled out in the first minute of a conversation. If a provider cannot name the code they have taught, the specialism being sold is generic.

One practical warning about Cambridge timetables. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Dubai schools know their zone. Parents planning revision from a timetable found through a search engine sometimes do not, and that is an avoidable way to lose a paper.

sections.heading: Tiering: the grade ceiling that is set before revision starts
paragraphs: Tiering is the single most consequential decision in an IGCSE year and the one parents in The Views are least often shown the arithmetic for. In tiered Cambridge subjects, a Core entry sits different papers from an Extended entry and cannot reach the top grades. In Pearson Mathematics A, a Foundation entry has a numerical ceiling and a Higher entry has a floor below which no grade is awarded except a narrow allowance. The entry is made months before the exam, and once it is made the ceiling is fixed regardless of how well the student then works.

Schools make the tier decision on evidence, usually a Year 10 mock and classwork. The decision is not arbitrary and it is not an insult. A student entered Extended who cannot complete the harder paper will score poorly on it and may finish below where a confident Core performance would have landed them. The error runs both ways, though, and the one that causes lasting damage is the capped entry made because a student had a bad term in Year 10 rather than because the ceiling is genuinely right for them.

This is where a specification-matched tutor earns the fee rather than by teaching extra content. The useful work is to find out, by the autumn of Year 10, which tier the evidence supports, and then either secure the higher tier in time for the entry deadline or make the capped entry deliberately rather than by default. That requires someone who can mark a script against the right mark scheme and say what the ceiling realistically is. It cannot be done in March of Year 11.

Ask the school two questions in writing. Which tier is my child currently projected for, and what evidence is that based on. And when is the entry deadline, after which the decision cannot change. Those two answers reframe the whole tutoring question, because they convert a vague worry about grades into a dated decision with a measurable target.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: Marks are not lost evenly across a specification. They cluster in a handful of predictable places, and a tutor who knows the paper can name them before meeting the student. In mathematics, the losses are arithmetic fluency on the non-calculator paper, method marks forfeited because working was not shown, and algebra that was never secure in Year 9 reappearing inside a trigonometry or a functions question. None of those is fixed by covering more topics.

In the sciences, the single largest avoidable loss is the practical component. A Cambridge 0625 or 0620 candidate sitting the written alternative to practical is being assessed on experimental reasoning without a bench: reading an apparatus diagram, identifying the control variable, explaining why a step was done in that order, and judging the reliability of someone else's data. Students who are good at the theory frequently treat this paper as an afterthought and lose a block of marks on skills nobody taught them explicitly.

In the essay and data subjects the loss is command terms. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate and justify ask for structurally different answers, and the mark scheme awards accordingly. A student who writes an excellent description where an explanation was required has produced good prose and few marks. This is diagnosable in twenty minutes from a marked script, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

The fourth cluster is timing. Most IGCSE papers are generous in content and tight in minutes, and a student who answers the first third beautifully and the last third in a rush has a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem. Timed practice with a real clock, marked against the real scheme, exposes it immediately. Doing it under a tutor's eye is worth more than doing it alone, because the student cannot see where their own minutes went.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: Parents routinely discover the entry calendar after it has closed. Awarding bodies need entries, forecast grades and component choices long before candidates sit anything, and the school's own internal deadline runs earlier still. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series illustrate the gap precisely: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry closed more than two months before the first paper.

Pearson's pattern is similar in shape. Pearson offers International GCSE exams in May or June and in November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the live PDF on the awarding body's site, rather than a date restated on a tutoring page, is the only safe thing to plan against.

What this means operationally is that the useful tutoring conversation happens in the term before the entry, not in the term before the exam. Tier decisions, whether to add or drop a subject, whether to sit a subject in November rather than June, and whether a private-candidate entry is needed, are all live questions at the entry deadline and dead questions afterwards. A family that knows the date can act; a family that does not simply inherits whatever the default was.

Three dates belong on the fridge. The school's internal entry deadline, which comes first. The awarding body's final entry deadline. And the results date for the series, because an enquiry about results or a remark has its own short window after it. Ask the examinations officer for all three in writing at the start of Year 11.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: what MoE equivalency actually requires
paragraphs: This is the gap in the market that costs families real money in misplaced effort, because one page ranking for these searches publishes the wrong number. Gulf Today's report on the UAE's clarified equivalency requirements states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion. The same report states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student carrying seven IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has five counting subjects only if the other five all clear the threshold. That is a planning fact worth knowing in Year 9, when subject options are chosen, rather than in the summer after results when the certificate is being submitted for attestation.

For the American track the same report gives a different test: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is stated in that article, and none should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one. Anything about IB equivalency has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the attestation authority directly.

Two boundaries matter here. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry of Education and the relevant authority run, not something a tutoring platform performs or can promise. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. What a tutor can legitimately do is help a student clear a grade threshold in a counting subject, which is a teaching job with a measurable target.

sections.heading: Why a code-matched specialist beats a nearby generalist
paragraphs: Put the two options side by side honestly. A generalist within a twenty-minute drive of The Views offers continuity, the ability to read the room, and a parent who can see the lesson happening. Those are real advantages and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. What the generalist typically cannot offer is familiarity with the specific paper: the way 0580 splits calculator and non-calculator work, the way an alternative-to-practical question is marked, the exact phrase a mark scheme wants for an explanation mark in 0610.

The specialist's advantage compounds over a two-year course. Knowing the paper changes what gets practised, which changes the mock, which changes the tier decision, which changes the grade ceiling. It also changes how quickly a problem is identified: a tutor who has marked a hundred scripts against the same scheme sees in one page what a generalist might take three sessions to find. Over a Year 10 and Year 11 that difference is worth considerably more than the drive time saved.

Online delivery is what makes the specialist option available at all to a community this size. It also brings its own practical gains inside the hour: the student's own marked script, the official specification page and the past paper open side by side, annotated live and saved for later. Nothing is photographed and emailed afterwards, and the student keeps their own calculator and their own notes, which are the ones they will take into the hall.

The honest conditions for online to work are the same three every time. A stable connection, a door that closes, and a laptop rather than a phone. In an apartment with siblings and a shared table, the third is the one that fails. Solve it before the first lesson. And for the sciences, be clear about what online cannot replace: the school's laboratory. A tutor can teach experimental reasoning and the alternative-to-practical paper thoroughly, but bench time belongs to the school.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE hour costs in Dubai, and what it should include
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages competing for IGCSE searches in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. The figures below are AED market rates drawn from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, each attributed. They are not an IB Gram price list. Our position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted rate once the specification, the tier and the target are known, because an hour of Higher tier 4MA1 technique is a different product from an hour of Year 8 support.

What should the hour include at each band? At the budget end, content re-explained competently by someone who knows the material. That is fair value for a Year 8 or 9 student who missed a topic and poor value for a Year 11 candidate three months from a paper. At the qualified band, syllabus-aware teaching and marking. At the specialist band, assessment technique against the published criteria, with the tier conversation included. The premium band is bought mainly in the final weeks, and what it buys is judgement about what to leave out.

The money that gets wasted in this catchment usually goes the same three ways. Hours bought before anyone looked at a marked script, so the first sessions are spent on diagnosis. Group classes bought for a tiered subject, where the whole point of the hour is that the questions are the student's own. And a long weekly commitment started in Year 10 that has burned out by the spring of Year 11, exactly when the mock evidence and the tier decision needed attention.

Ask three questions before paying anyone. Which specification code have you taught, and for how many series. What will the first session produce in writing. And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which u.ae records as introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The permit costs nothing, so there is no honest expense-based reason not to hold one.

sections.heading: Private candidates, retakes and sitting in November
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE candidate in Dubai sits through their own school. Students who have moved mid-course, who want a subject their school does not offer, who are retaking a single paper, or who are being educated outside a school roll, enter as private candidates through a centre that accepts them. That is a logistical process with its own deadlines, and it sits with the centre and the awarding body rather than with a tutor. What matters here is knowing that it exists and that it has dates.

The November series is the quiet tool most families never consider. Both main bodies run two series a year, so a subject that went wrong in the summer can often be re-sat a few months later rather than waiting a full year, and a crowded subject load can sometimes be split across two sittings. Whether that is sensible depends on the subject, the school's policy and the student's wider timetable, and the honest answer is sometimes no. But it is a conversation worth having before the entry deadline rather than after results day.

Retakes need a clear-eyed diagnosis to be worth the fee. A grade that missed by a narrow margin because of timing or one weak paper is a good retake candidate. A grade that reflects a genuine content gap across the whole specification needs a longer run of teaching, not a second attempt in ten weeks. The way to tell the difference is to read the component breakdown rather than the overall grade, and that breakdown is available to the school.

For any of these routes the first call is the school's examinations officer, then the awarding body's own guidance for private candidates. IB Gram arranges teaching and nothing else: we do not register candidates, run a centre, or administer entries, and we hold no awarding-body centre status. Being clear about that is more useful than implying a capability, because the family that needs an entry made needs to be talking to a centre today rather than next month.

process.title: Send the specification code
process.description: The awarding body and the code from the statement of entry, report or past-paper header: 0580, 4MA1, 0625, 4CH1. One line of information removes most of the guesswork from the match, and it is the first thing a genuine specialist will ask you for rather than something they shrug at.

process.title: Send one marked script and the current tier
process.description: A marked mock or test tells us whether the gap is content, technique, timing or tier. Pair it with what the school currently projects, and the first session can start on the actual problem rather than spending an hour discovering it at your expense.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: A live one-to-one lesson at the hour you can hold, with the tutor you would keep, on the real topic and the real paper. You watch the teaching and the shared screen; we find out whether the match is right. Nothing is paid before that lesson has happened.

process.title: Work backwards from the entry deadline
process.description: Fix the weekly slot, then write the three dates on the plan: the school's internal entry deadline, the awarding body's final entry date, and the results date. Decisions about tier, subject count and series are live before those dates and closed afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different tiers and different calculator rules. Matching on the specification rather than on driving distance from The Views is what makes a genuine subject specialist available at an hour your family can actually hold.

whyPoints.title: Tier decisions treated as a dated decision
whyPoints.description: A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade before revision starts, and the entry closes months ahead of the exam. We look at the evidence early enough for the decision to be made deliberately, and we tell you plainly when the ceiling is the right call.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Knowing this before the first booking is worth more than a search phrase that implies otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Dates and rules from the primary source
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines come from Cambridge and Pearson, equivalency rules from the Ministry of Education and the attestation authority, permit rules from MoHRE and u.ae. We cite and link rather than restate, because a date retyped on a tutoring page is a date that can go stale.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent matching platform. It holds no KHDA training-institute permit, no awarding-body centre status and no regulator endorsement. Those bodies are named on this page to explain what they do, which is a different thing from borrowing their authority.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE specification my child's school actually enters?
faqs.answer: Four places give you the answer within minutes. The statement of entry the school issues before each series names the awarding body, the syllabus code and the components. School reports and subject handbooks usually print the code beside the subject. The department head will confirm it by email. And your child's own past-paper practice carries the code in the header. Once you have it, the full specification is free on the awarding body's own site, which is the document to plan from for your child's exam year rather than anything restated elsewhere.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in The Views who knows the exact paper?
faqs.answer: Within a twenty-minute drive, not reliably across every subject. The Views is a compact cluster of apartment towers, and a specification-matched specialist for Chemistry, Economics and Second Language English who is also free at 7pm is not something a community of this size contains. IB Gram solves it by matching on the code and delivering lessons live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What is the practical difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are separate specifications with separate papers. Cambridge 0580 uses Core and Extended tiering and its current design separates a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiering with two equally weighted papers and a numerical grade scale. Content overlaps heavily, which is why a mismatch does not show up in early sessions, but paper structure, tier language and calculator rules differ. Check the current specification on the awarding body's site for your child's exam year before planning any revision.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation entry cap the grade my child can be awarded?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the point of tiering. A Cambridge Core entry sits different papers from an Extended entry and cannot reach the top grades. A Pearson Foundation entry in Mathematics A has a numerical ceiling. The entry is made months before the paper and cannot be changed afterwards, so the decision deserves evidence rather than a default. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is projected for, what evidence supports it, and when the entry deadline falls, then work from those two answers.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly have a maths paper without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Because the current Cambridge 0580 assessment design separates non-calculator work from calculator work, so arithmetic and algebraic fluency are examined in their own right. Students who practised every topic with a handheld meet that paper cold and lose marks on operations they can do but have not done unaided for years. The fix is short, regular, unaided practice rather than more topics. Confirm the exact paper structure for your child's exam year on the Cambridge syllabus page, because specifications are revised between cohorts.

faqs.question: Can my child sit subjects with two different awarding bodies at once?
faqs.answer: In practice, yes, and it happens routinely in Dubai schools where departments choose independently. A student might sit Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics in the same series. It is the school's entry decision rather than the family's, and it has a consequence worth knowing: the student is preparing for two different mark-scheme cultures at the same time. A tutor should be told both codes rather than being left to assume one body covers the whole timetable.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the exam do IGCSE entries close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the school's internal deadline comes earlier still. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson follows a similar shape and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. Ask your examinations officer for the school's internal date, the awarding body's final date and the results date, in writing, at the start of Year 11.

faqs.question: How is the science practical assessed if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The assessment itself happens through the school. Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or a written alternative to practical, and the alternative is examined on experimental reasoning rather than bench skill: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying control variables, explaining why a step was ordered that way, judging the reliability of supplied data. All of that can be taught thoroughly over a shared screen using past papers and mark schemes. What cannot be replaced remotely is laboratory time, and that belongs with the school.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE actually count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. Gulf Today's report on the clarified requirements states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One page ranking in this market publishes six, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before relying on it, because this is a regulatory process rather than something a tutor administers.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects in The Views?
faqs.answer: No. The same report states plainly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That has a real planning consequence: a student holding seven IGCSEs, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, only meets the requirement if the remaining five all clear the threshold. It is a Year 9 options conversation rather than a results-day discovery. Dubai schools must still teach these subjects under KHDA rules regardless of the licensed curriculum, so they will be on the timetable either way.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in this catchment struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at the tier boundary, the science practical and alternative-to-practical papers, and Second Language English where the task format carries as much weight as the language. In mathematics the problem is usually Year 9 algebra resurfacing inside later topics. In the sciences it is a paper nobody taught explicitly. In English it is ignoring the register and audience the task specifies. All three are visible from one marked script, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start?
faqs.answer: Year 10, by a wide margin, because that is when the tier decision is still open and the entry deadline has not passed. A Year 10 start means no topic is met for the first time under exam pressure and the tier is chosen on evidence. Year 11 is still worth doing, but the work changes: it becomes paper technique, timing and triage built from marked mocks rather than a build through the specification. A single-subject rescue after a bad mock is a legitimate and common reason to start late.

faqs.question: What should a tutor know about my child's school before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. The awarding body and specification code for each subject. The tier the school currently projects. The internal assessment and mock calendar, because a session three weeks before a mock should look different from one in October. And the Cambridge administrative zone if the school is a Cambridge centre, since Cambridge states that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE hour in Dubai cost, and what should it include?
faqs.answer: Market rates published by providers and in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table run roughly AED 45-150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200-450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist, and AED 500-650 at the premium end, with in-home visits quoted at AED 180-500. Those are the market's numbers, not ours. At the specialist band the hour should include marking against the published scheme and an explicit view on tier. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, once the code and target are known.

faqs.question: Can my child retake one paper in the November series?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because both main awarding bodies run two series a year, which makes a re-sit a few months later possible rather than a full year's wait. Whether it is sensible depends on why the grade fell short. A near miss caused by timing or one weak component is a reasonable retake; a gap running across the whole specification needs teaching rather than a second attempt in ten weeks. Read the component breakdown with the school, and talk to the examinations officer about entry routes early.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.closingHeading: Send the code, then the script
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.closingBody: The fastest way to get a useful answer for a student in The Views is to send two things: the awarding body and specification code your child sits, and one recent marked script. Those two items tell us more than a half-hour conversation, because together they show the paper and the problem. We will match a tutor to that specification, put a free trial lesson at an hour the Emirates Living school run leaves free, and tell you honestly if the specialist your child needs is not available at that hour. Lessons run live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. Entry deadlines, equivalency rules and permit requirements come from Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE, and we will point you at the source rather than restate it.

intro.heading: The subject list is the decision, and it is made in Year 9
paragraphs: A Dubai family searching for IGCSE tutors is almost always searching too late in the process to fix the thing that matters most. By the time a tutor is being looked for, the subject list is set, the awarding organisation is set, and in several subjects the tier is set as well. Those three facts decide what grades are available and which post-16 routes remain open, and together they do more to shape an outcome than any amount of weekly teaching.

This is not a counsel of despair. It is an argument for a specific kind of tutor. A general tutor will teach the subject. A specialist will ask which syllabus code, check whether the tier entry matches what the student can hold, and look at whether the combination on the timetable supports what the student says they want to do at sixteen. Those three questions take ten minutes and they occasionally change the entire plan from teaching to an urgent conversation with the school.

Codes are the practical mechanism. Cambridge subjects carry a four-digit number: Mathematics is 0580 but International Mathematics is 0607, Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, while Combined Science is 0653 and Coordinated Sciences is 0654. Pearson codes begin with a four: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Further Pure 4PM1, Physics 4PH1, English Language A 4EA1. These are not interchangeable. The papers differ, the specimen material differs, and a tutor working from the wrong set is wasting a family's money at a perfectly respectable hourly rate.

Three places in a Dubai timetable repay attention before anything else. The science route is the first: a student can sit three separate sciences for three grades, a double award for two, or a single combined award for one, and the lighter routes do not cover everything some post-16 science courses assume. The maths route is the second, because Additional Mathematics and Further Pure exist for students heading towards A Level Mathematics and are not on every timetable. The third is English, where the specific code determines whether a speaking component counts into the grade or is reported separately.

Grading adds a layer of confusion that is nobody's fault. Cambridge reports IGCSE results on the A* to G scale internationally. Pearson reports International GCSE results on the 9 to 1 scale. A Dubai student taking subjects from both boards can finish Year 11 holding one certificate in letters and another in numbers, with no official conversion a parent should rely on for comparison. Ask the school which scale applies to which subject, and get the answer in writing before anyone starts comparing siblings.

Finally, the number of subjects. Dubai students commonly sit eight to ten. The UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency route on the British track counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and excludes Arabic and Islamic education from those five. One ranking competitor in this market publishes six as the requirement, which does not match the published rule. Knowing the real number changes how a family thinks about a weak tenth subject. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every lesson here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-tutors.programmesIntro: Dubai secondaries run international GCSEs from two main awarding organisations, sometimes alongside O Level in particular subjects. What a family needs from this section is the mechanism for finding out which one applies to their child.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes, several subjects tiered into Core and Extended with different papers and different available grades, and sciences offering either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Results are reported on the A* to G scale internationally. The widest subject catalogue of the two boards, including Global Perspectives and a large modern-languages range.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your Dubai school which zone it sits in before planning around any published timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes begin with a 4. Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher; most other subjects are untiered, so a single paper set serves the whole ability range. Results are reported on the 9 to 1 scale. Several subjects offer a coursework route as an alternative to a second written paper, which is a genuine planning difference rather than a detail.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May or June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so work from the live official document.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Offered in a narrower set of subjects and still used by some schools with a long-established pathway. Paper structures and assessment arrangements differ from the IGCSE version of the same subject, so matching a tutor on the subject name alone produces a tutor working from the wrong documents.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school enters candidates for O Level in a subject, ask for the specific syllabus code in writing. It is common for a family to assume IGCSE throughout and discover one O Level entry on the statement of results, by which point the teaching year is over.

dubai/igcse-tutors.subjectsIntro: What follows is the Dubai IGCSE roster as schools here actually run it, with the codes that decide which papers a student sits. Match a tutor to the code, not to the subject name; the difference is the difference between the right specimen papers and the wrong ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Core sits on Papers 1 and 3, Extended on Papers 2 and 4, with different available grades. The commonest losses are unshown method, premature rounding, and questions that require turning a sentence into an equation before any arithmetic can begin.

subjects.name: International Mathematics
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580, not a variant of it. It requires a graphics calculator and includes an investigation component. Confirm the current paper structure in the syllabus document, and confirm that any tutor has taught 0607 specifically rather than assuming it is 0580 with a calculator.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Assumes the Extended content of the main maths syllabus and is taken by students heading towards A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities carry the heaviest losses. A thin specialist market in this emirate.

subjects.name: Mathematics A and Further Pure
subjects.description: 4MA1 is tiered, which catches families out because most other Pearson subjects are not. 4PM1 Further Pure is the Pearson parallel to Additional Mathematics and is equally scarce in terms of available specialists in Dubai.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the quantitative questions carry the heaviest losses, with unit handling and formula rearrangement behind a surprising proportion of them. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the two need different preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry in that order of difficulty for most Dubai candidates. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards precision about apparatus and about what an observation does and does not demonstrate, which is teachable and routinely untaught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, and the subject where students most often mistake familiarity for knowledge. Extended-response questions on transport, respiration and genetics reward sequencing and command-word precision far more than volume of recall.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0654 double award · 0653 single award · Pearson 4SD0
subjects.description: 0654 and 4SD0 yield two grades covering all three sciences; 0653 yields one. Sensible choices for many students and a constraint for a few, because certain post-16 science courses assume separate-science content. Check before Year 10 rather than after results.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing rather than literature. Cambridge 0500 sets a reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper. Marks go missing when candidates summarise instead of selecting, and when register and audience are ignored in the writing task.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Two codes for one subject, and the difference matters. 0510 carries a speaking endorsement reported separately from the grade; 0511 counts the speaking component into the grade. Establish which one the school has entered before planning any speaking preparation.

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.description: Set-text work where essays rise or fall on quotation integration and on answering the question asked rather than the one revised for. The subject most improved by a tutor who marks writing weekly rather than discussing the text.

subjects.name: Business Studies, Economics and Accounting
subjects.description: Application and evaluation carry the marks. Candidates who define terms accurately and then fail to apply them to the stimulus material plateau in the middle bands no matter how much content they hold. Accounting is more thinly supplied than Business Studies.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two separate subjects regularly confused at the point of booking. Computer Science is algorithmic and includes pseudocode and problem decomposition. ICT is applied and software-based. Matching to the wrong one wastes an entire block of sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic, Geography and History
subjects.description: Arabic as a first language, 0508, and Arabic as a foreign language, 0544, are separate syllabuses with separate codes and separate teaching populations. Geography and History both reward case-study specificity, which is the first thing thin revision notes remove.

dubai/igcse-tutors.regionsTitle: Dubai districts and the subject mixes they actually generate
dubai/igcse-tutors.regionsIntro: Subject demand is not evenly spread across the emirate. School type, cohort size and the dominant post-16 destination all change which codes families in a district ask about, and the differences are large enough to be worth naming.

regions.name: Al Sufouh, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Long-established British secondaries with strong A Level pathways. Requests here skew to Extended-tier maths, the three separate sciences, and Additional Mathematics, which is the hardest code in the emirate to staff.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Large eastern cohorts with a high share of Arabic-first households. Arabic as a first language, 0508, comes up more often here than anywhere else in Dubai, alongside the usual maths and science demand.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing mid-market communities with big year groups sitting nine or ten subjects. Demand here concentrates on the coordinated and combined science routes rather than on three separate sciences.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: A technology-leaning catchment where Computer Science 0478 is requested far more often than ICT 0417, and where families most frequently discover they booked the wrong one of the two.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills Estate and Mudon
regions.note: Villa communities with established secondaries and a strong pull towards UK university destinations. The commerce group, especially Business Studies and Economics, is unusually heavily requested from this cluster.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Central apartment districts with transient populations and frequent mid-course arrivals. Requests here often involve a student joining a Dubai school partway through Year 10 with a different board behind them.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and JLT
regions.note: Dense residential towers with a very mixed school spread, so a single building can send students to four different secondaries on two different boards. Establishing the code before the first session matters more here than almost anywhere.

regions.name: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Deira
regions.note: Established districts with a large Indian and Arabic-first population and a strong science and commerce orientation. Double-award science and Accounting 0452 both come up more frequently in this cluster than the emirate average.

schoolClusters.city: The western British-curriculum corridor
schoolClusters.note: Secondaries with long A Level pathways, which is why subject choice conversations here are usually about keeping science and mathematics routes open rather than about maximising the number of passes. Separate sciences and Extended-tier maths dominate the tutoring requests.

schoolClusters.city: Academic City and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: A mix of Cambridge and Pearson centres sitting close together, which is the main reason families in this part of Dubai arrive unsure which awarding organisation their child is entered with. The first question any tutor should ask here is the board and the code.

schoolClusters.city: The newer southern and central communities
schoolClusters.note: Large year groups, broad subject lists and heavy use of the coordinated and combined science routes. This is where the question of whether a lighter science route closes a post-16 door comes up most often, and where it is most often raised too late.

sections.heading: The three science routes, and the one that quietly closes a door
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 10 student sits science in one of three shapes, and the shape is usually chosen by the school on the basis of Year 9 performance. Three separate sciences means Biology, Chemistry and Physics as individual syllabuses yielding three grades. A double award, Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0, covers all three in less depth and yields two grades. A single combined award, Cambridge 0653, covers all three and yields one.

All three are legitimate and the lighter routes suit a large number of students well. Covering three sciences in two grades' worth of teaching time frees timetable space for a subject the student is better at, and a strong double-award result is more useful than three weak separate grades. The honest position is that the route should match the student, not the parental ambition, and schools in this emirate generally get that judgement right.

The problem is a specific one and it arrives two years later. Some post-16 science courses assume the content of a separate-science syllabus, and a student arriving from a combined route meets a content gap in the first term of Year 12 rather than at the point of choosing. The gap is real but bounded, and it is far easier to close with a short block of preparatory work over a summer than to discover in October of Year 12. What makes it a problem is that nobody flags it when the route is chosen, because at that moment the post-16 intention is usually unformed.

So the useful intervention is a question asked in Year 9 or early Year 10, in writing, to the school: given this science route, which A Level or Diploma science courses would my child be able to start without additional preparation, and which would need some? A school can answer that in a paragraph. It is the single highest-value question on this page and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: Two maths syllabuses, plus one extra, and who needs which
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most tutored IGCSE subject in Dubai and the one where families most often engage a tutor for the wrong syllabus. Cambridge offers 0580 Mathematics and 0607 International Mathematics, and these are different courses rather than variants. 0607 requires a graphics calculator and includes an investigation component; 0580 does not. A tutor who assumes 0580 when the school entered 0607 will spend weeks on the wrong preparation. Confirm the current structure of either syllabus in the official document before planning.

On the Pearson side, Mathematics A is 4MA1 and it is tiered into Foundation and Higher, which surprises families who have been told that Pearson International GCSEs are untiered. Most of its other subjects are, but mathematics is not, and the tier decision carries the same consequences for available grades that Cambridge's Core and Extended decision does. Establish it early, because it has an entry deadline attached and entries on both boards close months before the papers.

Then there is the extra subject. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 sit alongside the main maths syllabus and are taken by a small, able fraction of each cohort, usually students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. They assume the higher-tier content of the main syllabus and move into calculus and trigonometric identities. They are also the two hardest codes to staff in this emirate, which is a genuine availability constraint rather than a pricing story.

What a family should settle, in order: which syllabus code, which tier where one exists, and whether the extra subject is on the timetable or should be. The third question is worth asking even if the answer is no, because a student who will need A Level Mathematics and has not met any of its groundwork at sixteen starts Year 12 at a disadvantage that is entirely avoidable.

sections.heading: The English codes, and the one that changes what is on the certificate
paragraphs: English is where a syllabus code does something a family can see on the final certificate, which makes it worth more attention than it usually gets. Cambridge First Language English is 0500, assessed through a reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper. Pearson English Language A is 4EA1. Literature in English is a separate subject, 0475 at Cambridge and 4ET1 at Pearson, and it is routinely confused with the language syllabus when families book help.

The code that matters most is in English as a Second Language. Cambridge offers 0510 and 0511. In 0510 the speaking component is reported as a separate endorsement alongside the grade. In 0511 the speaking component counts into the grade itself. Which one a school has entered therefore changes both what preparation is worthwhile and what the certificate shows, and a family planning speaking practice without knowing the code may be preparing for something that does not affect the result they care about.

Where the marks actually go in English is consistent across both boards. On reading questions, candidates summarise when they were asked to select, and lose marks for including material that does not answer the question. On directed writing, register and audience are ignored: a student who writes well in their own voice and never adjusts it for the task ceiling out. On Literature, the recurring failure is quotation used as decoration rather than as evidence, followed closely by answering a question that was revised rather than the one on the paper.

All of which points to one mode of support rather than many. English improves when somebody reads the student's actual writing every week and marks it against the published criteria. It does not improve much from discussing texts, reading model answers, or reviewing notes. That is unglamorous, it needs a term rather than a block, and it is the one thing in English tutoring that reliably works.

sections.heading: Practical science when the tutor is not in the laboratory
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one a Dubai school enters is a decision made by the centre rather than by the family. The distinction matters a great deal to what tutoring can achieve, and it is almost never explained to parents, who reasonably assume that a practical component means hands-on work and that online tutoring therefore cannot help.

The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper about practical work. It asks candidates to select apparatus, identify variables, spot sources of error, read scales, tabulate results, plot and interpret graphs, and say what an observation does and does not demonstrate. Every one of those is teachable without a laboratory, and most of them are taught badly in schools precisely because they are treated as an appendix to the practical rather than as a paper in their own right. This is one of the clearest opportunities in the whole IGCSE science timetable.

A practical test sat under examination conditions in a school laboratory is a different matter and we will not pretend otherwise. Manipulative skill, apparatus handling and working safely at a bench need a bench. What tutoring can do is the thinking around it: planning, predicting, recording properly, and the write-up conventions that cost marks. What it cannot do is substitute for time at the bench, and a provider claiming otherwise is selling something it cannot deliver.

So the first question before buying any science support in Dubai is which paper the school enters. Ask for it in writing, by number. The answer changes whether a block of sessions should be spent on written practical reasoning, which is highly tutorable, or on bench technique, which belongs to the school. Families who do not ask tend to buy the wrong one, and the loss is a whole block of hours rather than a few minutes.

sections.heading: The commerce group: where application beats knowledge
paragraphs: Business Studies, Economics and Accounting are heavily taken across Dubai schools and heavily tutored, and the pattern of failure in all three is the same. Candidates learn the content, define the terms correctly, and then answer a question about a case study without ever referring to the case study. That caps a script in the middle bands regardless of how much the student knows, and no amount of further content teaching moves it.

The fix is a habit rather than a body of knowledge, which is why it responds quickly to one-to-one work and poorly to revision guides. A student has to be taught to read the stimulus material first, identify what is specific about this organisation or this market, and then select the tool that applies rather than the tool they revised most recently. In a session that means marking a paragraph, asking which words in it could only be true of this case, and rewriting it until some of them are.

Evaluation is the second half. Both Business Studies and Economics explicitly reward weighing alternatives and reaching a supported judgement, and most candidates produce a balanced list and then stop. The missing move is a conclusion that commits, with a reason tied to the specific context. Accounting differs: its marks are more procedural, and the recurring losses are presentation conventions and arithmetic slips under time pressure rather than evaluation.

Availability varies inside the group. Business Studies is well covered in this market; Economics is reasonably covered; Accounting 0452 is more thinly supplied, because fewer teachers have taught it recently and the procedural precision it needs is specific. If Accounting is the subject in question, ask for a marked past-paper question from a prospective tutor before agreeing to a block of sessions.

sections.heading: Arabic as a first language is not Arabic as a foreign language
paragraphs: Arabic appears on almost every Dubai IGCSE timetable, and it appears in more than one form. Cambridge offers Arabic as a first language, 0508, and Arabic as a foreign language, 0544, and these are separate syllabuses with separate papers, separate expectations and largely separate teaching populations. Pearson also offers an Arabic qualification. A family booking Arabic tutoring without naming the code is as likely to get the wrong match here as anywhere in the roster.

Behind the examination syllabuses sits a separate and non-optional requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for; this is a federal rule, under which private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the deadline for its current requirements.

KHDA also requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arabs. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential rather than a marketing phrase.

Two practical consequences for tutoring. Support must follow the stream the school has placed the child in, because material designed for the foreign-language stream will not serve a first-language candidate and the reverse is worse. And for the mandatory subjects specifically, KHDA prohibits the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, so a tutor proposing to teach these streams from an imported workbook is proposing something the school cannot accept.

sections.heading: A* to G and 9 to 1 on the same Year 11 certificate
paragraphs: Grading is the part of the IGCSE landscape that confuses Dubai families most, and the confusion is entirely reasonable because two scales are genuinely in use. Cambridge reports IGCSE results on the A* to G scale internationally. Pearson reports International GCSE results on the 9 to 1 scale. A student taking subjects from both boards, which is common in this emirate, finishes Year 11 holding results in two different notations.

There is no conversion a parent should rely on for comparison. Boards publish their own grade descriptions and the two scales were designed independently; informal equivalence tables circulate widely and they are not authoritative. What a family can do is ask the school, in writing, which scale applies to which subject, and ask any post-16 destination how it reads each notation. Both answers are quick and both are more reliable than an internet table.

A separate point about boundaries. Grade boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series, published afterwards, and they move between series. Nobody teaching your child knows where the line will fall. This matters for how a family reads a mock result: a mock marked against last year's boundaries tells you roughly where a student sits, not what they will get, and a student three marks below a boundary in a mock is in a genuinely different position from one fifteen marks below.

For tiered subjects the scale interacts with the entry. A Core-tier Cambridge candidate is working towards a lower ceiling than an Extended one, and a Foundation-tier Pearson mathematics candidate towards a lower ceiling than a Higher-tier one. Confirm the available grades for each tier in the current syllabus document, because a family comparing a Core grade with a sibling's Extended grade is comparing two different things.

sections.heading: How many subjects, and which five actually count
paragraphs: Dubai students commonly sit eight to ten IGCSE subjects, and families treat the total as a measure of seriousness. For one specific and important purpose the total is irrelevant. The UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency route on the British track requires a student to show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five.

That rule is published and it is worth stating accurately, because one competitor ranking in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. They do not. Beyond the five, the British track also requires either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The American track works differently, with an English proficiency threshold met by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450, and a mathematics requirement of at least SAT Math 450 before applying.

For the IB no equivalency points figure can honestly be published here, because the sourced material does not state one. Anybody quoting an IB threshold should be asked for the moe.gov.ae page it came from. And a general caution applies to all of it: equivalency is a process the Ministry carries out, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and nobody should suggest that tutoring is required for it. That would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

The practical use of the five-subject rule is a planning one. It changes how a family thinks about a weak ninth or tenth subject, about whether to drop something, and about which subjects are load-bearing for a particular destination. University admission requirements are a separate question from equivalency and are set by each institution, so a student aiming at a specific course should check its published entry requirements as well. Both checks are free and both are more useful than an extra block of hours.

sections.heading: Dropping a subject, and when that is the right call
paragraphs: Families in Dubai ask about dropping an IGCSE subject more often than any other structural question, usually in February of Year 11 and usually about the subject causing the most distress at home. It is sometimes the right call and more often the wrong one, and the difference turns on three things that can be established in a single conversation with the school.

The first is whether dropping is possible at all at that point. Entries on both boards close months before the papers, so the practical window for removing a subject is earlier than parents expect, and after the deadline the question becomes whether the candidate sits the paper or is absent from it, which is a different decision with a different consequence on the statement of results. Ask the school for the deadline in writing before deciding anything.

The second is whether the subject is load-bearing. A subject that is one of the five carrying the equivalency count, or that appears in the published entry requirements of a post-16 course the student wants, is not a candidate for dropping even if it is the hardest one. A ninth subject that serves neither purpose is a different matter, and the timetable space it frees may be worth more than the grade it would have produced.

The third is whether the distress is about the subject or about the total load. A student failing in one subject and coping in eight has a subject problem. A student struggling in four has a workload or a technique problem, and removing one subject will not fix it; the intervention there is examination technique applied across the whole timetable, which is bought once and used everywhere. That distinction is worth making before any irreversible decision, and it is usually visible from a set of marked mock papers rather than from a conversation.
