process.title: Send the board and the code for the subject in question
process.description: Not the subject name. 0580 is not 0607, 0478 is not 0417, and 0510 is not 0511. If you do not know the codes, ask the school in writing; it is free, it takes a day, and it prevents a tutor working from the wrong specimen papers for a term.

process.title: A free trial lesson against real material
process.description: One trial lesson per family, nothing to pay and no card required. Bring a marked paper or a recent piece of the student's own work. The trial produces a list of components and error types for that specific syllabus rather than a general impression of how things are going.

process.title: A written plan at component level
process.description: The plan names the syllabus, the specific components to target, the session length and frequency, and how many weeks before a review. Where the right answer is a question for the school rather than a block of hours, the plan says that instead and gives you the wording.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work
process.description: Timed questions from the correct syllabus, marked against the published mark scheme, with the marks visible to the parent. For the written subjects that means a piece of the student's own prose marked every week, which is the only thing that reliably moves an English grade.

process.title: A six-week review and an honest verdict
process.description: We re-run a timed component and compare it with the trial diagnosis. If the marks have not moved we change the tutor, change the target component or tell you to stop. If a second subject now matters more than the first, we say so rather than extending out of habit.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Every match starts with the awarding organisation and the four-digit or four-character code, because a tutor working from the wrong specimen papers is expensive at any rate. This is the single most common avoidable failure in the Dubai IGCSE market.

whyPoints.title: The science route raised before the grade is
whyPoints.description: Separate, coordinated or combined changes how many grades are awarded and what post-16 study assumes. We raise it at the first conversation, because in Year 9 it is a choice and in Year 12 it is a content gap.

whyPoints.title: The English code checked, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Whether a school entered 0510 or 0511 decides whether speaking counts into the grade or is reported separately, which changes what preparation is worth buying. We establish it before planning any speaking work.

whyPoints.title: The alternative-to-practical paper taught properly
whyPoints.description: It is a written paper about practical work and therefore fully teachable over video, and it is widely treated in schools as an appendix to the practical. That makes it one of the clearest opportunities on an IGCSE science timetable.

whyPoints.title: Arabic streams kept separate
whyPoints.description: Arabic as a first language and Arabic as a foreign language are different syllabuses, and Dubai schools are required to stream Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies by group. Support follows the stream the school placed the child in.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits both stated
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram makes no home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE. Where a component needs a school laboratory, we say so rather than talking around it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus my child is actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing for the awarding organisation and the syllabus code for every subject, plus the tier where one applies. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 or 0625; Pearson codes begin with a 4, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1. Schools answer this quickly and it is free. It matters because the codes are not interchangeable: 0580 and 0607 are different mathematics syllabuses, and 0478 Computer Science is a different subject from 0417 ICT. A tutor working from the wrong specimen papers is the commonest avoidable waste at this level.

faqs.question: Should my child take three separate sciences or a double award?
faqs.answer: It depends on what happens at sixteen, which is why the question should be asked in Year 9. Three separate sciences yield three grades and keep the widest range of post-16 science courses open with no preparatory gap. A double award, Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SD0, covers all three sciences in less depth for two grades and suits many students better. A single combined award yields one grade. The useful move is to ask the school, in writing, which A Level or Diploma science courses the chosen route leaves open without additional preparation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607 mathematics?
faqs.answer: They are different syllabuses rather than variants of one. 0607 International Mathematics requires a graphics calculator and includes an investigation component; 0580 does not. Both are tiered into Core and Extended with different papers and different available grades. Confirm the current structure of whichever one your school entered in the official syllabus document. The practical consequence is that a tutor who assumes 0580 while the school entered 0607 will spend weeks preparing the wrong papers, which is why the code comes before anything else in a match.

faqs.question: Does my child need Additional Mathematics as well as Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Only if a post-16 mathematics route is likely. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 assume the higher-tier content of the main syllabus and move into calculus and trigonometric identities. They are taken by a small, able fraction of each cohort, typically students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. A student who will need A Level Mathematics and has met none of its groundwork at sixteen starts Year 12 at an avoidable disadvantage. Both codes are also the hardest to staff in this emirate, so ask about availability early.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0510 the same as 0511 for English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference shows up on the certificate. In 0510 the speaking component is reported as a separate endorsement alongside the grade. In 0511 the speaking component counts into the grade itself. Which one a school has entered therefore changes whether speaking preparation affects the result a family cares about. Ask the school for the code in writing before buying any speaking work, because preparing hard for a component that is reported separately is a reasonable choice only if you know that is what you are doing.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring help with IGCSE science practicals?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component your school enters. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper about practical work: apparatus selection, variables, error sources, reading scales, tabulation and interpreting graphs. All of that is fully teachable over video, and it is widely taught badly in schools because it is treated as an appendix to the practical. A practical test sat in a school laboratory is different, and bench technique needs a bench. Ask the school which paper number your child sits before buying a block of science sessions.

faqs.question: Why are my child's results in letters and my friend's child's in numbers?
faqs.answer: Because two awarding organisations use two scales. Cambridge reports IGCSE results on the A* to G scale internationally, while Pearson reports International GCSE results on the 9 to 1 scale. A Dubai student taking subjects from both boards can hold results in both notations at once. There is no authoritative public conversion for comparison, and the informal tables that circulate are not reliable. Ask the school which scale applies to which subject, and ask each post-16 destination how it reads each notation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Computer Science 0478 and ICT 0417?
faqs.answer: They are separate subjects frequently confused at the point of booking. Computer Science is algorithmic: pseudocode, problem decomposition, data representation and computational thinking. ICT is applied and software-based, concerned with using systems and applications effectively. A tutor strong in one is not automatically useful for the other, and matching to the wrong one wastes an entire block of sessions. Confirm the code with the school. In technology-leaning parts of Dubai this is the single most common mismatch we see at the enquiry stage.

faqs.question: How many marks is my child losing to examination technique rather than content?
faqs.answer: A marked past paper answers it and nothing else does. Look for three patterns: answers that address a lower command word than the one in the question, questions left blank at the end of the paper, and correct reasoning with the method not shown. If those three account for most of the loss, the problem is technique rather than knowledge, which is good news because technique is a single skill bought once and applied across all eight or nine subjects. If the loss is spread across topics instead, it is content and it costs more.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics generates the most tutoring requests by a clear margin, followed by the three separate sciences. Within those, the recurring difficulties are consistent: moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry in Chemistry; electricity and quantitative questions in Physics; the extended-response questions in Biology where sequencing matters more than recall. In the written subjects, English First Language reading questions and Literature essays both fail on the same thing, which is answering the question actually asked. In commerce, candidates lose marks for not applying their knowledge to the case material in front of them.

faqs.question: Is Arabic as a first language a different subject from Arabic as a foreign language?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge offers Arabic as a first language, 0508, and Arabic as a foreign language, 0544, as separate syllabuses with separate papers and largely separate teaching populations. Separately from the examination syllabuses, Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA requires schools to run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibiting combined classes. Support should follow the stream the school has placed the child in rather than blending the two.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child sit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Schools here commonly enter eight to ten, and the total matters less than families assume for one important purpose. The UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency route on the British track counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education from those five. One competitor ranking in this market states six, which does not match the published rule. University entry requirements are a separate question set by each institution. Verify the current equivalency position on moe.gov.ae before planning around any figure.

faqs.question: Can my child take subjects from both Cambridge and Pearson in the same year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it happens routinely because schools choose the awarding organisation subject by subject. The consequences are practical rather than problematic. The student will hold results in two notations, A* to G from Cambridge and 9 to 1 from Pearson. The two boards run their series on different timetables, so entry deadlines and results dates differ. And any tutor needs to know which board each subject belongs to. Ask the school for a single written list of subject, board, code and tier; one document resolves all three issues.

faqs.question: Can we drop an IGCSE subject partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the entry deadline in writing before deciding anything, because entries on both boards close months before the papers and the practical window is earlier than parents expect. After that deadline the question becomes whether the candidate sits the paper or is absent from it, which has its own consequence on the statement of results. Never drop one of the five subjects carrying the equivalency count or one named in a post-16 course's published entry requirements. And if the student is struggling in four subjects rather than one, the problem is load or technique, not that subject.

faqs.question: Why do these subject sessions run over live video rather than in our home?
faqs.answer: Because matching by syllabus code matters more than matching by postcode, and because we would rather state the position than let a family discover it. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the scarce codes, 0606, 4PM1 and Arabic as a first language, the difference is decisive: those specialists are thin on the ground and should not be filtered by driving distance.

dubai/igcse-tutors.closingHeading: Send us the code, not the subject name
dubai/igcse-tutors.closingBody: Ask the school for one written list: subject, awarding organisation, syllabus code and tier. That document resolves most of what this page describes, and it costs nothing. Then send it to us with a recent marked paper if you have one. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with nothing to pay and no card required, and it produces a list of components and error types for that specific syllabus rather than a general impression. The written plan that follows names the component to target, the session length, and how many weeks before we review it with you.

dubai/international-city.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are the ones International City families book most: IGCSE Mathematics, the separate and co-ordinated sciences, and English as a Second Language. Each tutor teaches a named specification, and the first session is a diagnostic rather than a sales call.

intro.heading: Class does one half of the course; your child does the other
paragraphs: The usual story in International City is a child who works hard, hands everything in, is described by the school as diligent, and then produces a test mark that makes no sense against any of it. Parents reasonably conclude that something is wrong with the teaching, or with the child. Usually neither is true. The course has two halves - the taught half and the half the student is expected to do alone - and the second half has quietly not been happening.

This is structural rather than anybody's fault. A teacher with a full class can explain a method, model one example and set practice. What the teacher cannot do is sit beside each student while they attempt thirty unprompted questions and work out which of the thirty went wrong and why. That diagnosis is the whole value of one-to-one teaching, and it is also what nobody is doing at home when a student completes homework correctly and learns nothing from it.

International City adds a specific pressure to this, which is worth naming without euphemism. Households here are more often working to a tight education budget than in the villa communities to the west, and they are often funding tutoring out of a monthly figure that has other claims on it. The market's response to that is a supply of very cheap hours, and a cheap hour spent supervising homework produces the feeling of tutoring with almost none of the effect.

So this page is organised around the decision an International City parent actually faces, which is not whether to get a tutor but how to spend a limited amount well. That means being specific about which single subject converts an hour into marks fastest, which subjects a disciplined student can fix alone with a past paper and a published mark scheme, where the Core and Extended tier decision caps a grade before any revision starts, and what a cheap rate usually indicates.

On delivery: lessons run one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing so the tutor and the student work on the same marked script. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a household in International City that removes the travel premium an in-home tutor has to charge for the drive from the villa districts, and it widens the choice from whoever can reach Warsan to whoever teaches the specification.

Nothing on this page promises a grade, and no figure here is an IB Gram price. The rates quoted are market rates with the provider who published them named, so you can hold any quote - including ours - against them. What follows is the practical sequence: diagnose, fund the one subject that needs funding, and run the free half of the plan properly.

dubai/international-city.programmesIntro: International City children sit across several systems, and two programmes account for most tutoring requests. The notes below say what each one demands of the student outside lesson time, because that is the demand a budget has to cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11. Every syllabus has a code - 0580, 0620, 0625, 4MA1 - and the code determines the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet. Cambridge offers Core and Extended routes on several subjects with different grade ceilings. With eight or nine subjects running at once, this is the year group where the gap between work required and hours available is widest.
programmes.countryNote: Nearly all IGCSE requests from International City concern Years 10 and 11 at schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Mirdif and Silicon Oasis. The most valuable thing a parent here can do costs nothing: ask the examinations officer for the syllabus code and the tier on the entry form, because a Core entry caps the grade however hard the student works.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth a meaningful share of the grade. The independent load is the heaviest of any school qualification, because coursework in several subjects runs at the same time as past-paper preparation for all six.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students living in International City usually travel the furthest of anyone in the community, since the nearby schools running the full Diploma are few. That makes a later weekday slot or a weekend block the realistic arrangement, and it makes coursework checkpoints better value than a long weekly programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade. No external papers until an optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11, so every mark comes from interim tasks. A reported grade can therefore hide a weak criterion that will matter later, and parents are rarely shown the criterion breakdown unless they ask.
programmes.countryNote: MYP requests from this community are usually best handled as a short block on one criterion rather than a standing weekly slot. Six weeks pointed at a single weak criterion is a far better use of a constrained budget than a year of general support, and it has a visible endpoint.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with reporting against learning outcomes instead of marks. What decides how Year 7 goes is reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina, none of which a prose report shows clearly. At this age thirty focused minutes beats a tired hour, which also makes it the cheapest stage at which to intervene usefully.
programmes.countryNote: For primary children in International City the highest-value intervention is almost always reading. Twenty minutes of reading aloud daily, with a parent asking what just happened in the text, moves more than a paid hour a week at that age, and it costs nothing but the habit.

dubai/international-city.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects International City families ask about most, with an honest note on whether a paid hour is the right tool. Some subjects need a specialist watching the student work. Others need marked practice the student can run alone, and buying a slot for those is poor value.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The best single candidate for a limited budget, because the failures are specific and visible. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems mixing two topics with no method signposted. Check the tier before anything else: a Core entry puts a ceiling on the grade regardless of how the revision goes.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the written practical paper account for most of the lost marks. The practical paper tests reading someone else's method and finding its weakness, which is a skill almost no student practises, and it responds well to a handful of focused sessions rather than a term.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry decide the grade and both reward drill. A weekly slot earns its cost in Year 11; in Year 10 the same money is usually better left unspent, since the content is still being taught and self-marked practice does the same job.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Looks like memorisation, which is why students reread notes and make no progress. Marks turn on terminology precision and on answering the command term used. This is a subject a disciplined student can lift substantially alone with past papers and the published scheme.

subjects.name: IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Covers all three sciences at reduced depth for two grades. Sound for students not heading to a science destination, and lighter on the timetable. The trade is post-sixteen: some sixth-form science combinations expect the separate route, so check before assuming the choice is neutral.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with different papers and a different purpose. It is widely accepted and perfectly respectable, but some institutions and some first-language courses expect the other route, so the question to ask is what the student will need it for later.

subjects.name: IGCSE English First Language
subjects.description: Rewards a repeatable procedure for reading an unseen text under timing far more than it rewards wider reading. Directed writing and summary tasks have strict formats, and students lose marks to format rather than to language more often than parents expect.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Both reward applying a few tools to unfamiliar material under timing. Students describe the business when the question asked them to evaluate a decision, and skip the quantitative sections. Short pre-mock blocks work better here than a long weekly commitment.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus are the pressure points at Higher Level, and the exploration moves whole grades because it is marked against five lettered criteria and treated by students as a write-up. The term the exploration is drafted is the one where a slot pays for itself.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in every Dubai private school under KHDA rules, and the stream most budgets forget until a report lands. It needs its own tutor and its own target, and the match for Arabic as a first language is a different one again.

dubai/international-city.regionsIntro: International City is organised into country-named clusters with Warsan and the Dragon Mart corridor alongside, and almost every child here is bussed outward to school. The notes below cover the communities whose children share those routes and school lists.

regions.name: International City
regions.note: The country clusters - China, England, France, Greece, Italy, Morocco, Persia, Russia, Spain - plus the Warsan edge. Dense apartment living with no large school inside the community, so every secondary student is on a bus route of twenty minutes or more.

regions.name: Warsan and Dragon Mart
regions.note: The commercial edge of the community, where the main road out towards Al Awir and the Al Ain road corridor begins. Traffic here is shaped by freight as much as by school times, which pushes arrivals later than distance suggests.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: The nearest established villa district, holding several strong Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools. Most of the IGCSE requests from International City concern schools in this area.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: North-west towards Sharjah, with a long-standing school cluster. Buses from International City into Al Qusais take longer in the afternoon than the morning, which matters when setting a session time.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: A few minutes south, with schools inside the community and more in Academic City behind it. Families moving between International City and Silicon Oasis usually keep the same school and the same tutor slot.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Dense villa suburb to the north with its own school cluster and several continuum schools. Mirdif routes are short in distance and slow in practice because buses work through multiple communities.

dubai/international-city.modesIntro: Three arrangements cover almost every request from this community, and they differ in cost by a factor of several. The point of setting them out together is that the cheapest arrangement is sometimes the right one, and the market rarely says so.

modes.description: A single fixed hour on the one subject where marked work shows a specific failure, running for a defined block rather than indefinitely. Everything else in the plan is done by the student with past papers and the published mark scheme. This is the arrangement that fits most International City budgets and most International City problems.

sections.heading: What the school supplies and what your child has to supply
paragraphs: The direct answer first. A school reliably supplies content coverage, modelled examples, set practice and marked assessments. It does not supply the volume of unprompted practice that converts understanding into marks, and it cannot supply individual diagnosis of why a particular student's attempts fail. Those two things are the student's half of the course, and in most cases where a diligent child underperforms, that half is missing rather than weak.

The distinction is worth making concrete. A student who can complete an exercise set after a lesson has demonstrated that they can follow a method while it is fresh. A student who can do a mixed question three weeks later, with no indication of which method applies, has demonstrated something quite different, and only the second thing is examined. Homework mostly tests the first. That is why a child can have a perfect homework record and a poor test record without anybody behaving badly.

The table splits the main subjects that way, with a fourth column that matters most for a budget: the cheapest fix that actually works. In several rows the cheapest fix is free. Past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards, and a student who works through them under timing and marks their own attempts honestly is doing the single most effective revision activity available at any price.

The one caution on doing it alone is marking. A student marking their own work tends to be generous, because they recognise what they meant rather than what they wrote. Where a paid hour earns its cost early, it is often in teaching a student to mark strictly against a scheme - which is a skill that transfers to every subject and then needs buying only once.

sections.heading: If you can fund one subject, which one should it be?
paragraphs: Most families answer this by picking the lowest grade on the report, which is the wrong method. The right question is not where the student is weakest but where an hour of expert attention converts into marks fastest, and those are different things. A subject that is weak because the student has not done the work does not need a tutor. It needs the work. A subject that is weak because a specific, identifiable step breaks every time does need a tutor, and quickly.

The sorting rule holds up well in practice. Fund the subject where the failure is specific and visible in the marked script: a method abandoned halfway, a calculation attempted in the wrong order, a question that is never started. Do not fund the subject where the failure is diffuse - a thin essay, patchy recall, content half-learned - because that responds to repeated marked practice the student can run themselves with a published scheme.

There is a second filter, which is leverage. Mathematics carries into the sciences, so fixing algebraic fluency improves three subjects at once and is usually the best single purchase in Years 10 and 11. Marking technique transfers everywhere and only has to be taught once. Command terms transfer across every written subject. A budget spent on something that transfers buys more than the same budget spent on a single subject's content.

The table gives the recommendation against the pattern you can actually see in the marked work. Use it with the script in front of you rather than with the report, because the report shows the outcome and the script shows the cause. If nothing in the table matches, the honest answer is often that no paid hour is needed yet, and that six weeks of structured self-marked practice should come first.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: This is the single most consequential thing most International City parents have never been told. Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes on several IGCSE subjects, and they are not two difficulty settings on the same grade scale. A Core entry makes a narrower range of grades available than an Extended entry. A student entered on Core cannot reach the top grades no matter how well they perform, because the papers they sit do not award them.

The decision is usually taken by the school, sometimes in Year 10 and often without a conversation, and it is recorded on the entry rather than in the report. Entries are finalised months before the examination - Cambridge takes final entries for its March 2027 series on 27 November 2026 for papers beginning 3 February 2027 - so by the time a parent sees a mock result the tier may already be fixed for that series.

What a family should do is simple and free. Ask the examinations officer, in writing, for the syllabus code and the tier on each entry, and ask what the school's criteria are for moving a student between tiers and by when. If a child is on Core and heading for a sixth form that expects higher grades, that conversation needs to happen early in Year 10, not after mocks in Year 11 when the entry window has closed.

Pearson Edexcel generally runs a single tier on its International GCSE subjects, which removes this problem and introduces a different one: a student who would have been comfortable on a Core paper sits the full paper regardless. Neither arrangement is better in the abstract. What matters is knowing which arrangement your child is in, because the ceiling it sets is invisible in a school report.

sections.heading: English as a Second Language and the first-language question
paragraphs: A large share of students in this community sit English as a Second Language rather than First Language English, and parents are often unsure whether that matters. The straightforward position: it is a real, widely accepted qualification with its own papers and purpose, and for most students it is the right entry. It is not a lesser version of the other course; it is a different course with a different design.

Where it does matter is later, and only sometimes. Some sixth-form courses and some institutions specify First Language English or a particular grade in it, and some separately require an English proficiency test regardless of the school qualification. On the American equivalency track, for instance, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section - a school grade does not substitute for that.

So the useful action is to find out what the destination asks for, not to switch courses reflexively. If the student is heading towards a course that names First Language English, discuss the move with the school early, because it is a two-year course and a late switch is rarely sensible. If the destination is undecided, the stronger grade on the course the student is actually prepared for is worth more than a weak grade on a more prestigious-sounding one.

For tutoring purposes the two courses need different work. English as a Second Language rewards accuracy, register and following a task's format precisely; First Language English rewards analytical reading of an unseen text and controlled writing under timing. A tutor matched to the wrong one will teach competently and improve the wrong skills, which is another reason the entry code matters more than the subject name.

sections.heading: Past papers done properly: the free half of the plan
paragraphs: The most effective revision activity available to an IGCSE or Diploma student costs nothing. The boards publish past papers and mark schemes, and schools can supply them. A student who works through whole papers under timing and marks their own attempts strictly against the scheme will outperform a student who has twice as much tutoring and does none of this. That is not a motivational claim; it is what the practice actually produces.

It is also almost always done wrong. Students do papers topic by topic, with the book open, without timing, and mark generously because they recognise what they intended to write. Each of those four errors removes most of the benefit. Done properly the routine is narrow: whole paper, correct tier, strict timing, closed notes, then marking against the published scheme in a different colour, then a logged list of what was lost and why, retested a fortnight later.

Two rules keep it honest. First, mark to the scheme's wording rather than to your own judgement of whether the answer was reasonable - the scheme is the examiner. Second, log the reason for each lost mark in one of four categories: did not know it, knew it and misread the question, knew it and ran out of time, knew it and wrote the wrong structure for the command term. Those four categories lead to four different actions, and the log is what tells you which.

Copyright is worth a sentence. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. Access them through the official sites or through your child's school rather than through a reseller, and treat any tutor offering a downloadable pack of them with caution - redistributing those materials is not theirs to do, and it says something about the rest of the operation.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and when a cheap hour is false economy
paragraphs: Market rates in Dubai span roughly an order of magnitude, and the spread is not mostly about greed. At the bottom are university students and part-time tutors supervising homework. In the middle are qualified subject tutors teaching a named specification. At the top are specialists in a particular paper, and above them providers selling scarcity. All four exist in this market and all four are rational purchases for different problems.

The figures below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list; ask us for our figure before booking and hold it against the band. One piece of context worth having while budgeting: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package, so the school-fee side of a family budget is at least stable this year.

The judgement to make is about fit rather than price. An AED 60 hour that keeps a Year 8 student in the habit of doing their homework is good value. The same AED 60 hour pointed at a Year 11 Extended Mathematics paper is likely to be poor value, because the tutor may not know the tier, the paper structure or the mark scheme well enough to diagnose anything. Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision is the opposite error and just as common.

Two warning signs are worth knowing in the cheaper part of the market. A tutor who cannot tell you which syllabus code they teach is not teaching to one. And a tutor who has not heard of the MoHRE private tuition work permit is unlikely to hold it, which is a reasonable thing to ask about, since the permit is free of charge and takes two working days to obtain.

sections.heading: Which schools International City children attend, and why the board matters
paragraphs: There is no large school inside International City itself, so every secondary student here is on a bus. The two main directions are north-east into Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Al Mizhar, and south into Silicon Oasis and Academic City, with a smaller flow along the creek to the Garhoud and Festival City schools. Those destinations sit on different boards and different curricula, which is the fact that matters for tutoring.

The recurring error follows from it. A parent describes their child's course by subject and year group, a tutor is matched on that, and several sessions in it becomes clear the tutor has been teaching a different specification. Cambridge and Pearson differ in paper structure, in tiering and in what appears on the formula sheet. Indian-curriculum schools differ from both. The fix is one question to the examinations officer, and it is free.

Some scale for context: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen different curricula, with the British route largest by enrolment and the IB around 7% of enrolment. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places. The mix in a community's school list is therefore something that keeps changing rather than settling.

One clarification about the regulator, because parents sometimes assume more than is there. KHDA licenses and inspects Dubai private schools and publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. It does not license private tutors, and no tutoring platform is inspected under that framework. A school's band describes the school. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or licensing from KHDA or from any board.

sections.heading: The permit question, and what a very low rate often means
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the application with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor who does not hold it has usually not looked into the rules at all - and the same person is often the one who cannot say which syllabus code they teach. That is the real signal in a very low rate. It is not that cheap tutoring is illegitimate; plenty of permitted, competent tutors charge modestly. It is that the absence of the permit tends to travel with the absence of everything else you want to check.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. The permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so hiring your child's own teacher privately is not a route to take.

A business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different case again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and delivers lessons online. Nothing on this site claims approval or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because none is held.

sections.heading: Coursework support that keeps your child out of trouble
paragraphs: There are providers ranking for these searches that sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price, and the risk is worth stating plainly because the price makes it look like a service. A student who submits purchased work faces their school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma. The provider keeps the fee. The student carries the consequence for years.

Legitimate support is narrower and more useful than the alternative pretends. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. A tutor interrogates a research question until it is answerable in the word limit. A tutor questions method, data, sources and reasoning. A tutor reads a draft and replies with questions - why this comparison, what does the graph show that the table does not, which limitation would an examiner spot first. The student then decides, in their own words.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a rewritten version to retype. The test is whether the student can defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes. If they cannot, the help went too far whoever gave it and however it was described. That standard protects the student, which is the only reason it is worth holding to when a deadline is close.

The same boundary covers the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. Ask a prospective tutor directly how they handle a draft, and listen for whether the answer involves giving the student a better version of it. A provider who describes that openly is describing a risk they are not the ones taking.

process.title: Send the last marked paper, not the report
process.description: The report shows the outcome; the script shows the cause. Send the most recent marked assessment, including the one that went badly, and we can tell whether the problem is knowledge, procedure, timing or command terms. Those four need different responses, and only some of them need a paid hour.

process.title: Ask the school for the code and the tier
process.description: Request the syllabus code and, for Cambridge subjects, the tier in writing from the examinations officer. It costs nothing and it changes everything: a Core entry caps the grade, and past-paper practice on the wrong tier gives a misleading picture of where the student stands.

process.title: One diagnostic hour, then an honest recommendation
process.description: The first session works on the marked script and a short set of unprompted questions rather than teaching. Sometimes the recommendation is a weekly slot on one subject. Sometimes it is six weeks of structured self-marked practice and no paid hours at all, and we will say so.

process.title: Fund one subject with a target and an end date
process.description: Where a slot is needed, we agree the subject, a stated target, a number of sessions and a review point rather than an open-ended arrangement. Everything else in the plan goes to self-marked past papers, which is free and more effective than a second paid subject.

process.title: Run the free half of the plan every week
process.description: Whole papers, correct tier, strict timing, closed notes, marked against the published scheme, with each lost mark logged by reason. We set it, check it and adjust it. This is the part that does most of the work, and it is the part that stops if nobody is watching.

process.title: Review on marks, then stop
process.description: At the review point we compare against marked work and decide to continue, change tutor or finish. Finishing is the intended outcome. A provider with no end date is selling a standing order, and for a household budgeting carefully that is the worst product in this market.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when not to buy an hour
whyPoints.description: Where the marked work shows a diffuse weakness rather than a specific failure, the recommendation is structured self-marked practice and no paid sessions. A provider that never gives that answer is not diagnosing, it is selling.

whyPoints.title: One subject, chosen for leverage
whyPoints.description: Algebraic fluency carries into all three sciences; marking technique and command terms carry into every written subject. A constrained budget goes furthest on something that transfers, not on the subject with the lowest grade.

whyPoints.title: The free half of the plan is set and checked
whyPoints.description: Past papers and mark schemes cost nothing and outperform extra tutoring when used properly. We specify the routine - whole paper, right tier, timed, closed notes, strict marking, losses logged by reason - and check it each week.

whyPoints.title: Tier and syllabus code checked before matching
whyPoints.description: A Core entry caps a grade and a tutor on the wrong specification teaches the wrong paper competently. We ask for the code and the tier before a match is made, which is why the first question is about the entry form rather than the report.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to October 2026. Nothing on this page is presented as our price, and you can hold our quote against the same bands.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, no centre commute
whyPoints.description: Lessons run online, so you are not paying for a drive from the villa districts and your child is not adding a second journey to the day. The choice widens from whoever can reach Warsan to whoever teaches the specification.

faqs.question: We can only afford one subject. Which one should it be?
faqs.answer: Choose on leverage rather than on the lowest grade. In Years 10 and 11 the usual answer is Mathematics, because algebraic fluency carries into all three sciences, so fixing it improves several subjects at once. The second filter is whether the marked script shows a specific failure - a method abandoned mid-way, a question never started - because that is what a tutor can diagnose and fix. A subject that is weak because the work has not been done needs the work, not an hour. Send the last marked paper and the answer is usually obvious from it.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 50 an hour worth trying?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the job. At AED 50 you are generally buying homework supervision and content recap from a student or part-time tutor, which is genuinely useful for a Year 7 or Year 8 child who needs the habit of sitting down and working. Pointed at a Year 11 Extended Mathematics paper it is usually poor value, because diagnosing why a specific question failed needs someone who knows the tier, the paper structure and the mark scheme. Ask two questions before booking: which syllabus code do you teach, and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to International City apartments?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, so the tutor and the student work on the same marked script. For a household here that removes the travel premium an in-home tutor has to charge for the drive out from the villa districts, and it widens the choice from whoever can reach Warsan on a weekday evening to whoever actually teaches your child's specification.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in International City attend?
faqs.answer: There is no large school inside the community, so every secondary student travels. The main flows are north-east into Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Al Mizhar, and south into Silicon Oasis and Academic City, with a smaller number going along the creek to the Garhoud and Festival City schools. Those destinations sit on several different boards, which is why a tutor match has to begin with the syllabus code rather than the school name. Two children in the same building can sit different Physics papers depending on whether their schools entered Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE Core and Extended, and can we change?
faqs.answer: They are different paper sets with different grade ranges, not two difficulty settings on one scale. A Core entry makes a narrower band of grades available, typically C to G, while an Extended entry offers the full range. A student on Core cannot reach the top grades because the papers do not award them. Tier is usually decided by the school, often in Year 10, and is recorded on the entry rather than in the report. Changing is possible before the entry deadline at the school's discretion, so raise it early in Year 10 rather than after Year 11 mocks.

faqs.question: My child sits English as a Second Language. Does that limit anything?
faqs.answer: Usually not, but check the destination rather than assume. English as a Second Language is a full, widely accepted qualification with its own papers and purpose, not a reduced version of First Language English. Some sixth-form courses and some institutions do name First Language English or require a separate proficiency test - on the American equivalency track, English is evidenced by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and a school grade does not substitute for that. A strong grade on the right course beats a weak one on a more prestigious-sounding course.

faqs.question: How do we use past papers properly without paying a tutor?
faqs.answer: Narrowly and strictly. Whole paper, not topic by topic. The correct tier. Timed. Notes closed. Then mark against the published scheme in a different colour, to the scheme's wording rather than to your own sense of whether the answer was reasonable. Then log every lost mark under one of four reasons: did not know it, misread the question, ran out of time, or wrote the wrong structure for the command term. Retest the losses a fortnight later. Access papers through the school or the boards' official sites rather than a reseller.

faqs.question: Are group classes better value than one-to-one here?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, slower per hour, and it depends on the problem. A group works reasonably for general revision where everyone needs the same content covered again. It works poorly for a specific diagnosed failure, because the tutor cannot stop and watch one student attempt thirty unprompted questions while others wait. A tuition centre class adds a second commute to an evening that probably has no room for one. For most International City budgets, one well-chosen one-to-one subject plus free past-paper work beats a group class in three subjects.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same flat share a session?
faqs.answer: Yes, when they are genuinely at the same point in the same subject on the same specification. It roughly halves the cost per child and, just as valuably, halves the number of evening slots the household has to find. It fails when children two years apart are put together to save money: the tutor ends up teaching one and occupying the other. Review it after four sessions, because mismatch becomes obvious quickly. The same arrangement works for two neighbours' children in the same class, provided both families agree the target.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a Year 11 student be working alone?
faqs.answer: The useful measure is output rather than hours. For Year 11, two whole timed papers a fortnight across the subject set, each marked strictly against the scheme with losses logged, plus a short retrieval session on older topics most days, is a realistic and effective load. Counting hours encourages a student to sit at a desk rereading notes, which is the activity that feels most like studying and does least. If the weekly output is there, the hours take care of themselves; if it is not, more hours will not fix it.

faqs.question: My child does all the homework and still fails the test. Why?
faqs.answer: Because homework and tests measure different things. Homework usually follows the lesson, so the student knows which method applies and has it fresh. A test asks a mixed question weeks later with no indication of which method is wanted. A student can be completely reliable at the first and quite unable to do the second, and nobody has behaved badly. The fix is unprompted mixed practice: questions drawn from several topics, with no signposting, attempted cold and marked strictly. That is the half of the course the timetable does not cover.

faqs.question: Does a tutor charging AED 60 an hour still need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The requirement attaches to the activity rather than the price. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application is listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the permit costs nothing, not holding it usually means the rules were never checked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear line. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and what each is worth, question the focus of the work, interrogate method and sources, and respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections. What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure the argument, or hand back a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided. Purchased or ghostwritten coursework exposes the student to the school's academic honesty process and, in the IB, to a malpractice finding; the provider keeps the fee either way.

faqs.question: How long before marks move if we start now?
faqs.answer: It depends on which failure is being fixed. A procedural problem - not starting questions, misreading command terms, marking generously - often shows movement within three or four weeks, because the behaviour changes quickly once it is named. A content gap in mathematics takes longer, typically six to ten weeks of weekly work plus practice between sessions. A diffuse weakness across several subjects does not move on a schedule at all, which is why we measure against marked work rather than promise a timeline. Set the review point at six to eight weeks and judge it on scripts.

faqs.question: What should we send to get a tutor matched quickly?
faqs.answer: Four things. The syllabus code and tier from the entry form, or the IB subject and level. The last two pieces of marked work, including the one that went badly. The school's coursework deadline dates if coursework is live. And the time your child actually gets home, which sets the slot. With those the diagnostic hour is spent diagnosing rather than collecting information, and you receive a written assessment, a named tutor who teaches that specification, the rate in AED and a review date before anything is committed.

dubai/international-city.closingHeading: Spend the money where it changes a mark
dubai/international-city.closingBody: A limited budget is not a limitation on what a student can achieve; it is a constraint on where the money goes. Fund the one subject where the marked script shows a specific, fixable failure, pick the one with the most leverage, and run the free half of the plan - whole timed papers, right tier, strict marking, losses logged - every week without exception. Send the syllabus code and tier, the last marked paper and the time your child gets home. You will get a written diagnostic, an honest recommendation that sometimes says no paid hours are needed yet, the rate in AED, and a review date. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/jbr.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and IGCSE subjects to students at the schools JBR families use, working from the published syllabus for the exact code a child is entered for. Their first job on this page's model is diagnosis: finding what has been covered thinly, then teaching that rather than everything.

intro.heading: A tower full of children who are all taught well and all stuck in different places
paragraphs: JBR has no school inside it. Every child living in the towers along The Walk commutes out, mostly west into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha or inland towards Jumeirah Park and Dubai Sports City, and they scatter across a dozen schools with different curricula and different exam boards. One lift in one tower can hold a Year 11 sitting Cambridge IGCSE, a Year 11 sitting Pearson Edexcel for the same subject, and a DP1 student whose school runs the Diploma instead of A Level. That matters because it means the usual neighbourhood shortcut — asking which tutor everyone uses — is close to useless here.

What those families actually share is a problem that has nothing to do with school quality. A scheme of work has to cover an entire syllabus in a fixed number of lessons, which means every subject has strands that get one lesson when they need three, and components that get mentioned when they need practising. In Dubai, where KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale and schools are generally good at the taught curriculum, the thing left undone is almost never the content itself. It is the depth on two or three strands, the volume of timed practice, and the ability to read a mark scheme the way an examiner does.

That gap is invisible on a report. A report says the student is working at a grade, which is the school's best estimate from the evidence it holds. It does not say that topic 4.3 was taught in one lesson before half term, that the class has sat two full past papers all year, or that the student has never marked their own work against the official scheme. Those three facts, if true, predict a disappointing summer much better than a grade does.

So the useful first purchase for a JBR family is an audit rather than a course. Take the published syllabus for the exact code the school enters for — Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1, and so on — and check it strand by strand against what the student can actually do under timed conditions. The output is a short list of three or four strands that are genuinely thin, which is a thing you can buy teaching for. Buying a weekly hour without that list means paying a specialist to work out what to teach while the clock runs.

The second half of the audit is the independent work the school cannot supply at all. Past-paper volume is the obvious one: a timetable has no room for twenty full papers, so those have to happen at home. Mark-scheme literacy is the one nobody names: a student who cannot predict where the marks sit in a question is guessing at every extended answer. And retrieval, meaning short frequent self-testing across everything covered so far, is the study habit that replaces re-reading and almost nobody adopts without being taught it.

IB Gram delivers all of this online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time slots that start after a JBR child has got home. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a tower household that is usually the better arrangement anyway, because the specialist who knows the exact syllabus code and can mark to the official scheme is unlikely to be the tutor who can park nearby at six o'clock.

dubai/jbr.programmesIntro: JBR children sit across the whole range, because the towers feed into schools running different programmes. These are the four that matter most to the families who contact us from this postcode.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years per subject, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with practical or alternative-to-practical components in the sciences. Most Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers with different papers and different grade ceilings; Pearson specifications have their own paper architecture, and in several subjects no separate practical examination.
programmes.countryNote: In JBR the board varies household by household, and sometimes department by department inside one school. The practical consequence is that past papers bought for the wrong code practise the wrong paper structure. Ask the exams officer for the code in writing, subject by subject, and audit against that document rather than against a revision guide.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups with three at Higher Level, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge with an essay and an exhibition, and CAS. Scored out of 45 with 24 needed to pass, and three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Every subject carries an internal assessment with a fixed share of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: The coverage audit works differently for a Diploma student, because the thing most often thin is not a syllabus strand but an internal assessment that has been started and not supervised. Diploma students in this area are usually ahead on content and behind on independent components, which is a scheduling problem rather than a teaching one.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against criteria A to D in each subject group, with a Personal Project in the final year. Marks are criterion letters rather than percentages, which parents from other systems often find hard to read, and the command terms used are the same ones the Diploma will use later.
programmes.countryNote: For a JBR family the useful thing about MYP marks is that criterion letters are a coverage map in disguise: a student scoring well on criterion A and poorly on criterion D is telling you which skill the next two years will punish. That is more actionable than a percentage, once somebody explains what the letters assess.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, assessed by terminal papers with practical endorsement in some sciences depending on the specification. No compulsory breadth and no core, which concentrates all the risk into a small number of subjects and papers.
programmes.countryNote: With only three subjects, a thin strand does proportionally more damage than it would in a six-subject Diploma, so the coverage audit matters more rather than less. A single under-taught module in a Cambridge or Pearson A Level can account for a whole grade, which is why the audit is worth doing in the first term of Year 12 rather than in the spring of Year 13.

dubai/jbr.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the strands that schemes of work in this part of Dubai most often leave thin, and the component where the student is on their own. These are the things to check before buying any teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Thin strands in practice: vectors, transformation geometry, set notation and histograms with unequal class widths. The solo component is the non-calculator paper, which needs weekly short practice rather than a block before mocks, and which no timetable has room to drill properly.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Usually taught well on mechanics and electricity and thinly on thermal physics and nuclear. The solo component is the alternative-to-practical paper: identifying anomalous readings, naming control variables and explaining unreliability are examined skills that lab lessons do not assess.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry get proper time; qualitative analysis rarely does. The descriptive bank of tests, colours and precipitates is memorisation work that belongs at home, and students who have never built it lose a predictable block of marks every year.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The volume problem. Coverage is usually complete and retention is not, because the course is wide and the terminal paper asks about everything. The solo work is spaced retrieval across the whole syllabus, plus learning the syllabus's own wording for defined processes rather than a paraphrase.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Lessons cover the reading questions thoroughly and directed writing more lightly, because marking it is slow. The solo work is writing to a named form and audience under timed conditions, repeatedly, with the mark scheme open — which is exactly what students will not do unsupervised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, proof and series are the strands that most often get one pass. The solo component is the mathematical exploration, which needs a question narrow enough to finish and a schedule of intermediate deadlines nobody else will impose.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Content coverage in Dubai Diploma schools is generally strong; the individual investigation is where students are alone. It is an open-ended experimental project assessed against criteria, and the single most common failure is a research question chosen too late and too broadly to produce usable data.

subjects.name: IB Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Taught content is rarely the issue. The internal assessments — article commentaries in Economics, a research project in Business Management — are produced largely outside lessons against criteria students have not read closely. Supervision rather than teaching is what moves these.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and, at Higher Level, the HL essay are the components students prepare most alone. Both reward apparatus — the vocabulary for how meaning is constructed — which is taught in class and practised almost nowhere unless somebody sets it as work.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and IB Computer Science
subjects.description: Students who code are usually ahead on the programming paper and behind on theory: data representation, two's complement, packet switching, and the fetch-execute cycle in the syllabus's own words. That is pure solo learning and it is the half that costs grades.

subjects.name: Second languages: French, Spanish, Arabic and Hindi
subjects.description: Vocabulary and speaking practice are the solo components in every language specification, and both decay without weekly use. The strand most often thin in a scheme of work is the writing task's register requirements — formal letter, report, blog — which carry marks independent of language accuracy.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: No school has room to teach these weekly, so they are the purest example of what this page is about: components worth three of the 45 available points, produced almost entirely on the student's own time, with deadlines the student has to impose on themselves.

dubai/jbr.regionsTitle: Where JBR children actually go to school, and what the route costs the evening
dubai/jbr.regionsIntro: JBR sits at the western end of the Marina strip, with the tram along one side and Sheikh Zayed Road behind it. These are the places families commute to and from, with what each route does to the realistic start of a session.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The closest cluster of secondary schools to JBR, reached along Al Sufouh Road rather than Sheikh Zayed. A short distance that still takes time at 3pm, and the single most common origin of a JBR school run. Children on this route are typically home and settled by 4.30pm.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: A longer inland run, usually via Sheikh Zayed Road or Umm Suqeim Road, with the afternoon peak against you. Families on this route should assume 5.15pm at the earliest before a child is fed and at a desk, which rules out the 4pm session most tutors offer first.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village
regions.note: Reached across Sheikh Zayed Road and through the interchange, which is the slowest part of the route rather than the distance itself. A 6.30pm or 7pm online slot is the realistic first option, and it holds week after week in a way an earlier one does not.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Immediately next door and reachable on foot or by tram, which makes it the one direction where a short journey really is short. Marina and JBR households often share school buses, so a sibling pair split between the two communities usually comes home on the same timetable.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road from the Marina side, close in distance and separated by the crossing. Families here face the same tower-living constraints as JBR — a shared study space, a kitchen table, two children in one room — which is a real factor in choosing a session time.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Inland from the Marina on the far side of Sheikh Zayed Road, with a school inside the community itself, which is unusual in this part of Dubai. JBR families occasionally use schools here, and the run back along Al Thanya Street is quicker than the Al Barsha alternative.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Connected to JBR by a footbridge and a short road link, so households on the island run on effectively the same schedule as the towers. The same absence of a school inside the development applies, and the same scatter across Al Sufouh and Al Barsha follows from it.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Both close enough to appear on a JBR family's school shortlist and both reached on roads that clog in the afternoon rather than the morning. If a child is collected from either, treat 6.30pm as the earliest sensible session and keep a second slot later in the week.

schoolClusters.city: Secondary schools nearest JBR, in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: The schools most JBR secondary pupils attend, all inspected annually by KHDA on its published six-band scale. Exam boards differ between them and sometimes between departments, which is why a coverage audit starts with the syllabus code rather than the school name.

schoolClusters.city: Schools inland and along the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: Secondary options a little further out that appear regularly on JBR families' lists, usually where a sibling is already enrolled or a specific programme is wanted. Programme offerings and inspection outcomes change, so confirm both with the school and on the regulator's own site.

sections.heading: What a JBR parent is usually asking, under the search they typed
paragraphs: The search is for a tutor. The question underneath it is almost always some version of: the school seems fine, the teachers seem good, the reports are not alarming, so why does my child's work look thinner than I expected? That is a reasonable question and it has a specific answer in this part of Dubai, where school quality is inspected annually and generally decent.

The answer is that a taught course and an examined course are not the same object. A scheme of work is a plan for covering a syllabus in the lessons available, and every such plan contains compromises: strands given one lesson instead of three, components mentioned rather than practised, past papers sat twice a year rather than twenty times. Those compromises are not failures of teaching. They are arithmetic, and they are the same arithmetic in every school in the emirate.

What varies is which compromises a particular department made this year, and whether your child happened to be absent, distracted or behind when the thin strand went past. That is why the useful diagnostic is not the report, which gives a grade, but a strand-level check against the published syllabus, which gives a map. A grade tells you how far behind a child is. A map tells you where.

The second thing a JBR parent is often asking without saying it is which tutor the building uses. In a community with no school inside it and a dozen destinations outside it, that question has no answer: a tutor who was excellent for a child sitting Pearson 4MA1 may be the wrong purchase for a child sitting Cambridge 0580, and both live in your tower. The matching variable here is the syllabus code, not the postcode.
bullets: Inspection-good teaching still leaves thin strands; that is arithmetic, not failure
A report gives a grade; an audit gives a strand-level map

sections.heading: What a school lesson delivers, and what the household has to supply
paragraphs: Dividing the course honestly into school work and household work is the most useful thing a family can do in September, because most of the second column never gets allocated to anyone. Schools deliver content coverage, structured practice during lessons, marked assessment at intervals, feedback on that assessment, and the administration of entries and internal deadlines. That is a substantial amount and it is what fees pay for.

What schools do not deliver, because no timetable can, is volume. A full past paper takes between an hour and two and a half hours to sit and a similar time to review properly. A student who sits twenty papers across a two-year IGCSE course has spent somewhere near sixty hours doing it, and that time does not exist inside the school week. The same is true of vocabulary learning in a language, of the descriptive memorisation in Chemistry, and of retrieval across a wide syllabus in Biology.

There is a third column that belongs to nobody by default, and it is where most lost marks live: the metacognitive skills. Reading a mark scheme and predicting where marks sit. Recognising what a command term is asking for. Knowing whether an answer is finished. Deciding which question to attempt first in a paper. These are teachable in a handful of sessions and they are not on any scheme of work.

The table below sets out the split. The point of reading it is not to criticise a school; it is to work out which column your household has quietly been leaving empty, because that is where a tutor earns their fee rather than duplicating a lesson your child has already sat.

sections.heading: How to audit coverage without arguing with the school
paragraphs: A coverage audit sounds adversarial and should not be. The purpose is not to prove a department skipped something; it is to find out what this particular child can do, strand by strand, so that money is spent on three strands instead of on a subject. Most heads of department are perfectly willing to help, and several will hand over the scheme of work if asked plainly.

The method is mechanical. Start with the published syllabus for the exact code the school enters for — ask the exams officer in writing for the code, the tier and the series, subject by subject, because departments inside one school sometimes differ. The syllabus document lists the strands in order with the learning objectives for each. That document, not a revision guide and not a textbook contents page, is the checklist.

Then test rather than ask. For each strand, a short timed question set, marked against the official mark scheme. Asking a student whether they have covered topic 4.3 produces an answer about whether they remember a lesson, not about whether they can answer a question on it. Fifteen minutes per strand across a subject produces a map in two sessions, and the map is usually surprising in both directions: strands the family worried about are secure, strands nobody mentioned are empty.

Finally, hand the map back. A strand-level list with timed evidence attached is a document a head of department can act on, and it frequently produces an in-school response — a revision clinic, a changed tier decision, a targeted set of homework — that costs nothing. Families who go straight to a weekly paid session skip that step, and sometimes pay for something the school would have supplied.
