sections.heading: Mark-scheme literacy: the skill that transfers across every subject
paragraphs: Of all the things a student can be taught outside school, this one has the best return and the fewest tutors selling it. An examination mark scheme is a public document that states, in order, what earns credit in each question. A student who has read several of them starts to see questions differently: not as prompts to write about a topic, but as structures with a fixed number of places where marks live.

The practical difference shows up in extended answers. A six-mark explanation in IGCSE Physics has roughly six places where credit sits, and a student who writes three fluent sentences about the right topic can collect two of them. The same student, after four sessions on mark schemes, writes shorter and scores higher, because they have learned to make six discrete creditable statements instead of one coherent paragraph.

The same skill reads command terms properly. Describe, explain, suggest, evaluate, justify, compare and discuss are not interchangeable, and in both IGCSE and the Diploma they carry fixed expectations. A student who answers an explain question with a description has not misunderstood the content; they have answered a different question. That is a vocabulary problem and it is fixable in a fortnight.

Teaching it requires nothing exotic: official past papers, official mark schemes, and somebody who makes the student mark their own work before discussing it. The order matters. A student who marks first and discusses second learns the scheme. A student who is told their mark learns their mark. We do not reproduce or supply board papers and schemes here — they are published by Cambridge, Pearson and the IB on their own sites, and the official copy is both the lawful one and the current one.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around JBR, with the rates attributed
paragraphs: Published rates in this part of Dubai span roughly an order of magnitude, and knowing why helps a family read a quote. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which generally buys a university student or a non-specialist generalist. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor working online. At the specialist end, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above and TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

In-home visits are priced differently because travel sits inside the rate. Bestimate's figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent tutors quoting up to AED 500. In JBR that travel is not nominal: a tutor coming into the towers at six in the evening is dealing with the tram corridor, visitor parking and a lift queue, and the rate reflects it whether or not it is itemised.

Monthly packages in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All of those figures belong to the providers and tables that published them, read in October 2026.

What this page recommends buying changes the arithmetic rather than the rate. An audit plus targeted teaching on three strands is a bounded purchase with a stated end, whereas a weekly hour for a year is an open one. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, with the scope written down in sessions and strands, because a figure printed on a page would be a figure we had to defend rather than one a family could rely on.

sections.heading: A home tutor in a JBR tower against one-to-one online
paragraphs: Families here do search for a home tutor, and the question deserves an answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring exists across Dubai, it costs more per hour because travel is priced into it, and the pool is whoever will come to the Marina strip at the hour you want. Bestimate's Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independents quoting to AED 500.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video. On the specific question this page is about — finding and closing thin strands against a named syllabus code — the online arrangement is materially better, because the tutor has to be matched on the code rather than on driving distance. In a community where one tower holds students on two different boards, that is not a small difference.

There is a practical point about tower living that cuts the other way and is worth naming. Flats are small, and a JBR family may genuinely have nowhere quiet for a video lesson if two children study at the same table. The workable arrangements we see are staggered slots rather than simultaneous ones, a bedroom with a door for the older child, and headphones with a microphone rather than a laptop speaker. That is a real constraint and it is solvable with scheduling rather than with a visitor.

The third consideration is continuity. JBR is a high-turnover community; families move within the Marina strip, to Abu Dhabi, or out of the UAE entirely on a two- or three-year cycle. A relationship built over video survives all three. An in-home arrangement ends at the lease.

sections.heading: The independent components, and the deadlines nobody imposes
paragraphs: For Diploma students in this area the thin thing is rarely content. It is the set of components produced largely outside lessons: the internal assessment in every subject, the 4,000-word Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. Those carry a fixed share of subject grades plus three of the 45 available points, and they run on deadlines the student has to impose on themselves.

The failure pattern is identical across subjects. A research question is chosen late and too broadly, data or reading is gathered without a plan, and a draft appears in the fortnight before a school deadline. At that point the only available help is the kind nobody should buy. Everything useful happens earlier: narrowing the question so it can actually be answered in the word limit, and setting intermediate dates that somebody checks.

For IGCSE students the equivalent is smaller but real. Coursework routes in English, fieldwork-style investigations in Geography, programming tasks in Computer Science and portfolio work in Art all run on long horizons with soft deadlines. The same discipline applies: scope it down, write the intermediate dates into a calendar, and have somebody ask about them.

The boundary here is firm and we state it before any work starts. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria in the subject guide's own language, discuss a proposed question, model an approach on a different topic, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not become the author of assessed work. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting bought work is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

sections.heading: When a weekly session is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: A page recommending an audit owes families the cases where tutoring is not the answer at all. The first is a student whose audit comes back clean. If every strand is secure under timed conditions and the marks are still disappointing, the problem is execution — paper timing, question choice, careless loss — and that is a handful of sessions on technique rather than a year of teaching.

The second is a student who is not doing the household column. No amount of weekly teaching compensates for zero timed papers and no retrieval. In that case the useful purchase is the routine: set it up in two or three sessions, check monthly, and spend nothing else until the student is actually running it. Buying a weekly hour instead usually produces a student who is tutored and still unpractised.

The third is a thin strand the school is about to teach properly. Schemes of work sometimes schedule a topic late for sound reasons, and paying to pre-teach it in October duplicates a lesson coming in January. The audit catches this, which is one of the reasons to do the audit before buying anything.

The fourth is a timetable that has no room left. A Diploma student with six subjects, three internal assessments live and an Extended Essay deadline does not need a seventh commitment on a Tuesday evening. Sometimes the honest advice is to drop an activity, not to add a session. We will say that, because a session a student resents is money spent teaching them that help is a burden.

sections.heading: Getting started from a JBR address
paragraphs: The first useful message is short and specific: which school, which subjects, and the syllabus code and tier for each if you have them. If you do not have the codes, the one email worth sending goes to the exams officer asking for the syllabus code, the tier and the series for each subject in writing. Departments inside one school sometimes differ, so ask subject by subject rather than accepting a single answer.

Then a free trial lesson with the specialist who would actually teach the subject — one lesson, no card details, no commitment. Its second purpose is the start of the audit: timed questions across two or three strands, marked against the official scheme, so the first conversation afterwards is about evidence rather than impressions.

After that, a strand map and a quote with a scope: how many sessions, aimed at which strands, with a timed check closing each one. If the map says the real problem is the household column rather than the taught course, we will say that and quote for the smaller thing. If it says the school is about to cover the strand anyway, we will say that too.

On scheduling, be realistic about the route. A child collected from Al Barsha is unlikely to be settled before 5.15pm, and from Jumeirah Park later still, so the first slot we will suggest is 6.30pm or 7pm rather than the 4pm most providers offer. Sessions can move later during Ramadan to a post-Iftar time, and can continue through the summer if the family is in Dubai, at whatever hour actually works.

faqs.question: Are there any schools inside JBR itself?
faqs.answer: No. JBR is a residential development of towers along The Walk with no school inside it, so every child commutes out — most often west into Al Sufouh, inland to Al Barsha, or across Sheikh Zayed Road towards Jumeirah Park. That scatter is the defining practical fact about tutoring here: one building holds children at a dozen different schools on at least two exam boards, which is why asking the neighbours which tutor to use produces a worse answer here than in a villa community with a school in the middle.

faqs.question: My child's school seems good and the reports are fine. Why is the work still thin?
faqs.answer: Because a taught course and an examined course are different objects. A scheme of work covers a whole syllabus in a fixed number of lessons, which means every subject has strands given one lesson instead of three and components mentioned rather than practised. That is arithmetic, not poor teaching, and it happens in every school in Dubai regardless of inspection band. A report gives you a grade; what you need is a strand-level map showing which parts your child can actually do under timed conditions.

faqs.question: What exactly is a coverage audit, and how long does it take?
faqs.answer: It is two or three sessions that produce a list rather than a lesson. The tutor takes the published syllabus for the exact code the school enters for, sets short timed question sets across every strand, marks them against the official scheme, and classifies each strand as secure, shaky or not met. Fifteen minutes per strand produces a map of a whole subject in about two sessions. The result is usually three or four genuinely thin strands, which is a far smaller purchase than a year of weekly teaching.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's department uses?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the syllabus code, the tier and the series for each subject in writing. Ask subject by subject, because departments inside one school sometimes use different boards: Mathematics may be Cambridge 0580 while Chemistry is Pearson 4CH1. This matters more than it sounds. Buying past papers for the wrong code means practising the wrong paper structure for two years, and it is the commonest wasted effort we see from families in this part of Dubai.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a student actually sit?
faqs.answer: More than a school timetable can contain, which is why this is household work. A full paper takes one to two and a half hours to sit and a similar time to review properly, so twenty papers across a two-year IGCSE course is somewhere near sixty hours. Schools typically run two to four as mocks. The gap is real and it is nobody's responsibility by default. Setting a weekly volume per subject, and sticking to it, does more for most students than an additional teaching hour.

faqs.question: What is mark-scheme literacy, and can it be taught quickly?
faqs.answer: It is the ability to look at a question and see where the marks sit, and it is usually four to six sessions of work that then transfers across every subject. A six-mark explanation has roughly six places where credit lives, and a student who writes three fluent sentences about the right topic collects two of them. After learning to read schemes, the same student writes shorter answers and scores more. The method is simple: official past paper, official mark scheme, and the student marks their own work before any discussion.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, suggest, evaluate and justify, in that order, because each is routinely answered as though it said describe. In both IGCSE and the Diploma these terms carry fixed expectations: explain wants a causal chain, suggest wants an applied idea for an unfamiliar context, evaluate wants both sides and a judgement, justify wants a reason attached to a choice. A student answering an explain question with a description has not misunderstood the content, they have answered a different question, and that is a vocabulary fix rather than a teaching course.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a child at school in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Plan for 6.30pm. A child collected around 3.15pm from Al Barsha faces the afternoon peak on Sheikh Zayed Road or Umm Suqeim Road, and is rarely home, fed and at a desk before 5.15pm. From Jumeirah Park, with the interchange in the way, it is later. The 4pm slot that most providers offer first is exactly the slot that gets cancelled twice a month. An online session can also move by half an hour on a bad evening instead of being lost, which matters more than it sounds across a year.

faqs.question: Both my children study at the same table in our flat. Does online tutoring work?
faqs.answer: It works with scheduling rather than with more space. The arrangements that hold in JBR towers are staggered slots instead of simultaneous ones, a bedroom with a door for whichever child is in a session, and a headset with a microphone rather than a laptop speaker so the tutor hears the student and the student is not competing with the room. It is a genuine constraint and worth telling us about at the start, because it changes which slots we offer rather than whether the lessons work.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors charge around JBR and the Marina?
faqs.answer: Published figures as of October 2026: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the generalist end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor online; TutorChase lists AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the specialist and premium end. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and exam-year specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above. Those are their figures; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Do tutors come into the JBR towers, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. In-home tutoring does exist in Dubai at published rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and in JBR that travel is not nominal — the tram corridor, visitor parking and a lift queue at six in the evening are all real. For the work this page describes, matching on the exact syllabus code matters far more than proximity, and that search cannot be geographic.

faqs.question: My daughter understood a topic last year and got it wrong in the mock. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly decay rather than misunderstanding, which is a retrieval problem. A wide syllabus taught over two years is examined all at once, and knowledge learned in Year 10 and never revisited is not available in a Year 11 mock. The fix is unglamorous: twenty minutes of self-testing, three times a week, across everything covered so far rather than re-reading the current topic. It is the single highest-value study habit available and almost nobody adopts it without being taught the method explicitly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Diploma internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state before any work starts. A tutor may teach the subject skill, explain the criteria in the subject guide's own language, discuss a proposed research question, model an approach on a different topic, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not author any part of assessed work. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting bought work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: When is a weekly tutoring session the wrong thing to buy?
faqs.answer: Four cases. When the audit comes back clean and the marks are still poor, because that is execution and needs a few sessions on technique. When the student is doing no timed practice and no retrieval, because teaching cannot substitute for the household column. When the thin strand is scheduled properly next term and paying now duplicates it. And when a Diploma week already has six subjects, three live internal assessments and an Extended Essay deadline in it, where the honest advice is sometimes to drop something rather than add a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue through Ramadan and over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the time changed rather than the plan. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works better online than it does with a visitor travelling across the city late in the evening. Over the summer, families who remain in Dubai often keep a reduced schedule — one session a week rather than two — aimed at the strands the audit flagged, and families who travel pause or continue at whatever hour their timezone allows, since nothing about the arrangement depends on being in the Emirates.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist start for a subject in the final term?
faqs.answer: For the common combinations — Mathematics, the three sciences, English at either board, most Diploma subjects at Standard Level — usually within a few days, because the search is by syllabus code rather than by neighbourhood. Scarcer requests take longer: Higher Level Further Mathematics, a specific Group 2 language, Theatre, or a Literature set text in an early-evening Gulf slot. Where we cannot match within a useful window we say so with an honest estimate rather than offering an adjacent specialism and hoping it passes.

dubai/jbr.closingBody: If you are in JBR and the reports are fine but the work is not, the cheapest useful step is not a weekly tutor. It is one email to the exams officer asking for the syllabus code, tier and series for each subject in writing, and then a strand-level check against that published syllabus under timed conditions. Send us the codes and a free trial lesson follows, delivered live online after the Al Sufouh or Al Barsha run, with timed questions in it rather than a sales conversation. You will get a written strand map, and a quote that names the strands it is for.

dubai/jebel-ali.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both IGCSE boards. For Jebel Ali households the first question we ask is not which subject, but what time the bus gets home, because that decides everything else.

intro.heading: A district with two halves and one difficult afternoon
paragraphs: Jebel Ali is not one place. The name covers a long-established residential village of low-rise villas and the apartment blocks of The Gardens near Ibn Battuta, and it also covers the industrial area, the free zone and the port, which is one of the largest man-made harbours in the world. Families live in the first half and a large number of them work in the second, or in the logistics and freight businesses that cluster around it. Which half of Jebel Ali your address sits in changes your school options, your commute and the hour at which a lesson can realistically start.

Those three things are linked more tightly here than in central Dubai. The residential pockets are spread out, the schools serving them sit along the E11 and the Al Yalayis corridor rather than inside the communities, and the port side runs on shifts rather than office hours. A family in a Marina tower can assume a 17:00 session will work. A family in Jebel Ali Village with a child bussed to a school near Jumeirah Village cannot assume anything until they have timed the return journey for a fortnight.

That is why this page is organised around a clock rather than around subjects. The academic content is the same here as anywhere in Dubai; what differs is the number of hours left in the day and how predictable they are. Tutoring arrangements in this district fail far more often from scheduling than from teaching, and the pattern is recognisable: a 17:30 slot agreed in September, missed twice in October because the bus was late, moved once, then quietly abandoned by November.

The fix is not more discipline. It is a slot chosen from evidence. If the bus consistently reaches The Gardens at 16:10, a 16:30 start works and a 17:30 start wastes the best part of the afternoon. If a DP2 student travels from Jumeirah Village and reaches home at 17:00 exhausted, the right answer may be a 19:30 session after dinner or a Saturday morning, and either is better than an hour spent staring at a screen in a state of collapse.

What follows sets out the two Jebel Alis and their different school routes, the real shape of the afternoon commute, how to pick a slot from bus times, what Ramadan and the UAE term calendar do to a revision plan, what travel does to a tutor's rate, how holding a slot across a whole year actually works, and what the ten weeks before papers should look like hour by hour. All of it is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visiting exists only in our India service.

A slot chosen from two weeks of actual arrival times survives the year; a guessed one does not

dubai/jebel-ali.programmesIntro: Three programmes run across the schools this district uses. The notes below are about what each one demands of a student's unsupervised time, because that is the scarce resource here.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects sat across two years, with Cambridge using four-digit syllabus codes and a Core and Extended split, and Pearson Edexcel using codes such as 4MA1 with modular entry on some subjects. The workload is manageable in school hours until the final two terms, when past-paper practice has to happen outside them and there is no timetabled slot for it.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving Jebel Ali enter for both boards, sometimes differently by department. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge runs June and November series with a March series in some regions, so the revision calendar depends on which board and series your school uses.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The structural problem for a commuting student is that the Diploma assumes a substantial quantity of independent work, and a ninety-minute daily round trip removes most of the time it was supposed to occupy.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every IB session, upload and results date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than relying on a third-party page. This site publishes no IB dates, because none could be verified from the IB directly for this project, and school internal deadlines sit weeks earlier anyway.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, totalling thirty-two and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. Tasks assess some criteria and not others, so a student who revises content for a task weighted towards process or communication sees no movement and concludes that effort does not pay.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision near Jebel Ali sits mainly in the Dubai Investments Park cluster, so this stage normally comes with a bus journey attached. Families should expect the first MYP year to dip for logistical reasons as much as academic ones, and should not over-interpret it.

dubai/jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most requested across this district, described by the specific marks at stake rather than by syllabus headings.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The Core and Extended decision fixes a grade ceiling before any paper is sat. Within the paper, marks are lost on unshown method and on misreading what a question demands, both of which respond quickly to timed practice with a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Circuit reasoning under changed conditions is the IGCSE sticking point; the shift from recall to derivation is the Diploma one. Uncertainty handling in practical work is examinable and almost never deliberately practised.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic mechanisms carry most of the lost marks. The Diploma internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to measure with available equipment, which is where a supervising tutor earns their hour.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The content volume pushes students towards rereading rather than answering. Marks follow command terms precisely, so a description written where an explanation was demanded earns nothing at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Reasoning marks dominate, so a correct answer with no justification collects a fraction of what is available. Higher Level adds a long problem-solving paper that rewards persistence, which is hard to build in short sessions after a long commute.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application rather than recall earns the marks: a framework named but not applied to the stimulus loses the analysis credit. The internal assessment depends on an organisation that will supply real figures, and port-side families often have good access to one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision decides grades, and an unlabelled axis costs marks the prose cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative work, and the commentaries need published articles that will actually support the required analysis.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and comprehension under time pressure. The common loss is register: a student who writes a good essay in the wrong form for the stated audience loses marks that have nothing to do with their English.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into one or two awards, which punishes gaps rather than rewarding depth. Students weak at rearranging formulae lose the same marks repeatedly across physics and chemistry sections.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Taught in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Children arriving in Dubai after the early primary years need script and vocabulary work at a pace the timetable cannot set individually.

dubai/jebel-ali.regionsIntro: Each neighbouring area changes one thing for a Jebel Ali household: how long the return journey takes and therefore which slot survives the term.

regions.name: The Gardens and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment living beside Ibn Battuta with metro access and short bus routes to the nearest schools. Children here are often home by 16:00, which makes an early slot genuinely workable and distinguishes them from villa households further south.

regions.name: Jebel Ali Village
regions.note: Low-rise villas with the longest internal road loop in the district. The bus takes longer to clear the village than it does to cover the E11, so arrival times run fifteen to twenty minutes later than The Gardens.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Denser housing with its own schools and a metro connection on the Route 2020 line. A common destination for Jebel Ali children, and a route that moves well except between 15:00 and 16:30.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Where many older Jebel Ali students travel for British-curriculum places. The longest daily journey in this group, and the reason a number of DP2 students here take 19:30 or weekend sessions.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community
regions.note: The nearest IB continuum and Indian-curriculum provision. The route inland is quicker than the coastal one at peak, which is why some families choose school by traffic direction rather than by prospectus.

regions.name: Dubai South and Emaar South
regions.note: Further south towards the airport, with shift-working households and a shared scheduling problem. Families in both districts find weekend mornings more reliable than weekday evenings.

regions.name: Jebel Ali Industrial Area and the free zone
regions.note: Workplace rather than residence for most families, but the location that shapes the household day. Shift changeovers determine when a parent is available, which matters for primary children who need someone nearby during a session.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali Village, The Gardens and the port side
schoolClusters.note: The schools closest to residential Jebel Ali, covering British, Indian and IB provision. Several have been running long enough to have established upper year groups, which is the main advantage of staying local rather than travelling north.

schoolClusters.city: Al Furjan, Jumeirah Village and the E11 corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where families travel for additional British-curriculum capacity and wider sixth-form choice. The trade is thirty to fifty minutes each way at peak, which is the single biggest determinant of what time a lesson can start.

sections.heading: Two Jebel Alis, and which one you live in
paragraphs: Ask a tutoring provider about Jebel Ali and you will get an answer about Dubai. Ask a Jebel Ali parent and the first thing they tell you is whether they are in the village, in The Gardens, or out towards the industrial side, because those are different lives. The village is low-rise villas on a long internal loop, with the oldest school provision in the district. The Gardens is apartment living next to a metro station and a mall, with short bus routes. The industrial area and free zone are where the working day happens rather than where children sleep.

Each of those produces a different tutoring request. Apartment households in The Gardens ask about space and noise as much as about subjects, because two children doing homework in a two-bedroom flat is a real constraint and a lesson on a shared screen needs somewhere to sit. Village households ask about the length of the bus route. Port-side households ask whether a session can be moved when a shift changes, and are relieved to hear that it can.

The practical reason to establish this first is that advice does not transfer between them. A neighbour in The Gardens whose son has a 16:15 slot is not describing an arrangement a village family can copy, because the bus reaches the village later. A colleague on a day shift cannot tell you how to schedule around nights. Almost every failed arrangement in this district started with a slot copied from someone whose afternoon looked different.

So the first step, before choosing a tutor at all, is boring and effective: write down the actual arrival time at home, every day, for two weeks. Not the school finish time, not what the bus timetable says, the time the front door opens. Two weeks of that produces an honest picture, including the days that run late, and the slot chosen from it will still be working in March.

sections.heading: What the afternoon actually looks like on the E11 and Al Yalayis corridor
paragraphs: The journey home in this district is not symmetrical with the journey out. Morning runs start early enough to beat the worst of the traffic, and the school bus leaves before seven for routes heading north. The return is a different problem, because school finish times across Dubai cluster within an hour of each other and because the E11 carries the city's freight as well as its commuters. A route that takes twenty-five minutes at ten in the morning can take fifty at half past three.

Two particular pressure points matter. The first is the stretch of the E11 between the Jebel Ali interchange and the Jumeirah Village exits, which carries school buses, commercial traffic and commuters simultaneously in the mid-afternoon. The second is the Al Yalayis corridor towards Al Furjan and the inland communities, which moves well outside peak and poorly within it. Families who switch school for academic reasons sometimes discover they have also switched their afternoon by half an hour in each direction.

The metro changes this for some households and not others. The Route 2020 extension put stations within reach of Al Furjan and the Expo site, and the main line serves Ibn Battuta and the stations near The Gardens, which makes an independent journey realistic for a teenager whose school is near a station. For a child whose school is not, the metro is irrelevant and the bus is the only variable that matters.

The conclusion is not that Jebel Ali is badly connected, because it is well connected for a district built around a port. It is that the commute has to be measured rather than assumed before a weekly commitment is made. Every family in this district who has lost a tutoring arrangement to scheduling lost it to an assumption about the return journey.

sections.heading: Choosing a slot from the bus times rather than the bell
paragraphs: Once you have two weeks of real arrival times, the choice becomes arithmetic. Add twenty minutes for getting in, changing and eating something; that is not optional and a session that ignores it starts with a resentful child. Then look at what is left before the point at which your child stops being useful, which for most students under fourteen is around 19:00 and for most Diploma students is closer to 21:30.

The mistake almost everyone makes is to choose the middle of that window. If the door opens at 16:10 and a child is finished by 19:00, the instinct is to book 17:30, which leaves an hour of drift before and an hour of tiredness after. A 16:40 start uses the sharpest part of the window and leaves the evening free for homework, which is the thing most likely to be abandoned when a session runs late.

For the longest journeys the arithmetic produces a different answer entirely. A DP2 student reaching home at 17:15 from a school near Jumeirah Village has no good weekday hour at all: too late to start before dinner, too tired afterwards to do anything demanding. The honest recommendation in that case is a weekend morning for the main session and a twenty-minute weekday review, and we would rather say that in the first conversation than sell a weekday slot that will fail in week four.

Primary children need the opposite of flexibility. Short, frequent and early beats long and late every time at that age, because fluency work responds to repetition rather than duration. Thirty minutes at 16:30 twice a week, with five minutes of daily practice, outperforms an hour at 18:00 by a wide margin, and it fits a Jebel Ali afternoon far better.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE calendar breaks twice a year with complete predictability. During Ramadan the school day shortens, which changes arrival times for every child in the district, and the household rhythm moves around Iftar. Most families here settle on post-Iftar sessions for teenagers, which works well because older students are often studying late anyway, and reduce or pause sessions for younger children, which is sensible rather than a failure of commitment.

Eid and the term breaks matter in a different way. The weeks immediately after a long break are when content gaps become visible, because anything half-understood before the break has decayed over it. A student who was coping in the last week of a term and struggling in the first week of the next has not got worse; they have stopped being carried by short-term memory. That is a predictable moment to schedule a review session rather than a crisis.

The long summer is the biggest structural feature of the year, and the one most often wasted. For students going into an examination year, a small amount of work across the summer is worth more than any amount of catch-up in October, because it protects the content that otherwise has to be relearned. Four or five sessions spread across the break, with short practice between them, is enough. Twenty sessions in August is not better and usually produces resentment.

The practical approach is to agree the whole year in advance: which weeks run normally, which weeks shorten, which weeks pause entirely, and which weeks are protected regardless. The protected weeks are the four before mocks and the six before a public examination series. Everything else can move. Writing that down in September is what makes a Jebel Ali arrangement survive to March, and it takes ten minutes.

sections.heading: What travel does to the rate, and what the market charges
paragraphs: A tutor driving to Jebel Ali Village for a 17:00 lesson leaves their own area around 16:00 and is not home before 19:00. That is three hours for one paid hour, and the consequences are arithmetic rather than opinion. The rate absorbs the travel, the tutor can see fewer students a week, and the pool available to you shrinks to people who live close enough and are free at exactly that time. In a district on the edge of the city, that pool is small.

The market figures below were collected in October 2026 and each row names who published it. They are market rates, not an IB Gram price list, and the pattern they show is consistent: in-home delivery sits above online delivery at every level, because travel is inside the price whether or not anyone itemises it. Bestimate's Dubai figures put home visits in a higher band than online lessons across the board.

The second effect is the one that actually costs families marks rather than money. Subject depth is unevenly distributed across any city, and the number of people who can teach Higher Level Physics or the quantitative half of Higher Level Economics properly is limited. Filter that group by willingness to drive to Jebel Ali at five in the afternoon and most of them are gone. A parent who insists on a tutor in the room is choosing proximity over specialism, which in an examination year is the wrong trade.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the choice is not one we can sell either way. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, which means the hour costs an hour, the slot can move when a shift moves, and the tutor is selected on subject and level rather than on postcode. For this district that last point is the whole argument.

sections.heading: Holding a slot across a whole year
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this district do not end in a decision. They end in attrition: a missed session in October, a rescheduled one in November, a pause over a break that never restarts. Nobody chose that outcome and everybody recognises it. The causes are predictable and therefore manageable, and they are worth naming because the fix is procedural rather than motivational.

The first cause is a slot chosen optimistically. The second is a session cancelled rather than moved, which breaks the habit; a twenty-minute review on a different day keeps the thread alive where a cancellation severs it. The third is no written record, so neither parent nor student can say what was covered three weeks ago, and the sense that progress is happening quietly erodes. The fourth is no review date, so an arrangement that is not working continues until someone gets irritated enough to stop it.

What works against all four is dull. Choose the slot from two weeks of arrival data. Agree in advance that a late bus means a shortened session rather than a cancelled one. Take a written note after every session naming what was covered and what was set. And fix a review date six weeks out, where progress is checked against marked school work rather than against anyone's impression, with an explicit option to change the tutor or the plan.

That last point is where most providers are weak, because a review that can end an arrangement is commercially inconvenient. It is also the only thing that makes the arrangement worth keeping. If six weeks of work has not moved anything a teacher marked, the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is wrong, or the format is wrong, and adding hours to any of those three is the most expensive mistake available.

sections.heading: The ten weeks before papers, hour by hour
paragraphs: In the final stretch the constraint changes. Content learning stops being the best use of time, because anything learned in week eight will not be secure by the examination and the hours spent learning it displace the practice that moves marks. The work becomes timed papers, mark schemes, and the specific errors a student makes repeatedly. For a commuting Jebel Ali student, who has less unsupervised time than a classmate living near school, the sequencing matters more rather than less.

A realistic week in that period has three parts. One longer session with the tutor, best placed at a weekend morning when nobody is tired. Two or three self-directed timed papers, done at real length and self-marked against a scheme before anyone else looks at them. And short daily retrieval, ten or fifteen minutes on whatever the error log says is still wrong. The self-marking step is the one students skip and the one that teaches most, because it forces them to read a mark scheme as an examiner reads it.

The error log is the organising document. Every wrong answer gets one line: the question type, what the student did, what the scheme wanted. After three papers the pattern is obvious and usually narrow, which is the point. Most students are not losing marks across a syllabus; they are losing them in four or five recurring ways, and those are fixable in the time available.

During study leave the clock changes again, because school attendance stops being the structure and the paper timetable becomes it. Sessions move to the mornings of non-examination days, and the day before a paper is for light review rather than new work. We will also say, at the start of a ten-week block, what cannot be covered in the time remaining. A student who knows which two topics have been deliberately set aside revises better than one who believes everything is still in play.

Spaced retrieval on the four or five recurring mistakes
Confidence and recall, not new content

sections.heading: Getting started from Jebel Ali
paragraphs: Begin with the clock, not the subject. Send the actual arrival times at home for the last two weeks, the school and the syllabus code, the most recent marked piece of work, and the date of the next assessment. The arrival times are the part most families leave out and the part that determines whether the arrangement survives, so they matter as much as the academic information.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor reads the marked work with the student and separates four problems that look identical on a report: content not known, technique not trained, timing lost under pressure, confidence gone. You get a written summary naming which, and a recommended slot based on your own arrival data rather than on a standard template.

Then the limits, stated before any payment. We do not promise grades. We do not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE, so if you want someone at the door we are the wrong provider and will say so immediately. We do not supply board past papers or mark schemes, which belong to the boards and are held officially by your school. And where a scarce specialism is involved, the match may take longer than a week or the only available tutor may work hours that suit an early morning, and you will hear that before you commit rather than after.

One practical suggestion for the first month. Ask your child to be in the session rather than near it: logged in, with the exercise book, the marked script and a pen, two minutes before the start. That sounds trivial and it is the difference between a sixty-minute lesson and a forty-five-minute one, repeated weekly across a year. In a district where the afternoon is already short, five minutes of setup lost every week is most of a session lost by March, and it is the easiest saving available to any household here.

process.title: Measure the afternoon
process.description: Record the time your child actually gets home for two weeks, including the late days. Not the school finish time and not the bus timetable. That data decides the slot, and a slot chosen from it is the single strongest predictor of whether an arrangement lasts the year.

process.title: Send the academic four
process.description: School, exact syllabus code and tier, most recent marked work, and the date of the next assessment. For a Diploma student add the internal assessment deadlines the school has set, which sit earlier than anything the board publishes.

process.title: Diagnostic session
process.description: One online hour reading the marked work with the student to establish whether the problem is content, technique, timing or confidence. The written summary names which, and recommends a format: short and twice weekly, or longer and weekend-anchored.

process.title: Agree the year, not just the week
process.description: Mark which weeks run normally, which shorten for Ramadan, which pause for breaks, and which are protected regardless. The protected weeks are the four before mocks and the six before a public examination series. Ten minutes in September prevents most of the attrition.

process.title: Six-week review against marked work
process.description: Progress is checked on something a teacher marked, with an explicit option to change the tutor, the format or the diagnosis. If nothing has moved, adding hours is the wrong response and we will say so rather than extending the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The slot is chosen from evidence
whyPoints.description: Two weeks of real arrival times beat any assumption about when a lesson should happen. Most failed arrangements in this district died of a scheduling error in week four, not of bad teaching, and that is a solvable problem.

whyPoints.title: Shortened, not cancelled
whyPoints.description: A late bus turns a sixty-minute session into a thirty-minute one rather than into a missed week. Keeping the habit alive matters more than the lost half hour, and cancellations are what quietly end tutoring arrangements here.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, because nobody has to drive
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the tutor is chosen for the subject, level and board rather than for living near the E11. For Higher Level sciences and quantitative subjects, where local supply is thin, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is available.

whyPoints.title: A calendar agreed in September
whyPoints.description: Ramadan timing, term breaks, mock weeks and the protected weeks before papers are all written down at the start. Plans that survive to March are the ones that anticipated the UAE year rather than reacting to it.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no invented statistics, no accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. Every AED figure names its publisher, and every board date names the board that set it.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson realistically start for a child bussed out of Jebel Ali Village?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect. The bus takes fifteen to twenty minutes simply to clear the village loop, on top of the journey itself, so arrival times here run behind those in The Gardens. Allow twenty minutes after the door opens for changing and eating, then start. For a village household with a Year 9 child arriving at 16:20, a 16:45 start works well. For a DP2 student arriving at 17:15 from a school near Jumeirah Village, no weekday slot is good and a weekend morning is the honest answer.

faqs.question: Why is a 17:30 slot usually the wrong choice here?
faqs.answer: Because it sits in the middle of the usable window and wastes both ends. A child who gets home at 16:10 drifts for eighty minutes, arrives at the session already disengaged, and then has homework to do when the session ends and tiredness has set in. Starting at 16:40 uses the sharpest part of the afternoon and leaves the evening clear. The instinct to leave a comfortable gap after school is understandable and it is the most common scheduling mistake in this district.

faqs.question: Does the metro make a difference to tutoring arrangements?
faqs.answer: For some households only. The main line serves Ibn Battuta and the stations near The Gardens, and the Route 2020 extension put stations within reach of Al Furjan and the Expo site, so a teenager whose school sits near a station can travel independently and arrive predictably. For a child whose school is not near a station the metro is irrelevant and the bus remains the only variable that matters. Predictability is the real benefit rather than speed, because a predictable arrival makes a fixed slot possible.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for teenagers it usually works better than a daytime slot. School days shorten through the month, the household rhythm moves around the evening meal, and older students are frequently studying late anyway, so a post-Iftar session fits the actual pattern of the day. For primary children the sensible approach is to reduce frequency or pause, because a late session with a tired young child achieves little. Agreeing both arrangements in advance stops the month becoming an unplanned four-week gap.

faqs.question: My son is at school near Jumeirah Village. Is a weekday session possible at all?
faqs.answer: Possible, but rarely the best option. A Diploma student on that route reaches home around 17:00 to 17:30, which is too late to start anything demanding before dinner and too tired afterwards. The arrangement that holds is a ninety-minute weekend morning session as the anchor, plus an optional twenty-minute weekday review to keep momentum. That pattern survives the year, where a weekday evening slot in this situation typically fails somewhere in the fourth or fifth week.

faqs.question: What happens when the bus is late and we miss the start?
faqs.answer: The session shortens rather than disappearing. Thirty minutes of focused work on the planned objective is far more valuable than a cancellation, because cancellations are what end tutoring arrangements in this district. We agree this rule at the start so nobody has to make a decision under time pressure: if the arrival is late, the tutor works with whatever time remains and the written note records what was not reached, which goes first in the following session.

faqs.question: Are weekend mornings actually better for shift-working households?
faqs.answer: Consistently, yes. A weekday evening slot assumes a predictable end to the working day, which port-side, logistics and aviation rosters do not provide. A Saturday or Friday morning slot does not compete with a shift, nobody is tired, and no commute interferes. The pattern we recommend is a longer weekend session as the anchor with a short weekday check-in if it is useful, and we schedule against a published roster a month ahead rather than week by week.

faqs.question: Is it worth doing anything over the summer break?
faqs.answer: A small amount, placed well, is worth a great deal. For a student entering an examination year, four or five sessions across the break with short practice in between protects content that would otherwise need relearning in October. Twenty sessions in August is not better; it produces resentment and diminishing returns. The useful target is maintenance rather than progress: keep the hardest topics warm, keep the arithmetic or language fluency ticking, and arrive in September not having to start again.

faqs.question: Why do marks drop in the first week back after a long break?
faqs.answer: Because short-term memory was doing more work than anyone realised. A student who was coping in the final week of term and struggling in the first week of the next has not become weaker; the half-understood material has decayed and there is nothing underneath it. That is predictable and worth planning for: a review session in the first week back, aimed at the topics covered just before the break, costs one hour and prevents a term of compounding confusion.

faqs.question: Does a tutor travel to The Gardens or the village?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we operate only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. In this district that works in your favour twice over. A tutor driving here loses around three hours of their day for one paid hour, which is inside the rate whichever way it is itemised, and the people willing to make that drive are a small subset of the specialists available. Online, the tutor is chosen on subject and level alone.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs forty-five minutes or ninety?
faqs.answer: Age and arrival time decide it more than subject does. Under eleven, thirty to forty-five minutes twice a week beats a single long session, because fluency responds to frequency. Years 7 to 11 generally work well at forty-five to sixty minutes. Diploma students doing component work or timed papers need ninety, which is why that session belongs at a weekend when it will not follow a long commute. A long session after a fifty-minute bus ride wastes its last third.

faqs.question: What is an error log and why does it matter more than revision notes?
faqs.answer: It is one line per wrong answer: the question type, what the student did, and what the mark scheme wanted. Revision notes record what a student already understands; an error log records what they keep getting wrong, which is where the recoverable marks are. After three timed papers the pattern is usually narrow, four or five recurring mistakes rather than a whole syllabus, and that is a target a student can actually hit in the weeks available before a paper.

faqs.question: Do you tell us what cannot be covered before the exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, at the start of any final-stretch block. If ten weeks remain and three topics are substantially unlearned, attempting all of them produces shallow coverage of everything and secure knowledge of nothing. We name which topics are being deliberately set aside and why, so the student stops carrying the anxiety of an unbounded syllabus. Students who know what has been excluded revise more effectively than students who believe everything is still in play.

faqs.question: Who is allowed to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tuition runs on a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us to stop paying?
faqs.answer: A six-week review in which nothing a teacher marked has moved. At that point the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is the wrong match, or the format does not fit the household, and adding hours to any of those is the most expensive error available. We will say which we think it is and propose a change rather than an extension. We also make no grade promises, publish no success statistics, and hold no accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

dubai/jebel-ali.closingHeading: Start by timing the journey home
dubai/jebel-ali.closingBody: Before you choose a tutor for a child in this district, spend two weeks writing down what time they actually walk through the door. That single piece of information decides whether the arrangement you set up in September is still running in March, and it is the thing almost nobody records. Send it with the school, the syllabus code and the last marked piece of work, and one diagnostic hour online will tell you what the academic problem is and which slot and session length fit your afternoon. Where the honest answer is a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, we will say so rather than selling you a slot that will fail.

dubai/jlt.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma, IGCSE and Indian-curriculum subjects, and they are matched one per child rather than one per household. A tutor fluent in Cambridge 0580 is the wrong person for a CBSE Class 10 sibling, and we would rather send two specialists than one generalist.

intro.heading: Who actually lives in the JLT clusters, and why their school week is complicated
paragraphs: JLT is a cluster of towers around four artificial lakes, with a free zone threaded through it, two Metro stations on its edge and almost no low-rise anything. The households inside it are overwhelmingly apartment households, and a large share of the adults in them run or work for small companies licensed a few hundred metres from where they sleep. That produces a very particular family profile: two working parents, often with irregular hours, one or two children, and a flat with one spare room that is simultaneously an office, a study and a guest room.

The school picture follows from the economics rather than from a curriculum preference. Dubai licenses 17 curricula across 227 private schools, with UK-curriculum schools taking 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian-curriculum schools 26 per cent and International Baccalaureate 7 per cent in 2024-25. Indian-curriculum fees sit well below British-curriculum fees across the emirate, and the bus routes out of JLT run to both. The consequence, which we see constantly from this postcode, is a household where the older child is at a British-curriculum school sitting IGCSE and the younger is at an Indian-curriculum school, or the reverse, and neither parent chose that arrangement as a philosophy.

Running two systems at once is harder than running either one. The term calendars do not align: Indian-curriculum schools in the UAE usually run an April-to-March year and sit CBSE or ICSE board exams in February and March, while British-curriculum schools run September to July and sit IGCSE papers in May and June. That means one child's exam season is the other child's mid-year, every year, and a family holiday booked for one is a crisis for the other.

The report formats do not align either. One child comes home with percentages and a class rank; the other comes home with 9-to-1 grades or criterion letters A to D, and a tier decision nobody explained. A parent trying to compare the two children's progress is comparing two incompatible instruments, and the usual result is that the child on the less legible system gets less attention until something goes visibly wrong.

Then there is the practical matter of who is in the room at six o'clock. In a JLT household the adult who checks homework is frequently still at a desk two towers away, and the weekday window where a parent can supervise anything is narrow and late. That is not a failing; it is the shape of the community. It does mean that a tutoring arrangement which depends on a parent being present to let someone in, settle a child and hover nearby is an arrangement that collapses by the third week.

IB Gram works with this directly. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots, including late ones, with written notes after every session so a parent reading at nine o'clock knows exactly what happened. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a two-board household in a two-bedroom flat, a scheduled video session that needs nobody to arrive is the format that survives a real JLT week.

dubai/jlt.programmesIntro: A JLT household often needs to understand three systems rather than one. These are the four that appear most often in the same family, and the notes say what each does to a parent's week.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years per subject against a published syllabus code, assessed by terminal written papers with practical or alternative-to-practical components in the sciences. Cambridge subjects mostly split into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson specifications have their own paper architecture and in several subjects no separate practical exam.
programmes.countryNote: For a JLT parent the detail that matters is the tier. Core caps the achievable grade in most Cambridge subjects, the school decides at entry, and the decision is effectively fixed once final entries are submitted. A parent used to a system where everyone sits the same paper will not think to ask, and nobody volunteers it.

programmes.name: CBSE and other Indian-curriculum boards
programmes.description: An April-to-March academic year with board examinations in Class 10 and Class 12, reported as percentages, with internal assessment components in most subjects and no tiering. Content in Mathematics and the sciences typically runs ahead of the IGCSE Extended syllabus at the same age.
programmes.countryNote: The sibling comparison here is the thing parents get wrong. An 88 per cent in a CBSE subject is a solid result; a grade 6 at IGCSE is also a solid result; and neither converts into the other. Any tutor offering a conversion table is inventing it, because IGCSE boundaries are set per paper per series after marking.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups with three at Higher Level, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Scored out of 45 with 24 needed to pass. Every subject carries an internal assessment with a fixed share of the grade, produced largely outside lessons.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the heaviest programme on a household's evenings of any in this list, which matters in a flat with one quiet room. Families who move an older child into the Diploma while a younger sibling is preparing for board exams should expect the study-space negotiation to become the main domestic issue of that year.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against criteria A to D in each subject group, with a Personal Project in the final year, and marks reported as criterion levels rather than percentages. The command terms used are the same ones the Diploma will use later, which makes it good preparation and hard to read.
programmes.countryNote: Criterion letters are the single most common source of confusion in a two-board household, because they look like nothing else on the kitchen table. Read usefully, they are a skills map: strong on criterion A and weak on criterion D tells you which skill the next two years will punish, which no percentage ever does.

dubai/jlt.subjectsIntro: In a two-board household the same subject name means two different courses. Each note below says what the subject is in each system and where a sibling comparison misleads a parent.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1 / CBSE Class 10)
subjects.levels: Core, Extended and the Indian-curriculum course
subjects.description: A CBSE Class 10 student has met more content than IGCSE Extended requires, so the sibling who looks ahead on paper may be. What differs is marking: IGCSE pays for stated method, and the non-calculator paper has no Indian-curriculum equivalent. Comparing the two children's marks tells a parent nothing useful.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Numerical work is comfortable for most students in this corridor; six-mark explanation chains are not. The alternative-to-practical paper assesses experimental judgement — anomalous readings, control variables, unreliability — which neither a CBSE practical record nor a school lab lesson tests.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations transfer easily between systems. Qualitative analysis does not: the bank of tests, colours and precipitates is memorisation work that has to happen at home, and it accounts for a predictable block of lost marks in households where nobody has named it as a task.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The syllabus is wide and the terminal paper asks about all of it, so retention rather than coverage is the problem. IGCSE also expects its own wording for defined processes — osmosis, transpiration, enzyme specificity — where an accurate paraphrase earns less than the syllabus's phrasing.

subjects.name: English as a First or Second Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0510)
subjects.description: The decision between first-language and second-language English is often made for a transferring child by a school's placement test, and it has consequences at sixth form. Ask which specification your child is entered for and what the target sixth form or university accepts as proof of English before accepting the placement.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Diploma route expected by most engineering, physics and mathematics programmes, and the heaviest single subject on most timetables at Higher Level. Proof and series are the strands that most often need outside help, and the mathematical exploration needs imposed deadlines rather than teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led with technology permitted throughout, and a sensible choice for a wide range of destinations. Worth confirming against each target programme's own published prerequisite before the subject form goes in, because some engineering and mathematics courses specify the Analysis route.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry and Biology
subjects.description: Content coverage in Dubai Diploma schools is generally strong and the individual investigation is where students are alone. It is an open-ended experimental project assessed against criteria, and the usual failure is a research question chosen late and too broadly to yield usable data.

subjects.name: IB Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Popular with JLT households where a parent runs a business and the subject feels familiar at home. The internal assessments — article commentaries in Economics, a research project in Business Management — are produced outside lessons against criteria students rarely read closely, and supervision moves them more than teaching does.

subjects.name: Hindi, Urdu, Arabic and French as second languages
subjects.description: The second-language slot is usually the cheapest grade in the house to protect, especially where a child already speaks the language at home. Check which languages each school's option block offers, because siblings in two systems frequently cannot continue the same language.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and IB Computer Science
subjects.description: Students who code are usually ahead on algorithms and behind on theory: data representation, two's complement, packet switching and the fetch-execute cycle want the syllabus's own vocabulary. That half is solo learning and it is where the grade is decided.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education as mandatory subjects
subjects.levels: All year groups in Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. These periods occupy weekly timetable time in both of a household's schools, which reduces the free study time a parent is counting on.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: The nearest community with a school inside it, reached in minutes outside peak hours and reliably in traffic in the afternoon. A JLT child at school here is typically home earliest of all, which makes a 5.30pm session genuinely viable rather than theoretical.

regions.note: A substantial inland cluster of schools serving JLT, reached across Al Khail Road. The bus run is long rather than slow, and children often arrive home late and hungry, so a session before 6.30pm tends to be a session that gets rescheduled.

regions.name: The Meadows and Emirates Hills
regions.note: Reached inland through Emirates Living, with school buses that collect early and return late because the route serves several communities. Families on this run commonly choose two shorter sessions a week over one long one, simply because attention at 7pm is finite.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road and through the interchange, where the crossing rather than the distance is what costs time. This is one of the routes where an online slot that can shift by half an hour is worth more than a nominally earlier fixed one.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: A longer run against the afternoon peak, and the origin of most of the late arrivals we schedule around in this area. Plan for 6.30pm as a starting assumption, and keep the second weekly slot on a day with no after-school activity attached.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: The direction most Indian-curriculum provision for JLT lies in, which is why a two-board household often has two buses going two ways. Those buses rarely return at the same time, so the two children's sessions have to be staggered rather than stacked.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Immediately across Sheikh Zayed Road and on a similar household pattern: towers, small flats, no school inside the community. Sibling households split between the Marina strip and the JLT clusters usually find their evenings run on the same clock.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Dubai Media City
regions.note: Where several of the nearest secondary schools sit, reached on roads that clog in the afternoon rather than the morning. A child collected here is often home by 4.45pm, which makes this the one direction where an early-evening session holds reliably.

sections.heading: The JLT household types, and what each one's academic pressure point is
paragraphs: Communities get described in brochure language and it is useless for planning. What matters about JLT for tutoring purposes is that it contains four or five recognisable household shapes, and each has a different thing that goes wrong academically. Knowing which one you are in saves a term of guessing.

The first is the free-zone business household: one or both parents running a company licensed nearby, long and unpredictable hours, high engagement and low availability. Academic risk here is supervision rather than ability — nobody is home to notice a drift until a report lands. The second is the two-board household described throughout this page, where the risk is that the child on the less legible reporting system is under-attended for a year.

The third is the single-child professional household, often with both parents on corporate schedules and a child at a British-curriculum school some distance inland. The risk is over-scheduling: the child has three activities and a tutor, and no evening with nothing in it. The fourth is the transient household, here on a two-year posting, where the risk is a school and board change mid-course and predicted grades written by teachers who have known the child for six weeks.

The fifth is the multi-generational or shared household, common in the clusters, where a flat holds more people than bedrooms. The risk there is purely physical: there is no quiet place to work, and every academic plan that assumes one is fiction. That is solvable, but only if somebody says it out loud, which families are often reluctant to do.

sections.heading: Three boards in one household, compared properly
paragraphs: A parent running two systems needs one table rather than three conversations. The three that appear together most often in this part of Dubai are Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and CBSE Class 10, and they differ on almost every dimension that affects a family's planning: when the year starts, when exams fall, who decides what the child sits, how the result is reported, and what can still be changed.

The differences that cause the most trouble are tiering and timing. Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings and the school decides at entry; Pearson generally does not tier in the same way; CBSE does not tier at all. A parent whose first child sat a CBSE paper that everyone in the class sat will not think to ask which tier the second child has been entered at, and that single unasked question can cap a grade at 5.

Timing is the other. Cambridge runs June and November series with final entries months ahead — for its March 2027 series, final entries fell due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. CBSE board exams fall in February and March on an April-to-March year. One household therefore has entry deadlines, exam windows and results days scattered across the whole calendar.

Reporting is the third, and it is where sibling comparison does real harm. Percentages, 9-to-1 grades and criterion letters are different instruments measuring different things against different standards, and there is no conversion between them. Any tutor who offers one is guessing, because IGCSE grade boundaries are set per paper per series after marking precisely so that paper difficulty can be accounted for.

sections.heading: When the adult who checks homework is still at work
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement has hidden labour inside it, and in JLT that labour usually belongs to a parent who is not home. Someone has to admit a visitor, settle the child, keep a younger sibling out of the room, know what was covered, and follow up on what was set. In a villa community with a stay-at-home parent that is invisible overhead. In a free-zone household with two working adults it is the reason arrangements fail in week three.

The design that works here removes the adult from the critical path. A video session at an agreed time needs nobody to open a door. A written note afterwards — what was covered, what was set, what to ask the child about — means the parent can engage at nine o'clock instead of at six. And a consistent note format across two children on two boards means a parent can actually compare the two, which a verbal handover at the door never allows.

The second design choice is session timing. Most providers offer a 4pm or 5pm slot because it suits the tutor. In this community the honest window is later: after the inland bus run, after food, and often after a parent has come home. A 7pm or 7.30pm session that happens every week is worth considerably more than a 5pm session that is cancelled twice a month, and attention at 7.30pm with food inside a child is usually better than attention at 5pm without.

The third is what to do when a parent genuinely cannot engage at all for a period — a travel month, a company audit, a new baby. The answer is to reduce the number of moving parts rather than to add supervision: one subject instead of two, a fixed slot that never moves, and a monthly written summary rather than weekly engagement. Plans that depend on a parent's attention during their busiest quarter are plans that will fail in that quarter.
