sections.heading: What happens when a session has to move
paragraphs: Every family in this district will need to move a session. A match runs late, a sibling has a concert, the Al Wasl Road is closed, somebody is ill. How a tutoring arrangement handles that is worth more than the hourly rate, and almost nobody asks about it before booking.

With an in-home arrangement, a cancellation at short notice costs the tutor a journey they cannot recover, so in-home tutors reasonably charge for late cancellations and limit how flexible they can be. Their day is a route, and a hole in the route cannot be refilled from a different part of Dubai. That is not a criticism of in-home tutors; it is the economics of travel, and it is inside the AED 180 to 500 an hour the market charges for it.

Online, the same cancellation costs nobody a journey. A session can move to a different evening, or to a weekend morning, and the tutor can fill the original slot with a student in a different time zone. The practical consequence is that a Jumeirah 2 family gets flexibility without paying for it, and a session missed in a busy week becomes a session rescheduled rather than a session lost.

The second thing worth asking about is substitution. If a tutor leaves the country or is unwell for a fortnight, what happens? With a single in-home tutor the answer is usually nothing until they return. With a matched online specialist the answer should be a replacement from the same specialism, with the session notes handed over so the new tutor starts where the last one finished rather than from the beginning.

sections.heading: Protecting one hour is most of the intervention
paragraphs: This sounds too simple to be the main point, and it is the main point. The difference between tutoring that changes a grade and tutoring that changes nothing is usually not the tutor's expertise. It is whether the student did work between sessions and whether the sessions happened in sequence. Both of those are scheduling outcomes, and both are decided before any teaching starts.

A sequence works like this. The session identifies something specific, the student practises it during the week, the next session checks the practice and corrects what is still wrong, and the thing becomes automatic. Break the sequence and each session becomes a standalone lesson on a new topic, which produces understanding at the time and nothing durable. Three cancellations in a term is enough to convert the first pattern into the second.

So the one hour that needs protecting is not only the session. It is also the thirty to forty minutes of independent work that has to sit somewhere in the week. In a district where two or three evenings are committed to sport, that work has to be placed deliberately, usually on the same evening as the session or on a weekend morning, and it has to be named rather than hoped for.

Parents of younger children can do one further thing that outperforms almost any paid intervention: sit nearby for the practice, not to teach, but because presence changes whether it happens. For older students the equivalent is a visible weekly plan that the student writes and the parent sees, which is less intrusive and more effective than asking whether the homework is done.

sections.heading: Weekend and holiday tutoring: what families get wrong
paragraphs: Two mistakes recur. The first is treating weekends as sacred and then having no usable weekday hour, which means nothing happens at all. In a district with this much weekday commitment, one weekend morning session is often the only honest option, and it works perfectly well. Students do not learn less on a Saturday morning than on a Tuesday evening; they usually learn more, because they are not already tired.

The second is treating school holidays as a tutoring pause. Holidays are the only time this district has uninterrupted blocks, which makes them the right time for anything that needs a run at it: closing a diagnosed gap, bridging IGCSE content into the Diploma, collecting data for an internal assessment, or drafting an Extended Essay. A week of four or five sessions in July does more for a specific gap than a term of weekly sessions in October.

There is a caveat that matters here specifically. Families in Jumeirah 2 travel substantially over the summer, and a holiday intensive planned without reference to travel plans collapses. The useful conversation is which two weeks the family is actually in one place with a reliable connection, which may be abroad rather than in Dubai, and online delivery makes that location irrelevant.

The exception to all of this is the weeks immediately before an examination session. At that point adding new commitments is usually counterproductive, and the right move is light maintenance, timed past papers and sleep. Families who increase tutoring sharply in the final fortnight are generally buying reassurance rather than marks.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and what the rate does not include
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for Dubai tutoring searches publish no price, and the two that do quote in dollars. The AED figures here are market bands with their sources named. Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. Premium named tutors are advertised from AED 500 to 650. IB Gram quotes its own rate after a consultation, because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

What the hourly rate conceals is everything outside the hour. An in-home rate includes travel, which is why it sits above the online equivalent for a comparable tutor; the parent is paying for the journey either way. A group rate at a centre looks cheaper per student and includes the parent's own two journeys, which in this district is thirty to fifty minutes of driving per session.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set those against the school fee, which each school publishes on its KHDA listing and which KHDA confirmed would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

The useful way to think about value in a committed week is cost per unit of change rather than cost per hour. Two sessions a week in one weak subject for one term, with practice between them, is more likely to produce something than one session a week across four subjects for a year, and it is usually cheaper.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah 2, and the limits we state up front
paragraphs: Begin with the calendar rather than the subject. Write down the two or three weekday evenings that are genuinely free, whether a weekend morning is available, and which weeks the family travels. Then add the subject information: the examination board and syllabus code, the last mock mark with the mark scheme if the school released it, and any coursework internal deadlines. That combination produces a match in one conversation.

Then a trial session with the named tutor who would hold the slot, at the hour the slot would actually be. A trial at 15:00 on a Thursday tells you nothing about whether a 19:30 Tuesday will work. If the fit is wrong we rematch; the trial exists to test the working relationship, which no credential describes.

Three limits, said before you ask. Specialist cover is not uniform, and for a niche Diploma option or a narrow internal assessment specialism the right person may sit in a time zone that makes a 19:30 Dubai slot awkward. We say so rather than placing a generalist. We do not publish a price list, because the rate varies by subject, level and tutor. And no one here will offer a grade or a promised improvement.

One piece of due diligence applies to any tutor engaged in this market, including one found independently. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any circulating amount as unverified.

process.description: Forty-five minutes for primary, an hour for middle years, sixty to ninety minutes for Diploma, and two shorter sessions rather than one long one wherever fluency is the target. Homework is set between sessions, because the practice in between is where the change happens.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: For a primary child collected straight from school and not going to an activity, around 16:00 to 16:30. For a secondary student, plan on 17:00 at the very earliest and more realistically 19:00, because the window between 16:15 and 18:30 is where most sport and swimming in this district sits. The constraint is not distance to school but the two roads: Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road absorb the whole district's school traffic inside the same twenty minutes, twice a day, and a nine-minute off-peak journey becomes twenty-five.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a nine-year-old?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes, with a short break in the middle. Sustained attention in upper primary runs out somewhere between twenty and thirty minutes, so a sixty-minute session typically has fifteen minutes of nothing at the end and teaches the child that sessions are something to endure. Forty-five minutes is long enough for one concept plus practice and short enough to finish while the child is still engaged. Two of those a week beats one ninety-minute session for anything involving number fluency, because the spacing is what builds retention.

faqs.question: Our evenings are full of swimming and football. Does weekend tutoring work as well?
faqs.answer: It usually works better. Students do not learn less on a weekend morning than on a weekday evening; they generally learn more, because they are not already tired from a full school day and an activity. In this district weekday evenings are the scarce resource and weekend mornings are comparatively free, so a single weekend morning session is often the honest answer rather than a compromise. Longer weekend sessions also suit writing subjects, coursework and project work, which need a run at them rather than forty-five minutes.

faqs.question: If a session has to be cancelled at short notice, what happens?
faqs.answer: Online, it moves. The session can be rescheduled to another evening or a weekend morning, and the tutor can fill the original slot with a student in a different time zone, so nothing is wasted on either side. That is a structural difference rather than a courtesy: an in-home tutor who loses a slot loses a journey they cannot refill, which is why late cancellations are normally charged in that model and why flexibility is limited. Short-notice changes are common in every household, so it is worth asking before booking.

faqs.question: Why does tutoring sometimes produce nothing at all?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the sequence broke. Tutoring works when a session identifies something specific, the student practises it during the week, and the next session checks and corrects the practice. Three cancellations in a term converts that into a series of unconnected lessons on new topics, which produces understanding in the room and nothing durable. The second common cause is that no independent practice time was ever placed in the week, so each session starts from the same point. Both are calendar problems rather than teaching problems.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we realistically support at once?
faqs.answer: One or two. A weekly hour spread across four subjects reliably moves none of them, because the student has no remaining time for the independent practice that converts understanding into fluency, and in a week as committed as this district's that effect is sharper. Choose the subjects from evidence rather than impression: mock scripts with mark schemes beside them tell you where marks are actually being lost, which is often not the subject that feels hardest. One subject with two sessions a week for a term does more.

faqs.question: Should we pause tutoring during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: We would suggest moving it rather than stopping. School hours shorten, afternoons are low-energy for fasting students, and the usual late-afternoon slot becomes the least productive hour available. A post-Iftar session generally produces better work in less time, and because tutors are matched across time zones a later slot is straightforward to hold for the month. Stopping altogether costs four weeks at a point in the year when coursework deadlines and mock examinations are often close, which is when the loss is hardest to recover.

faqs.question: When in the school year is tutoring most effective?
faqs.answer: September to November, which is when families are least inclined to book it. A gap diagnosed in October closes quickly because nothing is competing for the student's time. The same gap in February has to compete with coursework deadlines, mock examinations and revision, so it takes longer and costs more. The least effective time to start something new is the final weeks before an examination session, when the right move is light maintenance, timed past papers and sleep rather than new commitments.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our house in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. In scheduling terms that is the point rather than a limitation: with no travel on either side, a 19:30 slot is as easy to hold as a 17:00 one, a session can be moved by a day without anyone losing a journey, and two children can be placed back to back on the same evening.

faqs.question: What should the room and equipment look like for online sessions?
faqs.answer: A room with a door, rather than a shared space with a television in it. A second screen or a tablet so the student can work on paper while still seeing the tutor, which matters a great deal in mathematics and the sciences. For any mathematical subject at Higher Level, a graphics tablet is worth the cost because tutor and student can write on the same page in real time. And headphones, which cut the household noise that otherwise turns a session into a series of repetitions.

faqs.question: Is a holiday intensive better than weekly term-time sessions?
faqs.answer: For a specific diagnosed gap, usually yes. A week of four or five sessions concentrates on one thing and finishes it, which is exactly what closing a known gap, bridging IGCSE content into the Diploma or collecting data for an internal assessment requires. For ongoing exam technique and fluency, weekly term-time sessions with practice between them work better, because spacing is the mechanism. The caveat in this district is travel: plan an intensive into the weeks the household is actually in one place with a reliable connection, wherever that is.

faqs.question: What do tutors charge per hour around Jumeirah and Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist, with premium named tutors advertised from AED 500 to 650. Monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; our rate follows a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

faqs.question: Does a group class at a tuition centre work out cheaper?
faqs.answer: Per billed hour, usually yes. Per hour of the household's time, often not. A centre class in this district adds the parent's own two journeys per session, typically thirty to fifty minutes of driving, and it fixes the timing to the centre's timetable, which frequently clashes with the sport that already owns those evenings. Group teaching also cannot work from your child's own marked script, which is where the specific losses are visible. For core content at a modest level it can be reasonable value; for component-level diagnosis it is not.

faqs.question: How do we make sure the independent work between sessions actually happens?
faqs.answer: Name where it sits, rather than hoping it appears. Put it on the same evening as the session or on a weekend morning, write it into the family calendar the way sport is written in, and keep it short: thirty to forty minutes is enough for most subjects if it is genuinely practice rather than rereading. For primary children, sitting nearby while it happens outperforms almost any paid intervention, not to teach but because presence decides whether it starts. For older students, a visible written weekly plan works better than asking.

faqs.question: What if our tutor leaves Dubai or is unwell for two weeks?
faqs.answer: With a matched online specialist, a replacement is found from the same specialism and the session notes are handed over so the new tutor starts where the previous one finished rather than from the beginning. With a single in-home tutor, the usual answer is that nothing happens until they return, because there is rarely a like-for-like substitute within driving distance who is also free at your hour. This is worth asking about before you book rather than after, since it is the scenario most likely to interrupt a term.

dubai/jumeirah-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both main IGCSE boards for families in Jumeirah 3 and the Jumeirah coast. Each one teaches a named syllabus rather than a general subject, so ask for the paper your child is weakest on.

intro.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 school teaches, and what your child is left to do alone
paragraphs: A Jumeirah 3 family rarely has a school problem. The schools along this stretch of coast are among the most heavily inspected in the country, the teaching is competent, and the reports come back readable. The problem is arithmetic. A Diploma subject at Higher Level is allocated roughly 240 teaching hours across two years. Inside those hours a teacher must cover the full syllabus, run the practical or portfolio work, set and return assessments, and prepare a class of twenty for three papers. What that leaves no room for is the single thing that moves a grade: one student, one weakness, one hour, repeated.

Count what sits outside the taught timetable. A Mathematics exploration that must be conceived, researched and written in the student's own time. An Extended Essay with a 4,000-word ceiling and three supervisor meetings, which in practice means the research is unsupervised. Two Theory of Knowledge components. A Group 4 project. Then the whole of revision, which in a two-year Diploma means revisiting content first met eighteen months earlier, without a teacher present. For an IGCSE student in Year 11 the ratio is worse: eight or nine subjects, each with two or three papers, and a mock season that arrives before half the syllabus has been consolidated.

This page is built around that gap rather than around the neighbourhood. Jumeirah 3 is a villa district between Jumeirah 2 and Umm Suqeim 1, bounded by Al Wasl Road inland and Jumeirah Beach Road at the water, and the practical consequence for tuition is simply that most children here are home by 15:15 and most parents are not. The schools children in Jumeirah 3 attend sit a few minutes away in Al Safa, Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah 1, and they run three different exam systems between them. A tutor who does not know which of those systems your child is entered for is guessing.

IB Gram is a matching platform, not a tuition centre. There is no branch in Dubai and no tutor is sent to a Jumeirah 3 address: home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, which is how a Jumeirah 3 student ends up with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has marked the current guide rather than with whoever happened to be free within a twenty-minute drive of Jumeirah Beach Road. That trade is the whole argument, and the comparison table further down puts numbers on it.

What follows is deliberately concrete. The hours a syllabus really needs. The AED the Dubai market charges, with the source of every band named. The coursework calendar counted backwards from the May session, which is the one thing no competitor page publishes. What a tutor is permitted to do with an exploration and what would constitute malpractice under IB rules. And the Ministry of Education equivalency rules an IGCSE or Diploma leaver needs if they intend to apply to a UAE university, where one widely-read competitor page publishes the wrong subject count.

dubai/jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Children in Jumeirah 3 are spread across three assessment systems that look similar from the outside and award marks on completely different principles. The programme notes below describe what each one asks of a student working alone, which is where tuition earns its place.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Final points run to 45, of which three come from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Every subject carries an internally assessed component worth 20 to 30 per cent that the student produces in their own time, under a supervisor who reads drafts but cannot direct the work.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah 3 students typically reach the Diploma from an IGCSE Year 11 at a British school in Al Safa or Umm Suqeim, or from the Middle Years Programme at an IB school on the Jumeirah strip. The two routes arrive with different habits: IGCSE leavers can answer a structured question and have never written an unscaffolded 4,000 words, while MYP leavers are comfortable with extended writing and short on timed-paper speed.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no single examination unless the school enters students for eProjects or on-screen examinations in Year 11. Marks come from task-specific clarifications written by the teacher, which is why a parent reading a report cannot always tell what went wrong.
programmes.countryNote: The Jumeirah and Al Safa IB schools run MYP through to Year 11, so a Jumeirah 3 family often faces a choice at 16 between staying in the IB continuum and moving to an IGCSE school a few minutes inland. The honest version of that decision turns on Criterion C and D performance in Mathematics and Sciences, not on the overall MYP grade, because those two criteria are closest to what Diploma Higher Level demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined terminally in a June or November series, syllabus by syllabus. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a figure and letters, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge Mathematics and the Sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped below the top grades.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Jumeirah 3 sit Cambridge, a minority sit Pearson Edexcel, and a few split boards by department so a single student holds entries with both. Checking the code on the statement of entry before booking tuition takes a minute and prevents a term of work on the wrong paper structure, because the two boards tier, time and weight the same subject differently.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: A transdisciplinary framework with no external examination, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages, so gaps in number fluency or reading age can go unremarked until a child meets the Middle Years Programme and suddenly has criteria applied to them.
programmes.countryNote: Several primary campuses serving Jumeirah 3 run PYP or an English National Curriculum primary and then feed children outward at 11 to secondary schools in Al Safa, Umm Suqeim or Arabian Ranches. That transfer is the quietest risk in this district: a child can leave Year 6 well regarded and arrive in Year 7 two years behind the written-mathematics expectations of an MYP cohort.

dubai/jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Jumeirah 3 families request most, described by what the assessment actually rewards. Where a subject has an internally assessed component, the note says so, because that component is the part the school cannot supervise hour by hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 3 is a two-part extended problem worth 20 per cent and is where most of the grade is lost, because it rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. The exploration adds a further 20 per cent. Students who scored well in IGCSE 0580 Extended often arrive fluent in method and unpractised at justification.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and calculator-dependent throughout, with Paper 3 at Higher Level built around modelling in context. The common failure is treating the graphic display calculator as the answer rather than as a tool whose output still has to be interpreted in sentences that earn method marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The current guide splits external assessment across two papers plus a 20 per cent internally assessed scientific investigation. Marks drain away in uncertainty treatment and in the extended-response questions that ask for an explanation rather than a derivation. Mechanics and fields reward diagram discipline more than algebra.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the Higher Level load, and the data-based questions punish students who have never written an error analysis. The internally assessed investigation is marked on research design and on evaluation, so a technically clean experiment with a thin evaluation still caps out in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade here more than content does. Distinguish, outline, explain and evaluate each carry a different expected answer length, and students who revise by reading rather than by answering past questions consistently under-write the six-mark items.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is three commentaries on three different articles, each tied to a different unit, each capped at 800 words. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a quantitative paper that students from a non-mathematical background routinely underestimate. Diagram accuracy is worth more marks than diagram quantity.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure and is the component that separates grades. Higher Level adds a 1,200-1,500 word essay on a studied text. The Individual Oral is internally assessed and needs a global issue that is genuinely arguable rather than merely topical.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study paper plus an internally assessed research project at Higher Level. Students lose marks by describing a company instead of applying a tool to it, and by choosing a research question that cannot be answered from the evidence they can realistically gather in Dubai.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. It contributes to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students treat it as an opinion piece; the assessment rewards precise knowledge claims and counterclaims with named real-world examples.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a subject the student chooses, supervised across a handful of meetings. Most failures are scoping failures that happen in week one, when a research question is too broad to argue in 4,000 words or too narrow to find sources for.

dubai/jumeirah-3.igcseSubjectsIntro: Half the children in Jumeirah 3 sit IGCSE rather than an IB programme at 16, and the syllabus codes below are the ones that appear on statements of entry at the British schools nearest this district.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended is two papers with a grade ceiling at A*; Core caps lower. Pearson 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher. The decision between tiers is usually made by the school in Year 10 and is reversible far later than parents assume, but only before the final entry deadline.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks. The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper about experiments, not an experiment, and it rewards students who can read an apparatus diagram and spot the controlled variable quickly.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic families account for most dropped marks. Qualitative analysis tests have to be memorised as a table, and students who revise chemistry by reading notes rather than by writing equations lose marks they already understand.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance carry the hardest questions. Six-mark items expect a structured answer with named terms, and students who write fluent paragraphs without those terms score in the lower bands.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
igcseSubjects.description: A compressed route through all three sciences taken by students with crowded option blocks. The compression means every topic is examinable but none is revisited, so a gap from Year 10 stays a gap. Worth checking which award your child is entered for before planning tuition.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and a composition, assessed on structure and register as much as accuracy. The reading paper rewards selective quotation and punishes narration. Students at bilingual schools near Jumeirah 3 often read well above their writing accuracy, which shows up as a plateau at grade B.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: A separate syllabus from First Language with its own mark scheme, and the one most often mis-entered. Exercise 5 and 6 writing tasks have fixed word ranges and a required register, and marks go missing on register rather than on grammar.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward application to the stimulus material rather than textbook recall. Economics 0455 has a quantitative element students rarely practise; Business 0450 has an evaluation requirement in the final questions that is worth more than all the definitions above it combined.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Paper 1 theory covers data representation, networks and security; Paper 2 is algorithms and pseudocode. Students who code confidently in Python still lose marks on pseudocode conventions and trace tables, which are a written discipline rather than a programming one.

dubai/jumeirah-3.regionsTitle: Jumeirah 3 and the streets around it
dubai/jumeirah-3.regionsIntro: Tuition is delivered online, so none of this changes who is available. It changes when a session can realistically start, which is the only local variable that matters once the tutor pool is national rather than within driving distance.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Villa plots between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road, with Jumeirah 2 to the north-east and Umm Suqeim 1 to the south-west. Most children here are collected at 15:00-15:15 and a 16:00 session start is comfortable on a normal weekday.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: The next district inland along the same beach road, feeding many of the same schools in Al Safa and Jumeirah 1. Families often share bus routes, so siblings in different year groups arrive home together and two back-to-back sessions work better than two separate slots.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Denser and closer to Al Hudaiba and La Mer, with several secondary schools inside walking distance. A Jumeirah 1 student can often start at 15:45, which matters in the final term when a Diploma candidate wants two sessions a week rather than one.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Immediately south-west, with a heavy concentration of British-curriculum primaries and secondaries. Shared school buses between Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah 3 mean an unpredictable arrival window of fifteen minutes, so sessions are scheduled on the later edge of it.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Inland across Al Wasl Road, home to several of the secondary schools Jumeirah 3 children attend. Afternoon traffic at the Al Safa interchange is the single biggest cause of a late start, which is one reason an online slot holds better than a tutor in a car.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: A quieter villa district further inland, often chosen by the same families for space. Children here tend to be on longer bus routes, so a 16:30 start is more realistic than 16:00 during term time.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer waterfront developments at the Jumeirah 1 end, with apartment households and younger children. Primary-age sessions here run shorter and earlier, typically 45 minutes at 15:45, because concentration rather than scheduling is the binding constraint.

regions.name: City Walk and Al Safa Park
regions.note: Low-rise apartment living with no secondary school inside the development, so every child commutes outward. Families here frequently book the same weekend slots, and Saturday morning fills first across the whole Jumeirah coast.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Reached from Jumeirah 3 along the coast, with its own school buses on a fixed trunk route. The crossing adds time in both directions, and Palm households more often ask for evening slots after 18:00 than anywhere else on this stretch.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The secondary schools closest to Jumeirah 3 run three different exam systems between them, which is why a tutor needs the syllabus code rather than the school name. Students supported through IB Gram attend schools in this cluster; no relationship with any of them is implied.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: A short drive along the coast and a common destination for Jumeirah 3 families who want a particular sixth form. The IGCSE-to-A-Level and IGCSE-to-Diploma splits differ school by school here, so the Year 11 decision is made against a specific institution rather than a general plan.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
schoolClusters.note: Where many Jumeirah 3 families send children who began at a Jumeirah primary and moved outward for secondary. The bus journey is long enough that a 16:00 session start is unrealistic in term time, and tuition tends to be scheduled at 17:00 or at weekends.

dubai/jumeirah-3.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this district. All of them run over live video; the differences are in session length, frequency and how the time between sessions is used.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a single syllabus
modes.description: Sixty or ninety minutes a week against one named syllabus, with a specific weakness named at the start of each term and reviewed at the end of it. This is the format that suits a Year 10 or a first-year Diploma student who is competent but drifting, and it is the cheapest way to stop a small gap compounding across two years.
bullets: One syllabus code, one tutor, one recurring slot
Short written task between sessions, marked before the next one
Termly review against the school's own assessment data

modes.title: Coursework supervision for the exploration, Extended Essay or commentaries
modes.description: A block of shorter sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines rather than to a weekly rhythm. The tutor works on scoping, method, criteria interpretation and feedback on the student's own drafts. The student does all the writing and all the analysis; the tutor reads, questions and points at the criterion that is not yet met.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Scoping session before any writing begins
No drafting, no editing to completion, no supplied content

modes.title: Intensive paper practice before a series
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week in the eight weeks before a Cambridge, Pearson or IB series, built entirely around timed questions and the marking of them. Works only when the content is broadly known and the problem is execution: timing, command terms, working shown, answers not carried forward. It is the wrong format for a student with real content gaps.

sections.heading: The taught hours and the hours nobody supervises
paragraphs: A Higher Level Diploma subject is allocated around 240 teaching hours across two years and a Standard Level subject around 150. Those hours are consumed by content delivery, practical work, internal assessment administration and the school's own mock cycle. The arithmetic leaves very little room for reteaching, which is why a student who misses the fields unit in Physics in Year 12 is still missing it in the February before the papers.

Set against that, the unsupervised load is large and specific. A 4,000-word Extended Essay. A scientific investigation or mathematical exploration worth a fifth of the subject grade. Three Economics commentaries if that subject is taken. A 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay and an exhibition. Then the whole of revision, which for a two-year course means recovering material first taught eighteen months earlier with no teacher in the room.

The same pattern runs at IGCSE in a compressed form. Eight or nine subjects, each examined terminally, each with two or three papers, and a mock season in November or January that arrives before the syllabus is finished. Year 11 students in Jumeirah 3 routinely report that the content is fine and the papers are not, which is an execution problem rather than a knowledge problem and responds to a completely different kind of tuition.

The table below is the honest division of labour. It is not a criticism of any school; it is what a timetable can and cannot contain. Tuition is worth buying for the right-hand column and worth skipping for the left.

sections.heading: Where the final Diploma year actually leaks marks
paragraphs: Marks are not lost evenly. Across two years of Diploma teaching the same four or five failure modes recur regardless of school or subject, and three of them are invisible on a school report because they only appear under timed conditions.

The first is command-term blindness. A question that says evaluate expects a judgement supported on both sides; a question that says outline expects two or three lines. Students who revise by rereading notes answer every question at the same length, which systematically under-writes the high-tariff items and over-writes the low ones. The fix is mechanical and fast: answer fifty past questions, sorted by command term, and mark them against the published scheme.

The second is the internally assessed component treated as an essay rather than as a criterion-matching exercise. An exploration is marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations, and a piece of work that reads beautifully while never engaging with one criterion loses those marks outright. Reading the criteria before writing, and then again against the draft, recovers more marks per hour than any amount of additional content revision.

The third is Paper 3 at Higher Level in the subjects that have one. In Mathematics it is 20 per cent of the grade and consists of extended problems that reward sustained reasoning; in Economics it is a quantitative paper; in the sciences the extended-response and data-handling questions play the same role. Students practise Papers 1 and 2 because those exist in abundance and neglect the paper that carries the marginal grade.

The fourth is simply timing. A student who knows the content and writes at two-thirds of the required pace will lose a grade. That is diagnosable in one session with a stopwatch and a past paper, and it is the single most common finding in a first tuition session with a Jumeirah 3 Year 13 student in January.

sections.heading: The IGCSE term nobody schedules: Year 11, term two
paragraphs: The structural problem at IGCSE is that mocks arrive before the syllabus ends. A school finishes teaching in March or April for a May-June series, sets mocks in November or January, and therefore marks students on content they have not been taught. Parents read a disappointing mock grade as a verdict when it is often a timetable artefact, and the useful question is which part of the gap is untaught and which part is misunderstood.

Separating those two is a half-hour exercise with the mock paper and the syllabus document side by side. Questions on untaught topics get set aside. What remains is the real diagnostic, and it is usually narrower than the overall mark suggests: a single algebraic technique, a confusion between two electrolysis cases, a habit of not reading the mark allocation before answering.

The second structural problem is entry decisions. Cambridge tiers Mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Those entries are made months before the exam and a Core entry caps the available grade. A student who improves sharply in term two can sometimes still be moved, but only inside the board's entry window, and the window closes long before the exam itself.

Term two is also when subject counts come up. A student carrying nine subjects with two weak ones will usually do better on eight, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule for the British track needs five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education. Knowing that number makes the drop decision arithmetic rather than emotional.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Jumeirah 3, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. Dubai parents transact in dirhams, so the bands below are set out in AED with the source of each one named. These are market rates observed across published provider pages and a Dubai rate survey, not IB Gram's own price list.

The spread is wide for a reason. At the bottom are university students and non-specialist tutors teaching online, advertised from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour by one Dubai content provider and from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 by one platform. In the middle sit qualified subject tutors online, where one Dubai agency publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. At the top are named specialists and former examiners, where one provider publishes AED 650 an hour.

In-home visits carry a travel premium that is rarely itemised. A Dubai cost survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. That premium buys proximity, not subject depth, and in a villa district a few minutes from Al Wasl Road it buys less proximity than the price implies, because the constraint on a Dubai tutor is the drive between households rather than the distance to any one of them.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages, because the rate depends on level, subject scarcity and session length, and a number printed here would be wrong for most families reading it. The honest route is a trial session and a quoted figure before anything is booked. What this page can do is show you what the market charges so that whatever you are quoted, by us or by anyone else, can be judged against it.

sections.heading: Online lessons set against an in-home tutor on this stretch of coast
paragraphs: This is the decision most Jumeirah 3 families are actually making, so it deserves a table rather than a slogan. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address and makes no home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. The case for online here is not cost, although it usually is cheaper. The case is the size of the pool you are choosing from.

An in-home tutor in Jumeirah 3 is drawn from the set of suitable people willing to drive to Jumeirah 3 at 16:30 on a Tuesday. For Year 9 Mathematics that set is large. For Chemistry Higher Level under the current guide, or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, or a Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 entry specifically, it narrows quickly, and the usual outcome is a competent generalist rather than a specialist. Over live video the geography disappears and the selection criterion becomes the syllabus.

The second difference is continuity. A travelling tutor loses sessions to traffic, to school holidays when they are out of the country, and to the end of their own contract. An online slot survives a family trip to the UK, a Ramadan timetable change and a move from Jumeirah 3 to Arabian Ranches without a gap. Over a two-year Diploma that reliability is worth more than any single lesson.

There are real advantages on the other side and it would be dishonest to skip them. Young children focus better with an adult physically present. Practical laboratory technique cannot be taught through a screen. A household with poor connectivity or no quiet room will struggle. Those are the cases where an in-home tutor is the better buy, and in a villa district with space and good fibre they apply less often than the price difference suggests.

sections.heading: The coursework calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster publishes a calendar. That is strange, because the deadline that costs families most is never the exam: it is an entry deadline or an internal coursework deadline months earlier, and by the time it is missed nothing can be done.

Cambridge publishes its key dates series by series. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge lists an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct from 13 May and certificates in late June. The pattern is the point: entries close roughly ten weeks before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May-June and November series and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each, so dates must be read from the live official timetable rather than from any summary.

IB session dates are deliberately not stated on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; your child's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates and the school's internal deadlines, and those internal deadlines are the ones that actually govern the exploration and the Extended Essay.

What a family can do is work backwards from the window they know. If papers are in May, the Extended Essay is effectively finished the preceding autumn, the exploration in the term before that, and any tier or entry change has to happen earlier still. The table sets that sequence out with the owner of each deadline named, because half of them belong to the school rather than to the board.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an exploration, and what would be malpractice
paragraphs: This matters more in Dubai than families realise, because the same search results that produce legitimate tutors also produce services selling finished Internal Assessments. One such operation in this market lists completed IAs at a fixed price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller.

The line is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each lettered criterion is asking for, interrogate a proposed research question, point out that a method will not generate usable data, read the student's own draft and say which criterion is not yet met, and teach the referencing convention. All of that is teaching.

A tutor may not author any part of the work, supply text for the student to insert, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, provide the data, or hand over a worked exploration as a template to adapt. The test a supervisor applies is authenticity: the work must be the student's own, and a student who cannot explain their own method in a viva voce has already failed that test regardless of what the document says.

Practically, this is why coursework support is sold here as a block of sessions around the student's own drafting schedule rather than as a writing service. The student arrives with a draft, leaves with a list of criterion-specific problems, and does the work. It is slower than the alternative and it is the only version that survives an authenticity check. Any provider offering otherwise is selling your child an expulsion risk.
bullets: Permitted: content teaching, criterion interpretation, questioning a research question, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: authoring text, supplying data, rewriting to final form, providing a model to adapt
The viva voce exists to test authenticity; a student must be able to explain their own method
Services selling finished Internal Assessments put the student at risk, not the seller

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale and the published report is the one document that tells you something comparable about a school. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit of any kind and claims no standing with the authority; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises, which this platform does not have.

The part that affects a Jumeirah 3 timetable is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states those requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

KHDA also requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. For the mandatory subjects, KHDA states that use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

Two consequences follow for a family here. The first is arithmetic: those lessons occupy timetable space, so an IGCSE or Diploma student in Dubai has fewer free periods than the same student would have in the UK, and the unsupervised coursework load is squeezed into evenings. The second is that Arabic is a real examined subject with real marks attached, and it is the one most often left until it becomes urgent.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for a Jumeirah 3 school leaver
paragraphs: If your child intends to apply to a UAE university, the certificate needs equivalency from the Ministry of Education. Almost nobody in this search cluster mentions it, and one well-ranked competitor publishes the wrong subject count, which is an expensive error to inherit.

On the British track, the requirement reported from the Ministry's clarification is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is the one that changes option-block decisions in Year 9.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. No International Baccalaureate points threshold is published in that clarification, so this page does not state one; a Diploma family should read the current requirement on the Ministry's own site or ask the emirate's attestation authority directly.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tuition is not a requirement for it. The rules are listed here because they change which subjects a student should keep, and because a family that discovers the five-subject rule in Year 13 has lost the chance to act on it.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Every regulatory source checked for this page agrees it is granted free of charge, for two years, and the service is listed by MoHRE as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is broader than families expect. The published list includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

There is a second rule that bears directly on a common request. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Asking for your child's own class teacher privately is therefore the one request that should not be made, however convenient it looks.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram operates as an online matching platform with no Dubai premises and holds no such permit, which is stated plainly rather than left for a parent to discover.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The first conversation is diagnostic and it needs three things in front of you: the most recent school report, the latest mock or assessment paper with the marks shown, and the statement of entry or subject list with codes on it. Without the third, any match is approximate. With it, the question becomes narrow enough to answer in one session.

A trial session follows, on the weakness you named rather than on a general assessment. The useful output is not a verdict on the child but a plan with a number on it: how many sessions, against which paper, and what should have changed by when. If a tutor cannot tell you what they intend to fix first, that is information.

Scarcity is real and worth stating. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics at Higher Level are in demand across every Dubai district at the same hours, and the 16:00 to 18:00 window on weekdays fills first. For a niche combination, such as a Pearson Edexcel science entry alongside an unusual Group 6 subject, the honest answer is sometimes that nothing is free this week at the time you want. In that case the choices are a different slot, a weekend session, or a wait, and saying so is better than seating a student with a tutor who does not know the syllabus.

The rest is ordinary. A recurring slot, a short task between sessions, marking that comes back before the next one, and a review at the end of each term against the school's own data. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video; there is no Dubai centre to visit and no tutor arriving at a Jumeirah 3 villa, because that is not the service being sold.

process.title: Send the three documents
process.description: The latest school report, the most recent marked paper, and the subject list with syllabus codes. The codes are the part that matters: 0580 and 4MA1 are not the same course, and a tutor matched to the wrong one will teach a paper structure your child will never sit.

process.title: Name one weakness, not a subject
process.description: A request for help with Chemistry is harder to act on than a request for help with organic mechanisms and the evaluation criterion of the investigation. The narrower the brief, the better the match, and the faster the first session produces something useful.

process.title: Take a trial session on that weakness
process.description: The trial runs on the problem you named rather than as a general assessment. At the end you should have a plan with a count of sessions in it and a stated first target, plus a quoted rate before anything recurring is booked.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run
process.description: Most Jumeirah 3 children are home by 15:15, so 16:00 holds on a normal weekday; children on longer bus routes from Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills do better at 17:00. The slot is weekly and recurring, which is what makes the between-session task work.

process.title: Review against the school's own data
process.description: At the end of each term, compare the tutor's view with the school's assessment marks. If the two disagree, that disagreement is the most useful information available and should change the plan rather than be explained away.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 assess the same chemistry differently, and the Diploma guides changed recently enough that a tutor's own school experience may be out of date. Matching starts from the code on the entry form rather than from the subject name.

whyPoints.title: The whole country's tutor pool, not the drivable part
whyPoints.description: Choosing online removes the twenty-minute-drive constraint that decides who is actually available in a villa district. For Higher Level sciences and Paper 3 subjects, that is the difference between a specialist and a capable generalist.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the date stated. No figure here is presented as IB Gram's own price, and a quoted rate should always be weighed against the bands above.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Support on an exploration or Extended Essay is feedback on the student's own work, criterion interpretation and method questioning. No text is supplied and no draft is rewritten to final form, because the alternative puts the candidate at risk.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry or examination-board accreditation and says so. No school is presented as a partner. No grade is promised, and no satisfaction statistic appears on this page without the data behind it.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through travel and Ramadan
whyPoints.description: An online slot survives a summer in the UK, a timetable change during Ramadan and a move to another Dubai district. Across a two-year Diploma, keeping the same tutor through those disruptions matters more than any single lesson does.

faqs.question: My child's school in Jumeirah 3 is strong. Why would we still need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because a good school and an unsupervised workload are different problems. A Higher Level subject gets around 240 taught hours across two years, and those hours cover content, practicals and the mock cycle. The exploration, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the whole of revision sit outside them. Tuition is worth buying for that outside column and worth skipping for the inside one. If your child's difficulty is attendance, behaviour or a teaching gap, raise it with the school first; if it is a timed paper they cannot finish or a criterion they cannot interpret, that is what a tutor fixes.

faqs.question: How many hours outside school does an IB exploration actually take?
faqs.answer: Between twenty-five and forty across a term, spread unevenly. Choosing and narrowing the topic takes the longest and produces nothing visible, which is why students postpone it. Data collection or mathematical development is usually quicker than expected. Then the writing, and a round of criterion-checking against the published mark allocations, which is the stage most often skipped. Families who plan for ten hours are surprised in the final fortnight. Planning for thirty, starting earlier, and doing the criterion-check twice turns the same piece of work into a calmer and better-scoring one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Jumeirah 3 families run one-to-one over live video, at a fixed weekly slot, with the session recorded on request. The reason is pool size rather than cost: an in-home tutor is drawn from the people willing to drive to this district at 16:30 on a weekday, while an online match is drawn from everyone who teaches that syllabus. For a Higher Level science or a specific board entry, that difference decides whether you get a specialist.

faqs.question: What do tutors charge per hour in Dubai, in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Market bands, each attributed on this page: budget online and non-specialist tuition runs roughly AED 45 to AED 150, with one Dubai provider advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and one platform from around AED 33. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. IB Gram quotes a rate after a trial rather than printing one here.

faqs.question: Is a Core IGCSE entry a problem if my child is now doing well?
faqs.answer: It can be, because Core caps the achievable grade while Extended does not. Cambridge tiers Mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended and Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher, and those entries are submitted months before the papers. A student who improves sharply in term two can sometimes be moved, but only inside the board's entry window, which closes well before the exam. Ask the examinations officer for the entry deadline and the current tier in writing, then decide. For the March 2027 Cambridge series, final entries were due 27 November 2026.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may interrogate the research question, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, suggest where to look for sources, teach the referencing convention, read the student's own draft and say which criterion is not yet met. A tutor may not author any part of it, supply text to insert, rewrite a paragraph into final form or hand over a model essay to adapt. The authenticity test is the viva voce: a candidate who cannot explain their own argument and method has a problem no document can solve. Services selling finished essays put the student at risk.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Jumeirah 3 usually attend?
faqs.answer: The secondary schools nearest this district sit in Al Safa, Jumeirah 1 and Umm Suqeim, and they run three exam systems between them: British-curriculum schools entering students for IGCSE then A Level, IB continuum schools running the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma, and a few that offer both routes at sixth form. Families also commute outward to Al Sufouh, Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills for a particular sixth form. Because the systems differ, the useful detail for tuition is the syllabus code on the statement of entry, not the school's name.

faqs.question: When can a weekday session realistically start in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Most Jumeirah 3 children are collected between 15:00 and 15:15, so a 16:00 start works on a normal weekday with time to eat first. Children on longer bus routes from Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills or Palm Jumeirah do better at 17:00. The 16:00 to 18:00 window is the one every Dubai district wants, so it fills first across popular subjects. Weekend mornings are the next most requested. Saturdays at 10:00 fill before anything else, particularly in the final term before a May series.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a licence, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Ask any individual tutor whether they hold it. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see online as unverified.

faqs.question: Why does my child's mock grade look so much worse than their class work?
faqs.answer: Usually for one of three reasons, and they need different responses. The syllabus may not have been finished, so the paper tested untaught content; compare the mock against the syllabus document and set those questions aside. Timing may be the problem, which a stopwatch and one past paper will reveal in half an hour. Or command terms are being answered at a uniform length, which systematically under-writes the high-tariff questions. Only the third is really a knowledge issue, and all three are fixable. A mock mark on its own tells you very little.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count towards the five subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The Ministry of Education's clarification for the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Both remain compulsory school subjects in Dubai under KHDA's mandatory-subject rules, so a student takes them and they occupy timetable time; they simply do not count towards the equivalency total. That is worth knowing in Year 9 when option blocks are chosen, because the five has to come from elsewhere. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider claiming that should be asked to show the permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, involving initial approval, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram is an online matching platform with no Dubai premises and holds no permit, accreditation or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. The page names those bodies to explain what they do, nothing more.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 13 Diploma student have?
faqs.answer: One per weak subject is the usual starting point, moving to two in the eight weeks before the papers if the problem is execution rather than content. More than two a week in a single subject rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time between sessions, not contact hours. A student carrying three Higher Levels and an unfinished Extended Essay is better served by a short coursework block to clear the essay, then weekly subject sessions, than by stacking four tutors at once.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or a family trip abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the practical arguments for an online slot. During Ramadan many Dubai families shift sessions later, often after Iftar, and schools run shortened days, so the usual 16:00 slot stops working for a month. A travelling family can keep the same tutor from another time zone rather than losing a month and restarting. Sessions move by agreement with the tutor rather than being cancelled, which matters most in the final year when a four-week gap in February is expensive.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor for my child's subject is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: You will be told, rather than seated with someone who does not know the syllabus. Higher Level Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics are requested across every Dubai district in the same 16:00 to 18:00 window, and unusual combinations narrow the pool further. The options are then a different weekday slot, a weekend session, or a short wait for the right match. A generalist teaching a Pearson Edexcel paper structure they have not taught before is worse value than waiting a fortnight for someone who has.

dubai/jumeirah-3.closingHeading: Start with the gap, not with the subject
dubai/jumeirah-3.closingBody: The useful first question for a Jumeirah 3 family is not which tutor, but which part of the course is being done without supervision and going wrong. Send the latest report, the most recent marked paper and the subject list with its syllabus codes, and name one weakness rather than one subject. The trial session runs on that weakness. Lessons are one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly slot, scheduled around the school run on this stretch of coast. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the market and is attributed; a rate for your child is quoted after the trial, before anything recurring is agreed.

dubai/jumeirah-golf-estates.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here cover what this community asks for most: Higher Level Mathematics and sciences for Diploma students, IGCSE Maths and the separate sciences, A Level support for students on the British route, and coursework method for the Extended Essay. Each works to one named specification.

intro.heading: A full week, a gated community, and no school inside it
paragraphs: Jumeirah Golf Estates is a low-density gated community built around two championship golf courses off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, with Al Furjan to the west and Jumeirah Village to the north. It has no school within its boundary. Every child here leaves the community every morning, most often towards Jumeirah Village, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Al Barsha or further along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor, and the drive back is the thing that sets the shape of the evening.

The households are generally smaller than in the apartment belt and the children are often older. What distinguishes a tutoring enquiry from this community is not the subject - it is the number of other commitments competing for the same hours. Golf coaching at the academy, swim squads, football academies and tennis at the community courts fill the slot between 17:00 and 19:00 that most tutoring agencies treat as their core offering. A tutor proposing 17:30 on a Tuesday to a family here is proposing a collision.

The second feature is travel. A meaningful share of these families spend several weeks a year outside the UAE: summers in the UK or Europe, winter breaks, school holidays taken a week either side of the official dates. Under a conventional in-home arrangement that means the tutoring stops, restarts and spends the first session re-establishing ground. Across a school year a family can lose eight or ten weeks that way without ever deciding to.

The third is the academic calendar itself, which shifts in ways a generic revision plan does not anticipate. Ramadan compresses the school day and moves the whole household's rhythm. Eid breaks land differently each year. Examination series sit in windows set months in advance by Cambridge and Pearson, with entry deadlines earlier still. A plan that survives all three has to be built with them in it rather than adjusted around them when they arrive.

All of our UAE teaching is one-to-one and delivered over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a gated community with a full calendar that is the arrangement that actually holds: a 20:00 slot after training is perfectly workable on a screen and almost impossible to staff with a visiting tutor, and a family in London for five weeks in July keeps the same tutor at the same Gulf Standard Time hour translated into local time.

What follows is written for that week rather than for an idealised one. The commute table gives realistic home arrival times by destination school. The calendar table sets out the periods that reliably move a plan and how sessions move with them. There is a rate table that states what each format includes rather than only what it costs, and a hiring checklist of eight questions that applies to us as much as to anyone else selling tutoring in this city.
