dubai/jumeirah-park.programmesIntro: Families here frequently keep two routes open for as long as the system allows. These are the programmes we support, written from the point of view of a parent trying to work out which door each choice leaves open.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through boundaries the school publishes. The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the first piece of genuinely independent extended work most students meet, and it is assessed against its own criteria rather than on the quality of the object produced.
programmes.countryNote: For a Jumeirah Park family the MYP question is usually comparative: how does an MYP route at a nearby IB school compare with the IGCSE route at the school inside the community. The honest answer is that they test different things, and the better choice depends on whether the child writes fluently under time pressure or works better across a long project.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations at 16, with tiering in several subjects and a June and November series each year for Cambridge, May/June and November for Pearson Edexcel. The option choices made at the end of Year 9 set what can be taken: dropping a separate science or a language at 14 removes routes at 16 that cannot be recovered later without a year's catch-up.
programmes.countryNote: The route most Jumeirah Park children take, because the community's own school examines at 16. We are asked most often about whether triple science is necessary, whether a second language should be kept, and whether a capped tier in Mathematics affects the Diploma application. Those questions have precise answers and they are time-limited.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level sciences carry a third written paper. Each subject's internal assessment is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the final grade and is submitted well before the written papers, so Year 12's second term is heavier than its timetable suggests.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Park Diploma students travel out to school, typically towards Al Barsha, The Sustainable City or Dubai Hills. The practical consequence is that Higher Level work lands in the evening, and the subjects that cause the most difficulty here are HL Mathematics AA, HL Chemistry and HL Economics, in roughly that order.

programmes.name: A Level, as the alternative to the Diploma
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, assessed by terminal papers, with no compulsory core beyond what the school adds. Students who want to specialise early, or who write well in a narrow field rather than broadly, often do better here than in the Diploma. University offers are made in the same currency through a published tariff.
programmes.countryNote: Keeping this route open is a large part of what the Year 9 options conversation in Jumeirah Park is actually about. A student who may want A Level Physics needs the right science route at 16; one aiming at the Diploma has more flexibility. We set out what each choice requires rather than recommending one system over the other.

dubai/jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects we are asked for most often from this community, with the specific decision or difficulty attached to each rather than a syllabus summary. Matching is always to a named specification.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic, proof-based route. Paper 1 has no calculator, which is where weak manipulation becomes visible immediately. HL adds Paper 3, an extended investigative paper that rewards structured problem solving rather than recall. Required or preferred for most engineering, mathematics and physics degrees.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, built on modelling, statistics and real data sets. The mark loss is in interpretation rather than computation. Accepted for a wide range of degrees including economics and the social sciences, but checked carefully by some engineering and mathematics faculties.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The Higher Level content jump is real: organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most dropped marks. The internal assessment is marked heavily on methodology and on how uncertainty is handled rather than on whether the experiment produced a tidy result.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are the recurring difficulty, and the command term controls the mark scheme. A question asking a student to deduce requires reasoning shown; one asking them to state does not. Students who answer the question they expected rather than the one printed lose marks they knew the physics for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision and evaluation decide the grade. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a third paper. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on published news articles, and students who choose an article that cannot carry real analysis cap their own marks before writing a word.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Tier confirmation comes first, because a capped tier removes the top grades regardless of teaching. Beyond that, multi-step problems and graph transformations produce the most mark loss. A student fluent in individual skills who fails mixed papers needs practice selecting methods, not more topic revision.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics, Chemistry and Biology
subjects.description: The triple science route, and the one most relevant to a student keeping Higher Level sciences open. The alternative-to-practical paper is the common weak point, and it is almost entirely trainable. Six-mark extended answers are where strong students still lose grades.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined Science
subjects.description: Fewer papers covering all three sciences, which changes what can be omitted and what cannot. It does not close the Diploma door, but it does mean a student entering HL Chemistry has content to cover that a triple-science classmate already has. That gap is worth knowing about in Year 11, not Year 12.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score poorly; the marks are for handling knowledge questions with precision. It affects the Diploma total through the core points alongside the Extended Essay.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both assessed on process rather than product: the goal set, the criteria chosen, the research recorded, the reflection written. Our role is to teach method, question framing and referencing, and to give feedback on what the student has already produced. The content stays the student's own throughout.

sections.heading: The Year 9 options decision, and what it quietly closes off
paragraphs: The options form at the end of Year 9 is the most consequential piece of paper a British-curriculum family signs, and it is usually presented as a timetabling exercise. A student picks subjects from blocks, the blocks are constrained by staffing, and a choice that looks like a preference turns out two years later to have been a gate. Nobody at the school is hiding this; it simply does not fit into the twelve minutes allocated at a parents' evening.

Three choices do most of the damage when they go wrong. Dropping a separate science in favour of Combined Science leaves a student with less content when they reach a Higher Level science, which is recoverable but costs time in Year 12. Dropping a language at 14 closes a Diploma Group 2 option that may be needed at 16. Being placed in a capped tier in Mathematics removes the top grades from that subject for that series, which matters for both A Level and Diploma applications.

None of those choices is automatically wrong. A student who will not take a science beyond 16 loses nothing by taking Combined Science, and gains timetable room for a subject they are better at. The error is not the choice; it is making the choice without knowing what it decides. One session spent mapping the consequences, with the parent in the room, puts a family in a position to ask the school a precise question rather than a general one.

The table below sets out the decisions we are asked about most from this community, with the window in which each can still be changed. Windows close earlier than parents expect: by the time a Year 11 student sits a mock, most of these are settled for that examination series.

sections.heading: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This choice is made at the start of Year 12 and read by university admissions tutors three years later, which makes it the single most consequential subject decision in the Diploma. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-based with a non-calculator paper; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with a calculator permitted throughout and a strong emphasis on interpreting real data.

The academic fit question and the admissions question are different, and families often answer only one of them. For fit, the useful indicator is not the IGCSE grade but how the student got it: a child who enjoys manipulating expressions and following a proof belongs in Analysis and Approaches, while one who is strong on data, context and explanation is often better served by Applications and Interpretation. For admissions, some engineering, mathematics and physics faculties state a preference or a requirement, and that has to be checked against the actual course pages rather than assumed.

The level decision compounds it. Higher Level in either route adds Paper 3, an extended investigative paper that many students meet for the first time in a mock and find unlike anything they have practised. A student who takes Higher Level because it sounds stronger, without the algebraic security to support it, usually ends up with a lower grade than the Standard Level grade they would have earned, and the difference is visible on the certificate.

The table compares the two routes on the things that actually decide the outcome. We go through the intended degree subject and the student's own IGCSE working - not just the grade - before offering a view, and we are willing to say that the school's recommendation is the right one.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level: what the difference costs in hours
paragraphs: Parents are told that Higher Level is more demanding and Standard Level less so, which is true and not useful for planning. The practical question is how much additional work a Higher Level subject requires each week, and whether a student taking three of them has the time that implies once the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS are counted.

The structural differences are specific. Higher Level carries more teaching hours, a longer content list, an extra paper in most sciences, and in several subjects a higher weighting on the internal assessment relative to the papers. A Higher Level science student is sitting three written papers rather than two, and the third is typically the one students have practised least because it appears last in the course.

Where this matters most for a Jumeirah Park family is subject selection in the spring of Year 11. Three Higher Levels chosen because they look impressive, in subjects where the student is competent rather than strong, produces a Diploma that is harder than it needed to be and a set of grades below what a better-balanced choice would have delivered. Dropping one Higher Level to Standard Level early in Year 12 is a legitimate, unglamorous and frequently correct decision.

The table sets out what changes between the levels and what each change means for tutoring hours, so a family can plan a term's workload rather than discover it. The totals matter: a student with three Higher Levels, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay has four pieces of extended independent work due within roughly the same six months.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost no tutoring page in this market names an examination session, a registration deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the calendar is the thing that determines when work has to happen. A student who starts revising when the school says revision begins is starting after several deadlines have already passed, and the deadlines that matter most are administrative rather than academic.

Cambridge International is explicit about the structure. IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations run in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

The March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of how far ahead the administrative dates sit. The examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

IB session dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site cannot be read automatically, so no IB examination or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified date would be worse than publishing none. UAE schools sit the May session; for the specific dates, ask your child's IB coordinator or check ibo.org directly. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a date restated on a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes across the border
paragraphs: Dubai families tend to assume KHDA is the regulator for private schools generally. It is the regulator for Dubai, and it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Cross into another emirate and the authority changes, along with the inspection framework and in some cases the approval of fees and curricula themselves.

The complete map is short and almost nobody publishes it. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In the researched competitor corpus, the Abu Dhabi regulator is named by nobody at all.

The differences are not cosmetic. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. At the federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations - the rule that produces every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a Jumeirah Park family this matters at two moments: when considering a school in another emirate because of a fee band or a specific programme, and when a parent works in Abu Dhabi and the household is weighing a move. The regulator determines what the inspection report means, what fee changes are possible, and which authority to approach with a complaint. The table below is the whole map in one place.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, the Extended Essay and where the line sits
paragraphs: Both of the extended independent pieces a student meets in this system are assessed on process, which is the detail that makes legitimate support possible and illegitimate support obvious. The MYP Personal Project is marked on the goal set, the criteria chosen, the research recorded and the reflection written, not on how impressive the finished object is. The Extended Essay is marked on the research question, the engagement with sources, the argument and the reflection, not on the elegance of the prose alone.

Legitimate support is therefore specific and teachable. A tutor explains each criterion and the marks attached to it. A tutor helps a student narrow a question that is currently too broad to research in 4,000 words. A tutor teaches a referencing convention, demonstrates how to read an academic source critically, shows what a research journal entry should contain, and gives feedback on a draft the student has produced alone. A tutor helps plan backwards from the school's internal deadline so the piece is not being finished the week it is due.

The line is equally specific. A tutor does not supply content, restructure the piece into its final shape, or correct it sentence by sentence until the voice is no longer the student's. At least one site ranking for tutoring searches in this market sells finished internal assessments outright; buying one risks a malpractice finding that falls on the student, not the seller. A page offering to produce assessed work is offering your child a genuine danger, whatever it calls the service.

We also decline to supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the boards, and reproducing them is both a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. We cite them, link to the official source, and work from what the school has legitimately provided to the student.

sections.heading: A school inside the community, and the effect on the evening
paragraphs: Jumeirah Park is one of a small number of Dubai communities where a meaningful share of children attend a school within walking or minutes-driving distance. Dubai British School Jumeirah Park sits inside the community, which produces a household rhythm that is unusual for this city: children home by 15:30 rather than 16:45, and an afternoon that is genuinely available.

That changes what tutoring can be scheduled. A 16:00 session is realistic for a primary or lower secondary child here, which it is not in communities whose children bus out to Dubai Investments Park or Al Barsha. For families in that position we schedule earlier and shorter rather than later and longer, because a Year 7 student at 16:00 is far more useful to work with than the same student at 19:00.

The exception is the Diploma cohort. Most IB students from Jumeirah Park travel out to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Dubai Hills, which puts them back home at the same time as everyone else in the city. Higher Level sessions therefore sit at 19:00 or 19:30, and a 90-minute block is the right length because that is what a timed paper section plus feedback actually takes.

One practical consequence of the short commute is worth naming. Families here often have room for two sessions in one evening across two children without either of them running past 20:00, which makes a household arrangement easier to hold through a busy term than it is in the apartment belt. We build the schedule around that advantage when it exists rather than applying a standard timetable.

sections.heading: What a parent should expect to receive after each session
paragraphs: Progress reporting is where tutoring arrangements most often disappoint, and the disappointment is usually structural rather than personal. A tutor teaches for an hour, the student says it went fine, and three months later nobody can say what changed. That is a reporting failure, and it is straightforward to fix by deciding at the start what will be written down.

After each session we record what was covered against the specification, what the student could do unaided by the end, what remains insecure, and what was set before the next session. That is four short lines, not an essay, and it accumulates into something genuinely useful: by week six a parent can see whether the insecure list is shrinking. If it is not, the plan is wrong and should change.

The second thing worth agreeing in advance is what evidence will be used. School assessments are the obvious measure and they are not frequent enough to steer by. Timed questions marked against the published criteria, in the tutor's own sessions, give a monthly read. For coursework the measure is the criteria themselves: which bands the current draft would reach and what specifically would move it up.

We also keep session records for a reason beyond parental reassurance. When a school supervisor asks what support a student received on an internal assessment or Extended Essay, an accurate answer should be available on request. A tutoring arrangement that cannot describe its own involvement in a piece of assessed work is a problem waiting for the wrong moment to appear.

process.title: Say which decision is close
process.description: An options form in six weeks, a Mathematics route to confirm, a Higher Level subject under review, or a paper in the next series. The answer changes completely depending on which it is, and the first conversation is quicker if we know before it starts.

process.title: Send the specification details, not the subject names
process.description: The exam board, the syllabus code and the tier for IGCSE subjects; the subject, level and Mathematics route for Diploma students. Your child's school can confirm all of it in one email, and it determines which tutor is the right match rather than an approximate one.

process.title: Use a decision session before committing to teaching
process.description: One or two sessions with the parent present for part of them, mapping what each choice permits later and what it rules out. You leave with a written summary and a short list of precise questions for the school. Weekly teaching only starts if you want it to.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: A full session at no cost before anything is booked. You hear the explanation style, your child decides whether they can work with the person, and we form a view on where marks are currently going. A wrong match means a different tutor, not a discount.

process.title: Agree what gets written down, and review at week six
process.description: Four lines after each session: covered, secure, insecure, set. At week six the insecure list should be shorter. If it is not, we change the approach rather than continuing and hoping. Frequency moves with the calendar in both directions.

whyPoints.title: Decision support is a service, not a sales call
whyPoints.description: Options, Mathematics routes and level changes can be bought as one or two sessions with no teaching attached and no term commitment. A family that leaves with a clear answer and no booking has had the thing they actually needed.

whyPoints.title: The calendar drives the plan
whyPoints.description: Cambridge entry deadlines, forecast grade dates and results dates are published, and we build plans backwards from them. Where a date is not verifiable - which is the case for every IB session date in this project - we say so and point to the official source rather than restating a number we cannot stand behind.

whyPoints.title: Specification-level matching
whyPoints.description: Board, code, tier and level, confirmed before a tutor is proposed. Two subjects with the same name under different boards diverge precisely where the marks are, which is why we will not match on a subject name alone.

whyPoints.title: Written notes after every session
whyPoints.description: What was covered, what is now secure, what remains insecure, what was set. Four lines that accumulate into a record a parent can read in two minutes and a school supervisor can be shown if they ask about coursework support.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on coursework help
whyPoints.description: Criteria, method, referencing and feedback on the student's own drafts. No content supplied, no board material distributed, and no service offering to produce a finished internal assessment. The limit is published because the alternative puts the student at risk.

faqs.question: How early should a Jumeirah Park family start thinking about IGCSE options?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the autumn term of Year 9, several months before the form is signed. By then a student has enough Year 9 evidence to make a sensible judgement, and there is still time to demonstrate higher-tier capability in Mathematics if that is in question. Leaving it until the options evening means making three or four decisions in twelve minutes, each of which sets what is available at 16 and 18. One advisory session beforehand puts a parent in a position to ask the school precise questions instead of general ones.

faqs.question: Should my child take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on two things that families often answer separately. For academic fit, look at how your child earned their IGCSE grade rather than at the grade: a student who enjoys algebraic manipulation and following a proof suits Analysis and Approaches, while one strong on data, context and explanation often does better in Applications and Interpretation. For admissions, check the published requirements of the specific faculties being considered, because some engineering, mathematics and physics courses state a preference. Raise any doubt in term one of Year 12, when a change is still realistic.

faqs.question: Does Combined Science at IGCSE rule out Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, but it adds work. A student entering Higher Level Chemistry from Combined Science has covered less content than a triple-science classmate, and the gap shows in the first term of Year 12 rather than at the end of the course. It is closable with six to ten focused sessions on the specific topics that were thinner, and it is much easier to close before Year 12 starts than during it. If Higher Level sciences are a realistic ambition, the triple route at 16 is the simpler path.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from Jumeirah Park usually attend?
faqs.answer: Dubai British School Jumeirah Park sits inside the community, which gives a significant number of families an unusually short commute for this city. Beyond it, families use Regent International School, Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, and Arcadia Global School or Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle. Diploma students generally travel further, towards Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Dubai Hills, to schools including GEMS Wellington International School, Kings' School Al Barsha, Dubai College and the American School of Dubai.

faqs.question: When are Cambridge IGCSE exams held and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Administrative deadlines sit far ahead of the papers. For the March 2027 series the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May. Every centre belongs to one of six zones with its own timetable version, so confirm the zone with your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the IB directly. The IB's own site cannot be read automatically, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a date restated from a secondary source onto hundreds of pages would eventually be wrong somewhere. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much is safe to say. For specific dates ask your child's IB coordinator or check the IB's assessment pages yourself, then plan backwards from what you are told rather than from a tutoring website.

faqs.question: Can we book one or two advisory sessions without ongoing tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for decision work it is often all that is needed. One or two sessions with the parent present for part of them, working through a specific choice - options blocks, the Mathematics route, whether to drop a Higher Level subject - and ending with a written summary of what each path permits later. You also leave with a short list of precise questions for the school. No weekly booking follows unless you ask for one, and we would rather give a clear answer than convert an enquiry.

faqs.question: Is three Higher Level subjects plus the core realistic for an average student?
faqs.answer: Three Higher Levels is the Diploma's standard requirement, so it is designed to be possible, but the choice of which three matters enormously. Three Higher Levels in subjects where a student is competent rather than strong, taken alongside the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay, produces four pieces of extended independent work due within roughly the same six months. Dropping one to Standard Level early in Year 12 is a legitimate and frequently correct decision, and it usually raises the overall points total rather than lowering it.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to villas in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not place a tutor at any UAE address; visits to a student's home are something we offer only in India. All teaching here is one-to-one over live video. For the work this community asks for most - route decisions, Higher Level subject teaching, coursework method - the format makes little difference to the quality and a substantial difference to the match, because your child is paired with someone who has taught that exact specification rather than with whoever is free to drive to this community at 19:00.

faqs.question: Which regulator inspects my child's school, and what if we move emirate?
faqs.answer: In Dubai it is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve fees and curricula as well as inspecting. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The regulator determines what an inspection report means and who handles a complaint.

faqs.question: How much help can a tutor give with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, help narrow a research question that is too broad for 4,000 words, teach a referencing convention, demonstrate critical reading of sources, show what a research journal entry needs to contain, and give feedback on a draft the student has written alone. A tutor cannot supply content, restructure the essay into its final form, or edit it line by line until the voice has changed. The supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and our session notes exist so that declaration can be accurate.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for my child to practise with?
faqs.answer: We do not distribute board material as downloads. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing them is a copyright problem - for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. What we do is cite the official source, link to it, and work from material the school has legitimately given the student. Within a session a tutor can set questions, mark against the published criteria and explain exactly how a mark scheme awards credit.

faqs.question: What does my child need to have done by the February half-term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: For a June series: the whole specification covered at least once, at least two full timed papers per subject completed under exam conditions, and a written list of insecure specification points being worked through rather than revisited at random. Entries and tier will already be fixed by then. For a March or November series the same checklist applies earlier. The administrative work - confirming the correct zone timetable with the exams officer, checking entries match the subjects taught - should be done before, not during, the revision period.

faqs.question: What should we receive from a tutor after each session?
faqs.answer: Four things, briefly: what was covered against the specification, what the student could do unaided by the end, what remains insecure, and what has been set before the next session. That record accumulates into something checkable - by week six the insecure list should be visibly shorter, and if it is not, the plan needs changing rather than extending. We also keep the record so that a school supervisor asking about support on a piece of coursework can be given an accurate answer.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Higher Level specialist be matched for a Jumeirah Park student?
faqs.answer: Common Higher Level subjects - Mathematics in either route, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Economics - are usually matched within a few working days, with a free trial lesson following. Narrow requests take longer: a specific Group 2 language at Higher Level, or a fixed slot that only works at one hour on one day of the week. Where the pool is genuinely thin we say so and offer a different time with the right specialist, an alternative tutor with an honest account of their coverage, or a short wait with a date attached to it.

dubai/jumeirah-park.closingHeading: Name the decision, then the deadline
dubai/jumeirah-park.closingBody: Tutoring in Jumeirah Park is most valuable slightly before a family thinks they need it. If an options form, a Mathematics route or a Higher Level review is coming up, one or two advisory sessions will usually tell you more than a term of weekly teaching started afterwards. If the decision is already made and the work is subject teaching, send us the board, the code and the level, and we will match a specialist and arrange a free trial lesson. Either way the first useful step is the same: tell us which decision is close and when it closes.
